| A deferred action reports an admitted prerequisite and recovery path without pretending the user can invoke it yet. | A permanently deferred/unavailable control is counted as a successful required product capability, or missing admission is relabeled as deferment. | Preserve truthful deferred state but require an independently eligible positive path for capability-completeness acceptance. |
| The renderer exposes only disclosable availability and accessible busy/disabled status, while the server binds the actual current principal. | Distinct private Membership failures are leaked through reasons, or disabled HTML is used as authorization or command deduplication. | Preserve disclosure scope and real server-side validation; visual state cannot confer or revoke model authority. |

This table defines expected finished-system semantics, not a claim that the
present Gesso view helpers already implement every availability category.
*** A small view API

Once preparation succeeds, view code can remain ordinary Hiccup:

#+begin_src clojure
(defn request-card-view [{:keys [request actions]}]
  (let [claim (actions/require-prepared! :request/claim (:claim actions))]
    [:article.request-card
     [:h3 (:title request)]
     [:p.status (name (:status request))]
     (case (actions/availability claim)
       :available
       (gesso/action
        {:binding (actions/binding claim)
         :presentation {:pending-label "Claiming..."
                        :class "gesso-action gesso-action--primary"}}
        "Claim")
       :unavailable
       nil
       :deferred
       [:span.action-status "Claim is temporarily unavailable."])]))
#+end_src

This example's Claim preparation contract admits available, policy-unavailable
(as =:unavailable= in this illustrative view API), and deferred variants. A
deferred result has a declared prerequisite and recovery path; it is not a
missing plan disguised as a temporary UI state. The final Claim mutation has
no input-collection phase; an unexpected needs-input result is a typed contract
mismatch, not an implicit nil or enabled empty form. By contrast, an explicitly
authored Reassign *entry* may have a complete helper-selection flow even while
its final mutation still needs an eligible selected target. Construction
failure is raised by preparation/validation before this view can serve an
incomplete active control. A hidden required action remains subject to
the declared preparation and application-acceptance checks.

The renderer derives routes, HTMX attributes, command-wire fields, plan and
artifact references, correlation, and progression handling from the assembly.
A view author does not repeat these details in strings. If required metadata is
missing, the renderer reports the exact missing edge and rejects incomplete
managed construction. An explicitly non-executable unavailable affordance
is permitted only when the *declared semantic policy* selected that
availability outcome with a complete non-executable rendering contract.
It is not a catch-all fallback for missing plan, route, artifact, command
binding, or browser runtime. The failing path cannot emit an otherwise
active physical request.

Semantic identity is preserved through rendering. Binding, encoding, and
transport selection may elaborate an operation but cannot silently substitute
another operation or weaken its required protocol. A valid pre-serialization
Hiccup annotation records the author's intended semantic identity, but cannot
by itself prove that the *physical* browser request matches it. The checked
surface must join the actual method, concrete route, target/submitter behavior,
plan, artifact and required transport to the assembled operation. Additional
= hx-get=, =hx-put=, native form submission, form overrides, or conflicting
string/keyword render attributes may create a second or ambiguous request
even when a canonical button's semantic metadata remains intact. The
complete inspected physical request coordinates must be compatible with the
declared mode; one marked request does not exempt sibling or alternate
requests.

The framework may retain in-process Hiccup metadata for pre-serialization
inspection; that metadata does not automatically survive HTML serialization
or authenticate anything returned by the browser. An opaque encoded binding is
not necessarily authenticated, and authentication of its bytes would still not
establish current model authorization.

*** Prepared affordance is not a security capability

The term /prepared affordance/ is preferable for the object consumed by a view.
If the implementation calls it an operation capability, diagnostics must
qualify that meaning. It is not an irrevocable or unforgeable authorization
credential merely because the server prepared it.

A trusted execution capability has a different contract: it permits a scoped
server action under current admission rules. A view binding cannot supply the
transaction handle, authenticated principal, or other trusted resource required
by the model.

Browser-returned observation information is an observed-basis claim unless a
trusted boundary establishes something stronger. An authenticated receipt can
prove its issuer's stated historical fact under that receipt contract. It does
not prove the human saw the card, the browser installed it, or permission still
holds now.

Gesso constructs or admits stronger semantic values at the boundary with enough
information. Web developers should not have to hand-assemble proof wrappers to
render an ordinary button. In-process admission discipline prevents accidental
misuse; it is not a sandbox against a determined author with arbitrary trusted
host access. A received operation identifier, observed-basis claim, plan
fingerprint, command identifier or encoded client value is input under its
declared trust contract, not an execution credential. Trusted server-side
operation resolution, authenticated principal, current domain guards and
qualified command-outcome disclosure remain independent obligations.

*** Raw HTMX and presentation freedom

Ordinary HTMX remains a first-class mechanism for interactions deliberately
outside Choreo's promises. The distinction is explicit: an ordinary affordance
has its ordinary contract; a managed affordance has a complete managed
realization or a precise non-executable failure/unavailability state.

An ordinary route still obeys server authentication and model safety. It must
not occupy a route reserved for a managed operation as a way to bypass its
protocol. This prohibition concerns the *physical* method and route, including
a native form's actual action and submitter override, not only the presence
of =:choreo/op= metadata. A view may intentionally use raw HTMX on a separate,
legitimate route, or an explicitly admitted non-optimistic realization of
an operation when its own contract is complete; it may not use either path
to bypass an operation's required protected server-side model semantics.
Declaring fewer client guarantees does not authorize direct unprotected
writes. A malformed managed request must not silently become raw HTMX
because its metadata was lost during a render or swap.

Views own text, element choice, semantic CSS, icons, layout, ARIA, pending
labels, and how provisional or authoritative states look. They must not
interpret a newer database token as command rejection or choose reconciliation
policy. They display the decisions made by the admitted model/runtime contract.

Status must be understandable without relying only on color or motion.
Keyboard activation, form submission, disabled/busy semantics, and duplicate
activation handling must match the declared entry policy. Loading and
provisional treatment must not be falsely announced as authoritative
incorporation or adopted current state. An available action and a complete
input-collection entry must remain operable using the declared keyboard,
focus and accessible-status path; a policy-hidden, deferred or failed
construction must not retain an accidental active native/HTMX submit path.
Disabling a button alone is not the framework's command deduplication
mechanism, nor does an =aria-disabled= or =aria-busy= marker provide server
authentication, an actual pending-command lock or transaction-current
permission.

*** Assembly obligations and diagnostics

An enabled managed control creates obligations for its complete path: operation,
choreography, projected plan, loaded browser artifact, transport, trusted server
entry, model realization, outcome mapping, acquisition, and presentation.
Part VII checks these *before each relevant surface is served*, including
dynamically generated surfaces. Its later position in this document does
not permit serving incomplete controls until a future check runs.

Actual dynamically rendered Hiccup is checked against the admitted
ApplicationAssembly at the serialization boundary, so a newly eligible branch
cannot bypass preflight merely because it was absent from a sample snapshot.
The result is scoped to that actual rendering and the trusted serving path
that invokes the guard. It does not enumerate all possible Clojure branches,
prove that every deployed server entry used that wrapper, or validate arbitrary
pre-serialized HTML without an appropriate enforcement boundary. Subsequent
asset, route, deployment or binding changes require fresh applicable
admission; a prior successful check is not permanent authority.

Errors preserve source component, operation, role/subject when disclosable,
expected binding/plan/capability, and the missing or incompatible edge, with
physical request method and route where relevant. Missing plans should not
collapse into generic malformed HTML errors. Diagnostics must preserve the
difference between policy unavailability, input collection, deferral, and
implementation failure. Public-facing errors disclose only permitted reasons;
private repair reports may carry the fuller source and correspondence context.

*** Paired rendered-affordance and no-downgrade cases

The following cases distinguish a checked, useful view from a Hiccup-shaped
certificate that has not yet been connected to an actual physical operation.

| Eligible positive history | Adverse or incomplete history | Required evidence |
|---------------------------+-------------------------------+-------------------|
| A prepared Claim binding renders a single managed button whose actual POST path, plan, artifact and trusted entry all match the assembled Claim operation. | The same annotated button also emits an alternative =hx-get= or an overriding native submitter action into another route. | Validate *each* physical request coordinate, not merely the existence of canonical metadata on the node; reject any unadmitted extra or alternate request. |
| An ordinary HTMX interaction uses its declared non-Choreo route, while a separate managed Claim uses its exact registered semantic route. | A raw =hx-post= or native form submits to a managed Claim route without an admitted =:choreo/op= operation, or the managed metadata disappears during rendering. | Preserve raw HTMX as a valid option, but fail closed on the assembled semantic route collision and missing managed identity. |
| A prepared manager Reassign entry opens its complete input-collection form and, after selecting a distinct eligible helper, prepares the final guarded Reassign. | A hidden final Reassign lacks target input, but rendering silently replaces it with ordinary HTMX or counts a permanently disabled selector as feature completion. | Treat complete =:needs-input= entry and complete final mutation separately; reject construction failure and independently test eligible positive product behavior. |
| An accessible Claim button displays provisional pending status while C42's incorporation or canonical installation remains unestablished. | A green button, busy marker, or local success animation is used as proof of command confirmation, current authority, or server-side deduplication. | Display only admitted provisional knowledge, and require separate command and physical evidence for stronger claims. |
| A dynamically rendered, user-specific Claim branch is checked under the current assembled application before its Hiccup is serialized. | A snapshot-only scan is treated as exhaustive, or another deployed raw/pre-serialized HTML path bypasses the actual guard. | State exactly which rendered occurrence and served path were checked; require full deployed entrypoint coverage for broader certification rather than inventing it. |

A successful positive case must exercise the intended browser and trusted
server entry under the actual operation contract. A negative test must
reach the physical collision, altered request, malformed construction,
or missing-admission boundary it claims to test, not merely be rejected
earlier by unrelated fixture data.


** Clojure and ClojureScript execution
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: req-portable-execution
:END:

The permanent executable semantic core gives projected behavior one meaning
across supported hosts. Shared =.cljc= definitions are the preferred realization
where practical. JVM, Node, and Chromium must not carry independently handwritten
versions of the same state machine merely because their callbacks differ.

This commitment does not make the whole application portable. Database access,
trusted authentication, arbitrary server code, DOM manipulation, and network
integration belong to declared host boundaries. Full-language actions remain
available there. The core interprets their contracts and admitted completions;
it does not need to understand or emulate all application code.

Portability is a *semantic* obligation, not merely the ability to compile the
same namespace. Supported plan versions and inputs must give the same
transition, role-local value, classification, effect request and ownership
decision on JVM Clojure and supported ClojureScript hosts. Where a result
depends on equality, numeric representation, map/set membership, ordering,
serialization, exception classification or absent-versus-=nil= distinctions,
the plan's portable value contract either fixes that meaning or rejects the
unsupported value/operation at admission. Different printed diagnostics,
source coordinates and physical handle representations are not differences in
semantic behavior; differences in branch selection or effect authorization are.
An opaque backend basis cannot be compared with host-local lexical or numeric
order, regardless of whether both environments can print it.

The executable semantic core is distinct from the later proof kernel/checker.
The former executes admitted transition meaning. The latter checks derivations
or other stated judgments about that meaning. Compiler, verifier, and proof
machinery need not ship to the production browser. The artifact executed by a
production browser must be the compatible checked projection, not an
independently handwritten approximation of the verified behavior. Build-time
checks and tests may observe that semantic machine, but diagnostic sidecars,
witnesses or optional proof metadata must not become hidden inputs that change
its transitions. A same-source or same-schema claim is not itself a compiler,
runtime, host-effect or global refinement proof.

*** One vocabulary from construction through execution

Part III's role-local vocabulary is canonical:

| Node kind | Runtime responsibility |
|-----------+------------------------|
| =:local= | Request the declared local action and consume its admitted completion. |
| =:authoritative= | At the appropriate trusted role, request a public model operation and consume its admitted typed result. |
| =:branch= | Select a declared successor using an established typed value. |
| =:send= | Issue a declared participant communication with the required known payload. |
| =:receive= | Await an admitted participant message matching one unambiguous alternative. |
| =:await= | Await a declared environment event from its registered source contract. |
| =:return= | Complete this role's local trajectory with its declared outcome. |

Optimism does not introduce a separately handwritten transition-table language
with different guard or outcome semantics. Provisional derivation, command
handling, acquisition, and installation are declared actions/events coordinated
through the same vocabulary and the browser adapter's explicit ownership
contract.

A projected =:receive= is not satisfied by an environment event with the same
keyword. A normalized map cannot select its own trust or ownership class.
Participant communications, authoritative observations, local action completions,
and environment events retain their distinct admission paths.

The plan format has closed semantic keys and versioned interpretation. Unknown
opcodes, unresolved action references, malformed successor locations, overlapping
receive alternatives, or unsupported event contracts are construction failures.
An explicit extension area can carry nonsemantic metadata without changing
execution. Semantic extensions require a registered interpretation and their own
assurance contract.

An =:await= environment event does not satisfy an expected =:receive= merely
because the two events share a keyword or payload shape. A role-local
environment completion, a participant delivery, an authoritative operation
result and a qualified authoritative observation have distinct admission
provenance and effects on role knowledge. Admitting a decoded value must not
assign its own source class, trusted principal or authoritative basis.
Serialization across the browser/server boundary discards any authority
attributed solely to in-process wrappers; the receiver re-establishes the
relevant category using the declared trusted protocol and source.

*** State ownership and effects

The role-local machine owns its protocol state and established values. The
shared browser coordinator owns cross-execution target arbitration, obligations,
and resource lifetimes where required. These are composed responsibilities,
not competing copies of one machine. Each semantic fact has one declared owner.

The imperative shell owns physical handles: DOM references, timers, transport
objects, listeners, and opaque continuity captures. It interprets admitted
effects and reports correlated completions/failures. It does not independently
choose successors or reinterpret a domain outcome from a status string.

An abstract transition can update semantic intent immediately and request a
physical effect. The facts it records must match that point in the lifecycle:
request issued is not request completed; observation acquired is not observation
installed; installation permitted is not adoption completed. A host may report
immediate completion before the portable machine enters its formal await state;
the declared registration/buffering or ordered handoff contract must preserve
that completion without fabricating success or losing it. Effect completion
is admitted only for the issued physical effect, current permitted owner and
declared completion source, at the actual semantic boundary. Host exceptions
are runtime faults with recovery/retirement obligations, not proof that a
previously valid semantic state/event was impossible.

The runtime allocates fresh effect/resource instances through a declared
mechanism. Nondeterministic choices such as UUIDs and sampled time enter as
explicit admitted inputs or action results. A pure transition does not secretly
consult a global clock or allocate different command IDs when replayed in a
test. Before a command's first possible send, its stable binding is already
recorded by the appropriate owner.

Physical effects carry the owner, target/resource instance, operation/command
correlation where relevant, and typed payload/reference required for admission.
A callback copies the correlation issued with that physical resource. It must
not fetch a newly current execution ID and relabel an old callback as belonging
to the replacement execution.

The transition semantics are total over their *supported* states, normalized
event classes and declared contracts: an applicable event advances, stutters,
is classified duplicate/stale, requests recovery, or is rejected with a typed
fault. An unknown event, malformed payload, unsupported plan version or
unadmitted source cannot silently fall through into browser-specific callback
code. Where a state/event combination is excluded by construction, that
exclusion needs an explicit invariant and appropriate check; an unexpected
host exception must not be repackaged as a legitimate domain rejection.

A local execution's semantic retirement revokes its ownership immediately,
whether or not physical timers, DOM nodes or XHR handles still exist. Remaining
handles are cleanup debt. A successor may inherit declared command-resolution
or acquisition obligations through an admitted handoff, not the retired
execution's old timer callback, target incarnation or actor-local knowledge.
A value copied into =NormalizedEvent= is data for admission, not proof the
sender may revive that retired execution.

*** Cross-host portability and physical-boundary witnesses

The common conformance corpus executes the same admitted plan and *semantic
transition functions* in JVM Clojure, Node ClojureScript and Chromium
ClojureScript, comparing portable semantic results, typed rejection classes,
effect intents and owner/obligation state. Browser-host tests additionally
observe actual effect emission, callback correlation and physical completion.
An equal JVM/Node result is evidence for those exercised cases only; it neither
establishes all possible compiler behavior nor certifies Chromium or real host
effect correspondence.

| Eligible positive history | Adversarial or unsupported history | Required result |
|---------------------------+------------------------------------+-----------------|
| The same admitted branch selector, closed event payload and portable basis relation select the same successor in JVM, Node and Chromium. | A JS precision/identity or host-specific collection comparison changes the branch, or an opaque X20 basis is ordered by its label. | Preserve canonical portable value meaning or reject the unsupported input/version; never silently choose a different transition. |
| A role awaits a declared participant =:receive= and admits a source-qualified correlated message. | An environment =:await= callback arrives with the same event keyword or a forged map claims trusted message provenance. | Keep message and environment admission distinct; the wrong source does not satisfy role-local receipt or establish knowledge. |
| A physical installation request is registered, its immediate completion is buffered and later admitted for the current owner and target. | Completion arrives before the machine awaits and disappears, or the shell marks a board adopted merely because an effect was requested. | Preserve admitted completion across the race and require actual qualified physical evidence for adoption. |
| An execution retires E1 and its successor E2 takes separately admitted recovery obligations. | A late E1 timer copies E2's now-current execution ID, or a lingering DOM handle resumes E1. | Reject the old correlation without reviving retired semantic or physical rights; retain unresolved command/acquisition work through explicit handoff. |
| A supported but inapplicable event produces a specified typed stale/duplicate/fault outcome with no unauthorized effects. | An unknown opcode, malformed normalized payload or unexpected host exception falls through to an independent browser branch or becomes a false model rejection. | Enforce closed, total supported semantic interpretation; classify admission failure and host faults separately with declared recovery. |

The test corpus must retain both useful successful transitions and the
adversarial cases above; a reject-all machine or a synthetic matching report
cannot establish functional completeness. Actual provider, HTMX, DOM, XTDB
and deployment obligations remain independently qualified.
*** A concrete installation segment

The following is an inspection of a generated local segment using the canonical
node kinds. Entry already supplies an admitted observation reference and an
admitted installation request. Registered action and event contracts supply
schema, provenance, current-owner, and failure obligations not repeated in this
compact payload.

#+begin_src clojure
{:gesso.choreo/type :gesso.choreo/executable-plan
 :gesso.choreo/version 1
 :role :browser
 :initial 0
 :states
 {0 {:op :local
     :action :presentation/request-installation
     :requires #{:installation/request}
     :outputs #{:installation/effect-ref}
     :next 1}
  1 {:op :await
     :events {:presentation/installation-completed 2
              :presentation/installation-failed 3}
     :event-contracts
     {:presentation/installation-completed
      {:required #{:installation/effect-ref :installation/completion-ref}
       :optional #{}
       :open-data? false}
      :presentation/installation-failed
      {:required #{:installation/effect-ref :installation/failure-ref}
       :optional #{}
       :open-data? false}}}
  2 {:op :local
     :action :presentation/adopt-completed
     :requires #{:installation/request :installation/completion-ref}
     :outputs #{:presentation/adoption-ref}
     :next 4}
  3 {:op :local
     :action :presentation/retain-and-recover
     :requires #{:installation/request :installation/failure-ref}
     :outputs #{:presentation/recovery-owner-ref}
     :next 5}
  4 {:op :return :outcome :presentation/ready}
  5 {:op :return :outcome :presentation/recovery-handed-off}}}
#+end_src

The representation version is illustrative. A concrete emitted segment must
satisfy the actual selected schema and its registered interfaces; this excerpt
is not a second author-maintained implementation. The source-level
=:presentation/installation-completed= and =:presentation/installation-failed=
names describe *distinct admitted source outcomes*, not two strings the
browser may choose by examining a response code. The failure-reference
contract includes failed, partially completed and indeterminate realization
with an explicit affected-target/coverage classification where supported.
If the host cannot determine what physically installed, it must retain that
uncertainty rather than constructing a false completed or wholly failed event.
An absent callback is neither event; interruption, deadline and owner-loss
paths belong to the registered wait/recovery contract.

The request action completes when installation work has been registered and
issued under the host contract. It does not claim that the DOM changed. The host
must buffer or otherwise serialize an immediate completion so it cannot be lost
before the machine reaches its await boundary.

Registration binds an effect instance, source observation, target incarnation,
current owner, method of realization and completion/failure contract *before*
the physical action can complete. An HTMX before-swap allowance, HTTP success,
request-finished event, or provisional DOM render establishes neither the
required physical replacement nor canonical adoption. If installation consists
of multiple independent targets, completion is a scoped per-target fact rather
than an unconditional whole-board success. A promised all-or-nothing
installation requires an actual physical mechanism or an admitted compensation
and recovery policy.

The completed event is admitted only from that issued effect, the declared
host completion source and the current permitted target owner. The completion
reference resolves to actual physical completion evidence with the matching
effect instance, target incarnation, observation scope and installed footprint.
It does not become authoritative because an environment payload calls itself
completed, nor can a late callback claim the generation of a successor.

The adopt action consumes admitted completion and rechecks the shared
coordinator's *current* owner, scope, source observation, independently newer
adopted facts, and obligations accumulated since installation was requested.
Merely possessing a reference with a familiar shape is insufficient. A
qualified installation may discharge precisely covered obligations; it does
not erase later Live invalidations, a pending granted Refresh, a newer
creator-local card/membership, or unrelated targets. If the source was
valid but the completion owner was superseded, the old callback cannot
promote or overwrite a newer installation.

The failed path preserves the failure's scope, including partial or
indeterminate installation where applicable, and establishes the declared
recovery owner before returning. It does not reject an already incorporated
command. Already installed targets, remaining unsafe/intermediate DOM,
unfulfilled acquire-and-adopt obligations and local continuity cleanup need
their own typed physical evidence and repair disposition. A recovery handoff
cannot inherit retired callbacks, timers, target grants or role-local
knowledge merely because it inherits the pending requirement.

Owner retirement, source loss, or unbounded absence of a completion follows
the segment's registered interruption/deadline and recovery contract. Assembly
must reject a required physical effect with no such handling when it can
strand this wait. An implementation-specific synchronous effect interpreter
does not make asynchronous host completion impossible: the projected machine
suspends at its declared =:await= and receives qualified completion through
the adapter/host boundary.

The fragment does not claim that all browser state belongs to one execution.
The adopt action communicates with the shared coordinator through its admitted
interface. That coordinator updates current adoption and advisory debt from its
latest state, preserving obligations which arrived after installation was
requested.

*** Claim execution uses independent outcome and installation paths

A complete generated Claim trajectory composes segments like the one above with
command handling. The following table describes semantic boundaries rather than
an alternative executable format:

| Boundary | Required successor behavior |
|----------+-----------------------------|
| Invocation admitted | Record stable intent and execution ownership; derive permitted provisional presentation; issue declared effects. |
| Command submitted or delivery attempted | Retain pending/unknown knowledge until evidence establishes more; submission alone is not incorporation. |
| Accepted command evidence | Record qualified historical incorporation knowledge independently of whether a current card is available or installed; the status is not a claim about the current RequestAssignment. |
| Rejected command evidence | Record terminal command rejection only under the qualified, binding-scoped exclusion/disclosure contract; one failed physical attempt is insufficient. |
| Unknown delivery or local deadline | Preserve unresolved command attribution unless stronger qualified evidence already exists; retain or transfer command and presentation recovery independently. |
| Observation acquired | Validate scope and progression; propose installation without claiming adoption. |
| Installation completed | Admit completion under the current owner; update adoption and discharge only covered obligations. |
| Installation failed | Preserve command knowledge and unresolved presentation debt; follow repair or reacquisition. |
| Execution retired | Revoke its local rights; preserve or transfer unresolved command/work obligations according to the contract. |

A deadline racing with a participant response requires explicit arbitration
between the projected machine and its owner-relative adapter. The timeout is
not smuggled into =:receive= as a forged participant message. The supported
waiting/interruption mechanism must preserve the declared race semantics; a
projection backend lacking that mechanism rejects the unsupported construction
rather than dropping the timeout branch. Both events retain the generation
and physical resource correlation issued with their original owners;
the losing callback is stale for that execution and cannot resume its
terminal branch. If a late source-qualified outcome establishes historical
C42 success, a separately admitted recovery owner may incorporate that
knowledge without resurrecting the old E42 machine or target grant.

Whichever event is admitted first may change local ownership, but it cannot
change what evidence means. A later success can still resolve a retained command
through an admitted recovery owner. It cannot restore retired installation
rights. A late timer cannot erase a known success. Nor can a successful C42
replay force Alice's historical Claim back into a card now reflecting Bob as
primary helper after a later authorized Reassign. The qualified current
Request/RequestAssignment observation and installed source decide current
presentation; C42's retained result decides only its attributable history.

*** Paired installation and Claim execution witnesses

These cases exercise real runtime boundaries. A caller-supplied map containing
=:installation/completion-ref= is not itself an admitted physical completion,
and a green callback report is not independent product acceptance.

| Eligible positive execution | Adverse or ambiguous execution | Required result |
|-----------------------------+--------------------------------+-----------------|
| A qualified scoped card is requested, its matching after-swap physical completion arrives for the current owner, and the coordinator adopts only the installed coverage. | The before-swap permission or HTTP 200 is treated as completed adoption, or a callback from a retired request claims the new request generation. | Separate allowance, actual host completion and qualified adoption; stale callbacks cannot advance the newer frontier. |
| Installation is registered before the host completes synchronously; the queued completion is delivered at the matching =:await=. | Completion fires before the waiter is armed and is lost, or a duplicate completion advances twice. | Preserve once-correlated admission and deterministic duplicate handling across the registration-to-await race. |
| A current Request card installs while a newer board invalidation or separate creator-local card was registered after the request began. | The stale broad installation clears the newer requirement or overwrites a newer locally adopted card. | Re-read current coordinator obligations and protected footprint at adoption; preserve unsettled work and independently newer facts. |
| One of two installation targets completes and the other is indeterminate; the recovery owner receives exactly the remaining repair work. | An all-or-nothing installed label is issued or the command is marked rejected because DOM work partly failed. | Report partial/unknown physical effects, retain per-target coverage and command knowledge separately. |
| C42's server-qualified historical Claim outcome is incorporated under current disclosure while a later Reassign has installed Bob as helper. | A late E42 timeout erases success, or C42 replay reinstalls Alice's obsolete presentation. | Retained command outcome and independently qualified current RequestAssignment remain distinct. |
| A timer and a participant message race at one suspended execution; the first admitted event settles the local branch. | The timeout is forged as a participant message, or the losing old-owner callback resumes a retired machine. | Preserve distinct source classes, current resource generations and the declared recovery continuation. |

These positive cases are independent of reject-all safety checks: installation,
Claim, recovery and user-visible current presentation must be reachable under
eligible premises, and failures must be observed at the actual stated host,
semantic or trusted command boundary.

*** Boundary shapes, knowledge, and provenance

Actions declare required values, optional inputs where supported, closed outputs,
possible failures, effects, and completion behavior. Validators are compiled
for the admitted schema/registry version and invoked unconditionally at the
relevant boundaries. Optional assertions disabled in production are not boundary
validation.

Missing, present nil, false, and absent optional output are distinct according
to the schema. A later completion which omits an optional field must not inherit
an old value accidentally. An unknown branch selector is a typed contract fault
rather than permission to choose an arbitrary default. Validation binds the
selected *issued effect instance* and its declared action/event contract,
including its loaded interpretation version; passing a value check for a
different action, completion generation or schema is not admission.

When an event omits an optional output, the resulting state follows its
explicit retention/clearing rule instead of accidentally reusing a stale
value from a prior completion. Duplicate, delayed and wrong-generation
events are checked before they can change that state. A closed result schema
cannot become open by inserting extra fields in an external callback.

Passing a value schema establishes shape. An opaque local function returning a
map is not automatically an authoritative source. Its output retains the
provenance and asserted properties justified by its declared action contract.
Authoritative outputs and observations cross their dedicated admission boundary;
ordinary event normalization does not upgrade them. Value shape, source
provenance, current owner, qualified observation scope and authorized
disclosure are *separate* premises. A callback cannot claim that its
response came from a participant, trusted backend or current physical
target merely by copying an in-process event tag or binding token.

Full-language implementations may access facilities beyond the portable core
under their declared host contracts. Properties such as purity, effect footprint,
termination, and semantic accuracy remain explicit premises when not derived or
enforced. A managed local action with an asserted functional contract is valid
under an accepting assurance policy; an unresolved action reference is not.

*** Normalization precedes admission

The browser boundary converts raw HTMX, timer, EventSource, DOM, and lifecycle
callbacks into bounded normalized data. It may decode and copy primitive values
and issued correlation. It does not derive authority from mutable attributes,
HTML shape, event names, or a physical handle's continued existence.

Admission identifies the event class from its registered source path, resolves
the declared owner, checks current applicability, validates payload and binding,
and then delivers the event to the appropriate semantic transition. Untrusted
fields cannot opt into a weaker ownership class. The issuer of a physical
effect retains an immutable reference to the instance, generation, source,
expected completion and target incarnation. An asynchronous callback carries
that issued identity, rather than reading the currently active execution and
relabelling itself. Admission is checked again at the semantic transition
boundary; normalizing bytes is neither a replay grant nor a physical
installation/completion witness.

A nominal record or opaque wrapper may prevent accidental substitution within
cooperating code. After untrusted serialization, the receiving boundary must
re-establish the required category through validation, authentication,
acquisition, or verification. The wrapper's name is not transferable proof.

*** Explicit transition and failure results

For every supported state/event class, the runtime has an explicit result:
advance, accepted no-op, stale/duplicate rejection, recovery transition, or
runtime/contract fault. Unknown event classes and invalid plan versions are
classified at admission. Unexpected exceptions are faults, not evidence the
input combination was mathematically impossible.

Event-admission results use a separate vocabulary from presentation settlements
and model outcomes. For example, =:step/applied= and =:step/ignored-stale= describe
a runtime decision; they do not mean Claim was accepted or rejected.

Selection must be deterministic under the declared contract. Construction
rejects overlapping alternatives unless their equivalence or explicit arbitration
is established. A runtime must not simply take the first matching event keyword
from several candidates and silently ignore the rest.

A total dispatcher over a supported event vocabulary does not prove arbitrary
Clojure callbacks terminate. It also does not imply every event is valid. The
scope of totality, supported value domain, and callback premises must be stated.
Invalid states can produce typed invariant violations with a safe fault/recovery
path rather than undefined mutation. A semantic step classification such as
=:step/ignored-stale=, a host effect failure, a qualified historical command
result and an installed authoritative card inhabit different namespaces
and evidence domains. None may be used to infer another simply because a
diagnostic report presents them together.

An admitted transition updates portable semantic state before interpretation
of the effects it emits, so a synchronous physical callback cannot observe
an obsolete pre-transition owner. This ordering does not certify the physical
effect: synchronous exceptions and asynchronous rejection retain their
declared failure/recovery classification without fabricating command
rejection or completed installation.

*** Cross-host portability

The shared core and corpus run under JVM Clojure, Node ClojureScript, and
Chromium ClojureScript. Tests compare normalized semantic transitions, emitted
abstract effects, correlation, and fault classifications for the same admitted
inputs, including stale and adversarial schedules.

The portable data contract specifies numeric range and precision, equality,
collection semantics, missing/nil/false behavior, encoding, and errors. JavaScript
numeric precision must not silently alter an identity or selector. Platform
objects, mutable DOM references, and arbitrary functions do not appear in the
portable plan payload. Registered action references bind host implementations
through the assembly's separate implementation contract.

Source sharing reduces divergence but does not prove every compiler/runtime
behavior equivalent. Cross-host conformance tests remain evidence for exercised
cases. A stronger claim identifies its formal correspondence and external
compiler/runtime premises.

Production tests execute the canonical emitted plan and the production semantic
core. Pure tests can substitute declared effect interpreters; browser integration
tests additionally exercise the actual shell and DOM/HTMX lifecycle. A mock that
always returns installed does not establish physical installation correctness.
Advanced compilation and actual packaged assets need their own relevant checks.
Conformance spans the emitted canonical plan, the exact bound implementation
and production asset rather than a test-only stand-in with the same source
name. The check records precisely which JVM/Node/Chromium cases ran and which
physical browser callbacks, deployment paths and provider effects remain
unexamined. A matching diagnostic/source stamp is not proof that the
physical asset contains that plan and implementation closure.

*** Compatibility and deployment

The runtime distinguishes plan representation version, operation/interface
meaning, protocol compatibility, admitted assembly identity, and exact packaged
artifact identity. Deployment identity records physical rollout where needed;
it does not substitute for any of these contracts or give all resources one
shared lifetime.

Parsing old bytes does not establish continuation compatibility. A suspended
browser can retain an unresolved command while its old local plan is retired.
The admitted compatibility/recovery policy must preserve that command reference
and current disclosure requirements without resuming incompatible state.

On version or assembly change, compatibility is checked separately for
(1) parsing the plan, (2) executable semantic operation and interface meaning,
(3) registered host actions and physical protocols, and (4) permission to
continue each currently suspended execution. A recognizable but incompatible
plan is not malformed, yet must not be resumed. The old execution is
semantically retired first; physical cancellation, listener removal and
resource cleanup follow under their own fallible contract. A new compatible
runtime may receive *declared handoff obligations* for command-specific
reconciliation, scoped reacquisition, installation, and retained Live/Refresh
requirements. It cannot inherit old generation/callback rights or role-local
message knowledge by copying a state map.

If the physical cleanup or authoritative reconstruction fails, retain the
unresolved obligations and report the failure under the appropriate scope.
The original historical command's stable binding must not silently become
a new command, and a current Request card cannot establish the disposition
of that old command. Likewise, an already completed command outcome does not
prove that a new browser asset has installed a compatible authoritative view.

Exact executable payload identity, compatibility judgment and packaged
asset identity answer different questions. A rollout identifier or an equal
source/digest label does not justify cross-version continuation, proof-sidecar
attachment or physical entrypoint coverage without the requisite binding
evidence.

The production browser executes admitted local plans; it does not reconstruct
the global choreography, rerun projection, load proof DAGs, or solve obligations
to decide an ordinary transition. Executable guards and necessary admission
contracts remain executable. Their explanations remain separate.

*** Paired admission, compatibility and deployment cases

The positive corpus exercises real admitted transitions and compatible
recovery, while adverse histories reach the protected boundary rather
than passing because some unrelated fixture was invalid.

| Eligible positive history | Adverse or uncertain history | Required classification |
|---------------------------+-----------------------------|
| A registered local action completes with the current effect generation and an explicit optional-output clearing rule. | A late callback for an older generation omits that optional value and accidentally inherits its predecessor, or supplies undeclared result keys. | Admit only the registered source/contract and current instance; apply missing/nil/false and clearing semantics explicitly. |
| A participant message enters via its authenticated and correlated source path; an environment timer separately enters via its issued owner. | A decoded map uses the expected event keyword or wrapper name to impersonate a participant or currently installed target. | Normalize as data; require source-specific admission and reject the wrong provenance without inventing role knowledge. |
| A new browser asset starts a compatible plan, while an older incompatible suspended execution retires and hands off C42 resolution and board acquisition. | The old plan parses so it is resumed anyway, or retiring the execution erases unknown C42 and pending Refresh/installation debt. | Distinguish parse, plan, interface, host and continuation compatibility; retain obligations under newly admitted owners, not stale callbacks. |
| The semantic state commits its transition before a synchronous effect immediately calls back; a failed host effect follows the declared repair path. | A callback observes pre-step ownership, or a DOM exception is mapped into an authoritative command rejection. | Preserve transition/effect ordering and report physical failure independently of model outcome. |
| The exact built artifact, executable plan, handler closure and served entrypath are checked together in an exercised production-mode browser case. | A test-only plan, stale copied stamp, untested alternate asset or supported source-name match is promoted into deployment certification. | Qualify exact identity and installed coverage; parity and inspection evidence support only their stated subjects and executions. |

These are obligations of the completed Gesso design. A current test,
source-derived report or diagnostic sidecar does not itself establish
trusted event provenance, general compiler correctness or deployment
correspondence.
** Executable projection and diagnostic sidecars
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: req-executable-plan-sidecar-boundary
:END:

Construction emits one canonical =ExecutablePlan= per projected role and
separate compiler/diagnostic evidence products. The executable plan is the
semantic runtime payload used by production and tests. A
=DiagnosticProofSidecar= may explain it but cannot complete or alter its meaning.

A build may use a rich internal representation while checking and projecting.
The commitment is that production does not execute one machine while verification
or proof-enabled tests quietly execute a different, richer client machine.
Compiler transformations still need their stated correspondence; separating the
sidecar does not eliminate the projection or packaging proof obligation. The
build must distinguish an executable plan's *exact bytes/terms* from the
verified global choreography and its observable outcomes. Multiple distinct
global subjects may produce identical projected local plans, even for every
role, while differing in a source-level terminal proposition or other
unprojected semantic condition. Thus exact plan equality cannot by itself
authenticate a claimed global theorem, the exact authored source, or a
complete refinement. Source-specific structural and behavioral correspondence
are separately checked against the actual admitted global subject.

*** What belongs in each product

| Product | Contents |
|---------+----------|
| ExecutablePlan | Supported local node structure, executable selectors/guards where defined by the format, action/message/event contracts, successors, and runtime interpretation fields. |
| Admitted runtime state and inputs | Concrete command/execution/resource bindings, established values, observations, outstanding effects, and lifecycle state. |
| Assembly/implementation binding | Registered action realizations, trusted boundaries, loaded versions, supported host capabilities, and applicable admission policy. |
| Compiler correspondence data | Mapping from source semantics to actual runtime locators, including generated/synthetic states and continuation relationships. |
| DiagnosticProofSidecar | Explanations, source locations, checked derivations or references, named premises, and exact executable correspondence. |
| Packaged artifact manifest | Relationship between the admitted plan set, implementation/runtime closure, and emitted assets. |

These products need not be stored as six separate files. Their meanings and
trust boundaries must remain distinct. In particular, application execution
cannot depend on a source span or optional explanation object to discover which
guard it was supposed to run.

One assembled application may contain several roles and independent
operations, each with its own exact executable identity. The compiled
plan-set identity and manifest must bind the complete intended *role-to-plan*
inventory, including role absence/presence and relevant assembly generation.
An exact match for one browser role cannot certify that a changed server
role, missing supported operation, or replaced implementation is consistent.
The plan set is an explicit construction subject, not the application's
entire behavioral/physical certification.

The executable semantic core and browser coordinator do not accept a diagnostic
sidecar as a transition input. The conceptual interface is:

#+begin_src clojure
(semantic/step executable-plan admitted-state admitted-event)
;; Returns the next semantic state, declared abstract effects,
;; an explicit step classification, and the actual transition locator.
#+end_src

Guards operate on admitted runtime premises and executable contracts. The proof
kernel/checker may explain why those guards contribute to a property; it does
not supply current runtime permission by having accepted a derivation earlier.

*** Exact identities and their domains

The design distinguishes:

| Identity | Question it answers |
|----------+---------------------|
| Runtime locator | Which state, transition, or effect in this exact emitted plan was selected? |
| Source semantic name | Which authored or generated concept does that locator explain? |
| Normalized semantic dependency identity | Which exact semantic definitions and dependencies a claim or construction uses. |
| Proof-obligation identity | Which proposition/derivation is being checked or explained? |
| Exact executable identity | Does this sidecar describe this exact canonical runtime payload and coordinate layout? |
| Compatibility identity/judgment | May this runtime safely participate or continue under the selected server/assembly contract? |
| Packaged asset identity | Which actual emitted browser/server asset bytes are loaded? |

Runtime locators need not be stable across compilations. Source names can remain
useful while behavior changes, so equal names do not preserve proof applicability.
Two plans can be compatible while having different exact payload identities.
The same plan payload can also be bound to different opaque implementations;
applicable assurance therefore includes the relevant implementation/assembly
closure, not merely the plan digest.

A named semantic subject, the normalized transitive dependency identity
described in Part I, a verified source-to-executable correspondence judgment,
and an executable content digest answer different questions. A proof for one
global terminal outcome cannot be transferred to a globally different subject
whose projected executable happens to be the same. Neither can a proof tied
to an old opaque host-action contract be transferred to a changed implementation
under the same plan bytes. Runtime locators remain coordinates *of that exact
emitted plan*. Diagnostic correlation obtains them from the selected transition
and actual compiler mapping, not from a second execution of a reference
machine or a nearest-name lookup.

*** Canonical payload identity

The exact identity recipe specifies:

- the object being identified: canonical plan terms, a plan set, or exact asset
  bytes;
- encoding and schema versions;
- type-preserving representation of supported scalars and collections;
- deterministic map/set ordering without discarding semantic distinctions;
- unsupported values and their rejection behavior;
- excluded self-identifying fields, or an external identity envelope;
- the digest algorithm and its accepted collision premise;
- interpretation dependencies bound separately when not included in the payload;
- an explicit domain tag distinguishing a single plan from a role-keyed plan
  set, a semantic subject, a proof obligation, or packaged asset bytes;
- injectivity of the supported canonical value encoding up to its declared
  equivalence relation, including unambiguous type tags, lengths and boundaries;
- the exact role inventory and ordering-independent role bindings for a plan set;
- the trusted source of the bytes or terms actually digested, not a caller's
  assertion that some independently recomputed object was the shipped one.

A printed EDN map is not automatically a canonical encoding. Nil versus absence,
keyword versus string, list versus vector where meaningful, numeric forms, and
map/set order require explicit treatment. Host functions and DOM objects cannot
be silently printed into a supposedly portable canonical digest. The
canonicalizer must define which scalar classes, Unicode/byte encodings and
numeric forms belong to the supported domain, and must reject the remainder
rather than fall back to host-specific =pr-str= output. Distinct admitted
values must not collide merely because their printable forms, default
stringification, comparison keys or container iteration order coincide.
Map keys and set members must have deterministic, unambiguous encodings,
including when a host compares dissimilar keys or scalars differently.
The required portable digest should be reproducible on its specified
platforms from the same canonical value domain; a current JVM-only
hash implementation is not automatically a complete cross-host codec.

An identity may intentionally ignore metadata that is *not* executable,
such as source coordinates. Such exclusion must be declared in the identity
domain and must not discard a guard, event schema, runtime successor,
semantic interpretation dependency or any other field that affects the
actual execution. Equal digests mean equality of the explicitly
identified canonical subject only, subject to the algorithm's collision
premise; they do not mean semantic equivalence of arbitrary programs.

A convenient design keeps the payload free of its own digest:

#+begin_src clojure
(def executable-identity
  (artifact/digest
   {:algorithm :sha-256
    :encoding :gesso-plan-canonical-v1
    :value executable-plan}))

(def plan-manifest-entry
  {:role :browser
   :executable-identity executable-identity
   :plan-format-version 1
   :runtime-contract-ref runtime-contract-ref
   :implementation-closure-ref implementation-closure-ref})
#+end_src

The algorithm and format labels illustrate a declared recipe, not a new trust
source. If identity is embedded in an envelope, the payload domain excludes that
self-identifying field. It must not hash an object including the very digest
being computed.

Hashing canonical plan terms is not hashing the emitted JavaScript bundle.
Packaging must establish which plan set and runtime/implementation closure the
actual asset contains. This requires a checkable relationship from the exact
admitted plan/role set and current host-action contracts to the built output,
the emitted asset bytes, and the asset actually served/loaded at the admitted
entrypoint. Advanced compilation, bundling, stale caches, service-worker
delivery, alternate script entrypoints, or swapped deployment files may
invalidate that relationship without changing the original source plan digest.
Where that physical provenance is unavailable, the correct status is
unestablished correspondence, not a retroactive change to the executable's
semantic identity.

A copied or stale generated stamp cannot substitute for that relationship.
Exact equality of a stamp supplied by two untrusted locations is not
construction evidence. An exact executable match is a necessary condition
for sidecar coordinate correlation, not sufficient proof of the sidecar's
authorship, checker result, assumptions, or installed application correctness.
A diagnostic sidecar mismatch disables that explanation; it must not disable
an otherwise independently admitted executable runtime or authorize a
best-effort locator match.

*** Paired artifact-identity and assembly witnesses

The following cases distinguish legitimate reuse, exact-match diagnostics
and genuinely applicable proof/deployment evidence.

| Eligible positive case | Adverse or insufficient case | Required result |
|------------------------+------------------------------+-----------------|
| Two projections differ only in map insertion order or excluded nonsemantic source-location metadata, and the declared canonical recipe yields equal executable identities. | Meaningful event schema, successor, scalar type or semantic dependency changes but the encoder silently drops it or converts it to an ambiguous printed form. | Stable digests for precisely declared equivalence; distinct executable subjects remain distinct, or unsupported representations fail closed. |
| A compiler emits an exact role-keyed set and independently binds its verified source semantics and structural correspondence. | The browser plan is unchanged but the server role or global terminal result changes; a browser-role digest alone is used to preserve the old global proof. | Check all intended roles and source/semantic dependency subjects; plan equality does not authenticate global semantic or terminal correspondence. |
| A diagnostic sidecar names an actual runtime locator of the exact emitted plan and has separately checked issuer, proof claim and premises. | A stale or fabricated sidecar copies the right plan digest but asserts a different theorem, a former coordinate or an unverified proof result. | Match exact payload for coordinate lookup, then separately validate provenance and claim; fail diagnostic attachment closed without changing execution. |
| Compatible plan versions permit a newly admitted runtime to recover command and presentation obligations while using fresh physical resources. | A plan has a different exact digest but is declared compatible, or the same digest is used to resume an incompatible host/assembly binding. | Compatibility and continuation are independent judgments; different exact identities are not automatically incompatible, and equal digests do not grant continuation. |
| The manifest binds the emitted browser plan/roles, current handlers and the exact deployed bundle served at the checked route. | A copied build stamp agrees while bundling substituted a stale script, an alternate entrypoint or a changed opaque handler. | Preserve the identity-to-packaging-to-serving chain; do not treat matching untrusted stamps as installed-application certification. |

These are required finished-system positive and adversarial witnesses. A
digest comparison alone is neither a model proof nor confirmation that
the installed browser executed the matching plan.

*** Binding sidecars to the actual compilation

Compiler correspondence is generated alongside the executable plan from the
same admitted semantic subject. It records the actual mapping, including
synthetic states or compacted continuations, rather than reconstructing it later
from similar state names. The compiler's source-to-runtime mapping includes
direct and synthetic states, semantic continuations and every source
alternative intentionally collapsed into one receive or runtime locator.
One compact locator need not mean one unique authored predecessor; a
diagnostic explanation may not silently discard other sources.

The sidecar, structural projection evidence and concrete correspondence
witnesses are bound to the admitted global semantic subject and the
actual complete role-to-ExecutablePlan set. Identical local plans may
still arise from distinct global choreographies with different terminal
outcomes. Exact plan identity cannot authenticate global source meaning
or a claim about installed opaque implementations.

A sidecar inspection view can be:

#+begin_src clojure
{:sidecar/version 1
 :role :browser
 :executable-identity executable-identity
 :semantic-subject-ref semantic-subject-ref
 :checker-result-ref checker-result-ref
 :implementation-closure-ref implementation-closure-ref
 :locations
 {installation-complete-locator
  {:semantic-id :request-claim/presentation-installed
   :source-ref source-ref
   :claims
   [{:proposition-ref adoption-proposition-ref
     :mechanism :checked-derivation
     :evidence-ref derivation-ref
     :premises [shell-completion-premise
                current-owner-premise]
     :coverage-ref coverage-ref}]}}}
#+end_src

The locator comes from the actual emitted plan mapping. The symbols above denote
bound values; replacing them with copied identifiers cannot authenticate the
claims. The sidecar may contain checked and unverified claims with distinct
status. Its existence does not prove every listed obligation was discharged.
A structural projection certificate establishes its named structural
property; a lockstep or weak concrete correspondence witness establishes
only its replayed schedule and premise-relative observable trace.
A correctly bound *failed* witness remains failed, not successfully
proved merely because exact digest matching succeeded. Finite replay
does not quantify over all fair schedules, nor certify actual browser
installation, backend execution or HumanHelp product capability.

Attaching behavioral correspondence evidence requires the exact semantic and
executable subject to agree with the artifact being explained. Evidence for
choreography A cannot be composed with an artifact generated from choreography
B merely because their operation names or state counts match.

Diagnostic admission first validates the sidecar format and exact executable
identity. Where tooling labels claims checker-verified, it additionally validates
provenance, the checker result, applicable premise set, and implementation
binding. A fabricated sidecar can copy the digest. Exact correspondence and
trusted claim acceptance are separate checks. A copied =:valid? true= or
=:mechanism :checked-derivation= is a claim, not a trusted checker result.
The admission mechanism must identify its proof/checker version,
source inputs, witness, result, named assumptions and dependencies
under an accepted trust boundary. A source-bound conditional theorem,
a finite witness, an externally asserted action and a physically
installed realization have distinct evidence statuses.

If construction requires a proof or preflight result, enforce that
required gate at build/assembly admission, independently of optional
runtime diagnostics. Omitting a sidecar from production neither
revokes a previously admitted executable nor waives a required build
failure. Attaching one cannot authorize a rejected construction.

If exact identity mismatches, diagnostics must refuse correspondence for that
plan. They cannot guess by timestamps, similar names, or near-matching runtime
coordinates. Ordinary execution may continue if its own admission and
compatibility remain valid. An unavailable explanation is not an executable
failure and is not evidence of a safe transition either.

*** Observe the selected transition, not a recomputation

A trace contains the locator selected by the actual semantic step, its admitted
subject identity, and a bounded description of its result/effects. The observer
uses that locator to retrieve correspondence. It must not rerun guards or
transition selection independently to guess what happened. A stale,
ignored, malformed or rejected-before-selection event may have no
selected transition locator; do not invent a successful one for it.
Where a generated locator has multiple source origins, preserve the
actual admitted alternative and the complete compiler mapping.
Host-effect failure after a valid semantic step is a distinct,
correlated physical outcome, not a retroactive rewrite of its locator
or a fabricated domain rejection.

Recomputation can diverge if callbacks are effectful, registries change, state is
not identical, or the observer has different inputs. Even when the pure core
would reproduce the same result, reporting the actual selected locator gives a
clearer correspondence contract.

Optional diagnostic access is read-only. It does not receive mutable live
objects or authority-bearing handles it can modify. Redacted immutable trace
values are preferable to whole contexts, DOM captures, credentials, or unrestricted
command payloads. Missing or redacted data is reported as such; an explanation
must not invent an unavailable premise. The observer receives an immutable,
bounded diagnostic projection rather than aliases to mutable owner
registries, resource handles or privileged server facts. Redaction
must precede disclosure to a less-trusted observer; copying a current
scope token or executable digest into the trace does not grant
its recipient authority or permission to read private data.

*** Diagnostic noninterference

For the same admitted initial state, canonical plan, runtime interpretation,
and normalized event sequence, adding, removing, corrupting, or replacing a
sidecar must not change semantic transitions or abstract effects, apart from
permitted diagnostic output.

#+begin_example
semantic-trace(run(plan, initial-state, events))
  = semantic-trace(run-with-diagnostics(plan, initial-state, events))
#+end_example

This is a conditional noninterference claim over fixed semantic inputs. It does
not claim instrumentation has no wall-clock, memory, scheduling, or resource
cost, or that every real browser receives the same event sequence with debugging
enabled. The fixed-input comparison includes step classifications,
portable semantic state, command and resource ownership, outstanding
acquire-and-adopt obligations, and the ordered required abstract effects,
modulo optional diagnostic observations. A stronger assertion about
physical scheduling or fairness requires separately stated nonblocking
and effect-delivery premises. Stripping diagnostic-only adapter effects
from a pure test is not a proof that arbitrary same-process custom
observers cannot block a real browser.

Excluding a sidecar parameter is necessary but insufficient. Ambient mutable
registries, shared callbacks, exception propagation, hidden source lookups, or
observer decisions fed back into admission can reintroduce a control path.
Module/API boundaries and implementation contracts must prevent those paths.

Optional diagnostics must not gate required effects or completion delivery. The
normal path records the actual transition and issues its required work according
to the semantic contract. A bounded best-effort trace queue can feed observers
independently; overflow drops diagnostic work under a visible diagnostic policy,
not semantic work. Diagnostic capture, redaction and bounded queue
admission must not delay or reject a required semantic effect merely
because a trace sink is full or malformed. A required correctness
or compliance audit instead belongs to a declared semantic effect
with a real durability and failure/recovery contract, not an
optionally dropped diagnostic queue.

Catching an observer exception does not contain a nonterminating or blocking
observer. In-process custom observers require an explicit bounded/nonblocking
premise, or execution isolation adequate for the promised containment. The
framework cannot prove arbitrary observer code harmless just because its return
value is ignored. Redaction and diagnostic failure reporting must also be
bounded and contained. A =try=/=catch= around user observer code
does not stop a callback that never returns. The claim must either
name an admitted bounded/nonblocking observer premise or provide
isolation and enforceable resource budgets appropriate to the
promised containment. Diagnostic failure may not be reclassified
as command rejection, accepted incorporation or physical installation.

If an audit action is required for the operation's correctness or compliance
contract, it is a declared semantic effect with its own failure policy. It must
not hide inside an optional observer whose loss is advertised as irrelevant.

*** Paired sidecar and observer conformance cases

| Eligible positive case | Adverse or incomplete case | Required result |
|------------------------+----------------------------+-----------------|
| The actual selected runtime locator is reported with all merged receive alternatives and generated origins. | An observer reruns a branch guard, guesses a nearby source name, or drops the other predecessor of a compacted state. | Use the selected locator and full emitted compiler correspondence; do not manufacture a unique source branch. |
| A structural certificate and a valid concrete witness are checked against the exact current role-plan set and admitted global source. | Another global choreography yields the same executable plans but a different terminal proposition; alternatively a correctly bound witness fails. | Bind actual source and checker premises separately from digests; report failure and concrete-witness scope honestly. |
| The same admitted state/event corpus runs with no, matching, and corrupted sidecars. | A diagnostic lookup affects ownership, accepted events, required effect ordering or adoption debt, or falls back to similar locators. | Identical semantic traces modulo diagnostic output; refuse bad explanations without changing independently valid execution. |
| A bounded observer reads a redacted immutable trace; overflow drops optional diagnostics alone. | A throwing, indefinitely blocking, mutable-registry-writing or credential-leaking observer is given host authority. | Enforce isolation/bounded premises and prior redaction; diagnostic failure cannot affect required semantic work. |
| A required audit is declared and executed as a protected semantic effect with recovery obligations. | A compliance-critical audit is hidden in a lossy optional trace queue and silently dropped. | Preserve the audit's declared correctness and durability requirements independently of sidecar presence. |

Positive tests must exercise the intended compiler, transition and host
effect boundaries; neither a copied digest nor a reject-all observer
can establish full correspondence or noninterference.
*** Sidecars carry no authority

A browser-side sidecar cannot establish principal identity, current model
permission, authoritative state, subscription authorization, or permission to
read protected data. It cannot authenticate a principal, authorize a
protected Request/RequestAssignment, warrant a model transaction outcome,
claim a current board observation, establish a Live subscription or extend
the disclosure of a historical result. The server accepts commands under
its trusted boundary, regardless of the browser's proof-looking material.

Nor may a digest-matching sidecar turn a reported compiler theorem into
the browser's own permission to send, install, reread, settle, reveal or
retry. The trust boundary must be the same with no sidecar, a valid
sidecar, or a maliciously forged one. A user-visible diagnostic may
truthfully explain why an action is unavailable, but never supply a
missing trusted authorization or an executable workaround.

Sidecars can themselves reveal source details, policy names, or private values.
Production packaging omits them by default; authorized diagnostic distribution
follows the application's disclosure contract. Compiler source paths,
policy names, proof premises, operation IDs, observation references,
diagnostic traces and redacted values are each assessed for disclosure.
The reader's identity, permitted Organization/Location, tenant scope,
retention period and intended diagnostic purpose govern distribution
independently of exact executable identity. A complete copied sidecar
or trace from another authorized context is not implicitly disclosable
to the current browser or user. Normal execution must remain
complete when sidecars are absent; a mandatory semantic audit or
build-time proof admission remains separately mandatory.

The implementation can enforce part of this separation by dependency direction
and closed runtime formats, and test it with missing, malformed, mismatched,
throwing, and resource-heavy observers. Such checks support their stated scope;
they do not establish a sandbox for arbitrary same-process trusted code.
An optional observer that requires unbounded time, possesses mutable
owner/DOM handles, or can block required effects needs a different isolation
contract; merely ignoring its return value does not ensure noninterference.
Optional diagnostic failure is not equivalent to a failed command or
installation.

*** Build output and assembly closure

Build output supplies machine-checkable correspondence among the current
semantic subject, projected plan set, registered implementation closure, runtime
contract, packaged assets, and optional exact sidecars. Test, diagnostic, and
production modes execute the same admitted semantic payload for a given build.
The construction evidence explicitly binds the complete role/operation
inventory, trusted route and handler closure, physical transport, semantic
implementation contracts, generated plan set, runtime interpretation, and
actual asset bytes for every served entrypoint within the claim's coverage.
Compiler output, an in-memory ApplicationAssembly report and the
installation/serving environment remain distinct subjects.

Part VII's [[#req-assembly-construction-phases][assembly admission phases]] verify
that the served application loads the required artifacts and bindings. A source
file containing a correct plan is insufficient when the browser actually loads
an older bundle. A browser's claimed artifact identity is likewise not server
authorization. A valid rendered-surface preflight report applies to the
surface and handler path actually inspected; it does not prove that every
possible dynamic Clojure branch, pre-serialized HTML, alternate Biff
entrypoint or later middleware/asset replacement was covered.
Changes to the effective route, handler, compiled asset,
semantic dependency or accepted backend premise require the
applicable construction/recovery/requalification policy.

The build may legitimately transform or optimize code. Any transformation that
changes the object covered by a claim needs the declared correspondence or
requalification. Sidecar separation avoids a second proof-annotated runtime;
it does not excuse testing only an unoptimized development realization while
claiming the production shell has been exercised. Exact plan identity,
accepted source-relative structural proof, bounded JVM/Node/Chromium
semantic conformance, physical HTMX/DOM execution, trusted XTDB
write/readback correspondence, and a served production bundle each
require evidence at their own boundaries. A successful HTTP 200,
sidecar match or copied build stamp cannot substitute for any
missing physical or product-positive observation.

** Conformance and acceptance obligations

The same canonical semantics must support construction checks, runtime
interpretation, and focused conformance cases. Part IX supplies certification
judgments; Part X supplies the stronger soundness and implementation
correspondence arguments. This part requires the following cases at their
appropriate boundaries.

The acceptance report maintains three independent judgments:
(1) model/business-rule correctness under stated provider and writer
premises; (2) closed application assembly and actually enforced
rendered/served path coverage; and (3) behavioral completeness of an
independently specified, usable HumanHelp product. None implies either
other judgment. Each result records its exact source/version, premises,
positive and adverse witnesses, coverage, scope and unresolved or
inconclusive obligations. A failing or absent witness is not rewritten
as an accepted assumption to produce a green overall status.

| Area | Case | Required behavior |
|------+-------+-------------------|
| Provisional typing | Claiming label is rendered over an open Request. | Presentation phase does not become an undeclared authoritative domain status. |
| Entry knowledge | Required observation is absent or belongs to another Request. | The required optimistic construction is rejected; no silent ordinary-request fallback. |
| Creation | A local preview is created before authoritative entity existence. | Its declared collection/local-input premises remain explicit; the preview does not prove uniqueness or absence. |
| Command identity | Transport retries or a new execution continue an unresolved intent. | Stable command binding is preserved; physical retry does not allocate a new intent. |
