dimensions:

| Property | Required distinction |
|----------+----------------------|
| Kind and permitted footprint | Timer, listener, transport, provisional/authorized DOM target, continuity slot, local storage, subscription interest, or declared application-specific effect. |
| Semantic purpose | Execution progression, provisional presentation, authoritative installation, read/advisory coordination, command resolution, optional diagnostics or cleanup. |
| Ownership | Exact runtime, root/child effect scope, owner generation and resource instance; shared ownership is an explicit class and protocol. |
| Issue and completion | Issued, physically committed, completed, failed, partly realized, unknown, or cancelled under an effect-specific physical postcondition. |
| Timing and reentrancy | Synchronous host gate, immediate callback, Promise, deferred callback, host reentry and any required final-actuation permit. |
| Repetition | Repeatable read or cleanup, once-per-physical-resource mutation, command-bound transport retry, or nonrepeatable external act. |
| Revocation and release | Semantic removal of rights, best-effort physical cancellation, verified release, retained remnant and transferable obligations. |
| Compensation | No compensation, legal local restoration, declared repair, or a distinct authorized server command; no universal undo. |
| Evidence and assumptions | Proven adapter consequence, tested physical handler, external host/HTMX premise, or as-yet-unproved opaque behavior. |

One local DOM installation can be synchronous, reversible only until a stronger
authoritative projection arrives, and capable of allocating listeners whose
lifetime exceeds the installation step. A timer can be an asynchronous
callback source and a resource requiring release. The actual authoritative
observation remains an authority-source fact; the browser's physical
installation is not a new trusted model mutation.

*** One root effect scope per execution, with explicit owned children

An active local execution has one admitted root effect scope, with child scopes
for resources such as provisional presentation, its restoration permit,
settlement timer, transport attempts, continuity capture and local asynchronous
work. Fragment coordinators, shared SSE connections and durable command-recovery
owners have separately declared root scopes. All current managed effects must
be reachable through their admitted owner graph. A physical registry is a
mapping from semantic issued resource identities to opaque host handles, not a
second mutable model of which execution ought to win.

#+begin_example
execution E42 / generation G7
  -> provisional card target B1 / install effect F1
  -> settlement timer T1 / issued resource R1
  -> physical attempt H1 / issued transport F2
  -> local continuity slot L1 / physical capture F3

board coordinator B3 / distinct owner
  -> Live interest S9 / shared connection with explicit references
  -> applied query Q / advisory and adoption obligations

command recovery owner K8 / distinct lifetime
  -> unresolved C42 historical attribution and resolver obligations
#+end_example

This ownership graph is illustrative, not a second runtime API. Sharing the
command ID C42 does not make an old execution's timer or card current. A
coordinator may continue after E42 retires, and K8 may retain C42 while
E42's provisional resources are revoked. A current subscription invalidation
is admitted by its own registered source, not by E42's private callback.

Each physical resource identity includes an issuing runtime, owner, generation
and concrete incarnation sufficient to distinguish recycled timer IDs, DOM
selectors, register slots, transport IDs and reused handle values. Equality
of a CSS selector, numeric timer ID or current style value does not prove
ownership. An alias between identities is permitted only under an explicit
same-resource contract. Resource ownership transfer is a semantic transition
with old rights revoked and a current receiving owner established; it is
not two uncoordinated registry writes that leave a gap or dual owners.

A shared connection has an explicit reference/interest lifecycle. Detaching
one fragment interest must not close a connection still required by another.
Duplicate attachment or release must not grant a new interest or decrement
another owner's reference. Reference counting can realize the policy but is
not itself evidence of correctly admitted subscription scopes or protected
server disclosure.

*** Issue registration precedes host work; late handles remain owned

The adapter records an *issued effect and resource instance* in committed
semantic state before calling the physical handler. An immediate completion
may then be correlated with the issued work, and a nested event sees the
newly committed owner. That semantic order does not by itself close the
physical-handle race.

Some host APIs return a cancellation handle only after initiating work.
An injected scheduler may invoke its callback synchronously; a registered
listener may trigger a callback during registration; a Promise may settle
while the outer effect batch still holds other work; retirement may occur
before a host call finally returns a handle. The physical registry therefore
implements a protocol equivalent to:

| Physical state | Required treatment |
|----------------+--------------------|
| Issued, awaiting handle | The semantic owner and issue instance are recorded before host invocation; callback admission is already possible. |
| Callback/completion before handle | Completion or retirement is correlated to the same issue without inventing a second live resource or losing subsequent cleanup. |
| Handle returned for current issue | The opaque handle is registered only if the issue and owner are still current and the resource remains live. |
| Handle returned after retirement | The handle is never published as current; release/cancel it through the retired issue's exact cleanup rights. |
| Issue throws after partial registration | Record the actual uncertain physical footprint, attempt permitted cleanup, and preserve the originating semantic failure. |
| Duplicate/late completion | Apply the declared duplicate/stale admission disposition; do not settle a successor resource. |
| Release completes or fails | Mark only this resource instance released or report retained physical remnant debt; no fabricated successful cleanup. |

A late host return is not allowed to recreate a resource that a synchronous
callback or nested dispatch already completed. Checking only whether the
registry key exists *before* invoking the scheduler, then unconditionally
associating the returned handle afterward, fails this contract. The shell
may use an issuance cell, retired tombstone, effect-specific latch or another
bounded mechanism with an equivalent checked transition. Tombstone retention
must have explicit generation/reuse and resource bounds; retaining all old
handles forever is not the intended solution.

Registration also precedes every irreversible protected *act*, with a
still-current permit checked at the last controllable mutation boundary.
An outer dispatch's effect list is not a perpetual license: an immediate
handler callback can retire its owner before a later listed effect runs.
A deferred effect must not write to a newer target solely because its
completion event would later be rejected as stale. A physical action that
crossed its declared commitment point may be partial or irreversible and
requires actual completion/failure/repair evidence rather than fictional
rollback.

Local once-only physical actuation is distinct from remote command
incorporation. H1 and H2 can be different HTTP attempts for the same
immutable C42 under the admitted deduplication/repetition contract.
"Do not run this DOM effect twice" is not evidence that the server
received exactly one request or that C42 incorporated exactly once.

*** Semantic retirement precedes best-effort physical cleanup

Retirement first revokes the execution's semantic progression, callback,
rollback, target and pending-send rights. The host then attempts abort,
timer clear, listener detach, temporary-node removal and continuity/resource
release through the appropriate exact physical handles. A failed cancellation
does not restore the old owner's rights, and a late callback cannot mutate
the newer owner simply because it carries a stronger-looking observation
or has the same physical selector.

A cleanup operation is idempotent *for the same issued resource instance*
and safe in the presence of repeated retirement, timer/settlement races,
failed aborts and nested dispatch. Cleanup order follows declared resource
dependencies, normally reversing acquisition order where that matters.
Independent cleanup is best effort: if the first release throws, other
permitted releases must still be attempted. Cleanup failures are separately
recorded against the original owner and resource.

Deleting a temporary DOM node by re-querying today's ID is unsafe if that
ID now belongs to a successor. Resetting an applied CSS property only when
its current value matches the old value is also insufficient: a newer owner
can intentionally write the *same* value. Resource release must compare
ownership/incarnation or use an exclusive physical handle/lease capable of
distinguishing the writers. If a host API cannot provide that relationship,
the application must explicitly limit the guarantee, serialize ownership
or choose another safe realization; coincidentally equal values are not
evidence of unchanged ownership.

Physical-remnant records describe attempted, completed, failed and
indeterminate release separately from semantic retirement. The system
must specify finite or bounded retention, instrumentation, backpressure,
compaction and a safe degraded/unavailable state if physical remnants
accumulate. Logical single-flight does not bound lingering XHRs, timers
or native listeners after abort failure. An exhausted resource budget
may stop new work without granting old callbacks permission or erasing
unresolved command and subscription debts.

The runtime may recover current authority and install a new target after
semantic retirement, without waiting indefinitely for the last physical
cleanup. That independence depends on the still-retained old effects being
unable to act on or interfere with the new scope under the declared host
noninterference premises.

*** Restoration and continuity have narrow, expiring permits

A local provisional "undo" is a scoped, guarded physical action. It may
restore particular previously captured presentation only while the same
current owner retains the applicable target and no stronger admitted
authoritative or competing presentation has superseded it. A rollback
cannot reverse server incorporation, reassign a RequestAssignment or
overwrite a newly installed canonical card. Expiration occurs on owner
retirement, target replacement, admitted authoritative installation,
conflict-policy revocation or another specified semantic event.

Continuity captures are opaque physical resources whose implementation
and restore contracts are bound at capture. A changed registry of restore
functions cannot reinterpret a stale capture as an authorized new operation.
The supported capture may preserve focus, input draft, caret, scroll,
details-open state, or other declared local state. It must not promote
obsolete server data, a previous applied query, old operation bindings,
privileged HTML snapshots or expired disclosure rights to authoritative
state.

Continuity preparation required to protect a mandatory user draft must
run before the protected swap is allowed. Optional restoration, after
the authoritative installation has completed, is a separate best-effort
local effect: a failed scroll/focus restore cannot retroactively reject
the command or undo the current observation. Delayed animation-frame
callbacks must recheck that their capture and target owner remain current
before touching DOM. A resource's physical released latch can prevent
an old callback from acting, but does not replace the semantic owner
and target-generation check.

A provisional presentation timeout and a command-history resolver deadline
may have different owners. Settlement or authoritative supersession must
immediately revoke the former's ability to roll back, while the latter
may persist after the local execution retires. Blindly cancelling *every*
timer with the same command ID would lose a required unresolved-command
recovery obligation. Conversely retaining the presentation timer because
the command is still unresolved would risk stale physical mutation.

*** Fault containment preserves original causality and honest uncertainty

Failure before a pure semantic transition is committed and failure
after physical actuation begins have different consequences.
If an adapter step fails before commitment, its emitted effects
have not yet been interpreted, and the last valid committed state
is the relevant diagnostic reference. The declared failure path
retires unsafe owner rights rather than inventing a successful
step or blindly rewinding an already committed successor.

If a physical handler throws or returns an indeterminate result
after some actions have taken place, the runtime preserves the
committed semantic transition and records actual attempted,
completed, partial or unknown effects. It revokes unsafe rights,
continues permitted independent cleanup and repair, and retains
the original failure/command uncertainty. It must not blindly
reissue an entire effect batch, restore a superseded DOM snapshot
or translate a network failure into an authoritative
=:rejected= outcome.

The primary failure F and cleanup failures CA/CC have different
provenance and ordering:

#+begin_example
primary failure F
   -> semantic owner retired
   -> cleanup resource A: failed CA
   -> cleanup resource B: released
   -> cleanup resource C: failed CC

report primary F with subordinate cleanup evidence [CA CC]
retained resource debt for A and C; no invented release
#+end_example

Reporting, observer callbacks and diagnostics are not allowed to
select a different semantic successor. Optional observers require
bounded, declared failure isolation; a throwing/reentrant or
unbounded same-process diagnostic can still interfere unless the
implementation supplies that protection. A corrupt runtime-wide
physical registry may require retiring the entire runtime rather
than assuming each child owner remains isolated. Independent
owners may proceed only while their stated shared-resource and
noninterference contracts remain true.

Recovery keeps actual historical command incorporation, local
provisional presentation, authorized current observation and
completed DOM adoption as distinct evidence subjects. A failed
physical cleanup does not undo C42's server Claim; a failed DOM
installation does not prove that C42 was rejected; an expired
recovery window does not prove the original command never ran.

*** Paired managed-effect and cleanup acceptance histories

The finished system must provide eligible positive cases that
exercise real admitted host effects and nearby adverse cases
that reach the relevant physical lifecycle. A fabricated
success map, disabled operation or purely symbolic timer
is not by itself a conformance witness for the deployed browser.

| Eligible positive history | Adverse or incomplete history | Required conclusion |
|---------------------------+-------------------------------+---------------------|
| E42 issues T1 with a recorded effect instance; a synchronous test scheduler fires before returning its handle and T1 retires in the nested dispatch. | The scheduler then returns a handle and the outer frame registers T1 as a fresh live timer after retirement. | Registration-before-issue, immediate-completion handling and late-handle cleanup prevent phantom live resources. |
| E42 starts provisional B1; its callback reenters and lets a newer E43 own B2 before the outer effect batch finishes. | A later effect from the outer batch mutates B2 using a previously issued permit for B1. | Recheck current permit at last actuation; stale callback rejection afterward is not sufficient. |
| An exact old timer/resource handle is cancelled or released twice safely while the successor timer shares a label or registry slot. | Old cleanup looks up today's slot and cancels E43's newly installed timer. | Cleanup is instance-relative and idempotent; recycled keys do not transfer ownership. |
| A continuity owner installs a height lock and releases it while no successor owns that style. | A newer owner writes the same =min-height= value, then old release restores a previous value by value comparison alone. | Only a valid owner/incarnation lease may restore the property; equal CSS values are not proof of same ownership. |
| A newer authoritative card installs while E42's provisional rollback is semantically retired and a separate C42 resolver remains active. | Old settlement timer restores obsolete card content or all C42 timers are cancelled, losing the resolver deadline. | Expire presentation rights without erasing independently owned command recovery. |
| One shared SSE connection has two admitted current fragment interests; one owner retires. | Retirement closes the entire connection or leaves the retired interest authorized to mutate its old target. | Detach only the exact interest; preserve active shared owners and their security/continuity obligations. |
| A mandatory effect fails after partial host work; the runtime records its stage, retires the unsafe owner and attempts remaining cleanup. | The first cleanup exception aborts all releases or replaces the primary error with a fabricated command rejection. | Retain original F, subordinate CA/CC, unresolved physical debt and honest command uncertainty. |
| A current target's admitted swap finishes, then optional scroll restoration fails or a stale animation-frame callback arrives. | The runtime undoes the canonical swap, treats continuity failure as a command failure, or lets the old RAF mutate the successor. | Preserve authoritative adoption, isolate optional restoration and revoke stale physical continuation rights. |
| Several failed native aborts leave physical remnants while logical E42 work is retired. | The runtime asserts zero resources solely because its semantic maps are empty and continues allocating without limits. | Retain observable remnant/budget state; backpressure or require safe reset without reviving old rights. |

Part VII must account for the *actual* registered handlers,
rendered routes, third-party writers, startup paths and served assets.
Part VIII requires positive HumanHelp Claim/Reassign and
one-Refresh behavior through those physical paths. Parts IX–X
distinguish finite host tests, proof-kernel claims, source
correspondence and the real browser/transport assumptions.
** Async event safety
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: req-browser-async-admission
:END:

Every asynchronous event that can advance browser semantic state or cause a
protected physical effect passes the declared normalization and owner-relative
admission boundary. Timers, HTMX callbacks, SSE invalidations, Promise and
worker completions, cross-tab messages, deferred continuity work, command
resolver results, browser lifecycle events and delayed DOM effects are all
subject to this rule. No callback may independently choose which execution
"probably" owns the event or resume a Choreo machine outside the admitted
adapter.

An admitted event is a proposal for one semantic transition. It is not a
server credential, a trusted domain fact or permission to perform all
subsequent physical effects. Its *registered origin*, event class, payload,
owner, current resource incarnation, legality and claimed evidence are
separately established. A permitted semantic transition may issue physical
effects; those effects still require current actuation permits under
06.02, 06.05 and 06.10.

The conceptual gate is common across event types, but its requirements
depend on *owner class*. Requiring E42 on every event rejects genuinely
shared work; accepting all events without an execution ID allows private
callbacks to evade retirement. The general rule remains
[[#req-owner-relative-event-admission][Part II's owner-relative event admission]].

*** The event class follows the registered source

The assembled application's admitted source registration establishes
which event kinds an actual physical callback may deliver, the allowed
owner class and scope, the required correlation, accepted schema and
resource lifetime. Event metadata supplied in the payload does not
select a more permissive class. An old transport callback cannot
become current shared command evidence merely by adding
=:event/class :command-evidence= to its body.

| Registered source class | Admitted owner and purpose |
|-------------------------+----------------------------|
| Execution-private | A current execution and issued local/send, timer, transport or provisional effect generation. |
| Fragment coordinator | A current applied query, managed root and physical HTMX request/target generation for acquisition and installation. |
| Shared subscription | A current subscription/interest resource and authorized scope, independent of the active local command. |
| Command recovery | A surviving resolver owner and qualified C42 historical command-result binding, possibly after E42 retirement. |
| Runtime lifecycle | A registered =online=, =pageshow=, visibility, reconnect or deployment wakeup requesting further checks, not claiming those checks succeeded. |
| Optional observer | A bounded, nonauthoritative inspection of an actually selected transition/effect, without permission to forge semantic events or decide branches. |

A source registration has a runtime/owner incarnation, physical callback
identity, permitted event types, schema, effect or resource instance,
subscription/authority scope and retirement contract. It must be
established by the actual integration, not reconstructed from today's
DOM selector, mutable global or client-reported source label.

A registered SSE listener can establish that a message entered through
a particular local subscription path. It does not by itself prove that
the message's claimed XTDB basis or RequestAssignment facts were issued
by the trusted authority. EDN decoding, equality of duplicated wire
fields and correct DOM listener ancestry are structural/source checks,
not universal provider provenance. Worker and cross-tab APIs likewise
identify transport channels without making arbitrary message contents
authoritative. Server and model policy remains independently enforced
against hostile browser traffic.

A schematic normalized inspection event could be:

#+begin_src clojure
{:event :transport/succeeded
 :source-registration/ref registered-transport-source
 :runtime-instance/id runtime-instance
 :owner/ref [:execution E42]
 :resource-instance/id issued-resource-instance
 :execution-generation current-generation
 :effect-instance/id pending-send-effect
 :transport-request-id H1
 :gesso/command-id C42
 :payload decoded-result}
#+end_src

This is not a claim that the current adapter exposes those exact fields.
Some identities may be carried in trusted local registrations rather than
serialized in the event. Constructing a matching map is not admission.
An actual source/owner binding and the correct semantic evidence must
exist independently.

*** Admission checks owner, issued work, legal state and evidence

For a declared source class, the gate establishes all relevant conditions:

1. The physical callback is associated with a current source registration
   that permits the claimed event kind, scope and host lifecycle.
2. Its runtime, owner, resource instance and generation are current for
   that kind of work; reused labels, selectors and counters do not
   establish instance identity.
3. Where relevant, correlation matches a real issued local effect,
   H1 transport attempt, timer, subscription interest, fragment request
   or command resolver. A shared invalidation need not name E42.
4. The payload obeys the source-bound schema; evidence of command outcome,
   current observation, progression, absence or physical completion has
   the *required independent provenance*.
5. The current semantic machine/coordinator/resolver state legally accepts
   the event. A completion cannot settle an unissued effect; a timeout
   cannot reverse an already resolved presentation branch.
6. Duplicate/replay rules apply to the *correct layer* of identity and
   bind any repeated ID to its source, owner and equivalent payload.
7. Any subsequent protected transport, disclosure or DOM mutation obtains
   its own current permit. Event admission does not revive retired
   physical rights.

A single logical dispatcher commits its selected semantic state before
interpreting effects. An immediate nested callback therefore sees the
new owner and effect issuance records; the outer handler cannot overwrite
the nested successor state on return. Where multiple host tasks can
dispatch against one owner, their commits require real serialization.
Event arrival order does not establish authoritative progression or
server causality.

| Diagnosis | Meaning and required response |
|-----------+-------------------------------|
| Unknown source/correlation | No admitted issued work matches; never guess the newest execution. |
| Malformed payload | Declared schema or source-bound identity is violated; fail the required physical gate closed. |
| Stale owner/resource | Old generation/instance has retired; no old callback or physical mutation rights. |
| Duplicate delivery | Apply the class's admitted idempotence/consumption rule; do not rerun one-shot effects. |
| Conflicting duplicate | Same ID has incompatible binding/payload; classify and reconcile as a protocol/evidence fault. |
| Illegal current state | Source is known but its event cannot advance this machine or coordinator state. |
| Incompatible plan/context | Suspend/retire old private work under the explicit recovery/compatibility contract. |
| Unestablished authority | Source does not justify claimed command incorporation, current scope, basis, adoption or disclosure. |
| Physical failure or uncertainty | Preserve partial, failed or unknown effect results; do not fabricate domain rejection. |

These are browser-level classifications, *not* new public-model
outcomes. In particular, =:committed=, =:rejected=,
=:already-incorporated= and =:commit-unknown= require admitted
authoritative operation evidence. Expected stale callbacks may
produce bounded diagnostics without changing state; conflicting
current evidence or a broken invariant needs its declared typed
fault and recovery path, not universal silent ignoring.

For a synchronous HTMX gate, a typed error is not enough if the
physical request/swap still proceeds. A rejected protected action
must be stopped at an actually cancellable supported boundary.
A generic =afterSwap= callback cannot certify an unexamined OOB,
extension or successor-target mutation.

*** An early physical delivery can be consumed before it is legal

Physical delivery identity is distinct from command identity and
machine reception readiness. Some protocols consume a delivery ID
when that source *first observes it*, even if the current projected
machine cannot yet accept its envelope. If the ID remained unspent,
the same early message could be replayed once the machine reached
the appropriate receive state and become incorrectly fresh.

For such a protocol, E42 receives physical message M1 when its
machine does not accept that envelope. Admission records M1 as
consumed under its source and execution generation, but does
not advance the machine. When E42 later becomes ready to receive,
the same physical M1 is still a duplicate. That consumption is
a negative capability preventing a later unauthorized replay,
not proof that an earlier command incorporated or that some
new trusted resolver result must also be ignored.

The exact consumption point is defined by event class. A one-shot
timer may be spent upon firing. A shared advisory may be coalesced
under qualified scope/coverage, while a trusted historical
command result can be delivered repeatedly under an immutable
authenticated resolver contract. The application must not use
one global "deduplicate by C42" rule across transport attempts,
physical messages, command readbacks and current observations.

An observed-but-unaccepted delivery cannot be resurrected by
replaying its ID after that machine's state changes. A changed
runtime/resource incarnation or explicitly justified durable
replay fence can permit bounded compaction without allowing an
old callback to masquerade as newly issued work.

*** Independent owners can accept useful late information

Suppose E42 submitted HumanHelp Claim C42, but its provisional
presentation and execution-private resources have retired.
The current board subscription S9 is owned by coordinator B3.
Surviving command resolver K8 retains an unresolved C42
obligation. E43 may later make a separately admitted compatible
C42 retry with its own H2 attempt.

| Arriving event | Required treatment |
|----------------+--------------------|
| E42's old settlement timeout | Stale private resource; cannot reject C42 or restore an old card. |
| E42's deferred provisional callback | Expired target/rollback permit; cannot write to B2 even if it finds the same selector. |
| Current S9 advisory | B3 may record scoped debt under its interest and Refresh policy without an E42 command. |
| Retired predecessor S8 advisory | Stale resource/interest; matching fragment names cannot grant S9's rights. |
| K8's qualified C42 resolver response | May establish historical command incorporation/rejection/unknown according to authenticated binding and disclosure; does not resume E42. |
| Old E42 transport callback relabelled shared | Still from the retired private source; no second-chance shared admission. |
| H1 callback while E43 owns H2 | H1 cannot settle H2; common C42 does not merge transport-effect generations. |
| Browser reconnect wakeup | May establish a continuity-gap obligation, not that every missed invalidation was replayed. |

This rule permits *separate qualified late evidence*, not a
loophole to adopt an obsolete physical continuation. A current
Request card may install while C42 attribution remains unknown;
C42 historical incorporation may become known without proving
the current RequestAssignment helper or card adoption. Part IV
owns the trusted business result and Parts V/VI own local
presentation and physical realization.

*** Duplicate, conflicting and missing evidence have different lifetimes

A physical transport delivery, semantic C42 command, trusted
result, authorized observation and actual target installation
answer different questions. A duplicate at one layer is not
automatically a duplicate at the others. If a stable delivery
or result ID is repeated, the adapter checks the same admitted
source, operation/argument binding, scope and equivalent payload.
Conflicting payloads under the same ID require a typed evidence
or protocol fault; "last message wins" is not progression.

Known historical incorporation does not become unknown because
a later H2 transport attempt times out. A success-looking HTTP
response likewise cannot establish incorporation on its own.
A newer authorized Request/card observation may supersede
presentation within its qualified scope without retroactively
rewriting previously valid historical command evidence.

The runtime declares consumed-message, duplicate-result and
retired-resource retention or compaction. Unbounded tombstones
are not required, but deleting an old record while permitting
its callback to collide with a newly allocated incarnation
is unsafe. Epochs, fresh resource identities, bounded replay
horizons and qualified provider coverage can establish the
nonconfusion premise.

Shared invalidations may be duplicated, delayed or reordered.
The fragment coordinator preserves incomparable obligations
until an actual provider-covered acquisition or adoption stage
discharges them. A repeated advisory does not authorize an
extra one-Refresh read. Conversely stream silence does not
prove that an interest-registration or router-failover gap
was covered; the 06.06–06.07 fence/recovery contract still
applies. Liveness needs stated fairness, availability and
retention premises; stale-event safety alone does not prove
eventual convergence.

*** Fault handling, timeout retirement and adversarial scheduling

If a pure semantic step fails before state commitment, the
runtime must not manufacture effects it never issued or
restore an old machine and pretend the transition succeeded.
It retains the last committed state for diagnosis and
retires the unsafe owner under its fault contract. If an
effect already started, actual partial physical changes
and unresolved remote incorporation require independent
recording, compensation or readback. An entire previously
issued batch is not blindly rerun after a host exception.

Winning settlement or authoritative supersession revokes
competing *presentation timeout authority* before slower
continuity or DOM follow-up. Physical timer cancellation
may fail; the callback is still stale. A different
command-resolution deadline may survive under its own
recovery owner. Cleanup errors remain subordinate to the
original semantic or host failure.

Tests and sound abstract models explore source/owner
relations as well as adversarial ordering: response
versus timeout, early message versus later receive,
H1 completion versus H2 retry, authoritative
installation versus provisional rollback, shared
advisory while no command runs, reconnect versus
retired subscription, duplicate/conflicting result,
nested callback before remaining physical effects,
new principal context versus old source, and
invalidation during one-Refresh acquisition.
Checking a handful of particular generation integers
does not prove the required equivalence classes.

*** Paired asynchronous-admission acceptance histories

Each positive witness must execute an eligible
admitted source and legal machine path; the nearby
adverse case must reach the relevant source, owner,
trust or physical boundary rather than be rejected
for an unrelated malformed fixture.

| Eligible positive history | Adverse or incomplete history | Required conclusion |
|---------------------------+-------------------------------+---------------------|
| E42 receives completion for an actually issued current local effect generation. | The same completion belongs to a retired generation or an effect that was never issued. | Only the current legal issued effect advances. |
| M1 is observed early, consumed and leaves the projected machine waiting. | The identical M1 is replayed after the receive state becomes ready. | Early physical observation remains consumed; replay does not become fresh. |
| E42 accepts qualified settlement and revokes its presentation timeout. | A duplicate result ID carries conflicting content or a stale timeout tries to roll back after settlement. | Identical observation is idempotent; conflicting evidence faults; expired timeout is powerless. |
| K8 resolves C42 and B3/S9 accepts a legitimate scoped board advisory after E42 retires. | E42's old transport relabels itself shared or S8 impersonates S9 by copying the root ID. | Independent current owners are admitted; private-to-shared laundering is denied. |
| H1's correlated managed HTMX request completes its admitted specific target effect. | Stale H1 callback or unexamined OOB/extension mutation is credited with B2 adoption. | A registered callback is not universal physical completion; target-specific permits remain required. |
| H2 retries C42 with compatible immutable command binding and receives trusted resolver evidence. | H1 completion settles H2 or H1 timeout fabricates C42 rejection. | Attempt, command and historical evidence are separate. |
| O1 and O2 arrive on a current shared interest during one granted A1 Refresh. | Duplicates erase incomparable O2 or start an ungranted A2 successor. | Preserve scoped debt and actual acquisition permission. |
| A lifecycle wakeup detects a subscription gap and follows an admitted recovery policy. | =online= or =sseOpen= is treated as proof of replay/currentness. | Wakeup is advisory; a qualified fence/reacquisition is separate. |
| An immediate physical callback reenters after semantic state commit and retires a pending effect. | The outer batch acts on its revoked permit or registers a late handle as live. | Recheck current actuation and late-handle lifecycle. |
| A current authenticated user receives a properly scoped callback. | A cross-tab payload copies source IDs after logout or Organization change and demands disclosure. | Client identifiers never supply current server authorization. |

A fake source map, diagnostic trace or always-disabled
affordance cannot establish conformance. Part VII must
check the actual registered handlers/entrypoints; Part
VIII requires independently positive eligible HumanHelp
Claim/Reassign and remote one-Refresh behavior. Parts
IX–X separate finite test/model evidence, proof subject
and actual browser/backend correspondence.
** Authoritative absence
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: req-authoritative-absence
:END:

An authorized observation may establish that a domain entity is absent
under a qualified entity lookup, or that a previously displayed entity
does not belong to a *particular covered projection*. These are positive
authoritative statements with specified provenance and scope. They are
not consequences of an empty HTML element, a missing response, local
filtering, a timeout, a missing DOM target or a rejected read.

The browser treats the following as distinct knowledge and physical
states, even when they produce similar-looking empty presentation:

| Observation or realization state | What it actually establishes |
|----------------------------------+------------------------------|
| Present | An admitted authoritative value or membership under its declared actor, query, field and temporal scope. |
| Authoritatively absent | A qualified negative entity or membership fact under an admitted coverage and progression contract. |
| Not yet acquired | No applicable source observation has established the requested presence or absence. |
| Acquisition failed or indeterminate | The attempted read did not establish the requested fact; earlier justified knowledge and outstanding recovery remain separately qualified. |
| Not disclosed or no longer authorized | The participant may not currently learn or retain protected content; the policy may deliberately hide the existence of an entity. |
| Physically not displayed | The actual current DOM/host does not show the entity, possibly because of filtering, retirement or failed rendering; no model absence follows. |

An authoritative absence may therefore be installed and adopted just
as an authoritative presence may. The *evidence* that the entity is
excluded and the *physical completion* of removing its representation
are separate propositions. Adoption of negative knowledge is not a
browser-only tombstone that will forever override future authorized
presence. It remains subject to the same source, projection,
progression, local continuity and ownership contracts as presence.

*** Absence requires actual covered authority, not an omitted row

The admitted source identifies the principal and Organization/tenant
disclosure context, applied query identity, server-side predicate and
arguments, entity or membership subject, projection/field coverage,
temporal and consistency interpretation, relevant authoritative
basis/progression, and the meaning of its negative result. A complete
membership observation can justify the omission of a member only
within the universe whose membership it actually closes.

A successful empty list is not automatically a complete query. A
paginated page, truncated or top-N result, projection missing the
membership field, filtered subset, cached partial response, redacted
record, tenant-limited view, or speculative client-side search result
does not certify exclusion from a larger universe. Even a complete
*authorized* query says nothing about entities that policy deliberately
does not disclose. A failed or denied read must not be converted into
"no Request exists" or expose protected existence through an
overprecise error.

An explicit trusted exclusion response may justify a narrower negative
membership fact without loading every card. It must bind the exact
entity, applied query/predicate and authorized context, provider
coverage/temporal semantics, and the exclusion reason it claims.
For example, "R17 is not in Bob's open-Requests board" need not
establish whether R17 still exists, was completed, was reassigned,
became inaccessible or was deleted. When the reason itself would
reveal protected state, only the permitted nondisclosing proposition
can be returned.

The provider's negative fact is admitted through a real acquisition
or qualified persisted observation. A client-written
=:provenance :authoritative= tag, a matching plan digest or a
structurally valid basis token cannot certify its truth. The generic
browser may preserve an opaque source/evidence reference and
scope; the trusted consistency/model boundary owns the provider
proof or expressly named premise. Absence need not allocate a
permanent tombstone for every theoretically missing entity: a
complete cohort observation or checked compact exclusion summary
can represent justified negatives within its declared retention.

The membership scope is distinct from the domain entity's existence
and from its fields. A Request can be excluded from an "open for
helper" board while remaining accessible in an authorized completed
Requests projection. An omitted optional field may reflect a
projection contract rather than a declaration that its domain
value is absent. These forms of negative knowledge have different
queries and cannot silently substitute for each other.

*** Worked example: R17 leaves Bob's open-Requests board

Bob has an admitted and physically adopted open-Requests board
observation B100 for applied query Qopen, Organization O and his
current authority context K. It includes Request R17. A subsequent
trusted operation changes R17's state so that it no longer matches
the predicate for Qopen. Depending on authorization, R17 might still
be present under an independently queried completed-Requests
projection Qdone; R17's absence from Qopen alone does not establish
its deletion or a different helper's Membership.

The next authorized acquisition is evaluated against these
possibilities:

| Candidate evidence | Valid conclusion about R17 |
|--------------------+----------------------------|
| An admitted complete Qopen membership observation B105 under K, with qualified progression and R17 excluded. | R17 is absent from *Qopen membership* at B105's stated provider interpretation. |
| An admitted explicit R17 exclusion witness for Qopen/K with the necessary coverage and temporal meaning. | R17 is excluded from that membership without claiming all other board members were acquired. |
| R17 omitted from page two, while Qopen covers multiple pages and no complete membership/exclusion witness exists. | No negative membership fact for R17 follows. |
| An admitted Qdone observation contains R17 as completed. | R17 is present in Qdone; Qopen exclusion still requires a qualified Qopen/predicate judgment. |
| Bob's permitted board changes from Qopen to Qdone or he toggles a local =show-terminal?= view option. | Distinguish a new applied server query from client presentation over an already justified cohort; neither action invents authoritative absence. |
| The server denies R17 disclosure after Bob's Membership changes. | Apply the required privacy/display revocation; do not assert that R17 was deleted or absent for all readers. |
| Qopen acquisition fails, is cancelled, or produces incompatible/indeterminate content. | Preserve the qualified previously adopted evidence where policy permits, plus stale/recovery debt; no newly proven absence. |

For the eligible complete B105 case the semantic path is:

#+begin_example
qualified source establishes R17 excluded from Qopen at B105
        |
confirm K/Qopen coverage and provider progression
        |
prepare current membership outcome :absent for R17
        |
issue current scoped removal/installation permit
        |
check exact board owner, target incarnation and representation
        |
perform permitted physical removal or checked no-op
        |
admit real matching physical postcondition
        |
record adopted absence for the covered membership
#+end_example

A prepared negative result is not yet physically adopted. The
permit binds the current runtime/assembly, actual Qopen coordinator,
B105 source and covered membership, current board/card instances,
target representation, mutation footprint and effect generation.
A stale prior request or an OOB/extension mutation cannot bypass
the permit by targeting the same HTML =id= attribute. If a
multi-target update removes a card but fails to install a new
count or status control, its actual per-target outcomes and
repair obligations remain distinct.

The physical postcondition must establish that the *current
owned representation* for R17's Qopen membership no longer
appears or grants obsolete managed actions. A generic "target
not found" may indicate an unmounted board, wrong owner,
selector mismatch or an already-correct current target. A
no-op removal can count as completed only if the qualified
host contract verifies the intended absence under the
current scope and owner. A generic =afterSwap= event does
not by itself establish that predicate.

Once a qualified absence is adopted, it retires obsolete
provisional/continuity restoration rights for the
corresponding presentation scope. A late stale callback
must not recreate the removed card from an old capture.
A current authorized later presence can legitimately
restore R17 to Qopen through its *new* qualified
observation and physical install. Absence does not
represent an irreversible global tombstone.

The local filter distinction is especially important:
Bob may hide an already acquired terminal Request
through =show-terminal?= or text-search without
starting a new read. Hiding the item is a local
presentation choice, not new authoritative
membership evidence. Re-showing it needs retained
still-justified authorized content and current
presentation ownership. If intervening authority
has excluded it or revoked its disclosure, the
local filter cannot resurrect stale markup or
grant a new subscription/operation binding.

*** Provisional presence and negative authority remain separate

Suppose E99 provisionally inserts Request R30 into a
local creator view while Create command C99 is
unresolved. A complete board acquisition omits
R30. The system must answer three *different*
questions before changing presentation:

1. Does an admitted source actually establish
   R30's exclusion from this exact applied
   query, actor/context and coverage horizon?
2. Does that negative evidence, its qualified
   progression and the selected presentation
   policy permit superseding E99's provisional
   presence in the current physical target?
3. Does a separately qualified command-result
   source establish whether C99 incorporated,
   was rejected, or remains =:commit-unknown=?

The acquisition may have occurred before C99's
possibly pending transaction incorporated, or
under a different query/actor scope. In that
case R30's omission is not automatically
rejection or proof of nonexistence. Even
sufficiently progressed *current board*
absence does not by itself establish C99's
historical attribution. A subsequent C99
incorporation, if still possible under the
model's temporal/deduplication contract,
requires its separately authorized
reconciliation and potential later read.

The application may keep a visibly labeled
pending overlay outside adopted membership,
remove the provisional card upon an admitted
negative-authority supersession, or use a
declared conflict-resolution/reacquisition
strategy. It must state the scope, owner,
command-outcome and temporal premises for
that choice; it cannot silently make an
unresolved Create a rejected command, or
misrepresent the overlay as an adopted
current Request.

If stronger authorized absence supersedes
E99's provisional representation, revoke
the old DOM/rollback/timer ownership before
physical cleanup. The C99 resolver
obligation survives under its proper owner
where promised. Removing an obsolete card
does not justify cancelling all C99 history,
repeating an unknown command with a fresh
identity, or treating a missing physical
target as a successful server operation.

A manager's later Reassign and the affected
RequestAssignment facts illustrate the same
distinction: a helper's card may no longer
belong in one projection while its
historical Claim was genuinely incorporated.
Entity/query membership, current assignment
and historical command disposition remain
separate trusted questions.

*** Absence participates in qualified progression and adoption

Presence and absence are both qualified
observation outcomes. The runtime compares
them using the source provider's declared
scope/coverage and progression relation,
not the lexical/numeric order of basis
labels, SSE arrival sequence or browser
request generation. Two distinct opaque
bases are not ordered merely because
one was fetched later.

For the *same* applicable membership scope,
a later provider-proved exclusion may
supersede an earlier present card; a
subsequent provider-proved presence may
supersede that absence. When basis values
are incomparable, the coordinator retains
the competing obligations or invokes
the declared read/merge/conflict policy.
A complete board membership from R
can coexist with an independently newer
creator-local card S only if the
qualified scope-aware merge preserves
both provenances and does not assert
a single atomic backend snapshot.

A scoped negative fact may satisfy an
advisory requirement only if its source
establishes the required query,
authority context, coverage, progression
and discharge stage. Acquisition of a
negative result does not clear
adoption-stage debt before the actual
current DOM removal/no-op postcondition
has been admitted. Failing to install
a negative membership result preserves
repair debt without falsifying the
underlying acquired fact.

Absence from an open-Requests board
does not discharge a complete-query
requirement for a different Organization,
a partial page or a card-specific
historical command resolution.
One explicit user Refresh continues
to obey its original read budget:
discovering an omission cannot
silently authorize another fetch
to "check whether it was really
deleted." If more evidence is
necessary, obtain a new permitted
read or enter an honest blocked/
unknown/reconciliation state.

Security and privacy revocation is
a different actuation contract.
A current principal losing access
may require immediate removal or
quarantine of protected presentation
even without evidence that the entity
is absent from the model. That
revocation does not permit a
new protected read and must not
reveal nondisclosable existence.
No browser-side cleanup can erase
data an adversarial client already
recorded; the trusted server
continues to enforce authorization
at every read, stream and write.

The initial baseline/subscription
and multi-node router gaps from
06.06–06.07 apply equally to
negative knowledge. Missing
invalidations must not leave a
newly excluded Request
permanently displayed under a
guarantee of current-state
convergence; the promised
replay/fence/reacquisition and
user-action assumptions must
actually support the claim.

*** Paired authoritative-absence acceptance histories

The finished design requires real eligible
trusted sources, complete coverage or qualified
exclusion and actual host completion. Negative
fixtures must reach the relevant absence,
scope or physical boundary rather than
pass solely by producing an empty element.

| Eligible positive history | Adverse or incomplete history | Required conclusion |
|---------------------------+-------------------------------+---------------------|
| Complete authorized Qopen B105 excludes previously present R17 and is provider-proved compatible with the installed membership. | R17 is merely omitted from one page of a paginated query or from a redacted subset. | Admit negative membership only under sufficient covered Qopen evidence; partial omission is unknown. |
| Trusted explicit R17/Qopen exclusion witness has narrower sufficient coverage. | Browser bytes copy =:provenance :authoritative= and a plausible basis without a qualified source. | The real narrow witness may establish exclusion; copied tags do not. |
| R17 is absent from Qopen while a qualified Qdone projection still contains it. | The browser infers global deletion or historical Claim failure from Qopen exclusion. | Preserve projection-relative membership, domain existence and command attribution as different facts. |
| A current authorized removal permit operates on the matching Qopen card and checks its physical postcondition. | A generic =afterSwap= or missing CSS selector is credited as proof the current card disappeared. | Only a qualified completed removal or valid current-target no-op establishes adopted absence. |
| New qualified B105 exclusion retires R17's old provisional/rollback rights; later provider-proved presence may reintroduce it. | A stale timer reinserts an old card, or an irreversible tombstone blocks new authoritative presence. | Prevent obsolete restoration while permitting later justified presence. |
| C99 Create remains unknown and R30 is omitted from a board read that predates possible incorporation. | Omission is declared terminal C99 rejection or permission for blind duplicate Create. | Distinguish temporal exclusion, provisional presentation and historical command result. |
| Bob hides a retained authorized R17 under a local text/sort/terminal filter and restores it while membership still justifies the content. | Local re-showing overrides a newer authoritative exclusion, query change or disclosure revocation. | Local visibility choices create no new server truth or stale presentation rights. |
| A complete authorized removal of one card and matching count update both physically finish under their distinct permits. | Card removal finishes, count/OOB update fails, yet the whole board is marked adopted. | Preserve per-target completion and repair debt; no imaginary atomic installation. |
| An acquired negative result satisfies O1 but installation fails and one-Refresh grant is exhausted. | The coordinator clears adoption-stage O1 or starts an ungranted second acquisition. | Keep acquired evidence, outstanding physical adoption debt and exact read budget separate. |
| Access is revoked and the honest client clears protected presentation under a current privacy policy. | The client displays "R17 deleted" or attempts a protected read without permission. | Revocation is not domain absence; enforce nondisclosure and trusted server authorization. |

These cases specify the required negative-knowledge
and physically verified removal contracts for every
profile claiming authoritative-absence adoption.
Part VII must inspect actual model,
writer, renderer and browser entrypoints;
Part VIII requires nonvacuous HumanHelp
Claim/Reassign/Done, creator-local
presentation and remote one-Refresh
behavior; Parts IX–X distinguish
finite tests, trusted model premises
and real physical host refinement.
** Failure, liveness, and convergence

Browser safety, eventual progress, bounded resource use, and recovery are
different claims. The finished framework must express each with the
correct subject, quantification, source and environmental premises.
A runtime that retains an unresolved command, a failed installation
or unmet advisory debt while reporting that condition truthfully can
remain *safe* without being currently *live*. A system that eventually
renders the right card after first issuing an unauthorized Claim was
not safe merely because it converged later.

The application construction and assurance pipeline must distinguish
proved semantic obligations, checked finite reference cases, tested
actual implementations, qualified physical host correspondence,
runtime-enforced admission and still-trusted external assumptions.
No successful diagnostic, model fixture or optional proof artifact
may become the permission by which production chooses a semantic
transition. Parts IX–X retain the separate proof and certification
contracts.

*** Failures preserve authoritative truth and its observer-relative limits

A failure classification answers *what happened at which boundary*
and *what this participant is justified in knowing*. It cannot
derive domain truth from a generic network or browser error.

| Failure or disposition | Required semantic and physical treatment |
|------------------------+------------------------------------------|
| Rejected local input/operation admission before protected send | Report local nonadmission; do not manufacture a server-side =:rejected= outcome or assert nonincorporation of another earlier attempt. |
| Qualified trusted operation rejection | Preserve original command/actor/operation binding and permitted terminal exclusion evidence. Rejection is a business result, not a runtime crash. |
| Qualified incorporation or compatible already-incorporated outcome | Retain historical incorporation even if later notification, DOM installation, or current entity acquisition fails. |
| Transport loss after possible physical send | Preserve =:commit-unknown= until a qualified resolver/deduplication contract establishes more; physical abort is not nonincorporation evidence. |
| Trusted commit followed by invalidation/stream failure | Commit remains true; retain missing-delivery/interest-gap and application-specific adoption obligations. |
| Failed acquisition, denied disclosure, missing provider witness | Do not invent presence, absence, collection membership or progression. Retain required scope-specific debt and honor disclosure boundaries. |
| Prepared installation, host mutation or OOB effect fails | Distinguish acquired observation from completed per-target physical adoption; retain partial/indeterminate repair debt without reversing authoritative commit. |
| Stale or incompatible continuation | Revoke obsolete semantic/actuation rights before best-effort physical cleanup; preserve separately durable historical command and Live obligations. |
| Resource cancellation/release fails | Preserve physical remnant information and enforce resource budgets; never treat failed cleanup as revival of old rights. |
| Adapter invariant or source-normalization failure | Contain the affected semantic owner/runtime, retain original causality, and use a declared bounded recovery rather than trying a different informal interpretation. |
| Lost compatibility, grant, storage or recovery evidence | Report blocked/unknown/expired/manual-reconciliation as applicable; unsupported replays and old private effects remain forbidden. |

A UI timeout belongs to its actual owner: it may expire a provisional
spinner, cancel a physical waiting policy, trigger a qualified resolver
attempt, or mark a local presentation deadline. None of those facts
alone says whether C42's trusted RequestAssignment Claim committed.
A timer that makes E42's presentation stop waiting need not retire
K8's distinct command-history recovery deadline. A domain
=:rejected=, =:already-incorporated=, conflict disposition or
current "not applicable" result is not synonymous with a broken
HTMX/FFI integration, malformed response or impossible adapter state.

The runtime must retain source-relative evidence and primary fault
causality. If physical effect F partly executed and cleanup CA/CC
failed, report F with subordinate release failures and the actual
remaining obligations. It may safely quarantine, reacquire or use
declared compensation, but cannot blindly repeat a nonrepeatable
effect batch or restore an obsolete provisional snapshot. A current
authorized Order/Request card can be reconstructed while the
historical command that may have created it remains unresolved.

*** Safety properties quantify over all admitted relevant transitions

Under the named semantic contracts and actual implementation/host
premises, safety requires at least:

- **No unadmitted physical act:** a protected HTTP send, DOM mutation,
  OOB/response-header effect, timer-triggered restoration or disclosure
  operates only under its current relevant registered source,
  issuance/owner identity and last-controllable permit.
- **No stale authority revival:** retirement removes E42's private
  semantic/physical rights independently of whether abort, listener
  detachment or timer cancellation succeeds. A late callback cannot
  settle E43 or mutate B2 using B1's old selector.
- **No fabricated business outcome:** local timeout, transport failure,
  successful parsing, plan compatibility and physical installation
  cannot manufacture incorporation, rejection or current
  RequestAssignment facts.
- **No false authoritative adoption:** a current authorized acquisition
  supplies only its actual covered positive/negative observation,
  while adopted presentation requires the matching physical
  target-specific completion and permitted scope.
- **No invented progression/absence:** opaque XTDB bases, duplicated
  metadata, SSE arrival order, partial query omission and browser
  generations are not trusted provider ordering/exclusion witnesses.
- **No obligation loss through scheduling:** advisory, subscription-gap,
  command-resolution, partial physical-effect and adoption debts
  survive until their own declared discharge conditions hold,
  regardless of queued-slot or logical-cycle cleanup.
- **No permission bypass:** automatic versus one-user-Refresh policies,
  server read/write authorization, tenant disclosure and compatibility
  are separately enforced at real physical boundaries.
- **No incorrect restoration:** local continuity or provisional
  rollback does not overwrite newer qualified canonical state or
  transfer physical resource ownership because two values or CSS
  selectors happen to match.
- **No false assurance provenance:** observed adapter effects,
  physical host actions, trusted model results, finite model
  checks and full application certificates are not collapsed
  into one success label.

These are families of invariants indexed by runtime, principal,
scope, owner, resource instance, command, attempt and effect
identity—not just assertions about one convenient concrete
Request ID. A safety proof must quantify over the declared
transition/environment relation, or limit its claim to a
faithfully checked finite subject. A test of E42/E43 with
two chosen integer generations cannot by itself prove
noncollision for arbitrary reuse or server deployment.

An application with opaque Clojure side effects, a third-party
DOM writer, an unverified HTMX extension or a progression
provider not yet related to actual XTDB executions can still
be useful, but guarantees depending on those components
retain the named trust/physical correspondence premises.
Failing to establish a required premise means the stronger
claim is *not established*, not that the proof silently
assumes every opaque function did the right thing.

*** Terminal reachability and liveness are not interchangeable

Finding a path from each reachable state to some terminal
state does not establish that every applicable execution
will reach it. A machine can remain forever at =waiting=
if the environment never supplies settlement, timer,
allowed user action or authoritative read:

#+begin_example
waiting --qualified settlement--> resolved
        --timer fires-----------> local recovery / C42 still unknown
        --nothing enabled-------> still waiting
#+end_example

Safety excludes invalid steps; liveness adds explicitly
quantified progress premises. A claim that "every
submitted command eventually reaches a trusted result"
needs more than a browser timeout: it depends on a
resolver that can distinguish incorporation from
nonincorporation within its retention horizon,
eventually available authoritative services, relevant
fairness/retry scheduling, surviving command binding
and present disclosure permission. Where the resolver
cannot decide after history expires, the supported
progress claim may instead reach an honest manual
or unknown recovery terminal; it may **not** claim
a proven committed/rejected outcome.

The assembly and checker distinguish:

| Progress property | Essential premises or limitation |
|-------------------+----------------------------------|
| Eventual local retirement | The relevant local transition/callback is eventually scheduled, or a separately safe shutdown/admission boundary can revoke rights. |
| Eventual command attribution | A qualified durable resolver/deduplication record survives and eventually responds with permitted evidence; otherwise only a blocked/manual state may be reachable. |
| Eventual authoritative acquisition | A current authenticated read remains permitted and a sufficiently covering provider response can eventually be obtained. |
| Eventual physical adoption | Current compatible target/host permits persist sufficiently, mandatory installation can finish or recover, and competing higher-priority owners do not permanently prevent it. |
| Eventual Live agreement | Relevant state/query/authority eventually stabilizes or has a suitable convergence contract; gap detection/replay or reacquisition works; permissions and scheduling allow outstanding reads and installs. |
| Eventual cleanup/resource recovery | Physical handles can eventually be released or the implementation can safely reset/degrade within a specified bound. Cancellation alone is not guaranteed successful. |

Weak/strong fairness assumptions must attach to the
actual enabled transition and scheduler, not merely
appear as a generic label. An environment that keeps
a callback disabled, repeatedly revokes permission,
partitions the network or changes authority forever
may prevent eventual progress without violating
the safety invariant. An application cannot promise
unconditional convergence while allowing permanent
denial of current data or indefinite suspension
of its only authorized user action.

Liveness proof obligations also avoid vacuity. If every
real operation is disabled, no invalid command reaches
the server, but the product still fails its required
positive Claim, Reassign or Refresh behavior. An
acceptance test must establish that eligible paths
actually execute through trusted model, transport
and physical display stages, then challenge the
corresponding failure and adverse scheduling cases.

*** Agreement debt may converge under scoped quiescence

Different participants may legitimately adopt different
authorized views while writes continue. A participant
should know which observations it has adopted, their
authority/source, query/field coverage, provider
progression and any unfulfilled advisory/gap debts.
The strongest generally useful promise is *scoped
conditional convergence*, not instantaneous equality
of every browser's DOM or knowledge.

A representative contract is:

#+begin_example
Assume:
  relevant model state and applied query/authority eventually stabilize;
  a sufficiently covering authorized observation is eventually obtainable;
  the interest gap is fenced, replayed, or repaired by reacquisition;
  the selected acquisition grant is eventually available and actually used;
  the required host/transport/renderer and fair scheduler eventually succeed;
  retained obligations are not lost and no incompatible owner blocks forever.

Then:
  the participant eventually acquires and physically adopts the
  promised stabilized covered projection, or meets its explicitly
  declared weaker recovery/blocked terminal where the liveness
  contract permits that outcome.
#+end_example

To claim *actual adopted convergence* rather than a
weaker recovery alternative, the assumptions must
exclude permanent failure and grant absence. It is
invalid to place a "manual help available" state in
the conclusion and then claim every user eventually
observes the latest board. The current model truth,
a participant's acquired evidence, installed view,
unresolved C42 history and advisory/Refresh debt
are separate components, not one monotonic
counter named current.

HumanHelp's remote one-Refresh policy intentionally
allows an interval in which Bob knows an advisory
exists but has not authorized acquisition or
adoption. Its liveness target is conditional on
Bob's qualifying user action. The creator's
correlated local S card may be more advanced
than an older R whole-board membership result;
a correct convergence merge retains the
separate qualified scope evidence instead
of inventing a common XTDB snapshot.
One Refresh may satisfy multiple accrued O1/O2
obligations if its actual acquired and installed
observation covers them, but never silently
issues A2 when G1 permitted only A1.

A browser that missed changes from X17
through X900 may recover a *current-state*
view directly through a sufficiently qualified
X900-or-later observation rather than replaying
every intermediate SSE packet. That result
requires real query/authority/progression
coverage and permitted physical adoption.
It does not establish that every intermediate
business event or side effect was processed.
Applications requiring durable per-event
processing need a separately declared
event/log and exactly applicable effect contract.

The initial baseline-to-interest gap, late
registration and multi-node router failover
retain the same semantics as single-node:
a missed event not generated under any
interest cannot be restored by redelivering
the known events alone. A valid fence, durable
replay or qualified current-state reacquisition
is required to make the promised continuity
and convergence conclusion. SSE silence
or an =online= event does not prove currentness.

*** Boundedness is not supplied by single flight

The application declares resource budgets,
overflow policy, retention horizon and
recovery for distinct categories:

| Budgeted resource | What the bound must account for |
|-------------------+---------------------------------|
| Logical coordinator cycles | Active acquisition/installation cycles and their qualified owner identities. |
| Queued successor scheduling | Number of successor slots, without confusing the slot with acquisition permission. |
| Pending advisory/requirement information | Potentially incomparable obligations, provider-sound compaction and retained gap/adoption debt. |
| Command resolution and deduplication | Original binding/records, durable retention, expiry, replay fences and still-unknown results. |
| Physical attempts and host remnants | Requests that cannot be aborted, native listeners, timers, DOM/continuity captures, OOB effects and cleanup failures. |
| Delivery replay/identity history | Consumed message IDs, retired resources, allocator epochs and safe compaction windows. |
| Diagnostics and evidence buffers | Observer throughput, trace redaction, retained failure provenance and bounded storage. |
| Current adopted/retained projection | Permitted board/card data, privacy/disclosure expiry, presentation resources and restoration captures. |
| Retry and recovery work | Attempts, backoff, reloads, resolver reads, grant consumption and manual escalation. |

The default one-active/one-coalesced-successor
coordinator bound is a bound on *logical
scheduling*, not a theorem that all HTTP,
DOM or resource costs are bounded. A single
queue slot can stand for unboundedly many
incomparable requirements; a failed abort can
leave physical work alive even when semantic
state declares it retired.

Coalescing is safe only where the provider's
coverage/progression contract proves that a
sound summary retains all required
discharge conditions. A stronger complete
read may collapse several obligations where
admitted; choosing a maximum-looking opaque
basis or dropping the oldest request because
the queue is full does not. If no sound bounded
summary exists, the application must choose a
declared backpressure, resynchronization,
storage, or visible capacity-failure
contract. It cannot simultaneously promise
unbounded distinct obligations, bounded
memory and no durable external storage
without a sound representation theorem.

Resource exhaustion must preserve safety:
block new protected sends or physical
effects, revoke/retire unsafe owners,
report actual missing work and allow
only permitted reset/recovery. Silent
downgrade to unprotected raw HTMX,
erasure of pending C42, unreported
drop of O2 or fabrication of a complete
installation is not an overflow policy.

Even where a resource budget is finite,
liveness may fail because capacity
remains exhausted. The target assurance
must separately state whether cleanup,
durable compaction, user intervention
or process reset eventually restores
capacity, and which commitments survive
that failure domain.

*** Layered assurance distinguishes checks from assumptions

The following evidence classes support
different, noninterchangeable claims:

| Evidence or check | What may be established, and what is not implied |
|-------------------+-------------------------------------------------|
| Portable executable semantics and invariant checker | Safety for the declared semantic subject and admitted transition relation under proven premises; not automatically real browser/XTDB behavior. |
| Exact finite Recife/TLC check | Obligations on the selected finite reference model and its enumerated assumptions; not a generic inductive theorem, all operations, or an application certificate. |
| Actual adapter-step observation | A transition selected by the current executable adapter for those admitted inputs; not an attestation that abstract send reached the server. |
| Executor-bound source/physical observation | Precisely observed bounded execution evidence under its registered executor, extractor and source binding; not proof that all possible executions correspond. |
| Browser/Chromium conformance trace | Actual tested host effects and callbacks on the specific HTMX/asset/extension profile and fixture; not universal behavior of all browsers and alternate routes. |
| Trusted backend operation or authorized readback | Qualified incorporation/negative result or current observation under the exact model, principal, query, XTDB/progression contracts; not physical DOM adoption. |
| Matched physical installation postcondition | Completed target-specific effect and possible scoped adoption; not an unrelated whole-board frontier or server command result. |
| Application assembly and deployment certificate | Only the explicitly checked full inventory, semantic/proof subject, trust premises, served asset/handler closure and supported environmental profiles. |

A proof kernel is distinct from the
portable executable semantic core. The
former checks precisely defined evidence
or derivations; the latter drives
production execution. Neither diagnostic
observer nor proof report is allowed
to alter the chosen runtime branch.
Gesso application authors declare
business rules, operations and Gesso
construction; they are not required
to manually write Recife, Quint or
TLA+ specifications. Generated proofs
and checks require explicit correspondence
from application declaration to model
and from model to the running
implementation/host.

When a finite checker rejects, times
out, is malformed or becomes unavailable,
its obligation remains unestablished;
the system does not attach a success
label or conflate the checker failure
with a domain-model rejection. An
optional diagnostic may be omitted under
a declared weaker assurance policy,
but an application requiring that
specific assurance cannot be certified
by executing without it.

The specified assurance level determines
which construction, provider and physical
correspondence obligations must be discharged.
A runtime or deployment unable to establish
a required premise reports that limit
rather than silently weakening the
normative guarantee.

*** Paired failure, liveness and boundedness histories

Each positive witness must use an eligible
application path and check its actual
command/read/physical result. Each
adversarial witness must reach the
intended failure, fairness or capacity
boundary without being rejected for
an unrelated malformed input.

| Eligible positive history | Adverse or insufficient history | Required conclusion |
|---------------------------+---------------------------------+---------------------|
| A qualified C42 Claim incorporates; its response is lost but authorized readback later proves the original command result. | H1 timeout is declared a trusted rejection or a new ID is issued blindly. | Retain correct incorporation/unknown and original binding under the resolver's retention/fairness contract. |
| An authoritative Request card is acquired and its permitted physical target install completes. | The HTML response succeeds but physical swap/OOB effect fails and view is marked adopted. | Acquisition and adoption differ; preserve target-specific repair debt. |
| E42 is retired, its stale callbacks fail admission and exact cleanup eventually releases old resources. | Failed abort leaves live native callbacks that mutate B2, or cleanup failure is hidden as zero resource cost. | Stale-act safety is invariant; physical remnants remain bounded or cause an explicit unavailable state. |
| Bob sees O1, grants exactly one A1 Refresh, and installs a covering result that also satisfies O2. | An advisory launches ungranted A2, or a result lacking O2 coverage clears the glow. | One read suffices only with actual provider coverage/adoption, while unmet debt and grant budgets remain. |
| Under quiescence, available authority, grant, fair scheduling and working fence/reacquisition, Bob eventually adopts the promised Q view. | A terminal graph path is cited as a convergence proof while user never grants Refresh or the stream gap remains unclosed. | State actual fairness, user-action and continuity premises; do not claim unconditional liveness. |
| A current read at X900 establishes the promised board state after missing earlier invalidations. | The system claims every intermediate business event was executed from one final board snapshot. | Current-state convergence and durable event processing are different contracts. |
| O1/O2 are provider-justifiably compressed into one covered obligation; resource use stays within declared limits. | Incomparable requirements are dropped or numeric-maxed because only one queue slot is allowed. | Sound obligation compaction or explicit capacity failure; single flight is not bounded debt. |
| A trusted excluded-member result removes R17 from its current board target while retaining its possible presence in another query. | A partial page omission, DOM absence or revoked disclosure is treated as global deletion. | Negative model truth, scope and physical absence demand separate evidence. |
