| An eligible Claim/Reassign and remote Refresh complete through real model, transport and browser callbacks. | All positive operations are disabled, so the checker sees only safe rejections and claims application acceptance. | Positive product conformance is independent of negative-only safety. |
| A finite reference check reports bounded assumptions and nonclaims for its exact derived execution subject. | The finite pass is presented as an inductive proof of all Gesso apps, actual XTDB or the deployed HTMX browser. | Keep finite model, implementation, proof-kernel and physical/certification evidence separately scoped. |

Part VII must certify
the actual installed operation, route,
subscription, renderer and handler
inventory. Part VIII must exercise
real HumanHelp Claim/Reassign,
creator-local updates, remote
one-Refresh and continuity behavior.
Parts IX–XII must preserve the
correct proof, physical/backend
correspondence, deployment and
multi-node trust boundaries.
** Refinement, correspondence, and conformance evidence

The browser refinement claim relates one admitted executable semantic
plan and its source-normalized transition/effect history to the actual
physical behavior of the selected browser, HTMX/SSE integration, backend,
renderers and other installed effects. These are *different subjects*.
A valid role-local adapter transition is not a trusted server commit;
a requested send is not actual delivery; an observed browser receive
does not by itself prove a corresponding sender emitted it; a local
machine finishing does not prove the global choreography terminated.

Gesso's finished assurance pipeline makes these distinctions useful:
the application author declares domain rules, Gesso construction and
the supported physical profile, while the assembly and evidence
pipeline generates, checks and relates its semantic witnesses.
Authors need not manually write Recife, TLA+ or Quint. Generated
evidence does not confer semantic authority on diagnostics or let
an unsupported host action pass a physical gate.

The *object being certified* is always explicit: exact choreography
and projected executable artifact, admitted application/operation
assembly, actual source event or host trace, specified backend
execution, selected release/profile and the claimed safety or
liveness property. A pass over an attractive surrogate does
not establish correspondence of the application that ran.

*** Observe actual adapter transitions and independent physical occurrences

A diagnostic about the browser's internal machine starts from the
*actual* adapter step, not an externally proposed successor that a
report happens to describe. The recorded next state and ordered
abstract effects come from one execution of the admitted portable
transition function against the exact before-state and normalized
event. The observation carries the current execution, owner,
effect and applicable artifact identity and cannot itself create
an installation or command result.

The physical shell and qualified external sources additionally record
or attest the concrete actions to which the guarantee applies.
For each claimed physical step, the evidence names its own producer,
registration, environment/asset profile, observation point,
occurrence identity, effect/target incarnation, and real disposition.
A report that merely restates the adapter's intended effect is
not physical evidence that the effect happened.

| Evidence layer | Proposition it can establish | Proposition it cannot establish alone |
|----------------+------------------------------+---------------------------------------|
| Selected portable adapter step | The real semantic adapter selected this next state and ordered abstract effects for these admitted inputs. | HTMX sent a request, a server committed, or the DOM changed as intended. |
| Role-local projected machine history | This role locally performed or accepted the recorded step under its executable plan. | The global sender, network and other roles actually participated. |
| Abstract =:transport/send= effect | The semantic runtime requested a correlated transport attempt. | The physical browser sent it or the peer received it. |
| Correlated physical host issue/return | The selected host performed the reported issue/completion boundary under its qualified profile. | Domain incorporation or unrelated secondary effects not covered by the observation point. |
| Trusted domain command/result witness | The authenticated model operation or qualified resolver established a particular C42 historical disposition. | Current RequestAssignment/card state or physical presentation adoption. |
| Qualified authoritative acquisition | The trusted provider established stated query/entity/absence, scope, context and progression. | Installation of the representation, or universal ordering of opaque bases. |
| Real scoped physical installation witness | The current permitted effect established its declared target-specific postcondition, including supported OOB/partial behavior. | Another target, the complete board, an unrelated command result or a common backend snapshot. |
| Participant adoption transition | The participant admitted the actual covered installation into its current scoped presentation state. | That every other participant has adopted or that their obligation debt vanished. |
| Checked concrete correspondence witness | A specific independently sourced and bound trace satisfies the stated relation and checker premises. | Every future schedule, all deployments, or correctness of unobserved physical effects. |

For the actual host trace, issue, send, send-failure, receive,
response processing, native swap, OOB target mutation, timer callback,
resource release and completion may be distinct occurrences.
The selected profile says which observations are available and
sufficient for each protected contract. If that profile does not
expose a controllable or observable protected mutation, the
application must reject the strong realization, use another
qualified host contract or explicitly retain the unproved premise;
it cannot obtain a universal witness by giving an unobserved step
the same label as a known one.

An event-source registry and an adapter-created correlation value
help bind an actual callback to issued work. They do not authenticate
arbitrary client-payload claims. Trusted backend/XTDB and command
evidence must be produced at their own authoritative boundary.
An actual physical browser observation cannot be replaced by a
synthetic event sequence merely because the same adapter steps
appear when replayed.

*** Refinement relates concrete traces, not similar-looking outputs

For an admitted initial relation, one may state a conditional
forward-simulation/refinement obligation as follows:

#+begin_example
Assume the named executable, source, backend and host contracts.
Let R(c, s) relate a concrete running state c to semantic state s.

For each actual concrete protected transition c -> c':
  either:
    there is a matching permitted semantic transition s -> s'
    with its required identity/evidence/physical bindings, and R(c', s');
  or:
    the concrete transition is an admitted internal stuttering step
    with R(c', s) and no hidden protected effect or lost obligation.

For every claimed semantic physical completion:
  an appropriately sourced concrete occurrence establishes its
  exact permitted target/effect postcondition.

No concrete protected effect is omitted from the correspondence.
#+end_example

This is a *conditional proof obligation* whose discharge requires
evidence for each supported browser/HTMX profile and deployment. The relation
has to cover source-normalized event admission, current owner and
resource instance, physical commitment points, partial mutations,
runtime faults, recovery obligations, qualified progression, and
observations/authority context. A model containing only successful
send/swap histories cannot refine an implementation with failed
abort, duplicate settlement, OOB changes and stale callbacks.

A concrete step can correspond to zero semantic progress only
if its "internal" status has been justified. A DOM replacement,
unadmitted second request, cross-principal disclosure,
resource-generation change that revives old rights, or loss of
pending O2 debt cannot disappear into an unspecified stutter.
Conversely purely local observer bookkeeping, bounded trace
buffer maintenance or a harmless ignored stale event may
stutter when its noninterference contract really holds.

Safety refinement and liveness are separate. Infinitely many
internal steps can satisfy a naive safety stuttering relation
while preventing an enabled authoritative installation forever.
A stronger liveness conclusion requires an explicit divergence
condition and the fairness, provider, grant, recovery and
physical scheduling premises of 06.13.

The relation need not impose one artificial total order on
independent concurrent operations. A declared weak or commuting
correspondence may account for causally independent steps and
permitted internal actions. It must preserve the actual
happens-before edges, per-resource and per-command order,
server transaction constraints, physical target serialization
and every externally observable effect whose order matters.
Commutation cannot swap a settlement ahead of its issuing send,
a DOM completion before its current permit, or an old callback
past the revocation that makes it powerless.

*** Trace alignment preserves actual occurrence identities and provenance

A concrete trace matcher checks occurrences, not merely
similar maps or eventual output values. It establishes a
declared mapping from each relevant real occurrence to
its role-local/semantic counterpart and verifies that
neither side supplies invented send, delivery,
incorporation, completion or adoption events.

For a supported exact or weak correspondence, the matcher:

1. Binds the exact admitted choreography, projection,
   executable plan and application/assembly subject;
   checks the artifact relation rather than relying
   on a friendly source name or copied plan digest.
2. Binds the concrete trace to its actual executor/
   physical source, runtime/deployment instance and
   declared extraction point. A caller-supplied list
   of plausible observations is not evidence that
   those events happened.
3. Preserves relevant individual occurrence IDs
   and their issued effect, owner generation,
   command, transport attempt, target,
   observation and resource incarnation.
4. Requires every *protected concrete* action
   to be accounted for exactly under its
   permitted semantic or independently
   justified internal classification.
5. Never duplicates one physical send, receive,
   target mutation or completion to satisfy
   two unrelated obligations; never drops
   the inconvenient occurrence and calls
   the remaining sequence aligned.
6. Checks the declared causal and ordering
   relation, allowing only proven
   independent commuting steps.
7. Distinguishes absent physical evidence,
   a reported physical failure, an
   explicitly checked no-op and actual
   successful completion.
8. Carries source/provider trust premises
   forward; a structurally validated
   =:advances= or =:committed= carrier is not
   a self-authenticating authoritative witness.
9. Exposes ambiguous matches and their
   assumptions rather than guessing the
   desired witness from the final state.
10. Rejects traces whose extraction, version
    binding, loss reporting or coverage
    cannot support the requested property.

An effect request and its completion may share a semantic
effect identity but remain *different occurrences*. Multiple
compatible HTTP attempts H1/H2 can share C42 yet retain
distinct physical IDs and possible delivery outcomes.
A trusted command resolver may prove C42's historical
incorporation while the actual H1 receive still lacks
a transport witness. A successful DOM replacement can
be physically observed while an unrelated board
advisory remains outstanding.

The trace extractor is part of the assurance boundary.
It must be sufficiently independent of the semantic
claim it is checking that it cannot silently fabricate
the required fact. For a physical host claim, a reporter
that merely copies =:htmx/allow-swap= into
=:authoritative/installed= is not a witness to a
real swap. For source/backend claims, submitting a
model result as an opaque request's expected value
does not prove the actual transaction followed that
model. The emitted record must identify who/what
observed the actual execution and at which point.

Completeness is relative to the claimed footprint.
An instrumented real Chromium test can establish
one concrete tested lifecycle and admit the remaining
uncovered extension/browser paths as explicit
assumptions or unsupported. It cannot claim complete
physical correspondence if the instrumented hook
does not see mutations from permitted scripts,
OOB processing or another DOM writer.

A digest can bind evidence to exact bytes under its
canonicalization and collision premises; equality
of digests is not admission of the evidence itself.
A diagnostic/proof sidecar is read-only: runtime
operation/branch selection depends on the executable
semantic plan and current admitted inputs, not on
whether a favorable certificate happens to be
attached or can be forged.

*** Global communication and termination need independent witnesses

A browser role-local =:send= is normally hidden from
the distributed-observation alphabet until actual
communication requirements are established. A role
receiving an envelope can produce a *candidate*
distributed communication shape, but cannot prove
from its receive history alone that the expected
sender emitted the same event, that transport
delivery corresponds to that send, or that a
global admissible schedule exists.

The corresponding independent witnesses include:

| Candidate global claim | Required additional evidence |
|------------------------+------------------------------|
| Browser role-local receive corresponds to distributed communication | Sender emission, delivery/correlation and global schedule admissibility under the canonical choreography. |
| Browser role-local terminal outcome corresponds to global return | Global terminal outcome, all-role terminal compatibility and schedule admissibility. |
| Browser local authoritative observation means trusted model step occurred | Authenticated operation/transaction evidence with exact schema, actor, causal operation binding and backend/provider premises. |
| Browser adapter requested transport and therefore remote effect occurred | Actual physical send/delivery plus qualified receiver and operation evidence as appropriate to the claim. |
| Browser installed a view and therefore application reached agreement | Current scoped physical/adopted observation and independent other-participant coverage/adoption where agreement is claimed. |

Importing an already-advanced browser machine at
=:execution/start= cannot attest the steps that
occurred before import. Likewise machine history
erased on retirement cannot be reconstructed as
observed merely because a terminal effect was
emitted. The evidence pipeline records these
unwitnessed intervals and refuses to promote
candidate observations into certified global
facts.

A local execution becoming terminal is not the
global choreography reaching its specified
return outcome; an outer role-local success
envelope is not the trusted final model result.
To establish a global claim, the independent
role/sender/authority evidence is related
to the actual observed schedule with the
declared correspondence checker. This
avoids a self-confirming loop in which the
browser emits both the assertion and the
supposed proof of its truth.

The portable semantic implementation may
have independently checked canonical
choreography-to-projection correspondence
for a selected concrete witness, including
weak/commuting alignment. That evidence is
valuable but still witness-scoped until
a quantified refinement argument or
separately justified complete abstraction
has been established. Linking to the
actual browser host and backend execution
is an additional obligation, not
automatic from projection agreement.

*** Execution isolation is local except for declared shared effects

Execution-private state and effects belong
to their exact owner generation. E42's
timer, transport completion, provisional
rollback, local output and target lease
cannot advance E43 or mutate E43's
private physical target simply because
both executions reference the same Request
or historical command C42. An old
callback may remain physically present
after logical retirement, but it has
lost actuation rights.

The model also admits *intended shared
interactions* through their declared
semantic owners. A current fragment
coordinator may receive a scoped SSE
advisory, adopt an authorized
RequestAssignment observation, revoke
old provisional presentation or
apply a declared resource-pressure
policy while several local
executions are active. Those
operations affect multiple executions
in ways the semantic relation must
represent rather than exclude as
unmodeled interference.

| Interaction | Required isolation/correspondence treatment |
|-------------+---------------------------------------------|
| E42 private callback after E43 starts | Deny E42's progression and stale physical target rights; optional bounded diagnostic only. |
| Current B3 shared advisory during E42 work | Admit under B3's current subscription/interest and applied scope, independent of E42; preserve outstanding debt and selected Refresh policy. |
| Shared authoritative card supersedes E42 provisional display | Revoke only the applicable weaker presentation rights under a real qualified scope/progression policy; retain independent C42 resolver ownership. |
| E42 and E43 attempt to mutate the same DOM target | A current serialization/merge/supersession relation determines the winner; distinct execution IDs alone do not isolate the target. |
| An old owner and new owner share a timer ID or same CSS height value | Exact resource/owner incarnation controls release; old cleanup cannot cancel or restore new owner's physical state. |
| Current whole-board R result overlaps newer creator-local S | Preserve separately qualified card/cohort representation or reacquire the conflict; do not claim an invented single snapshot. |
| One coordinator retires while a shared SSE connection serves another | Detach only its exact interest and revoke its callbacks; preserve other valid owners and their continuity gaps. |
| Deployment/runtime fails and shared capacity is exhausted | Apply declared runtime-wide containment/backpressure and retained debt; do not pretend completely independent progress where shared resources failed. |

An isolation theorem therefore names
the protected state/physical footprint,
allowed cross-owner transitions and
the environmental noninterference
premises. It cannot mean "no
execution ever affects another"
when the application intentionally
coordinates shared authoritative
views. Nor can two execution
names make a common DOM target
or native browser side effect
thread-safe by declaration.

Where one effect interferes with
another, the assembly supplies
an admitted serialization,
supersession, transactional
physical primitive or
scope-aware merge. If a host
reenters during a protected
multi-target action, the
protocol names actual
intermediate states and partial
failure disposition. JavaScript's
event loop alone is not proof
that an arbitrary multi-target
HTML swap is physically atomic.

An actor/tenant change,
permission revocation or
incompatible deployment can
justifiably retire several owners
at once. Each affected resource,
advisory requirement and command
resolution obligation still
requires a current scoped
disposition. The server
independently authorizes reads,
subscriptions and writes against
a hostile client that may ignore
all browser isolation gates.

*** Diagnostics and witness extraction do not alter execution

Observing the execution must
not be a second executable
semantic interpreter.
For the same admitted plan,
event sequence and actual
physical input behavior,
attaching or removing a
read-only diagnostic observer
must not add, remove,
reorder or rewrite semantic
transitions, abstract effects,
command sends, owner state
or authorized completion.

A throwing, malformed, slow
or disabled observer follows
an explicit bounded
failure-isolation policy.
An ordinary in-process
callback without scheduling/
resource isolation can still
block or reenter execution;
calling it "optional" is not
proof of noninterference.
Instrumentation effects and
buffer capacity need a
real contract. A production
certificate cannot depend on
collecting complete traces
from a buffer that silently
drops relevant mutations
without loss markers.

The actual source boundary
and physical capture must
be audited for completeness
and trust assumptions.
The strongest runtime
conformance check may require
dedicated instrumentation
or an external observer
outside the semantic
decision path. The
application's semantic
branch never switches
because a proof report is
present, absent or favorable.

*** Paired refinement and isolation acceptance histories

Every positive test exercises
a real admitted transition,
source, physical effect or
concrete independent witness
as appropriate. Its
adversarial counterpart
reaches the relevant
correspondence boundary,
rather than trivially
rejecting an unrelated
malformed fixture.

| Eligible positive history | Adverse or incomplete history | Required conclusion |
|---------------------------+-------------------------------+---------------------|
| A real adapter step emits a specific ordered effect vector and the observer rederives it from the same state/event. | A caller substitutes a plausible successor, reorders effects or copies a matching-looking report from another step. | The actual step is observed; source-derived equality alone grants no global/physical certificate. |
| E42's role-local receive has matching independent sender, delivery and global-schedule witnesses. | The receiver reports the envelope but sender emission or delivery evidence is absent. | A candidate distributed event is admitted only when all named witnesses are supplied; no invented send. |
| Two roles finish under a globally admissible terminal schedule with an independent global outcome witness. | The browser role alone completes and the report claims the global choreography returned. | Preserve role-local completion versus global terminal correspondence. |
| H1's actual issue and host completion are observed with registered correlation, and trusted C42 evidence is separately acquired. | A requested send is copied as a physical delivery or HTTP 200 is copied as model incorporation. | Distinct source/transport/model evidence remains separately bound. |
| A permitted real HTMX card swap installs B2 and a qualified target-specific postcondition is observed. | A similar =afterSwap= or unexamined OOB mutation is matched to B2 while its actual owner/target differs. | No wrong-target matching or invented physical completion; keep partial repair debt. |
| A weak/commuting witness reorders only proved independent private steps while preserving required causal edges. | It swaps settlement before send, physical completion before permit, or drops a conflicting shared mutation as "stutter." | Trace alignment preserves causality, protected actions and admitted commutation rules. |
| A current B3 shared invalidation coexists with private E42/E43 work and affects only declared scopes. | E42's retired callback is relabeled shared, or a shared coordinator is omitted from the isolation model. | Permit legitimate shared effects without letting private callbacks launder authority. |
| E42 and E43 compete for one target; a qualified supersession policy revokes old rights and preserves newer installed content. | Distinct IDs are treated as proof of physical independence while an old queued effect mutates the successor. | Isolation requires actual target arbitration and last-actuation checks. |
| The same plan and inputs produce identical semantic/effect traces with and without a bounded read-only observer. | The observer changes a branch, throws into the semantic transition or hides a physical fault after buffer overflow. | Observer noninterference and honest trace loss are independently verified. |
| An artifact-bound concrete Choreo witness passes its real checker, and a separately sourced host/backend trace supplies the required physical premises. | The artifact witness alone is called universal browser refinement or the extractor fabricates the expected host actions. | State witness-local conclusion and independent physical/source proof obligations; no circular certification. |

Part VII must close the
deployed application inventory
and installed entrypoints;
Part VIII requires positive
HumanHelp Create/Claim/Reassign,
creator-local and one-Refresh
behaviors through actual
model/browser effects.
Parts IX–X specify the exact
checker, proof-kernel, source
and physical correspondence
premises. This section
defines their joins; the
correspondence checks and
trust assumptions must be
discharged for each claimed
supported realization.
** Browser realization invariants and conformance

*** Authoritative installation and resource invariants

Part VI closes the browser realization contract by stating what the
*actual admitted implementation* must preserve under every relevant
event, source, owner, target and failure class. An invariant about one
portable transition is not automatically an invariant of an external
HTMX callback, an opaque effect handler, XTDB transaction, third-party
DOM writer or installed deployment. Each stronger statement requires
the corresponding realization or independently accepted assumption.

The executable browser semantics owns current coordination, local
Choreo progression, abstract effect issuance and admission. The shell
interprets those effects through registered physical handlers and
normalizes actual host events back into the same semantic state owner.
The actual protected actions remain subject to their supported
physical gates. Trusted business operations and authoritative
observations remain separate model/backend concerns. Diagnostics
and assurance artifacts may explain this process, but do not decide
which transition production executes.

**** Installation and adoption invariants

For every admitted authoritative *presence or absence*
installation, the following propositions must be maintained
under the declared observation, host and authority contracts:

| Invariant family | Required property |
|------------------+-------------------|
| Source and disclosure | The observation is qualified for the actual principal/authority context, applied query, entity or collection, fields, temporal meaning, coverage and provider progression. |
| Exact representation | The prepared content and generated operation bindings correspond to that observation, the permitted render contract and relevant executable/protocol identity. |
| Permit and current target | The runtime issued a current permit for the exact effect, owner, physical target incarnation(s) and entire mutation footprint, including admitted OOB/secondary effects. |
| Last-actuation control | Each protected physical mutation remains permitted at the last controllable act; deferred or reentrant work cannot use a revoked permit to mutate a successor. |
| Physical result | Completion records an actual correlated target-specific postcondition; partial, failed, absent or unknown physical results are not promoted to full success. |
| Scoped adoption | Acquired, installed and adopted facts are recorded only for actually covered and completed scopes; an entity card does not certify a whole board cohort. |
| Obligation discharge | Only advisory, gap, acquisition, installation or recovery obligations whose separately declared satisfaction conditions now hold are discharged. |
| Nonregression | Older board R cannot silently erase a separately newer justified card S; an old provisional snapshot cannot overwrite newer authority. |
| Negative knowledge | A removal follows a complete covered membership observation or qualified exclusion, not a missing page, selector, redacted field or denied read. |
| Independent command truth | Neither browser installation nor local timeout changes a historical command's trusted incorporation/rejection evidence. |

An acquired fact can be valid while its installation is
pending or failed. A physical card can be correctly removed
while an unrelated counter/OOB target fails, leaving only
its own completed scope adopted. A current authorized
RequestAssignment observation can coexist with a previous
historically successful Claim and later manager Reassign;
the current card does not rewrite the earlier command
outcome. A checked no-op removal counts as physical
completion only if a current qualified postcondition
covers that exact representation and owner.

The provider's progression relation, not basis-string
arithmetic, determines whether an observation supersedes
previously adopted data. Different authorized cohorts
and independently installed cards may coexist only under
a declared scope-aware merge/reacquisition policy.
A mixed view is not evidence of a fictitious single
XTDB snapshot.

**** Resource, retirement and recovery invariants

Every live semantic resource is owned by one current
execution/coordinator/recovery scope or an explicit
shared-ownership class. Physical handles may remain
opaque, but the semantic issue ID, generation and
exact owner binding are established before host issue
and retained through callbacks. A late host handle
returned after retirement is cleaned up under its
retired issue; it cannot be installed into the
successor's live registry.

For an execution E that has *semantically retired*,
the central R4 property remains:

#+begin_quote
No subsequently delivered execution-private callback or
deferred effect may use E's revoked rights to advance
current semantic state, alter current protected presentation
or assume ownership of a successor's physical resource,
regardless of whether E's physical cancellation succeeded.
Separately admitted shared coordinator and historical
command-resolution work retains only its own rights.
#+end_quote

This property does not mean physical resource cleanup is
instantaneous, perfect or free. Failed aborts, retained
listeners, delayed timer callbacks, stale layout captures
and partial DOM effects are bounded/observable cleanup
and repair obligations. Physical cancellation is an
optimization and resource-management mechanism, while
semantic revocation plus last-actuation prevention
supplies the protected safety property.

A resource cleanup operation is idempotent for *its
issued resource instance*, not for whatever now
uses the same registry key, timer number, DOM selector
or CSS value. A newer owner writing the same
=min-height= value is not proof that the old owner
may restore the style. Where the host lacks an
adequate isolation primitive, the realization must
supply owner-aware arbitration, a genuine exclusive
lease, an admitted weak guarantee or an unsupported
profile rejection.

An unresolved command's lifetime can exceed the
execution that submitted it. Its immutable command
binding, trusted resolver, deduplication contract,
retention and disclosure rules must survive the
specified failure domain where recovery is promised.
The system cannot infer =:rejected= from timeout,
browser retirement or absent current card; it
cannot infer =:committed= from HTTP 200 or
a similar-looking current entity. Unknown
incorporation and currently acquired/adopted
model state remain separate.

The fragment coordinator has at most the
declared number of active logical cycles
and coalesced scheduling slots. That bound
does not cap unbounded incomparable
requirements, pending physical attempts,
stale handles or retained command history.
Every category has its own sound
compaction, retention, backpressure,
reset or explicit unavailable policy.

**** Event/source and runtime safety invariants

Every semantic event is normalized through its
actual registered source and admitted for its
declared owner class, current resource, issued
effect, generation, legal machine state and
duplicate/replay contract. A stale private
callback cannot relabel itself as shared.
A legitimate current SSE advisory may affect
a shared coordinator after the initiating
execution retires; the event must still
respect subscription interest and authority
scope.

A physical delivery ID consumed upon
source observation stays consumed if an
initially illegal receive later becomes
legal. Conversely an independently
qualified historical command resolver
result is not discarded just because
an old transport attempt used the same
semantic command ID. Transport H1,
command C42, effect/target incarnation,
subscription interest and trusted
model observation are not interchangeable
identity classes.

The runtime installs selected next
semantic state before interpreting
effects. Immediate nested callbacks
see current state, and all later
effects in the outer batch check their
own still-current physical permit.
An error or missing mandatory handler
fails at its actual boundary; neither
observer nor optional diagnostic is
permitted to fabricate a successful
semantic effect.

The supported HTMX/asset profile must
identify genuinely effective synchronous
gates for protected sends and
mutations. A handler that logs failure
after HTMX has already performed an
unauthorized swap is not conformance.
If no supported gate exists, choose
another qualified realization or
reject that managed combination.

*** Adversarial-browser authority boundary

The protected server is exposed to arbitrary client behavior.
An adversary may bypass the generated application, alter
=hx-*=  attributes and hidden inputs, forge plan/permit
maps, replay command IDs, invoke endpoints directly,
change its DOM, retain earlier received content, emit
syntactically valid request bytes or choose unexpected
ordering and multiplicity. A correct honest browser
adapter is an implementation-quality guarantee; it is
not a security boundary that the server may trust.

Under the named authentication, model, XTDB,
cryptographic and deployment premises, the trusted
boundary must enforce at least:

- **Principal derivation:** identify the authenticated
  actor using trusted credentials/session state, not
  browser-supplied role, Organization, Membership,
  permission or plan annotations.
- **Current guarded transitions:** validate typed
  operation/argument bindings and required current
  Request, active primary RequestAssignment,
  Membership and Organization facts at the
  transaction's authoritative conflict boundary.
  A pre-read is not an atomic guard.
- **Original-command binding:** qualify immutable
  command IDs, actor/operation/schema and canonical
  arguments, deduplication, compatible replay
  and allowed retention; a copied ID cannot
  confer command rights or mask changed inputs.
- **Read and Live disclosure:** authenticate every
  protected entity/collection read and subscription,
  with current scope, tenant and source/interest
  admission. Result readback may require *current*
  disclosure permission even for historically
  incorporated commands.
- **Provider evidence:** issue or qualify the
  command, observation, collection absence,
  scope and progression assertions actually
  justified by trusted model/backend operation.
- **Failure and privacy:** distinguish inaccessible
  from absent, and unknown from rejected, without
  leaking nondisclosable existence or claiming
  secrecy can be retroactively restored after
  an adversarial client has saved data.
- **Physical interpretation boundary:** client
  certificates, rendered affordances and
  DOM installation permits never replace
  trusted operation authorization, regardless
  of any browser-side assurance success.

The strong theorem, for its admitted server
transition relation, is that no arbitrary
syntactically representable client message
can cause an unauthorized domain transition,
protected disclosure or subscription merely
by inventing browser-side proof/correlation
metadata. The precise theorem must name
authentication, model authorization,
transaction atomicity, consistency,
request schema and output-disclosure
assumptions. A framework cannot certify
arbitrary opaque model side effects merely
by testing its HTTP dispatcher.

Client content safety and browser permissions
are separate: even an authenticated authoritative
observation may contain unsafe interpolated user
content. Escaping, script/extension handling,
response headers, OOB targets and active
HTML policy follow the qualified 06.03
rendering/transport contract. An adversarial
client may modify its own DOM, so the server
security argument does not assert that
hostile-client presentation stays honest.

An invalid endpoint check should not prevent
the *positive* authorized operation from
working. HumanHelp's independent acceptance
therefore exercises real eligible Create,
Claim, Unclaim, Done, Cancel and manager
Reassign as their actual production model
rules allow, plus negative competing-Claim,
revoked-Membership and cross-tenant attempts.
Rejecting all submissions, including
authorized ones, is not product conformance.

*** Required conformance scenarios

The finished conformance program combines portable
transition/property checks, application construction/
preflight checks, exact finite or stronger semantic
proofs where applicable, trace/source correspondence,
real browser/HTMX physical tests, trusted backend
operation tests, and multi-node/recovery tests for
supported profiles. Each layer states its actual
test subject, assumptions and nonclaims.

For each required safety property, the suite uses
an *eligible positive control* that demonstrably
reaches the tested physical/model boundary and a
nearby adverse case that reaches the same boundary
with the decisive premise changed. A test that
rejects every action because no handler was
installed, no authenticated user exists, or no
network response can be obtained is not a valid
positive conformance test.

| Test area | Eligible positive witness | Adverse/uncertain witness and required result |
|-----------+---------------------------+----------------------------------------------|
| Synchronous HTMX gate | An authorized bound request/swap executes once using a qualified cancellable profile. | Stale or unprojected request reaches the effective gate and is stopped *before* send/mutation; no silent raw fallback. |
| Main, OOB and response-driven effects | Authorized complete multi-target footprint installs with checked postconditions. | =hx-swap="none"=, retargeting, headers, script or unpermitted OOB effects are prevented or the unsupported profile is rejected. |
| Physical issue and callback reentrancy | An issued timer/local effect can complete synchronously, correlated to committed semantic state. | It retires before its host handle returns; the late handle is released and later outer-batch effects remain gated. |
| Wrong-target and partial DOM effects | Current B2/observation permit physically installs its prepared representation. | Stale B1 callback or failed second target cannot mutate B2 or claim a complete board. |
| Optional continuity and ownership | Valid focus/draft/height restoration runs for its current capture and target. | Old same-value CSS cleanup or delayed RAF cannot clobber a newer owner; optional failure does not annul canonical adoption. |
| Valid command and timeout | Eligible C42 Claim reaches trusted RequestAssignment write and correct bound result. | H1 timeout/lost response remains unknown without trusted rejection; H2 cannot duplicate or reinterpret C42. |
| Independent model authority | Current authorized Request, actor/Organization and active primary assignment guard succeeds. | Competing helper, revoked Membership, cross-tenant/client-forged tags fail at trusted guarded operation, not by hiding the button. |
| Current card versus command history | A historical successful Claim and newer Reassign both have qualified evidence; the newest authorized card installs. | Old optimistic settlement cannot restore prior helper or relabel the earlier Claim rejected. |
| Qualified negative membership | Complete Qopen or explicit exclusion proves R17 absent, and current target removal completes. | Partial page omission, unauthorized read or missing DOM selector never proves global deletion or adopted board absence. |
| One explicitly granted Refresh | Bob's current Q read occurs exactly once, installs covered O1/O2 state and retains separately newer S card. | Advisory alone or queued successor does not issue A2; uncovered, failed or incomparable debt remains. |
| Initial subscription and reconnect | Baseline/interest fence or qualified replay/current reacquisition covers missed W and establishes the declared continuity. | Stream silence, router redelivery lacking never-generated W or lifecycle wakeup alone cannot claim no gap. |
| Query, principal or plan change | Current Q2 and supported P8/asset/host combination admit new owner with authorized disclosure. | Old Q1/P7 callback or stale principal rights cannot install/disclose; unresolved command survives separately as promised. |
| Registration and resource cleanup | Current effect/interest registrations are exact and cleanup releases only their own physical instances. | Throwing abort or reused timer/selector retains bounded cleanup debt but cannot revive old semantic rights. |
| Duplicates, early messages and conflicting outcomes | A legal delivery is consumed once and an identical qualified repeat follows declared idempotence. | Early M1 cannot be replayed later; conflicting same-ID evidence produces a typed fault/reconciliation. |
| Authoritative acquisition and installation | Qualified provider response and real target postcondition advance only their actual scopes. | HTTP 200, copied basis witness or generic afterSwap cannot manufacture full-board adoption. |
| Actual trace and global refinement | Role-local, sender/delivery/global schedule and independently sourced physical/model witnesses align for the claimed concrete subject. | Candidate-only receive, synthetic send, omitted OOB mutation or ambiguous identity cannot pass a stronger global certificate. |
| Diagnostics and proof noninterference | Same canonical plan and inputs execute identically with a bounded observer present/absent. | Throwing/corrupt/overfull instrumentation cannot change branches, hide losses or grant admission. |
| Capacity and liveness | Under stated quiescence, grant, fairness and availability, an eligible user acquires and adopts the required scope. | Permanent denial, exhausted read budget or overflow does not justify unconditional convergence; resource loss gets explicit safe disposition. |
| Hostile client | An eligible authenticated operation succeeds with correct model result and authorized disclosure. | Arbitrary request bytes, forged certificates/permits and changed actor/argument claims cannot cause unauthorized effects. |
| Release and application closure | Every actual admitted route, browser asset, handler, worker, subscription and positive HumanHelp path is covered by the installed assembly/profile. | Unknown alternate renderer, extension writer, old service worker or unchecked route prevents the stronger whole-application claim. |

Coverage generation varies message order, request and
callback delay, nested completion, physical cancellation
failure, OOB partial mutation, owner/resource reuse,
read and write races, provider incomparability,
query/tenant transitions, duplicate delivery,
network partition and durable recovery expiry.
It must not assume a single convenient concrete
integer instance for an unbounded identity property.
No test fixture may simply return the *desired*
progression token, attest nonexistent physical
completion or self-report a trusted backend
result as its own evidence.

A good finite test suite can establish a range
of actual executions under a precise host
profile and fail on real mismatches. It cannot
turn tested traces into a quantified inductive
theorem. An exact finite model checker can
establish its enumerated subject and
assumptions, while a source/physical
correspondence check must additionally bind
those model events to the *real* installed
code and external transaction/host behavior.
A stronger claim requires an independent
proof or justified abstraction and the
identified trust premises.

Conformance evidence identifies the exact
loaded runtime/library/configuration,
application/deployment assembly, backend
provider, renderer and physical handlers,
observed source/extractor, relevant tests,
known failures, unsupported paths and
assumptions. Replacing a dependency or
enabling a new HTMX extension may invalidate
the profile: nominal version compatibility
alone does not qualify a newly exposed DOM
writer. Unsupported protected paths are
rejected or explicitly accepted only under
a weaker named guarantee, never quietly
included in a strong certificate.

*** Assembly obligations and the browser realization invariant

The application constructor must account for
the actual managed paths it emits and serves,
not just a sample Hiccup function or one
favorable demonstration route. A closed
application inspection relates:

| Assembly obligation | Required closure |
|---------------------+------------------|
| Semantic operations | Model-owned operation definitions, roles, typed arguments, current guards, authoritative transaction/readback and eligible user paths. |
| Executable projection | The exact Choreo plan/operation/observation mapping, installed interpreter, semantic preflight and known dynamic recovery branches. |
| HTTP and rendering | All relevant Ring/Biff/HTMX routes, response modes, alternate writers, templates, fragment roots, target/operation bindings and content safety policy. |
| Browser startup and assets | Actual entrypoints, compiled CLJS/JS modules, handler registrations, HTMX/extensions, service workers, cache/deployment compatibility and lifecycle gates. |
| Physical resources | Timer/transport/continuity/optimism handlers, source registrations, exact target/owner incarnation, last-actuation gate, partial effects and cleanup policy. |
| Live/coordinator | Interest/subscription lifecycle, baseline/gap fence, applied query/grant policy, obligation retention, progression and actual adopted installation. |
| Recovery | Incompatible plan retirement, surviving command intent/resolver, unknown-result handling, current disclosure, capacity and unavailable/manual alternatives. |
| Assurance subject | Invariants, exact finite model subject or stronger proof, actual source/executor/physical evidence, kernel/checker scope, known trust premises and deployment version binding. |

The construction pipeline may use Clojure's
full language and opaque application effects,
but it must require the admitted contract
for the effects and relationships that
its guarantees rely upon. It need not
statically predict future XTDB values,
network delivery, DOM disappearance,
which actor wins a competing Claim,
or whether a target becomes inaccessible.
It must, however, reject a missing
mandatory operation/effect realization,
inconsistent source or route binding,
known unsupported protected host gate,
invalid plan/protocol relation, or
dynamic condition with no declared
safe failure/recovery path when that
path is required by the selected guarantee.

Preflight and deployed runtime have
different jobs. Static admission
establishes the complete declared
construction, supported profile
and required recovery contracts.
Runtime admission checks the
current principal, context, owner,
source, applicable progression,
target and effect at the actual
boundary. Physical tests and
trusted provider witnesses establish
remaining observable facts where
the stated assurance requires them.
A successful static report alone
does not justify executing against
a changed runtime, or assert that
a browser's actual DOM changed.

No silent downgrade is admitted
for a protected managed affordance.
If the selected projection,
preflight, handler registration,
qualified HTMX hook or trusted
operation route is unavailable,
the application must fail at
the appropriate construction,
startup or runtime boundary,
not submit an unprotected
command while reporting that
the managed flow was enforced.
Ordinary explicitly declared
raw HTMX interactions remain
supported under their own
complete server authorization
and rendering contracts.

**** Unified Part VI invariant

#+begin_quote
For every admitted managed browser action, the actual
application has one selected executable semantic meaning
and a current qualified owner, source, plan, effect and
authority/observation scope. Its physical realization is
declared for the installed host profile, and every
protected act is prevented unless the applicable
current permit remains valid at its controllable
mutation/send boundary. All reported consequences
are attributed to the actual issued work and suitably
independent source/physical evidence. A request or
trusted command result is not by itself completed
DOM installation; acquired authority is adopted only
for its genuinely covered and physically completed
scope. Stale owner and provisional restoration rights
expire before best-effort cleanup, without cancelling
independently surviving command-resolution or Live
obligations. Failed, partial, absent and unknown
evidence remains distinct from trusted incorporation
or rejection, and neither opaque basis arithmetic nor
uncontrolled response effects may invent progression.
Current trusted authorization remains mandatory even
if an adversarial client ignores the browser entirely.
Logical concurrency, physical resources, obligation
retention and conditional liveness obey their own
declared bounds and environmental premises.
#+end_quote

This is a *normative invariant of the finished
supported realization*. Its applicability is
established through independently checked
obligations at the semantic, construction,
trusted model, physical host, subscription
and deployment layers.
A real deployment claim must report
which ones are discharged and which
remain conditional, unknown or
unsupported.

**** Whole-part reconciliation and independent acceptance remain distinct

Completing the fifteen numbered Part VI
sectional reviews is a necessary editorial
milestone, not automatically accepted
whole-part architecture or proof. The
next reconciliation explicitly checks:

- consistent identity and terminology
  for command C42, execution E42,
  physical H1/H2 attempts, effect,
  representation, target incarnation,
  coordinator, grant, authority
  context and deployed artifact;
- consistent transitions from source
  admission to physical last-actuation,
  qualified acquisition, installation,
  adoption and unmet debt;
- absence of contradictory HTMX
  control, OOB/response-effect,
  refresh/single-flight or
  shared-subscription claims;
- actual recovery/retirement
  ownership across 06.08–06.11,
  including durable command
  promises and resource bounds;
- R4 preservation coverage without
  accidentally restoring
  superseded illustrative APIs;
- Parts IV–V and VII–XII joins,
  especially HumanHelp positive
  product behavior, real installed
  application closure, provider
  correspondence and precise
  formal proof subjects;
- source/publication assembly,
  cross-part Org references,
  stable anchors, examples,
  trust-premise consistency,
  conformance matrix and
  explicitly unfinished
  implementation requirements.

An independent candidate-acceptance
review then evaluates the *whole*
reconciled Part VI, including whether
the specified abstractions are
compatible and sufficient for the
finished-system target. Only that
later decision should mark Part VI
accepted. It is not obtained merely
by counting reviewed files or
successfully concatenating them.
* Part VII — Whole-application construction
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: part-07-whole-application-construction
:PART_REVISION: 07-20261108
:END:

This part specifies how one source-owned application definition becomes an
admitted construction and an actual serving application. It joins executable
Choreo projections, trusted model operations, Clojure/ClojureScript handlers,
server routes, generated browser assets, rendered controls, Live interests,
authoritative acquisition, recovery, and the physical lifecycle. Parts I–VI
define the meaning and ownership of those components; Part VII establishes
that the required *connecting edges* are present and are enforced in the
realization that actually runs. Parts IX–X provide the stronger proof and
implementation-correspondence arguments and preserve their evidence scope.

Gesso applications retain ordinary Clojure, ClojureScript, server rendering,
HTMX, and application-specific effects. The framework does not require all
business logic to be written in a formal language or every local operation to
use Choreo. Instead, construction identifies the interfaces, effects,
producers, consumers, runtime dependencies, trusted premises, and observable
boundaries on which each selected guarantee relies. A sound declaration of
an opaque effect remains a named contract or assumption until its relevant
implementation correspondence is established; calling it application code
does not make its effects disappear.

Examples use illustrative operation and assembly names. A valid-looking
inspection map, plan digest, source label or success report does not issue a
runtime permission or trusted transaction credential. Present execution
conditions, including the authenticated actor, current authorization, model
facts, resource incarnation and installation permit, are checked at their
proper runtime/model boundaries rather than inferred from construction.

** Whole-application realization and preflight closure
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: req-whole-application-closure
:END:

A valid choreography, model transaction, compiled browser plan or Ring route
can be correct in isolation while the combined application is broken. A
rendered Claim button may not emit its declared operation; its shipped plan
may be absent; a correct browser send may reach a different physical route;
the trusted route may lack its required execution provider; the command may
commit while no permitted authoritative acquisition or repair can establish
the resulting display. Each local component can pass its own tests.

*Whole-application closure* requires every effect and observation edge needed
by the selected application construction and assurance contract to have a
compatible, source-owned realization. This checks the composition of the
actual submitted application, not merely whether several independently
constructed registries look plausible. The supported construction is an
inspectable semantic/physical artifact with an identity, selected capabilities,
trusted premises, supported host/deployment profiles, and specific closure
and enforcement obligations.

Closure is *not* a second choreography. Choreo states which distributed
behaviors are admitted; projection derives executable role-local behavior;
application assembly establishes that each required concrete/browser/server
realization is supplied. A route cannot legalize an invalid Choreo trajectory,
and a valid plan cannot manufacture a missing route, model operation,
subscription or generated asset.

The required edges depend on the kind of work:

| Admitted application behavior | Realization that must be closed | Edges that are not invented |
|-------------------------------+---------------------------------+-----------------------------|
| Managed browser command such as Request Claim | Rendered affordance, projected plan, loaded browser/HTMX host, issued send, trusted method/route, guarded model operation, qualified outcome, acquisition and adopted presentation or declared recovery. | A fictitious global exact-once transport guarantee or a second runtime semantic interpreter. |
| Server-owned operation or background task | Registered event/worker, trusted operation and providers, applicable publication, durable intent/retry and readback or error policy under its own owner. | A browser plan and button for a task with no browser role. |
| Ordinary read-only HTMX or search route | Actual HTTP/read source, current disclosure authorization, declared query/coverage, rendered response/target and relevant Live or cache obligations. | A Choreo command solely because HTML is swapped. |
| Local draft/filter/focus interaction | Current local state owner, presentation and continuity permissions, effective physical effects, expiry and privacy boundaries. | A database transaction solely because the user types or changes a local filter. |
| Explicit ordinary mutating endpoint | Its declared model writer, authenticated input and current transaction guard, output/disclosure, invalidation and effect coverage. | Automatic exemption from invariants because the endpoint has no Choreo annotation. |

No semantic metadata is required on irrelevant static assets. However, a
managed route or physical writer whose effects can invalidate an invariant
must belong to that invariant's coverage argument or remain an explicitly
trusted and bounded environment premise. The application cannot claim
whole-writer safety while a reachable unaccounted raw route changes the
same RequestAssignment state behind its guarded Claim.

*** Three application claims remain independent

The authoritative [[#req-application-assurance-claims][Part I application-assurance claims]]
retain distinct evidence subjects:

| Claim | Required positive evidence | What the claim does not establish |
|-------+----------------------------+-----------------------------------|
| Declared structural closure | Every required operation, route, source, artifact, capability, observation, effect and recovery edge in the *declared application scope* has a compatible current binding; unsupported requirements are rejected or retain an explicitly allowed weaker profile. | That omitted business capabilities were intended or implemented; that arbitrary Clojure render states were statically enumerated. |
| Actual production enforcement | Real installed handler/startup paths, issued transport and renderer/HTML/HTMX boundaries perform the required checks *before* their protected send, trusted operation or response; the served/loaded asset and declared host are the ones checked. | The correctness of all future authority facts or an unobserved deployment merely because an assembly report passed. |
| Independent behavioral completeness | Eligible users can perform the required product operations using actual controls, trusted model effects, permitted acquisitions and physically installed results; nearby adverse and recovery cases also exercise those paths. | A universal proof of every execution from one positive browser example, or success when the relevant capability was intentionally disabled. |

The three claims can be simultaneously true, false or not yet established
in different combinations. A closed application can omit a required manager
Reassign control. Production may bypass its checked response wrapper even
though the assembly was valid. A test may manufacture C42 by calling a
helper directly even when the real Claim control emits no command. These
are distinct failures and cannot be flattened into one =:verified?= flag.

Application construction always requires its selected mandatory structural
and real admission boundaries. Stronger proofs and finite-model campaigns
are selected by an explicit assurance policy, not silently necessary for
every ordinary use. Omitting an optional theorem cannot disable required
route, actor, artifact, source or physical checks. Selecting an ambitious
proof does not make a disconnected checker an enforcing gate; only an
actual installed, correctly scoped boundary supplies enforcement.

*** Ownership of whole-Part-VII cross-section obligations

The Claim, Live and XTDB examples recur because they cross independently
checked boundaries, not because each section declares another model,
registry or policy. These sections own different *relations*:

| Section(s) | Primary whole-application obligation |
|------------+--------------------------------------|
| 07.01–07.03 | Application scope, source-owned assembly, typed closure and evidence graph. |
| 07.04 | Assurance policy, operation/exercise and physical writer coverage. |
| 07.05–07.07 | Actual trusted route/executor, built and served browser assets, effective rendered HTML/HTMX. |
| 07.08–07.09 | Command-specific settlement, Live/progression and required recovery handling. |
| 07.10–07.11 | Installed Biff lifecycle, actual serving adoption and physical fault-injection evidence. |
| 07.12–07.13 | Source-owned semantic audit, non-authoritative diagnostics and source-local repair. |
| 07.14 | Independent positive product acceptance and backend/evidence change qualification. |
| 07.15 | Qualified end-state security invariant and trusted authority boundary. |

Part I owns the application-assurance claims, Parts II–III model/Choreo
semantics, Part IV authoritative guarded transactions and command truth,
Parts V–VI browser realization and physical continuation. Part VIII owns
HumanHelp positive user acceptance; Parts IX–XII own stronger proof,
physical refinement, multi-node deployment and release obligations.
Part VII does not create duplicate semantic or proof authorities.

Complete *declared* operation coverage, independent promised product
capabilities and actual protected writer/deployment completeness are
three different inventories. The absence of an unknown raw writer
cannot be proved by an empty declared registry; a selected weaker
assurance profile cannot silently delete a known protected effect
or manager Reassign promised by the independent product profile.

*** Coverage follows effects, not the presence of Choreo metadata

Coverage is relative to the properties, security and product claims made.
The assembly identifies the admitted ingress, egress and state-changing
effects through actual HTTP routes, model functions, background work,
queues, scheduled tasks, administration, imports, initialization,
migrations, Live publication, external systems and browser/local writers
that may affect those claims.

An ordinary search endpoint can be the declared current authoritative
acquisition for a board without being a command choreography. A preference
update can use a simple guarded model operation. An explicitly raw HTMX
endpoint may remain legitimate under its own complete authorization and
effects contract. None obtains a silent right to bypass a selected
whole-application invariant because it lacks =:choreo/op= metadata.

A sound assembly represents *known writers*, their model-affecting
footprints, operation and route identities, required providers, publication
and observation obligations, and any explicitly scoped external writers.
Declared coverage is not a proof that a dynamically loaded plugin,
unobserved scheduler, hidden route or unbounded external system is absent.
Where discovery is incomplete, the report must distinguish an *unknown*
inventory from an actually enumerated empty one. A stronger closed-world
claim may require controlled registration, an enforced runtime boundary,
independent deployment inspection or an explicitly qualified assumption.

The closure graph has positive obligations for commands that succeed:
trusted incorporation must have the declared settlement, affected-scope,
publication, acquisition, adoption or repair path. Live interest without
a permitted first acquisition cannot establish a current initial view;
Live invalidation without a supported registration-gap recovery cannot
promise complete continuity. A command path that is perfectly guarded yet
always lacks its provider, or an entire screen that can never adopt its
observation, is not a realized product capability.

*** Construction-time knowledge and current-world authority

The finished assembly validates every requirement whose meaning and
inputs are available at construction, build, preflight or installation.
For example, it can check a declared missing plan, absent trusted route,
incompatible method/template, unsupplied required provider, stale browser
artifact/receipt, ambiguous physical realization, uncovered output,
unregistered source or undeclared recovery branch without waiting for a
real user to encounter the defect.

Some properties cannot be decided when the application is assembled:
the eventual Claim winner, the current principal, RequestAssignment
eligibility at transaction time, the outcome of an uncertain send,
the arrival of an SSE advisory, or the physical existence of a target
after another execution supersedes it. Each belongs to its current
trusted or physical admission boundary. A dynamic condition is acceptable
only where a specified enforcement and recovery/rejection path handles
it; it is not permission to replace a protected action with raw HTMX.

A production path is considered enforced only while the checked
construction is still the one being used. The checked callable must
be the installed callable, the verified asset must be served/loaded,
and the actual response must pass the required pre-serialization
or protected physical gate. Rebuild, handler replacement, route
override, alternate response encoding, stale service worker and
third-party extension paths must be closed by the qualified deployment
or remain named unsupported/assumed profiles. Successful compilation
or a copy of the expected report is not proof of these installed facts.

An application with arbitrary Clojure rendering cannot claim that a
finite catalog of sample Hiccup values enumerates every future
conditional control. It can still admit a current route/operation
backbone and enforce the required Choreo/physical request check
at every *actual canonical render*. Other response producers
need their own guard, an enforced shared serving boundary or
a weaker explicitly scoped claim. The absence of an observed
unauthorized control in a small snapshot is not completeness evidence.

*** Assurance vocabulary describes the checked proposition

The report retains what was checked, for whom, where, under which
version/coverage and what remains conditional. Useful distinctions
include:

| Evidence state | Interpretation |
|----------------+----------------|
| =preflight-closed= or =assembly-verified= | A specified declarative graph/construction was checked for its listed obligations at an identified current assembly and artifact identity. |
| =production-enforced= | Evidence ties the actual installed handler, physical effect, route or output boundary to the selected required check in the stated profile. |
| =runtime/model-enforced= | Present authentication, authorization and guarded model transitions are checked by their trusted current sources, not by a browser assertion. |
| =behaviorally-demonstrated= | An eligible end-to-end product case exercised real user, backend, transport and presentation paths within the stated test/environment limits. |
| =formally-proved= or =finite-checked= | Only the precisely defined theorem or finite model subject and its assumptions are discharged; neither term is a synonym for deployment correctness. |
| =inconclusive=, =unsupported= or =open= | A required premise is not established, the selected realization is unsupported or more evidence is needed; none is silently rewritten as success. |
| =contradicted= (evidence) | A grounded observation contradicts the exact proposition; it is not automatically a rejected domain command. |
| =rejected= (admission) | The candidate or invocation is blocked at its applicable construction/enforcement gate; distinct from Part IV's authoritative =:rejected= command outcome. |

For instance, one application report may state that Choreo semantics
are proved for a named finite/symbolic subject, the browser artifact
correspondence is assembly-verified, the authenticated principal
is runtime-enforced, and actual HTMX behavior is covered by tested
host assumptions. It must not summarize those subjects as a single
unqualified "verified Gesso application." A diagnostic label,
digest or report has no power to authorize a business transition.

*** R4 preservation: broken compositions and positive controls

The following adjacent histories describe eligibility *and*
the failure mechanism. They are not merely tests that all requests
can be rejected:

| Eligible application history | Broken composition or adverse history | Required construction/enforcement conclusion |
|------------------------------+---------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------|
| A rendered authorized Request Claim control has a bound plan, shipped current runtime and trusted POST route. | The view emits the same POST without its managed operation identity, or the plan is absent. | Fail before protected send/HTML delivery under the relevant supported boundary; do not silently downgrade. |
| The current generated browser asset and receipt match the installed assembly and selected host profile. | A stale browser bundle, alternate script entrypoint or service worker supplies an incompatible plan after preflight. | Construction/build or actual serving/currentness gate rejects the stale realization. |
| A guarded Claim route has the required authenticated principal, clock/transaction provider and model-owned operation. | A missing =:biff.fx/now= or otherwise required execution provider becomes apparent only on click despite a knowable missing binding. | Reject the missing declared capability early; runtime still checks genuinely dynamic provider validity. |
| A qualified C42 incorporation produces covered publication/acquisition and physically adopted card or honest repair. | The command commits, but no permissible authoritative acquisition or installation path exists. | Reject the structurally missing continuation or declare an explicit recovery/blocked path; never fabricate adoption. |
| An initialized Live interest has a permitted baseline and reconnect/interest-fence recovery. | A board subscribes only to future invalidations but has no initial knowledge or permitted read. | Do not claim initial/current Live agreement; close the initial acquisition or expose the weaker contract. |
| A canonical guarded Biff/HTML path validates the actual rendered control before serialization. | A later handler replacement or hand-built serialized Ring response bypasses that guard while an app claims universal response coverage. | Actual installation/served-route enforcement must cover the alternate path or explicitly narrow the guarantee. |
| An ordinary read/search HTMX endpoint is correctly authorized and responds as an ordinary route. | The same raw route mutates protected RequestAssignment state outside the claimed writer inventory. | Preserve ordinary HTMX as a supported mode; account for its real write effects and transaction guard. |
| A manager uses an eligible real Reassign control; another helper's competing Claim is rejected at the trusted model boundary. | Tests build a coherent shadow registry or submit synthetic commands although the production Reassign button is absent. | Distinguish production assembly from test surrogates and require independent positive product acceptance. |
| The assembly accounts for named background, scheduled, migration and administration writers affecting Request state. | A known external writer is omitted so a formally checked operation invariant ignores its reachable transitions. | State explicit source coverage, trusted external contract or an honest weaker claim; do not hide the writer. |
| An application enables stronger finite/proof assurance with its own checked subject and runtime gates intact. | The checker is not connected to the admitted artifact, or a finite pass is used as proof that all routes and browsers are correct. | Retain source-bound assurance scope and actual enforcement; neither proof presence nor absence changes runtime semantic authority. |

Part VII's later sections specify the ApplicationAssembly shape,
closure graph, concrete routes, renderer, artifact manifest, Live
and recovery mechanics, lifecycle and diagnostic surfaces. This
opening section establishes the admission *scope* and its three
independent success conditions; it does not provide a second
implementation of those later checkers.

Part VIII must exercise nonvacuous positive HumanHelp Create, Claim,
Reassign, Done/Cancel, creator-local presentation, remote advisory with
exactly one explicitly granted Refresh, and local search/selection/
scroll continuity as appropriate to the selected product contract.
Parts IX–X must relate admitted declarative edges and physical
occurrences to their actual formal and implementation evidence.
** Application definition and ApplicationAssembly
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: req-application-assembly
:END:

One source-owned application definition composes the declarations that their real
owners export. Its normalized realization is the conceptual
=ApplicationAssembly=. It is a graph of typed subjects, bindings, obligations,
and evidence, not a collection of unrelated success flags.

The public authoring surface should remain small. Source owners declare genuine
choices once; construction derives repeated identities and verifies independently
chosen physical correspondences. Applications should not maintain separate
operation registries for browser compilation, preflight, startup, rendering,
model checking, and tests.

*** Source ownership and derivation

| Source owner | Authored facts | Derived or checked products |
|--------------+----------------+-----------------------------|
| Domain/model module | Typed operation meaning, guards, dependencies, transitions, outcomes, command/recovery contract, opaque premises. | Model interfaces, candidate obligations, operation catalog, rule/audit views. |
| Choreography module | Distributed roles, permitted knowledge flow, coordination, local recovery choices. | Role-local plans and compiler correspondence. |
| View/component | Selected operation, concrete arguments/observations, presentation, availability choice. | Prepared action binding, effective transport annotation, render obligations. |
| Route/ingress module | Supported physical dispatch and input mapping. | Installed dispatcher, route index, selector-consistency checks. |
| Trusted execution adapter | Public model delegation and actual implementation/provider binding. | Issued callable, invocation gate, outcome encoder. |
| Acquisition/Live module | Projection/query scope, observation contract, subscription and refresh policy. | Acquisition bindings, coordinator requirements, advisory/recovery edges. |
| Runtime/build profile | Compiler/runtime, physical handlers, assets, supported host behavior. | Browser manifest, generated bootstrap, build receipt, qualification obligations. |
| Application composition | Selected modules, configuration, assurance policy, lifecycle/deployment profile. | One admitted application and its explanation. |

An exported declaration is not accepted solely because it came from a namespace
with the right name. Construction validates its semantic category and required
source/implementation correspondence. A raw declaration, an admitted operation,
an issued executor, and a copyable report can use similar host representations
without being interchangeable.

 
The application definition must also identify the *coverage of its source
inventory*: which declarations exhaust the selected deployment's known routes,
workers, scheduled writers, renderer producers, external effects, and extension
points; which are only sampled or discovered; and which remain unknown. A map
with no registered writer is not evidence that no relevant physical writer
exists. If a strong assurance policy depends on complete source or effect
coverage, incomplete inventory is an open or blocking obligation, not success.

Model semantics, physical route selection, provider selection, rendered
affordance selection and build/runtime installation are independently authored
choices. Construction derives facts that have one semantic owner, checks each
independent choice against that owner, and retains source provenance for
diagnostics and change invalidation. Matching strings or plausible metadata
must never convert a physical selection into semantic authority.

A schematic composition might be:

#+begin_src clojure
(defn application-definition [config]
  {:application/id :humanhelp/example
   :domains [request/definition
             organization/definition]
   :flows [request-flow/definition]
   :surfaces [request-card/definition request-board/definition]
   :ingress (routes/definitions config)
   :execution (server/execution-bindings config)
   :acquisitions (live/acquisition-definitions config)
   :providers (server/provider-bindings config)
   :browser-profile browser/profile
   :lifecycle (system/lifecycle-definition config)
   :assurance-policy assurance/managed-application-policy})
#+end_src

Each referenced module exports its actual owned declarations; the example does
not stand in for omitted definitions. The composition does not retype operation
IDs, argument schemas, settlement variants, or plan digests already determined by
those declarations. Independent physical route selection and provider selection
remain real choices that must be checked.

Tests instantiate this constructor with declared fixture configuration. They can
replace a clock or storage provider for a scoped test, but must identify that
substitution and avoid transferring its evidence to an unexamined production
provider. A hand-built shadow assembly is not production-closure evidence.

 
*** Worked Claim source-owner join

The following is schematic application composition. The referenced Vars and
the precise constructor spelling are illustrative, not claims about the
current public Gesso API. Each module exports its own actual declarations:

#+begin_src clojure
(defn claim-application [config]
  {:domains [request-model/definition organization-model/definition]
   :flows [request-choreo/definition]
   :surfaces [request-card/definition]
   :ingress (request-routes/definitions config)
   :execution (request-server/operation-bindings config)
   :acquisitions (request-live/definitions config)
   :providers (request-server/provider-bindings config)
   :browser-profile browser/profile
   :assurance-policy assurance/managed-application-policy})
#+end_src

For the =:request/claim= slice, construction checks the following distinct
facts instead of recopying one operation ID into six registries:

| Owner | Required relation and rejected near miss |
|-------+------------------------------------------|
| Request model/Choreo | The admitted Claim targets the current Request and RequestAssignment under trusted principal, Membership and Organization guards; a similarly named unchecked handler is not the same transition. |
| Request-card view | A real eligible control supplies the operation, typed Request argument and required observation/command binding; a disabled or absent control does not satisfy positive product acceptance. |
| HTTP route | Actual POST method, path template and decoded path Request match the command's Request target; a matching operation name with mismatched target is rejected. |
