| A real Chromium test exercises Claim, Unclaim, On-the-way, Complete, Cancel and Reassign with proper browser-generated commands. | Credit the scenarios actually observed, including committed reload and browser diagnostics; no claim of full distributed/fault/response-flow coverage or of test execution without a run. |

These scenarios keep the R4 user-facing test architecture:
unit model checks, Choreo projections, structural preflight,
effective rendered affordance, server integration and
real Chromium/HTMX product acceptance are distinct gates.
No test may create the real browser wire command for it
or treat a report map as authentication. Positive
cases must stay reachable while all negative cases
are correctly rejected or reconciled.

** Board projection and selective adoption
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: req-humanhelp-selective-adoption
:END:

The board separates authoritative truth from the information this browser has
adopted. A database change does not automatically change a user's visible board.
An advisory reports that the view may need attention; it is neither domain
content nor permission to fetch and install everything currently available.

The selected policy is prompt adoption of the user's own correlated results and
explicit Refresh for remote changes. Search, sorting, visibility options, and
ordinary details interaction operate on already adopted information. These
choices must be represented in application policy, not inferred from incidental
HTMX route or callback behavior.

*** Scope, cohort, and presentation

A board scope includes Organization, Location, authority context, projection
contract, temporal interpretation, and any declared collection bounds. Its
adopted cohort is the set of Request identities admitted into that scope, with
scoped observations and permitted display projections.

The default proving scope is one authorized Location and includes active and
terminal Requests within its declared collection bounds. Terminal visibility is
a presentation option. Reading only active Requests and later making “Show
terminal” issue a fresh collection query would violate that option's contract.

The profile declares finite response/retention limits. If a complete result
exceeds those limits, the server must return a typed scope-too-large result or
use an explicitly declared paging/window contract. Silent truncation cannot
justify complete membership or authoritative absence. A page covers its stated
window, not the whole Organization. Moving to another page or Location is a new
explicit acquisition intent, not a local sort operation.

Local text search and sort options do not change this authoritative collection
scope. They derive a visible subset and order from the cohort. A future remote
search feature must be labelled and specified as a different acquisition policy;
it cannot borrow the “local presentation only” guarantee.

The complete-board acquisition composes Request, assignment, and permitted User
display projections under the same qualified observation context. Repeated reads
against an advancing database are not silently treated as one snapshot. If an
integration deliberately combines observations, it preserves their separate
provenance and proves only the relationships that their evidence supports.
Current disclosure checks also remain distinct from the historical observation
being displayed.

 
*** Initial acquisition, truthful membership and counts

The first rendered =GET /app= obtains an admitted
initial Request cohort and permitted Request,
RequestAssignment and User projection. The
toolbar/list may be server-rendered, but a
fragment's token does not by itself prove
the other fragment has matching membership
or counts. Any relevant change between
initial read and subscription registration
requires a source-owned fence, replay or
authorized reacquisition. Merely connecting
SSE does not establish a no-gap baseline.

A complete cohort result has an exact
authenticated viewer, Organization/Location,
collection and terminal inclusion, projection
schema, temporal/query interpretation,
read basis, finite bounds and completeness
claim. Querying Requests, assignments and
User display fields through successive
reads against an advancing database does
not prove one atomic snapshot. Either
qualify their common context or retain
the distinct provenance of every subread.

Displayed =:total-count=, =:active-count=
and =:terminal-count= refer to this
adopted cohort (or explicitly narrower
adopted visible subset), not to the
current global database. Unsupported,
incomplete, unauthorized or truncated
collections must be marked as such:
empty results do not imply complete
authoritative absence. Disclosing an
old card still requires current
read permission, independent of the
basis at which it was first acquired.

*** State with distinct meanings

An inspection view of the board distinguishes the following records:

| Record | Meaning and owner |
|--------+-------------------|
| Board owner and scope | One active coordinator lifetime, authority context, and applied acquisition scope. |
| Adopted membership | Requests admitted by a complete scoped observation or a permitted selective membership rule. |
| Adopted observations | Per-card and collection evidence actually installed, with provenance and scope. |
| Advisory obligations | Information still requiring acquisition/adoption, including unresolved subscription continuity gaps. |
| Acquisition grant | User or policy permission for particular reads and installations, with scope, budget, and lifetime. |
| Active cycle | Registered request and installation resources with current ownership. |
| Local options and drafts | Search, ordering, visibility, expansion, focus, and bounded unsubmitted input. |
| Provisional overlays | Execution-owned speculative presentation, not authoritative observations. |
| Command recovery records | Unresolved command bindings and permitted reconciliation references that can outlive a card. |

These are not eight unrelated mutable registries. The executable semantic core
owns their transitions; physical adapters report observations and completions.
A presentation cache may store allowed fields, but it is not a second domain
model or a source of write authority.

 
*** Resource identity and admission of physical installation

The board owner, scoped cohort, fragment
resource instance, local option state,
each card's physical DOM instance,
issued acquisition, optimistic execution
and unresolved command each have
distinct identity and lifetime. The
same Request UUID does not make a
replaced DOM card the same active
instance; a delayed callback cannot
borrow the new instance's rights or
reapply a retired provisional marker.

For an observation to become adopted,
its trusted principal, permitted
scope and corresponding Request,
admitted progression/coverage,
current board/execution owner and
physical installation must all agree.
The physical swap must complete;
an HTTP 200 without installation
is not evidence of adoption.
A response prepared before a
newer justified local card update
cannot overwrite that card simply
because it arrived afterward.
Failed/cancelled swaps retain their
unfulfilled read/adoption obligation.

Local filter changes may preserve
focus, caret, scroll and compatible
open =<details>= state across a
managed HTMX replacement. Continuity
does not resurrect an expired
command, stale card owner or old
acquisition grant. A local Create
may admit exactly its correlated
new Request, while a local Claim
may update only its own qualified
card. Neither can claim whole-board
membership advancement through
the new result's later basis.

A schematic inspection value is:

#+begin_src clojure
{:board/owner-ref board-owner
 :board/scope-ref board-scope
 :board/authority-context-ref authority-context
 :membership/adopted-ref membership-evidence
 :cards/adopted-refs card-evidence-by-request
 :advisory/obligations pending-obligations
 :acquisition/grant-ref current-grant
 :acquisition/cycle-ref current-cycle
 :presentation/options {:search ""
                        :created-order :newest
                        :mine-first? false
                        :unclaimed-first? false
                        :show-terminal? false}
 :presentation/result-ref local-result
 :commands/unresolved-refs unresolved-commands}
#+end_src

The references name admitted runtime objects or inspection subjects. Constructing
this map cannot grant admission. In particular, replacing =membership-evidence=
with a newer card's basis does not make the cohort a newer complete snapshot.

*** A concrete HTMX-compatible realization

The primary realization keeps server-rendered cards and a small browser
presentation projection. An admitted observation supplies the card content and
the permitted fields needed for local search, stable sorting, terminal filtering,
and continuity. Local option changes select, order, or hide those already adopted
cards without issuing an authoritative collection acquisition.

The browser projection contains only data the viewer may receive. Search indexes
must not smuggle undisclosed email addresses, phone numbers, or other hidden
fields into page attributes. Client-side display metadata remains untrusted as
input to future server operations.

 
Search metadata is itself a disclosure surface. A match on an
undisclosed email, phone or other restricted identifier can reveal
private information even if it is never printed on a card. Indexes
therefore include only permitted display/search fields and are
retired or redacted when current access is lost. The current
source's index contents are documented in the preservation audit.

HTMX remains the qualified transport and installation mechanism for authoritative
updates. The application-specific local presenter uses declared managed effects
for its own DOM changes; it cannot re-create retired cards, copy old owner
annotations, or make an obsolete callback current. Stable Request identity is
separate from the current physical card instance.

A server-rendered local-options alternative is valid only if it renders a
retained, scope-bound projection without silently acquiring newer domain facts.
Any retained projection handle needs principal/context binding, expiry, resource
limits, and current disclosure checks. A browser-supplied list of Request IDs
neither proves membership nor authorizes reads. The primary browser presenter
avoids requiring this additional server snapshot service for ordinary options.

 
*** Search and options preserve admitted membership

The chosen realization may present an admitted browser projection or
a retained, owner/principal/scope-bound server snapshot. A GET that
requeries current collection membership is an authoritative acquisition,
not a harmless local search. It must have a separately authorized grant;
it cannot silently adopt remote Requests or discharge advisory debt.
If retained data cannot be used, the renderer reports unavailable or
offers explicit acquisition, never an unqualified latest-database
fallback. This is a cohort-adoption rule, not a prohibition on Clojure
or HTMX rendering. The existing requery path is analyzed in the audit.

*** Mixed observations are explicit

A board may retain its cohort from observation Q17, adopt a local result for S at
another qualified observation, and keep an older card for R. It must preserve
those distinctions. There is no scalar board “current revision” that proves all
these cards and membership were read in one database snapshot.

Collection counts are counts of the specified adopted cohort or visible subset.
A separately acquired current count needs its own scope and disclosure contract.
Neither a pending-obligation count nor a progression token is a count of new
Requests. The default advisory label is “Updates available”, not an invented
number of unseen Requests.

 
*** Positive and adversarial board histories

The independent product oracle uses
actual adopted membership, provider-
scoped read evidence and two
browser contexts where remote
actions matter. A test must
observe the remote advisory
*before* asserting that its
Request stayed absent; otherwise
the assertion may pass vacuously.

| History | Required result |
|---------+-----------------|
| The initially served =/app= includes a permitted terminal Request and a live interest is registered afterward. | Record authorized membership and initial coverage; recover or expose a gap for any intervening commit. |
| =show-terminal?= changes from false to true. | Reveal terminal members already in the cohort; neither a new database query nor a new permission is implied. |
| Alice creates R remotely while Bob's board retains Q17. | Bob receives advisory; R and any newer count remain absent until authorized adoption. |
| Bob searches for R's exact title after receiving its advisory. | Search only the admitted cohort; R remains absent and advisory debt survives. |
| Bob changes mine-first, unclaimed-first and newest/oldest after R arrives remotely. | Deterministic order of existing members; no new Request membership. |
| Bob creates S locally at P19 while remote R at P18 still waits. | Adopt only the correlated eligible S and preserve R's outstanding advisory obligation. |
| Bob's current filter excludes newly created S. | The correlated result remains visibly confirmed without silently clearing the filter or adopting R. |
| Bob Claims an already adopted T while R is remote. | Install a justified T observation only, preserving old cohort coverage and R debt. |
| S's card has basis P19 but board membership is still Q17. | Preserve different scope/progression provenance; do not advertise a complete P19 board. |
| Search/options invokes a fresh =requests-for-location= query without Refresh grant. | Classify it as unauthorized additional acquisition for the local-only policy, not an innocent presentation transform. |
| A retained server projection expires or belongs to another principal or deployment generation. | Reject reuse or require a newly granted acquisition; browser-supplied IDs confer no read authority. |
| Request and User display rows were read at different physical positions. | Keep independent provenance unless the selected backend/join evidence establishes their compatibility. |
| A result exceeds configured full-cohort limits. | Return typed incomplete/scope-too-large or a declared window; never silently truncate and claim complete absence. |
| An older Refresh response arrives after a newer local authoritative card was installed. | Keep the newer applicable card and current owner; do not regress via response arrival order. |
| New advisory O2 arrives while Refresh covers only captured O1. | Discharge O1 only after authorized physical adoption; retain O2 pending. |
| A local options rerender replaces an expanded card while search is focused. | Restore compatible =<details>=, focus/caret/scroll without reviving retired action rights. |
| A late callback addresses a Request with the same UUID but an obsolete card DOM instance. | Refuse it as a current owner; no resurrection of provisional view or consumed grant. |
| Viewer loses current Membership to previously adopted R. | Withhold further disclosure and retire/redact the forbidden projection under applicable policy. |
| Search indexes an unauthorized User email/phone value. | Prevent disclosure through match results, DOM fields or retained index, even if visible card text omits it. |
| Advisory UI displays “3 new Requests” based solely on notification count. | Reject unsupported numeric claim; use “Updates available” until a permitted count has been read. |
| User switches Location or explicit collection page. | Require a new authorized scoped acquisition and retire incompatible old cohort; this is not a local sort. |

The existing =example.board= unit tests
exercise source-level presentation
semantics on supplied production rows
and distinguish Live/XTDB observed basis
from Request revision. The existing
Chromium lifecycle test exercises
real browser operations and persisted
outcomes. Neither automatically
establishes this complete selective-
adoption and two-client board matrix.

** Creation and immediate local visibility

Create uses the production public operation, including trusted principal,
authorized Organization/Location, content validation, command binding, atomic
incorporation, and post-commit recovery. Client validation improves feedback but
does not replace public-boundary or transaction checks.

 
*** Trusted Create authority and preflight before the form is used

The rendered dialog collects editable Request content. The trusted server
resolves the authenticated production User and selected authorized
Organization/Location, not a posted requestor ID or a fixed fixture value
promoted into authority. The public
=net.humanhelp.site.model.request.core/create= operation owns content
normalization, active-user and operational-Location dependencies, command
construction and atomic Request incorporation. The reference application
may set a fixed example Location as a declared *fixture scope*, but it
must not infer tenant or Membership permission from that constant.

Model planning needs real current-time, generated-ID/seed, transaction
and XTDB capability inputs with the correct trust and lifetime. The
canonical Biff/Gesso assembly checks their required provider contracts
and actual handler adoption where knowable. A missing
=:biff.fx/now=, =:biff.fx/seed= or production commit dependency that
can be established before protected service is an admission defect,
not a surprise error after a user has filled the dialog. The exact
Biff FX provider mechanism is a physical host contract, not a
browser-supplied clock or a stand-in demo function.

Validation failure is *pre-effect*: preserve the user's submitted
title/details/location-detail, render source-owned field errors
without creating a Request, and preserve the current board and
its advisory/option state. A submit interrupted after the effect
may have occurred is *not* a validation failure. It follows the
stable command and unknown-outcome recovery contract.

On known successful creation, the user's own Request is acquired and installed
through a correlated result path. That path can adopt the new Request into the
current cohort only when it establishes the selected scope's membership
predicate and permitted display projection. An entity identity or success flag
alone is insufficient.

The response must not issue an unrestricted board query and replace the whole
list as a convenience. Such a query can reveal unrelated remote Requests that
this user has not chosen to adopt. A committed command's progression requirement
is a minimum read condition, not authorization for every observation at that
position.

*** Success while a local filter excludes the new Request

The user must receive visible confirmation without an implicit filter reset.
This design provides a “Your new Request” result area adjacent to the board when
the new card would otherwise be hidden by local options. It shows the permitted
authoritative card and explains that the current filters exclude it.

The result area offers a visible action to reveal the Request in the ordinary
list by explicitly changing the relevant local options. It does not offer an
unlabelled whole-board Refresh as if that were required to see the user's own
result. When the Request already matches the filters, it appears in the list
and the confirmation can reference that card without creating a second active
operation surface for the same logical target.

The area retains the latest completed local creation result; replacing or
closing it affects only that presentation. Prior creations remain in the adopted
cohort when eligible. A pending or unknown creation retains its independent
command recovery state and is not discarded by a later successful creation.

 
The result area has a stable, permitted installation owner and accessible
success/uncertainty message. Its “Reveal in board” action changes only
local search, ordering or terminal visibility when that is sufficient;
it does not issue an implicit new domain acquisition. When S is
actually outside the selected Location, page/window or authorization
scope, the area labels that difference and requires an explicit
navigation/new acquisition. Closing a success result cannot silently
discard S's admitted cohort membership, and rendering a second success
must not erase an earlier unresolved command's recovery reference.

The result area is a normative finished-product design choice.
When the applied search excludes S, the confirmed creator-local S
remains independently visible and actionable without resetting
options or admitting unrelated remote R. Acceptance establishes
the excluding filter *before* Create and verifies authoritative
incorporation and a usable visible result, not merely a toast.

If creation succeeds outside the current cohort's declared bounds, the result
area can still show the permitted result under its own scope. It must label the
scope difference and offer an explicit navigation/acquisition action rather
than pretending the board's membership rule admitted it.

Prompt visibility means that the confirmed result is usable after the declared
result installation completes. A provisional card before confirmation is allowed
but is visibly pending and owned by the creation execution. No toast, modal
closure, or speculative row by itself proves successful incorporation.

 
*** Commit, response, advisory and historical recovery are distinct

The production model's =:commit/status :committed= and scoped
=:progression= justify an authoritative incorporation/read
claim within their proven physical meaning. The stronger
Part IV same-command replay result, permitted historical
disclosure and browser =:accepted= presentation need
their own typed evidence. A generated Request UUID,
a visible toast or a current postcommit card does not
by itself prove the historical outcome for original
command C19.

The creator response and other-client notification are distinct
postcommit responsibilities. Correlated creator settlement may
succeed independently of advisory delivery. An advisory failure
does not reverse a committed Request or authorize blind retry.

There are additional histories to qualify. If Request
incorporation succeeds but creator-response rendering
throws before the advisory helper is called, the mutation
is still committed, neither creator installation nor remote
advisory delivery is established, and the participant
needs correlated recovery. If the response was constructed
but transport or OOB installation fails, the server
cannot infer that the creator saw S. If advisory delivery
fails after response construction, the creator's success
need not be revoked, but the other participants'
notification/reconnect obligations must have a declared
durable or otherwise honestly weaker recovery policy.
A best-effort error log does not establish durable or unconditional
remote delivery.

An application with reliable postcommit delivery
records the necessary publication intent and
command recovery debt under the selected atomicity/
retention premise. It must not claim two-phase
commit or cross-client exactly-once effects merely
because a single Node/XTDB transaction was
committed. Retried Create with the original
stable binding is resolved before re-incorporation;
an unqualified implementation without such
deduplication keeps the outcome uncertain and
does not blindly regenerate S.

*** Worked example: remote R and local S

Bob has adopted board observation Q17. Alice creates Request R. Bob then creates
Request S. Both are eligible for the same board collection; Bob's text filter
matches R but not S. P18 and P19 below name provider-issued positions with the
specified coverage judgments, not numbers the browser is allowed to compare.

| Step | Bob's adopted membership and presentation | Remaining obligation |
|------+-------------------------------------------+----------------------|
| Baseline Q17 is installed. | The baseline cohort only. | None established; subscription continuity must also be justified. |
| Alice commits R and a relevant advisory reaches Bob. | R is absent; “Updates available” appears. | Board adoption obligation for the relevant remote change. |
| Bob searches or changes sort options. | Only the baseline cohort is presented differently; R stays absent. | The remote obligation remains. |
| Bob commits S and installs its correlated permitted result at P19. | S is selectively admitted; its result area is visible despite the filter. R stays absent. | The card/result evidence for S does not discharge the board obligation for R. |
| Bob changes local options to show S in the ordinary list. | S is visible there; no new membership is acquired. | The remote obligation remains. |
| Bob presses Refresh and installs a complete authorized observation covering R and S. | Both are in the adopted cohort, subject to current local display options. | Discharge only the obligations that this installed observation actually covers. |

The test must assert S's visibility before changing the excluding filter. Clearing
search first would hide the product failure this scenario is intended to detect.
It must also wait for observable advisory delivery before asserting continued
absence of R, so that an assertion made before the remote event cannot pass
vacuously.

 
The test also checks Bob's pre-Refresh cohort identity and current
local options, one permitted Create result for S, requestor identity,
production persisted Request state, retained pending R obligation,
and physical installation of the dedicated S result area. A card
for R appearing merely because the Create success response queried
all new Requests is a failure, even if R's contents are accurate.
If the R advisory arrives after S's result, the absence requirement
is still meaningful; the test explicitly synchronizes that
notification and verifies that S's local result did not
consume it retroactively.

The R4 example is a *logical history*, not an instruction to compare
the decimal portions of P18 and P19. The provider defines which
basis/coverage statements may be composed. Local search and sort
must not silently query the newest database as a workaround.

*** Correlation is narrower than global adoption

A command result can justify updating its affected card and, where declared,
selectively adding/removing a member. It does not adopt every Request mentioned
in an unrelated response, every row from an incidental reread, or every change
before its progression position.

 
*** A correlated result is narrower than a recomputed board

For an admitted creator-local insertion, the settled result identifies
the newly committed Request and its original command/execution binding.
The trusted authority establishes its requestor and scope, the relevant
transaction/progression and a permitted Request/assignment/User display
projection. A successful HTTP status or submitted title alone does not
justify that new member or its physical DOM.

The implementation may acquire a single affected Request/card with
sufficient progression, or install the admitted complete result of a
separately granted board acquisition. It may *not* reuse Create success
as permission for an unrestricted =requests-for-location= reread
whose resulting toolbar/list quietly imports remote Requests that
the user had not chosen to adopt. A committed basis P19 can justify
the creator's S read while membership for unrelated R remains Q17.

The creator's accepted operation permits a scoped affected-Request
result; it does not authorize a whole-board reread that imports
unrelated remote R. A full-board result is permitted only under
its own admitted query and adoption grant. The view must preserve
prior adopted members and outstanding remote debt. The present
whole-board OOB source behavior remains documented in the audit.

A board fragment and toolbar may need different membership/count
evidence. A newer card for S does not make the toolbar's total,
open count or other cards current. The UI reports a mixed
cohort truthfully and preserves any pending remote advisory.

Advisory debt is discharged by the relevant observation and installation scope.
The application cannot clear “Updates available” simply because it received a
newer local result. Two obligations with different scopes or required stages may
need different evidence even when their provider positions are comparable.

 
*** Positive and adversarial Create acceptance histories

The actual `/app` Create dialog, public production Request model,
source-bound server response, managed browser assets, Live advisory
and physical DOM have distinct test witnesses. Required eligible
success must be observed, not inferred from negative-case checks
or a fabricated test-only Create result.

| History | Required result and scope |
|---------+---------------------------|
| An eligible signed-in user submits valid Request content. | Production Create incorporates one Request with authenticated requestor, permitted Organization/Location, stable identity and commit progression. |
| Client-side validation passes but trusted Request content validation rejects the title. | No protected effect; keep submitted values and show authoritative field errors. |
| Mandatory Biff =:now= or =:seed= provider is structurally missing. | Fail application/operation admission before protected service where knowable; never take the user through an impossible dialog path. |
| A forged form posts another requestor or an unauthorized Location. | Trusted context/model determines actor and scope; reject incompatible or unauthorized intent. |
| S commits with a matching filter and valid cohort scope. | Install its permitted authoritative card into the admitted cohort without duplicate live target. |
| S commits but the active search excludes it. | Keep the filter and visibly show “Your new Request” with S's authorized card and reveal control, before the user changes search. |
| S commits outside the current board's window or Location. | Show a separately scoped permitted result and explicit navigation/acquisition, not fabricated cohort membership. |
| Bob has Q17, Alice creates remote R, then Bob creates S locally at P19. | Bob sees S and retains R's advisory/nonmembership; local Create does not adopt the latest complete database query. |
| Bob searches for remote R after its advisory but before explicit Refresh. | Do not acquire R by changing the local query; preserve advisory debt. |
| S is successfully read at P19 while the board membership and toolbar counts remain Q17. | Preserve scoped evidence and truthful distinct counts; do not claim the whole board advanced to P19. |
| The success response includes a full, newly queried toolbar/list that now contains remote R. | Classify as an unintended board acquisition under the selected policy; passing read-your-writes alone is insufficient. |
| The Create response builds correctly, then the advisory fanout throws. | Keep committed creator result and log/retain remote notification debt under the selected delivery policy; no false rollback/HTTP failure. |
| Model commit succeeds but creator-response rendering fails before advisory dispatch. | Preserve committed authority and both unresolved local delivery and remote notification obligations; do not infer rejection or successful adoption. |
| Server writes a 200/HTML success, but HTMX OOB fragment installation is rejected or fails. | Participant still lacks adopted S until physical installation or authorized recovery; server-side response construction is insufficient. |
| Duplicate transport retry carries original Create command C19 after unknown response. | Resolve disclosed historical incorporation without making duplicate Request S under the qualified command-record contract; if unqualified, report unknown/manual reconciliation. |
| An unrelated remote advisory arrives while S's local result installs. | Retain that obligation, even if the provider-issued position is older or not directly comparable with S's local read. |
| A second successful local Create T replaces the result area's display of S. | Keep eligible S in adopted membership and its prior history, and retain any independent unresolved command records. |
| A stale callback from S's retired result target arrives after current board owner changed. | Refuse old resource installation rights; request identity alone cannot revive stale effects. |
| A current permission change makes S's details inaccessible to the creator. | Do not continue unauthorized disclosure merely because S was previously adopted; report a policy-appropriate non-disclosing state. |
| A test starts with search matching remote R, then clears it before creating S. | Do not count this as the filtered-local-result positive case; the test must preserve the excluding filter through S's confirmation. |
| Remote Browser B has no advisory yet because fanout was lost. | Do not claim no-gap eventual notification from a best-effort sender; require the selected reconnect/replay or explicitly weaker delivery guarantee. |

Section 08.04 owns the baseline cohort and disclosure scope;
08.06 owns remote lifecycle advisories, Refresh grants and
reconnect rules; 08.07 owns details and option interaction.
Create does not acquire an extra broad authorization merely
because the current example route happens to redraw the full board.

** Remote lifecycle adoption policy
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: decision-humanhelp-remote-lifecycle-adoption
:END:

Selected policy: remote creation and remote lifecycle changes both require
explicit board Refresh for ordinary domain-content adoption. This includes
changes to Requests already visible. An advisory may update the pending indicator
and explanatory status; it does not silently replace a card or its cohort.

This policy is intentionally separate from two permitted local continuations:

- The user's own accepted command may install its declared affected-card/result
  observation and selective membership effect.
- A rejected or uncertain local command may invoke its declared scoped recovery
  read. That read can reveal current state of the affected Request, even when
  another actor caused it. It cannot import unrelated collection members or
  automatically resolve the uncertain command's attribution.

An old displayed Claim button can therefore remain visible after another helper
claims the Request. Clicking it is safe only because the public model enforces
current authority. The resulting rejection and affected-card acquisition explain
the conflict. An advisory may say the view has updates, but must not infer the
winner or current domain state from advisory payload alone.

Authentication loss, explicit scope change, and an established loss of disclosure
rights are separate context transitions. They retire incompatible execution and
installation rights and remove protected projections where the supported client
can do so. They are not delayed merely to preserve a board Refresh preference.
No application can retract information already disclosed to an untrusted or
offline browser; the enforceable guarantee is current checks at subsequent
trusted disclosures and mutations, plus the declared supported-client behavior.

 
*** Remote lifecycle remains advisory-only

The selected end-state rule requires explicit Refresh for both
remote Create and remote lifecycle changes, even to already-visible
Requests. Managed Live invalidations must not bypass this
user-grant policy through automatic collection rereads. Local
affected-Request recovery and trusted revocation are separate.
The history of R4's choice and the current routing mismatch
are recorded in the 08.06 preservation audit.

A remote change to an already visible T must not reveal
its new helper, terminal status or Request content through
a supposedly advisory payload. A stale Claim button
remains subject to current Request guards. A rejected
or uncertain local command may independently acquire the
affected T to explain conflict, without silently importing
other Requests. Authentication loss or established revoked
read rights are different trusted safety transitions:
they retire forbidden projections and mutation permissions
rather than waiting for optional Refresh. Previously
disclosed bytes in an untrusted/offline browser cannot
be retrospectively erased.

** Explicit Refresh, coverage, and races
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: req-humanhelp-refresh-coverage
:END:

A Refresh click creates a grant for one logical acquisition of the current board
scope and authority context. It captures the outstanding requirements and the
current non-regression obligations. Its lifetime ends on completion, failure,
expiry, owner retirement, or incompatible scope/context change.

The default has one acquisition and no automatic successor read. It can obtain
a complete current query result that includes changes beyond the captured
requirements. Installation can discharge any current obligation covered by that
actual result within the grant's scope. It does not authorize a second read just
because another advisory arrived.

A new explicit Refresh or Retry can create a new grant. While a cycle is active,
additional clicks are coalesced into at most one user-authorized successor intent
with current captured requirements; they do not create an unbounded queue. A
pending indicator alone never creates that intent. The UI reports whether it is
refreshing, waiting for another explicit action, or unable to refresh.

 
*** Refresh permission and issued read scope

A single user gesture creates a bounded grant with an
authenticated principal, current Location/collection scope,
board owner and deployment generation, captured requirements,
physical target, expiry and permitted *one logical* query.
The trusted server checks its authority independently of
browser-supplied scope, basis, client stamp or form values.
A malformed/impossible progression token must be rejected
or boundedly deferred, not force an indefinite query wait.
Advisory arrival is not a new read permission.

A second real click while a query runs can authorize at
most one successor intent; neither an automatic retry
nor a duplicate wakeup may create an unlimited queue.
Expired, incompatible or cancelled grants preserve
unresolved advisory debt and allow an explicitly
admitted retry.

A rendered Refresh control and successful HTTP/OOB response do not
alone establish a one-use grant, captured requirement ledger,
correct response owner or qualified physical adoption. Each
stage needs its own source and observable acceptance evidence.

A deployment may choose a bounded automatic repair/drain policy instead, but that
is an explicit product-policy change with its own budgets, expiry, and acceptance
cases. It is not an adapter optimization invisible to the user contract.

*** Acquisition and adoption are separate stages

1. Register the cycle, transport identity, scope, target owner, and requirements
   before physical dispatch.
2. Authenticate the actual read and validate the query/progression input under
   the qualified provider contract. A hostile or impossible token must not force
   an unbounded wait.
3. Acquire a projection with evidence of actual observation, completeness, and
   applicable authority context. Echoing the requested minimum does not prove
   the read met it.
4. Admit installation against the current owner, target instances, grant, scope,
   compatibility, and non-regression requirements.
5. Perform the qualified physical replacement/merge and report completion.
6. Record adoption and discharge only obligations satisfied at their required
   stage. Render current local options over the newly adopted cohort.

HTTP completion, response receipt, a proposed swap, or a backend read alone does
not complete stage 6. If installation fails, acquired evidence may remain useful
but the adoption/repair obligation remains visible.

Toolbar counts, list membership, cards, and board evidence must refer to the
same declared installation or explicitly identified partial result. The primary
full-board path renders one coherent board projection and coordinates its
affected surfaces as one adoption batch. Where HTMX performs several physical
mutations, admission is checked before the protected work and completion tracks
each required effect; multi-fragment delivery is not claimed to be DOM-atomic.
A partial failure leaves the batch incomplete, prevents a false “up to date”
claim, and exposes repair without rolling back a newer independently admitted
card. Re-fetching toolbar and list independently cannot manufacture a coherent
board observation merely because both responses arrived successfully.

 
*** HTMX OOB output has distinct completion stages

With =hx-swap="none"=, a response may still change
toolbar, list, board-state and advisory targets through
individual out-of-band effects. The coordinator must
validate the planned complete board and current resource
ownership before the effects, observe each required
physical installation, preserve compatible current
search/options and only then mark the batch adopted.

If the toolbar swaps but the request-list target is
absent, HTTP receipt is not a coherent refresh.
The application records a partial batch, retains
unsatisfied advisory/repair requirements, and does
not discard a newer locally installed S card.
If one component needs a separately scoped
acquisition, the result is labelled *partial*
rather than falsely presenting a common snapshot.

Toolbar =:pending-open-count= and =:stale?= are presentation
fields, not semantic coverage evidence. Replacing advisory
markup cannot discharge incomplete, later or uninstalled
Refresh obligations or create a new query grant.

*** Race rules

The default allows a non-regressing complete-query advance even when a stronger
remote advisory remains outstanding. This is partial satisfaction of current
debt, not partial or fabricated completeness of the query result. The remaining
advisory stays visible for a later user action.

| Race or failure | Required result |
|-----------------+-----------------|
| A later advisory arrives during a Refresh. | Preserve it; clear it only if the actual installed observation covers it. |
| The read covers the captured obligation but not the later one. | Adopt the non-regressing result and retain the later obligation; no automatic successor without a grant. |
| A qualified read also covers the later obligation. | Discharge both after successful installation within the permitted scope. |
| A local Create/Claim result is installed while an older board read is in flight. | Recheck the incoming board result against the newer local observation/membership obligations; do not overwrite or remove the justified local result. |
| An older result cannot establish safe replacement. | Decline that installation, preserve the local result and debt, and expose Refresh/Retry. A separately admitted selective merge needs its own coverage argument. |
| A stronger result arrives from a retired request or board owner. | Reject its installation rights; stronger progression does not revive a retired resource. |
| A read succeeds but physical installation fails. | Preserve remaining adoption debt and a usable retry path. |
| Local search/options change during the read. | Install into the same acquisition scope if still valid, then apply the current local options; do not restore obsolete options from the response. |
| Organization, Location, page/window, or authority context changes. | Retire or explicitly transition the owner; the old response cannot populate the new scope. |
| A command remains unresolved when a board refresh completes. | Update permitted presentation without claiming the command succeeded or failed solely from current card state. |

A full-board replacement must not regress any retained observation whose scope
it supersedes. If proof of safe replacement is unavailable, the default rejects
that replacement and requires a new acquisition. It does not silently union an
old complete result with arbitrary newer rows and call the union a complete
snapshot. A mixed selective projection can be valid, but must retain its mixed
provenance and must not claim snapshot-wide properties.

 
*** Opaque progression and notification delivery premises

Generic Gesso progression bases are opaque. A trusted
XTDB/provider relation, not integer comparison,
HTTP arrival order or the latest visible token,
establishes whether a read actually covers a
captured or subsequently arriving requirement.
An affected-card observation may advance one
subject while the board cohort remains older.
The same user action can legitimately satisfy
more than one obligation if the *one* authorized
read and completed adoption cover each; a
later advisory never creates a second read grant.

HumanHelp's separate app-owned creation advisory
uses =client-plumbing= to queue non-adopting
Refresh OOB/toast presentation to connected
clients other than the creator. Gesso
=live.client= owns finite ephemeral pending
mailboxes, including disconnected-client
overflow and drop policies. This mechanism
does not prove durable eventual delivery
through disconnection, queue overflow,
multi-node failover or a missed subscription.
A stronger product guarantee needs
source-owned reconnect/fence/replay or
authorized reacquisition. Without it the
system must expose the weaker contract,
not report a permanently silent stream
as current board knowledge.

The notification is a wakeup, not the
authoritative current Request state,
a sufficient current disclosure capability,
or a count of unseen new Requests.
A durable command record and a board
Refresh are separate recovery subjects.

*** Membership removal and authoritative absence

An authoritative query result can remove a cohort member only with the required
coverage and current installation rights. A filtered-out row, a failed read,
missing markup, or an empty partial page is not evidence of domain deletion.
Terminal filtering hides =:done= and =:cancelled= in the default view without
removing their admitted cohort membership.

If an affected-card read establishes that a Request has left the authorized
scope, the UI follows the declared non-disclosing absence/unavailability branch.
It must not reveal whether an inaccessible entity was deleted, moved, or made
private unless policy permits that distinction. Such a read still does not
resolve a prior command's attribution without command evidence.

Pending provisional presence has a resolution owner. It cannot survive every
complete authoritative observation indefinitely, and it cannot disappear with
its command-recovery record merely because a DOM row was removed. Part VI's
separate rules for presentation supersession and command uncertainty apply.

 
*** Positive and adversarial Refresh acceptance histories

These are required finished-product scenarios,
not assertions that the currently checked
Chromium lifecycle source already passes
the complete two-client Refresh matrix.

| History | Required result |
|---------+-----------------|
| Alice creates R while Bob has adopted an older board. | Bob sees advisory, not R; Alice's correlated Create result is independent. |
| Alice claims T already visible to Bob. | Bob's T remains stale with advisory until user Refresh or separately authorized local affected-card recovery. |
| A manager reassigns Bob's visible T to another helper. | No changed-helper card is silently installed on Bob's board. |
| Another user completes or cancels an adopted Request. | Bob's card and terminal visibility do not silently advance; advisory debt remains. |
| Bob clicks the stale Claim button. | Current model guards reject or commit appropriately; permitted conflict recovery is scoped to that Request. |
| Bob loses read permission to a previously adopted Request. | Current trusted reads/mutations refuse disclosure and supported clients retire/redact as required, independent of voluntary Refresh. |
| An incoming =:updated= invalidation tries to schedule a managed list GET. | The final application converts it to advisory rather than automatically adopting remote lifecycle content. |
| A creation OOB advisory arrives without canonical Request HTML. | No remote Request membership is adopted by the toast or Refresh indicator alone. |
| Bob clicks Refresh once with obligation O1. | One authorized coherent board read may satisfy O1 only after validated physical installation. |
| O2 arrives after the O1 Refresh began. | Preserve O2 unless actual installed read coverage proves O2 satisfied; do not issue an automatic second query. |
| Bob clicks Refresh again while O1 is running. | Allow at most one separately user-authorized queued successor, never a wakeup-triggered infinite loop. |
| The Refresh caller sends an impossible basis or forges Location. | Reject/qualify input at trusted boundary without unbounded wait or cross-scope data. |
| Bob installs local Create S while an older full-board read is in flight. | Decline regressing full replacement or use independently justified selective merge; preserve S and unrelated remote advisory. |
| A returned Refresh belongs to a retired owner or old Location. | Do not install, even if the provider basis appears stronger. |
| Toolbar OOB succeeds but Request list target is detached. | Keep the batch incomplete and advisory debt recoverable; never claim complete adoption. |
| A response is delivered but the browser fails to install it. | HTTP success does not discharge pending requirements or consume semantic adoption evidence as if completed. |
| A coherent board query cannot prove compatibility of separately read Request/User projections. | Retain honest mixed provenance rather than inventing one database snapshot. |
| Search/options change while Refresh is in flight. | Keep current compatible options, not the stale values captured in the response. |
| A terminal Request is absent because =show-terminal?= is false. | Hiding does not prove authoritative deletion or loss of cohort membership. |
| Bob sees a changed helper after Refresh while C42 remains uncertain. | Current card knowledge does not identify whether C42 incorporated without command-specific evidence. |
| A notification is dropped after ephemeral client-mailbox overflow. | Qualify delivery as incomplete; reconnect/fence/replay or explicit weaker guarantee is required. |
| Advisory O2 is duplicated after a one-use Refresh grant was consumed. | Do not mint another read grant or erase still-uncovered scoped requirements. |

The real HumanHelp Chromium acceptance
source covers browser-generated Claim,
Unclaim, On-the-way, Complete, Cancel
and Reassign with persisted reloads.
It does not by itself establish all
these two-client advisory-only remote
updates, one-use grants, multi-target
installation, loss and failover cases.

** Search, ordering, visibility, and local state

The ordinary board presenter is a pure function of the adopted permitted
projection, normalized local options, and the current authenticated-viewer
projection. Its DOM realization is an admitted effect. Presentation does not
re-evaluate production write authorization and does not manufacture observations.

Search uses a declared shared normalization contract: trim the input, apply the
selected case normalization, and perform substring matching against the prepared
search text. The contract specifies the supported character behavior and is
checked on both host runtimes where both implement it. Search text comes from
already disclosed Request title, details, location description, and explicitly
permitted displayed labels. New private fields cannot become searchable merely
because they are present in a production document.

The empty search matches the adopted cohort. No match means no visible adopted
row matches; it does not assert that the database has no matching Request.

 
*** The adopted-cohort search and disclosure contract

The search index is an *already authorized projection*, not a
second Request model and not a backdoor query. For each current
viewer the index may contain only approved display/search
fields from the admitted Request, RequestAssignment and
User projections. Whether a field is drawn visibly or only
used to decide matches does not change its disclosure
classification: a match against an otherwise undisclosed
email or phone can reveal that information. Identity,
scope and current authorization changes revoke the
applicable retained search projection, not just visible
card markup.

A selected portable normalizer fixes whitespace trimming,
case folding and Unicode/locale behavior on every host
that implements the transformation. A ClojureScript
search and Clojure server renderer must produce the same
membership and order for the same qualified rows and
options; JS and JVM case conversion are not assumed
universally identical for all possible Unicode inputs
without a tested contract. Typed unsupported characters
or normalization differences must be reported/handled
by that contract rather than silently expanding a match.

Search and option changes transform the viewer's currently adopted,
authorized cohort rather than silently making a newest-database
collection query. Server-rendered HTML/HTMX remains valid when it
operates on a retained qualified cohort. This invariant needs
real-browser acceptance, including outstanding remote advisory.

Each search edit has a presentation generation.
If an earlier server response or scheduled
client effect arrives after a later edit,
it cannot restore the old search or install
an older filtered result. An empty result
means "no matches among the adopted permitted
Requests"; when membership is incomplete or
its continuity unknown, the message makes
that limit clear rather than claiming
that no matching Request exists in XTDB.

*** Ordering is a single explicit key

“Mine” means requested by the authenticated viewer or assigned to that viewer
as active primary helper. It is a presentation category, not permission to act.
The prepared projection supplies these facts from the production models. A missing
viewer ID must not make two absent identifiers compare as “mine”.

When both priority options are enabled, mine-first is the primary grouping and
unclaimed-first is the secondary grouping. Creation time then uses the selected
newest/oldest direction, with canonical Request identity as the deterministic tie
breaker. The UI makes this priority order apparent.

An illustrative key over prepared display rows is:

#+begin_src clojure
(defn board-sort-key [row options]
  [(if (and (:mine-first? options) (:viewer-related? row)) 0 1)
   (if (and (:unclaimed-first? options) (:open-unassigned? row)) 0 1)
   (case (:created-order options)
     :oldest (:created-order-key row)
     :newest (:reverse-created-order-key row))
   (:canonical-request-order-key row)])
#+end_src

The temporal order keys are prepared under the declared portable ordering
contract; the example does not assume arbitrary host timestamps are negatable
JavaScript numbers. Unknown order options are rejected or normalized through the
explicit option schema before this function runs. A malformed creation time is
a projection error, not silently the Unix epoch.

 
Malformed or absent timestamps are typed projection errors, not
valid epoch-zero values. Temporal sort keys must be portable across
selected hosts with deterministic identity tie breakers and no
unqualified overflow or representation assumptions. The JVM
algorithm currently inspected belongs in the section audit.

“Unclaimed” is a model-derived open/unassigned category. A terminal Request with
no active assignment does not become unclaimed. Multiple independent sort passes
must not accidentally change which option is primary.

 
Sorting acceptance covers simultaneous priority flags, ties,
missing authenticated viewer and the distinction between
open/unassigned and terminal Requests. Missing viewer IDs must
not compare as "mine"; a viewer-related grouping is never
business authorization for Claim or protected disclosure.

Order of transformations is declared:
authorized adopted cohort, terminal
visibility, local search, primary/
secondary sort groups, temporal key,
canonical identity. A filter does
not mutate adopted cohort membership;
a changed order does not grant
new authoritative read permission.

*** Defaults, drafts, and updates

The default options are empty search, newest first, mine-first off,
unclaimed-first off, and terminal visibility off. Search changes apply locally
as the user types using a bounded scheduled effect; stale callbacks cannot
restore earlier search text. Options-dialog drafts become applied options only
when the user confirms, and Cancel leaves applied options unchanged.

Authoritative Refresh preserves the current compatible local options. It does
not restore options captured when a slow request started. Initial loading,
explicit scope navigation, and user-requested reset have their own documented
initialization behavior.

 
*** Form and asynchronous presentation ownership

The options dialog has a *draft* distinct
from the applied values. Done commits
the whole compatible normalized draft
as one local presentation action; Cancel,
Escape and dismissal must not leak partial
option changes. The selection remains
visible, keyboard-operable and
persistently reflected in the controls
after permitted rerenders. Unknown sort
variants can normalize to documented
defaults only when the accepted option
schema allows that; a hostile
authorization, Request or progression
field submitted with the form is not
a presentation option.

Current =example.views/board-options-form=
renders newest/oldest, mine-first,
unclaimed-first and terminal controls
through a server-side HTMX POST,
and preserves search via =hx-include=
of the stable form. Its Done action
is real. These are valuable UI
building blocks, but a round-trip
that computes fresh board state does
not automatically meet the selected
local-only adoption or draft/Cancel
behavior under concurrent updates.
The source-level =board_test.clj=
exercises isolated filter/sort cases,
not every browser interaction.

Typing search is a bounded, cancelable
presentation effect (the current
example declares a 250 ms HTMX
keyup/search trigger). Late callbacks
from old form/card resource instances
are excluded by the current owner.
Refreshing after a search begins
must reapply the *current* search
to newly and legitimately adopted
board facts, not overwrite it
with the request's captured text.

Local state may preserve which Request details are open, focus, caret, scroll
anchor, and bounded unsubmitted text. It may not preserve old authoritative
status, helper assignment, removed command capabilities, or obsolete target and
owner annotations as if those were harmless continuity.

When a card disappears, restoration falls back to an existing safe target such
as the board heading or the next logical control. A local draft tied to that
Request must be labelled as no longer attached to an available target or retained
in its separate permitted draft surface. It cannot cause the old card to be
resurrected.

 
*** Continuity is physical restoration, not authority

Real-browser continuity tests must observe physical scroll,
focus/caret and native =<details>= restoration for valid
same-Request replacement and safe retirement. Declaring a
key or listener is not proof of completed restoration.

Restoration is admitted only when the
same authorized Request and compatible
new card/fragment owner survive.
A terminal filter may hide a card
without deleting its admitted cohort
membership; a Location change, loss
of read authority or authoritative
absence may retire the card entirely.
In that case details and old action
bindings are not restored, and focus
moves to a safe existing control.
Captured scroll or selected text
cannot bring hidden protected
content back into the DOM. An open
accordion alone is not permission
for a fresh model read or for a
provisional command to continue.

** Details, response interaction, and accessible feedback

Opening Request details reveals the permitted information already adopted for
that card. The default details interaction is local and non-mutating. It does
not implicitly update the card from the latest database state.

A separate explicitly labelled “Get current details” interaction may acquire a
new single-Request projection under its own grant. Its implementation must state
which card/details observations it adopts and how it preserves board membership
and outstanding board obligations. It is not an unrestricted collection refresh.

 
*** Details projection, disclosure and scoped current reads

The default details panel uses the
authorized Request projection already
owned by the card; opening or closing
it does not call =request.core=,
advance the cohort, change status,
or make a domain submission.
It does not implicitly disclose
email/phone or private Location data
that the signed-in viewer was not
allowed to receive. Any separately
labeled "Get current details" affordance
requires a trusted, current
single-Request acquisition grant,
read-time authorization and
progression/owner checks. It may
supersede that Request's details
observation while leaving unrelated
board membership and pending remote
advisories untouched.

An inaccessible Request need not
reveal whether it was deleted,
moved or made private. The
application follows the selected
non-disclosing failure branch
unless the viewer has permission
to distinguish those states.
A previously expanded card remains
subject to current disclosure and
resource retirement when a
new response is served.

Controls must be reachable by keyboard, have meaningful labels, and expose
pending, accepted, rejected, and unknown states without requiring color alone.
Updates-available and completion announcements are coalesced so repeated advisory
delivery does not repeatedly interrupt the user. A failed refresh remains
retryable; a disabled control explains its relevant availability condition where
disclosure permits.

Technical identities and proof vocabulary belong in diagnostics, not ordinary
product instructions. A user should see “We couldn't confirm whether your claim
succeeded; check again” with a recovery action, rather than a raw progression
requirement or resource-instance error.

 
Accessibility acceptance includes
native form/dialog focus order,
keyboard opening/closing of
=<details>=, visible focus,
discernible search/order labels,
logical focus fallback on removed
cards, state text and permitted
announcements for advisory,
pending, accepted, rejected and
unknown outcomes. Screen-reader
notifications are coalesced or
limited by the selected accessibility
policy; repeated SSE wakes
must not become repeated disruptive
announcements. The ordinary user
gets a next action, not a theorem,
command ID or internal XTDB basis.
A timed or disconnected response
retains a visible retry/recovery
action rather than a spinner
that can never settle.

Real-browser accessibility tests exercise labels, keyboard
interaction, dialogs, accordion state, focus fallback and
announced pending/unknown/repair outcomes. ARIA attributes
or a declared continuity contract alone cannot establish
that a real browser or assistive interface behaves correctly.

*** Independent response-flow contract
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: decision-humanhelp-response-flow
:END:

Status: unresolved product contract. “Response flow” is a required capability
name, but that name alone does not specify a user outcome. It cannot honestly be
implemented or accepted by choosing whichever existing handler is most convenient.

Before claiming full rich-board completion, HumanHelp must select one explicit
meaning and record its independent contract. It may mean responding by taking
responsibility through the lifecycle, contacting a requestor through a permitted
channel, or another defined interaction. Those alternatives have different
persistence, privacy, authority, and recovery obligations. This specification
does not invent a message entity, messaging provider, or contact-disclosure rule.

 
*** The product decision and assurance boundary

The response flow must be selected
by an independent HumanHelp product
decision, with a versioned acceptance
profile and a designated model/UI
owner. This section does not infer
a requirement to create messages,
send email/SMS, reveal contact
information or acquire a new
Request domain role merely from
the name "response flow". In
particular, an existing =Claim=
button does *not* automatically
resolve this decision. The product
may select "respond by claiming"
only if its independently authored
user-intent and outcome contract
explicitly says that this is the
full promised response experience.

The selected flow's permission,
storage and external-effect
assumptions must be checked against
production =request.core= and
the relevant public Organization,
Membership and User contracts.
If it is non-mutating, an
authorized read or local
disclosed interaction may
satisfy it under a separately
testable observable outcome.
If it mutates Request or
emits external communication,
it needs actual source-owned
semantic identity, guarded
model or qualified external
effect, durable/uncertain
outcome semantics and
valid real-browser execution.
The example cannot introduce
a parallel response store just
to satisfy this milestone.

The selected contract must define:

- the user's intent, eligible actor, Request preconditions, and actual affordance;
- input and validation, including what information may be disclosed to whom;
- the visible success result and any durable domain or external effect;
- the production operation or explicitly non-mutating interaction that realizes it;
- its relation to Claim, details, and other existing lifecycle capabilities;
- reload/reacquisition behavior and any relevant duplicate, concurrent, rejected,
  uncertain, cancelled, or abandoned interaction;
- an eligible real-browser completion scenario and the applicable negative case.

If the product chooses “respond by claiming”, acceptance must exercise that
complete labelled user journey and explicitly establish that no separate
capability is promised. If it chooses a different action, Claim tests cannot
stand in for it. An unchosen contract is reported as unresolved, not passed,
not silently dropped, and not counted as a framework failure.

 
*** Independent product acceptance for the selected response

Before accepting the full HumanHelp
rich-board milestone, record the
selected response-flow option,
eligible actor, observable user
intent, source/model owner,
specific control and permitted
outputs, whether and what changes,
recovery/deduplication and
privacy/disclosure assumptions.
Then execute at least one
eligible real-browser response
with fresh authorized
observation of the declared
outcome, plus an ineligible/
concurrent/uncertain path
appropriate to the selected
flow. If selected behavior
contains a communication
effect, its recipient and
delivery evidence must be
explicit; a toast is not a
delivered message.

An unresolved product decision
is *not* a Gesso type failure
or a license to remove the
independent requirement. It
is a named HumanHelp product
acceptance blocker. The
application's other
capabilities can receive
their narrower individual
passing evidence, while
the complete product profile
remains unaccepted until
selection and real outcome
verification.
 
*** Positive and adversarial interaction histories

The following cases exercise real
production-backed adopted rows
and the physical board, not a
test-only copied array presented
as the entire product. Source
unit evidence and real browser
evidence remain separate.

| History | Required result |
|---------+-----------------|
| The viewer types a trimmed, mixed-case search that matches an adopted Request title. | Filter the admitted cohort with the selected normalization, without a new domain mutation or unauthorized collection acquisition. |
| Alice remotely Creates R, Bob has not pressed Refresh, and Bob types R's exact title. | Do not reveal R through search; retain the remote advisory even if the database knows R. |
| The current server search route performs a fresh Request collection query. | Count it as a new acquisition under the explicit-grant policy, not an innocent transformation of retained adopted data. |
| A search term matches a private User email not disclosed to Bob. | Never reveal the match via result inclusion, DOM index, error detail or debug presentation. |
| Search text changes from 'hel' to 'help' while the first HTMX request is still running. | Discard the earlier response on arrival; current text and its compatible result win. |
| Empty search on a complete admitted cohort. | Show the whole permitted current cohort subject to terminal visibility and selected order. |
| Empty search on an incomplete/unknown cohort. | Do not claim no Requests exist or counts are globally authoritative. |
| Newest, then oldest are selected over Requests with distinct valid creation timestamps. | Display the exact inverse temporal ordering with deterministic Request-ID ties. |
| Both mine-first and unclaimed-first are enabled. | Mine is the primary category, unclaimed secondary, then selected time and identity; verify actual rendered order. |
| A viewer ID is missing while requestor/assignment IDs are absent. | Do not classify absent identifiers as 'mine' or derive authorization from sorting. |
| A terminal Request has no active primary assignment. | Do not classify it as open/unclaimed; hiding or showing it is presentation only. |
| A creation timestamp is missing or invalid. | Report a source/projection error; never silently treat the Request as epoch zero. |
| The user changes options in the dialog and presses Cancel or Escape. | Applied search/order/terminal options remain unchanged; drafts do not leak into the board. |
| The user confirms a valid draft while another remote advisory remains pending. | Apply options locally without acquiring remote state or clearing advisory obligations. |
| The current Refresh completes after the user has typed another search term. | Reapply the latest compatible local search to the newly admitted projection; no old input restoration. |
| A details accordion is open when a same-Request valid fragment replacement occurs. | Preserve compatible selected/open state, focus and scroll under the actual surviving owner. |
| A Request disappears from the allowed scope while its details were expanded. | Retire old card and effects, choose safe focus fallback; do not resurrect protected details. |
| The user opens details of a currently adopted Request. | Reveal only existing permitted projection, without fetching new Request state or changing domain truth. |
| The user explicitly selects 'Get current details' for an older card. | Authorize and adopt a scoped read of that Request only, preserving unrelated board membership and advisory debt. |
| Repeated duplicate advisories arrive while the page is focused. | Provide bounded, accessible updates without repeated disruptive announcements or an auto-refresh. |
| An unresolved Claim response yields unknown outcome. | Show comprehensible next action and the appropriate command-specific recovery, not an indefinite generic spinner. |
| HumanHelp has not selected the response-flow contract but Claim happens to work. | Report response-flow product acceptance as unresolved; do not infer that Claim is the selected response journey. |
| The product explicitly selects 'respond by claiming' and documents the complete user experience. | Exercise its actual labeled real-browser journey, committed model state, rejection and recovery under that independent oracle. |
| The product instead selects a separate authorized contact interaction. | Require its selected privacy, effect/delivery and observed-outcome evidence; an existing Claim test cannot substitute. |

The rich-board gate requires
positive and adversarial
interaction coverage, not
a permanently hidden controls
panel or a test that checks
only the selected option
labels. Section 08.08 owns
authentication, read authority
and Live reconnect; section
08.09 owns command-specific
optimistic recovery. Parts VI
and VII own physical continuity
and managed output.

** Authentication, read authority, and context changes

The example uses genuine authenticated sessions. Development persona selection,
if available, is a declared development authentication facility excluded from
ordinary deployment or protected by the intended development-only access policy.
A browser cannot become another user by selecting a User UUID in a command.

Every authoritative read, command invocation, outcome lookup, target-helper
query, and subscription registration performs its applicable trusted access
checks. Being the fixed demonstration Location is a selection rule, not read
authorization. Previously adopted Request IDs and signed/opaque projection
handles do not exempt a subsequent disclosure from current policy.

Authority context includes principal and the relevant authorization domain and
profile binding. Mutable Membership and Organization facts still require current
checks at their actual boundaries; a context identifier does not freeze them as
valid for an entire page lifetime.

Logout or a switch of principal/Organization retires incompatible board owners,
command presentation rights, subscriptions, and outstanding installations. An
old response cannot disclose one user's content into another user's page. The
command recovery service retains only the independently authorized records needed
for later recovery; it cannot disclose them to the newly active principal merely
because the same browser is used.

Read and command errors use the application's explicit non-disclosure policy.
Tests must not require a reason such as “Request exists in another Organization”
when the correct response intentionally hides that distinction.

 
*** Trusted session provenance and actor consistency

Authenticated principal evidence includes the configured login
issuer, protected cookie, expiry/revocation, middleware order
and current production User. All request-context actor slots
and connected-client recipient identities derive from trusted
middleware or are cross-checked against the session. Conflicting
slots must fail unless a separate authenticated impersonation
capability was explicitly admitted. Development persona fixtures
are restricted to their declared test profile. UUID shape,
first nonnil context value and a browser role name are never
authentication proofs. Current middleware and slot precedence
remain documented in the 08.08 audit.

Gesso's trusted operation role
may represent Request authority,
and one physical =:helper=
browser participant may display
requestor/helper/manager controls;
neither changes the *authenticated*
principal. Production Request,
Organization, Location and
Membership APIs determine
per-Request read, modification
and selected-target permissions
from the current subject/actor
context. The fixed example
Location and app-wide notification
scope are not evidence of
tenant-wide disclosure rights.
An unauthorized existence test,
recovery lookup, details read,
search index or advisory
recipient must follow the
same explicit non-disclosure
contract as the actual Request
projection.

*** Public HTTP and browser boundaries

The application validates command and acquisition input before use, including
interface versions, allowed fields, limits, domain identifiers, and protocol
encoding. Authentication, CSRF protection for applicable session-based mutations,
and safe content rendering remain required host obligations. A valid semantic
operation ID does not replace those protections.

The selected command wire schema rejects undeclared actor/principal authority
fields. A legitimate target-helper field is separately declared and policy
checked. A tampering test must assert that exact typed rejection or the exact
permitted domain outcome of the declared field; “anything below HTTP 500” is not
an acceptable oracle.

User-controlled title, details, and location text are escaped through the selected
rendering contract. Managed HTML must not execute undeclared scripts, install
foreign operation metadata, or cause a response from one target to issue arbitrary
out-of-band effects. The qualified browser profile states the permitted headers,
redirects, events, scripts, and swap forms and rejects unsupported behavior before
its protected effect.

 
*** Identity, CSRF, decoding and recipient-safe output as joined gates

The current HumanHelp site middleware
wires session, CSRF, parameter decoding
and application routing, while example
routes apply =wrap-signed-in=.
The finished source/physical claim
checks that their *actual installed
order* covers every managed POST,
HTMX request, fragment, stream,
pending OOB drain, command-result
lookup and reconnect entrypoint
as applicable. CSRF validation is
a session-bound mutation defense;
it cannot authenticate an actor
named in a JSON/EDN or browser
command, nor is it equivalent
to read authorization for an SSE
stream or target-helper query.

Decode the wire once according to
the admitted protocol/schema with
limits on nesting, size, keys,
operation identity, method/path,
Request selector, helper/target,
projection and content. Reject
undeclared actor/principal fields
rather than treating them as a
second identity source. An
authorized manager's chosen
target helper is a domain argument,
not an alternate principal.
The same authenticated actor must
own the server command, any
durable record binding, outcome
disclosure and permitted direct
acquisition. Different authorized
actors may independently receive
the *same current Request state*
without obtaining another
person's historical command record.

Physical OOB payloads and stream
messages are rendered under
recipient-specific current
disclosure rights. An app-wide
send target does not authorize
embedding private Request
contents, other Users' contacts,
numeric new-Request counts,
a copied CSRF token or executable
operation authority. A
receiver-rendered pending fragment
also revalidates authenticated
recipient, current connection/
client ownership, projection
generation and target scope
at its *drain* boundary; a
client ID or SSE URL parameter
is only an opaque selector.
The host must not accept another
user's stale pending mailbox
as a source of executable OOB
markup or identity. An expired,
logged-out or switched
participant retires both
stream and queued presentation
rights.

** Live publication, advisory routing, and recovery

Production model incorporation is the source of semantic changes. The example
routes them; it does not synthesize an independent success event from a toast or
HTTP status. Relevant RequestAssignment, Membership, Organization, and other
dependency changes need appropriate routing even when the Request document itself
did not change.

Live topics express observation interests. They are not a substitute for the
transaction's guarded dependency set. Likewise, overlap between topics does not
prove that two authoritative commands conflict or that all conflicting writers
have been found.

 
*** The production change graph and the missing writers question

Production Request transitions issue source-owned semantic change
intent under the selected publication profile. Managed Live
invalidation cannot convert a remote lifecycle advisory into an
ungranted current-collection reread. Relevant RequestAssignment,
Organization, Location, Membership and user-display/disclosure
