composition test's expected failure after the fact.

*** Required mutation families and protected meanings

| Family | Perturbation and first relevant guarantee |
|--------+--------------------------------------------|
| Schema and nominal identity | Missing/retyped field, optional to required or reverse, nullable versus absent, different nominal enum, closed variant added/removed, relationship endpoint/cardinality drift; a valid new schema can make an old consumer stale without itself being malformed. |
| Rule interpretation and evaluation | Boolean truthiness versus presence, nil versus missing, short-circuit or branch refinement reordering, illegal ordered-enum use, integer/codec boundary, different reader footprint or stale field; compare actual typed meaning, not just parsed shape. |
| Propositional derivation | Forged premise, shifted conclusion, changed antecedent, forward reference, incorrect conjunction child, injected checker rule, hidden inherited assumption or false goal under the original premise context. |
| Guarded transition and frame | Candidate prestate used as atomic prestate, wrong guard, omitted simultaneous assignment, wrong poststate, absent/nil conflation, invalid frame or effect outside the protected declared write footprint. |
| Inductive obligations and finite search | Omitted base/invariant/operation, changed shared initial state, incomplete reachability, contradictory/vacuous Init, partial exploration labelled exhaustive, valid safe fragment substituted for full original source. |
| Required source/dependency closure | Source-required graph edge/operation removed while the residual DAG remains structurally valid, changed upstream interface, fabricated compatible bridge, stale source+stale graph passed as current, or unjustified proof cycle. |
| Premise propagation and discharge | Copied assertion presented as proof, inherited premise dropped, evidence from different actor/Request/Organization/transaction used to discharge a required premise, or checked conclusion stripped of new conditional premises. |
| Choreo and role-local admissibility | Unknown discriminator, hidden private branch, unsupported receive overlap, lost actor/source knowledge, asserted-to-authoritative provenance promotion, communication omitted, unsupported outcome/recovery path or projection attached to wrong Choreo identity. |
| Outcome and durable command history | HTTP status masquerading as commit, compatible C42 replay written twice, incompatible command binding reused, old historical outcome inferred from current card, =:commit-unknown= converted to rejection, missing retention or unauthorized command-result disclosure. |
| Browser scope and resource ownership | Wrong target, OOB partial install, superseded execution/lease, stale plan, duplicate one-use Refresh capability, remote advisory silently becoming acquisition, or creator-local S importing unrelated remote collection R. |
| Certificates and untrusted admission | Success map, forged fingerprint, checker-status field, manually created opaque handle, stale/cyclic dependency, executable reader/unknown tag, partial durable package or unsupported checker version accepted as an issued certificate. |
| Issued implementation and actual host | Changed closure/Var, substituted handler, uninstalled issued executor, forged route/source inventory, unregistered direct XTDB writer, modified compiled browser bytes with copied stamp, unqualified provider change. |
| Physical effect and observation | Caller-supplied principal/node/prestate, second diagnostic transaction, mismatched real invocation/result, co-observed ledger/command records called causal without binding, post-effect failure reported as prevented incorporation. |
| Completeness and checker budgets | Truncated model/trace, weakened type domain, omitted mutant path, timeout, unusable external solver, opaque unsupported code or infrastructure failure reported as proved/accepted without proper scope. |
| Product policy and user capability | Accepted coherent but surprising rule, original HumanHelp Claim/Unclaim/Reassign positive retained, independent required capability removed from both program and proof, disabled Claim to satisfy only negatives, or unselected response flow declared complete. |

These families are *minimum semantic coverage*, not a fixed list
of particular file names. Every class requires a meaningful
positive neighbor. A type checker can correctly reject
=emailed < 18= while accepting a well-typed =age > 18=
policy even if the owner intended =age >= 18=. If
the latter violates an independently declared invariant,
the expected result changes to a property counterexample,
not retroactive classification as malformed syntax.
Human intent is not an implicit rule generated by
the mutation harness.

Typed semantics also require accepted and rejected
conformance cases for optional =absent= versus present
=nil=, nominal equality, ordered-vector versus
unordered-map normalization, short-circuit presence
guarding, branch-local knowledge, simultaneous writes,
reader footprints and actual source-derived operation
and invariant completeness. A changed rule can be
syntactically valid yet fail its *use-site* authority,
disclosure or temporal provenance obligation.

*** Injection points and immutable category discipline

Source mutations operate on fresh *unadmitted*
production declarations, before their source
construction/checker pipeline. A mutation of
a purported elaborated proof is candidate input
to an independent original-source checker.
Serialized-certificate forgery mutates inert
package bytes before safe decoding and
rechecking. It must never be modeled by
mutating a private, issuer-registered live handle
as if such a handle were an ordinary writable
application map.

An implementation mutation may replace an
unadmitted callable or dynamically selected
host dependency before issuance; a later
deployment substitution must be injected at
the actual trusted installation or runtime
boundary. The two test different claims.
An already issued certificate may describe
an unchanged abstract theorem while its
*physical applicability* fails against the
changed handler, provider, served asset,
or owner generation. It is not sound to
credit a semantic checker with detecting
a post-installation substitution that
it could not observe.

All mutation operators declare their
allowed edit footprint. Accidental changes
to the baseline source, unrelated fixture
users, provider trust assumptions or
execution order can invalidate the test
rather than exercise the intended claim.
Corpus generation is deterministic from
a recorded seed and original inputs,
or reports the chosen randomized seed,
shrinking/minimization history and
replayable schedule. Isolation includes
fresh checker registration, caches,
XTDB test node/session, browser state
and app generation where appropriate.
An order-dependent pass is a test bug
until its environmental assumptions
have been stated and controlled.

For physical mutations, the harness
uses an actual permissible effect
seam: model guarded submit, real
route/authentication dispatch,
host-selected writer, generated
browser-origin command, emitted
and served client asset or real
DOM target/adoption. A browser test
that manually inserts
=__gesso_live_optimistic_command=
exercises the server protocol
only; it is not the real
browser-to-command acceptance
oracle. Injecting a fake
submitted transaction receipt
does not establish an actual
XTDB observation. Separate
tests may deliberately exercise
synthetic payload validation,
but they report that narrower
boundary.

*** Oracle ownership and prohibition of post-hoc credit

The mutant's returned report, exception
or output value is *not* its own
independent success oracle. A
checker-origin verification result
can justify its stated internal
judgment; whether a forbidden
artifact was issued or a physical
effect occurred requires an
independent collector at the
relevant trusted boundary.
For example, an instrumented
writer sink must observe whether
a RequestAssignment was mutated;
an unrelated test-local boolean
=:effect-observed? false= supplied
by the mutant is not evidence.

The runner must distinguish all of:

- *Prevented:* admission or effect gate
  rejected before prohibited construction,
  submission, disclosure, acquisition or
  adoption, and a qualified independent
  observer establishes its absence
  within the declared observation window.
- *Detected after effect:* a checker
  accurately reported an inconsistency
  after an actual forbidden effect.
  This is useful diagnostics, but fails
  a policy whose obligation was prevention.
- *Unknown/incomplete:* the collector
  cannot establish whether a write,
  browser update, transport command
  or physical submission occurred,
  or the evidence retention horizon
  expired. Absence of a report or
  =nil= is not proof of non-occurrence.
- *Correct positive:* the legitimate
  original source was admitted and
  executed through the same relevant
  path with an independently observed
  permitted result.

The first enforcing gate can be rule
typing, proof kernel, required-source
closure, dependency composition,
assembly/preflight, trusted ingress,
atomic model writer, installed plan
or browser effect resource. A
negative test must exercise *the
earliest actual applicable one*
under the declared profile, not
force every failure into a
generic proof error. Conversely,
a properly rejected abstract
mutation cannot claim that the
XTDB writer was tested at all.

A corpus-specific exception from the
test harness is an infrastructure
event unless the expected check
genuinely comes from the production
boundary being exercised. Unexpected
errors and console failures are not
suppressed to make a browser test
green. The harness proves no absent
behavior for physical paths that its
instrumentation did not cover.

*** Representative case data and runner obligation

A finished framework can expose a
declarative corpus runner without
making application developers
write proof terms. The following
is a *conceptual fixture schema*,
not an existing Gesso API or
a set of guaranteed exported
namespace functions:

#+begin_src clojure
{:case/id :organization/stale-claim-certificate
 :baseline/ref :humanhelp/request-claim
 :profile/ref :humanhelp/checked-conditional
 :injection {:at :certificate/compose-candidate
             :change :organization/O14-to-O15
             :candidate :old-claim-rules-C21}
 :claim/ref :request/claim-eligible
 :required-boundary :source-dependency-composition
 :expected {:status :rejected
            :reason :semantic-dependency-mismatch}
 :must-not {:admit :old-Claim-executor
            :perform :request/claim-incorporation}
 :independent-oracles
 [:fresh-original-source :issued-handle-registry
  :qualified-writer-sink]
 :positive-control/ref :humanhelp/repaired-claim-C22}
#+end_src

The corresponding production-path case
can instead exercise a cache miss and
fresh elaboration of unchanged C21,
expecting unknown removed field or
another predeclared earliest genuine
source failure. Both must establish
that old C21 is not installed. An
unchanged source/name with a changed
opaque implementation must have a
*different* strong-realization
mutant: valid abstract proof reuse
does not authorize the new physical
writer without qualified binding.

R4's conceptual runner and
=:mutant/id=, =:baseline=,
=:mutate=, =:exercise= and
=:expect= declarations remain
a useful design precedent.
The implementation may choose
different public data names.
Required behavior is not dependent
on those exact identifiers.
A faithful runner reconstructs
fresh baseline source for each
case, verifies its valid
control first, exercises the
mutated source at the declared
boundary, and collects separate
checker and independent
artifact/effect evidence.
It compares the result against
the *predeclared* oracle and
emits a stable witness of
where the mutant was rejected
or deliberately accepted.

For readability, one schematic
outcome record is:

#+begin_src clojure
{:case/id :projection/missing-helper-knowledge
 :baseline {:status :accepted
            :evidence/ref baseline-evidence}
 :actual {:status :rejected
          :boundary :choreo/use-site
          :reason :knowledge-not-established}
 :independent {:issued-invalid-plan? false
               :observed-unauthorized-effect? false
               :scope/ref inspected-boundary}
 :disposition :correct-rejection}
#+end_src

Such a record only warrants the
disposition if independent
observation is genuine and the
scope is appropriate. An arbitrary
map containing the same fields is
not proof that the runner executed.

*** Positive, accepted and conditional controls

An adversarial suite is incomplete
without successful constructions.
For each injected defect, the
baseline is independently rerun
through the same supported path.
The corpus also requires:

- semantically unchanged source
  formatting or unordered-map
  entry order that may reuse a
  qualified abstract proof while
  refreshing relevant diagnostics;
- a legitimate new Organization
  closed-enum policy and fully
  repaired Claim C22 whose checked
  dependency closure is accepted
  rather than rejecting all
  interface evolution;
- a coherent application-owned
  age/approval policy change
  correctly classified as
  *accepted by design*, separate
  from independent product policy
  review and release acceptance;
- a trusted opaque model
  implementation permitted
  explicitly under one conditional
  profile with its premises intact,
  contrasted with an inadmissible
  strong profile requiring
  evidence that is not present;
- non-vacuous initial states,
  enabled Claim/Unclaim/Reassign,
  real eligible Create and the
  chosen positive browser paths
  under current model authority;
- actual command C42 replay,
  rightfully rejected new
  incompatible command,
  truthful submitted-unknown
  handling, creator-local S,
  remote advisory R and one
  scoped explicit Refresh;
- benign incidental code/asset
  changes that do not require
  rebuilding unrelated
  abstract theorems, alongside
  invalidation of affected
  installation correspondence.

Positive product gates remain
independent from proof/construction.
Removing Reassign from both the
source catalog and generated
model may leave a safe reduced
machine while failing HumanHelp's
required user capability. A
checker that refuses all Claim
attempts cannot satisfy a
positive Claim oracle. A
successful Claim pilot cannot
complete Part VIII's unselected
response-flow product decision
or other independent gates.

*** Independent semantic and physical conformance

Differential conformance compares
truly separate semantic
interpretations where practical,
rather than two wrappers calling
the same shared buggy evaluator.
For finite propositional checking,
a separately implemented Boolean
valuation oracle can distinguish
a semantically invalid accepted
step; it cannot establish theorem
truth of the opaque business
predicates represented by atoms.
For typed rules, the independent
denotation needs to preserve
presence, nil, nominal types,
short-circuit order and exact
reader footprints. Tests of
normalization must actually
execute the source and normalized
forms over discriminating
input states, not merely
compare their pretty printing.

Where a typed/rule mutation
changes the proof statement,
the test must show a witness
that activates its altered
meaning or demonstrate the
specific static rejection.
A mutation that never changes
the evaluated predicate is
not counted as a meaningful
semantic disagreement. A
proof checker may reject
semantically valid but
unprovable statements under
its selected limited rules;
that is an honest
unsupported/unproved status,
not evidence that the
formula is false.

Transition and induction
oracles need complete declared
initializations, relevant
state assignments and
operation cases. Finite search
reports actual bounds,
visited states, truncation
and whether a counterexample
is reachable under the exact
abstract model. A model
counterexample gives a
reproducible abstract trace,
not a physical XTDB history.
A solver that times out or
sees no states must not
report invariant preservation
as an unconditional theorem.

For installed host/XTDB and
browser tests, the corpus
records a qualified
environment version,
source/asset/plan and
service generation, actor,
command, application
declaration, expected
source-to-physical binding
and actual independent
observation. Tests should
cover concurrent guarded
RequestAssignment Claims,
changed Membership,
adversarial routing/writer
bypasses, valid durable
replay and lost result,
real generated browser
command, settled and
unknown UI, and actual
target-specific OOB
completion or failed
installation. Causality
and source completeness
remain conditional until
qualified evidence actually
establishes them; matching
transaction keys, ledger
rows and cards can be
mere co-observation.

Physical safety and
qualified progress must
have separate oracles.
A lost SSE invalidation,
missing outbox worker,
retired browser lease
or refresh-denied remote
viewer can satisfy one
safety proposition while
leaving a bounded recovery
or environment-progress
obligation open. The
expected positive behavior
follows the *selected*
HumanHelp Live/Refresh
policy, not automatic
whole-board convergence
invented by the harness.

*** Reporting, audit and completion boundary

A reproducible corpus report
preserves case ID,
original and mutated
source identity, profile,
injection point,
expected/actual structured
disposition, checker and
independent observation
origin, first enforcing
boundary, positive control,
tested semantic/provider
versions and relevant
source/test evidence.
It distinguishes missing
case coverage, cases
unsupported by a checker,
incomplete executions,
deliberately accepted
application policy,
correctly caught malformed
programs, property
counterexamples and
physical effect failures.

A published mutant
rejection score may help
track regression in this
specific corpus. It must
not call an unsupported
feature success, infer
checker soundness, prove
that every possible policy
branch was examined, or
convert a collection
of bounded physical
diagnostics into a
universal refinement
theorem. The independent
root report ties
the particular claim
and evidence to the
source/host generation,
premises and product
gate that they actually
qualify.

The corpus can be
incrementally expanded
as Gesso grows. Its
acceptance criterion is
*meaningful discrimination
at actual trusted
boundaries*: correct
negative cases reject,
correct positive cases
remain usable, and
conditional/unsupported/
untested cases retain
honest scopes. No
future source addition,
test refactor or
cached summary may
silently weaken a
predeclared case's
expected guarantee.

** Developer workflow and completion criteria

Gesso's assurance architecture succeeds only when ordinary application
development remains *source-first, declaration-first and repairable*.
The developer owns the intended business policy, public model contracts,
authoritative operations, Choreo, views and application assembly. Gesso
owns the mechanical elaboration, scoped proof terms, required obligation
inventory, checker/issuer bookkeeping, dependency identities, projection,
derived plans and intelligible root assurance reports wherever its
declared semantics can actually derive them. A developer must not
maintain an independent TLA+/Quint/Recife/Lean program merely to use
ordinary Gesso guarantees, copy transitive fingerprints into models,
manually assemble proof DAGs or mint checker-issued handles.

The full Clojure language remains available for ordinary implementation.
The closed, typed reasoning fragments are deliberately narrower than
arbitrary computation and carry executable semantic interpretations.
Where full-language code is opaque, its explicitly scoped implementation
contract enters the same ordinary assembly path without pretending that
Gesso has proved all of the function body. A user may choose a stronger
profile requiring more independent correspondence; the system reports
exactly what evidence is missing rather than silently granting it.

*** Developer-facing construction, feedback and ownership

The normal successful experience is conceptually:

#+begin_example
source-owned model schemas, rules, operations, choreography,
views, assets and application construction
                 |
                 v
             Gesso assembly
                 |
       +---------+-----------+
       |                     |
  source invalid       source admitted under profile
       |                     |
  typed first         independently checked local
  blocker and         judgments + complete source-
  repair context      derived obligation/assumption ledger
                             |
                         issued compatible
                         semantic/runtime products
                             |
                         host/asset installation
                         and current effect gates
                             |
                         claim-scoped root report
                         + independent product tests
#+end_example

This is a sequence of *semantic responsibilities*, not a required
single compiler pass or a promise that every step is statically
provable. The source-to-host and effect boundaries have independent
evidence owners; a green source report alone does not install code.
Likewise, browser and transaction execution can succeed while a
stronger proof or source-coverage claim remains unestablished.
Optional diagnostics may be computed and cached, but cannot alter
issued runtime transitions or grant authority after plan admission.

For an ordinary user, routine IDs, strings, maps and Clojure values
should not need hand-wrapped nominal/admission records at every
expression. Typed wrappers and opaque issuer-registered products
belong at the relatively few boundaries where a same-shaped raw
value would break a real semantic or authorization invariant.
The framework constructs those wrappers when it can; the developer
receives stable diagnostics when it cannot. Manual creation of a
similar-looking map is not a substitute for an admitted result.

The public workflow accepts explicit contracts for business facts
only an application can own. It distinguishes a model assertion,
a checked proposition, a conditional theorem with open premises,
a physical authorization/observation, and an installed application
capability. Declaring “this Membership is eligible” does not prove
that a present Request writer checked it; qualified production
authority still belongs to the model and installed trusted host.

*** Readable valid, invalid and conditional examples

The following is *schematic Clojure authoring notation*; it
illustrates the desired contract without freezing exact macro
spellings or asserting currently exported functions.

#+begin_src clojure
(rule claimable?
  (and (= request.status :open)
       (has-role? current-user :helper)))
#+end_src

With admitted RequestStatus and role sources, this can be an
intrinsically well-typed rule. It is not, by itself, the complete
HumanHelp Claim policy: current Membership, RequestAssignment
cardinality, Organization/Location association and actual writer
guards remain required by the governing public model contract.

A malformed use is:

#+begin_src clojure
(rule claimable?
  (< request.status 10))
#+end_src

No numerical ordering exists merely because RequestStatus is
represented using a host-language keyword. The source checker
reports the operator, actual nominal types, selected rule,
required versus supplied facts, and the earliest blocked
downstream artifact, without inventing a different policy.

A well-typed rule can also be *inadmissible at its use site*.
A helper browser may not branch on a private authoritative
=Request= review fact until the required role-local knowledge,
provenance, disclosure and program-point conditions hold.
Passing intrinsic type checking does not create a browser
observation or an authorization to disclose the fact.

If upstream Request schema S18 removes a status variant
required by rules certified against S17, the new schema
may be coherent while the *old dependent* proof/operation/
Choreo/plan is stale. Construction rejects the mismatch
at the first supported source/dependency boundary. A
checked compatibility bridge or a re-elaborated valid
rule may repair it; copied old signatures, names and
fingerprints cannot.

A same-shaped ={:valid? true}= or ={:checked-result true}=
map is never an issued rule or application certificate.
A fabricated derivation with a missing premise fails
its actual independent proof checker. A genuinely
accepted conditional Claim certificate may still
carry a named opaque Organization callable, XTDB
atomic-guard, external provider or deployed-route
correspondence premise; those are not silently
upgraded to truths or hidden from the root report.

The developer's repair options for an unsupported or
unestablished strong goal are specific: correct malformed
source, provide a supported derivation/evidence mechanism,
give a properly qualified explicit premise under a
profile that permits it, change the requested *named*
profile/claim with visible consequences, or revise the
actual business rule with application-owner authorization.
The diagnostic does not advise simply adding an
assertion of the failed theorem, swapping a trusted
principal for a browser parameter, or ignoring an
unresolved physical writer.

*** Source ownership and derived artifacts

Each stage has an accountable producer/consumer. Public
domain/model contracts and policy decisions belong
to application model authorities; source normalization
and required-judgment derivation belong to the specified
Gesso semantics; proof checking belongs to the small
kernel or dedicated checker with named assumptions;
issued products belong to the admitted source/profile
and dependency generation; actual routing and asset
adoption belong to the trusted installation context;
transaction and browser effects belong to their
actual enforcing physical boundaries.

An application builder derives the complete *declared*
closure, does not require the user to reconstruct
transitive dependency hashes, and differentiates
source-side completeness from independent physical
writer/host inventory and production source binding.
When source or policy changes, affected abstract proofs,
runtime plans, implementation correspondence and
installed resources are invalidated according to
their own scopes rather than conflated into one
namespace-wide success bit.

An unsupported opaque Clojure branch may be a valid
explicit implementation premise for one profile
and fail a stronger checked-causality or all-writer
profile. A module exposing the same named public
interface but a different callable cannot inherit
unverified previous implementation evidence.
The developer sees both which proof is still valid
and which physical assurance requires requalification.
A policy-intent finding from a human/heuristic/LLM
reviewer remains advisory until the application
owner deliberately changes the source-owned rule.

*** Compositional milestone acceptance contract

The framework's compositional-certification milestone
requires *all* of the following independent gates.
A gate is marked complete only with a declared
positive control, adversarial near-neighbor,
actual checker/host evidence and a source/profile
scope that the test exercised.

1. *Precise source semantics.* Supported rule,
   typed value/reader/effect, relationship,
   operation, Choreo and proof fragments have
   executable, versioned syntax, interpretation
   and checking judgments. Optional absent versus
   present nil, nominal enums, short-circuit
   branch refinement, reader footprints, frames,
   integer/codec limits and source normalization
   have discriminating conformance witnesses.

2. *Complete original-source obligations.*
   Construction independently regenerates
   required initialization, invariant,
   operation/base/step, branch, knowledge,
   dependency and positive-path obligations.
   A structurally valid reduced proof DAG
   missing a difficult Unclaim/Reassign
   case cannot establish the original claim.
   Declared source coverage and actual
   physical writer coverage remain separate.

3. *Real checked issuance.* Kernel/dedicated
   checker conclusions are bound to their
   exact original subject, inference
   semantics, checked dependencies and
   evidence class. Forged report/maps,
   constructed handles, incomplete
   proof packages and fake rule tags
   cannot issue the requested product.

4. *Conditional premise accounting.*
   Premises propagate per *used claim*,
   with issuer, actor, scope, source,
   knowledge, time and implementation
   applicability. Genuine discharge
   uses checked evidence/typed
   substitution and inherits the
   replacement's remaining conditions;
   no trusted assertion is promoted
   by matching labels.

5. *Opaque full-language integration.*
   Ordinary Clojure implementation
   remains usable through declared
   contracts in the same authoring
   path. The source audit identifies
   checked closed subsets, explicit
   opaque implementations, actual
   detected semantic-policy escapes
   and uninspected decision paths,
   without assuming absent policy
   where no inspection occurred.

6. *Correct composition and reuse.*
   Exact semantic/proposition,
   implementation, installation
   and runtime identities remain
   distinct. Changed upstream
   commitments invalidate affected
   consumers; permissible bridges
   are checked and directional.
   Currentness comes from the
   trusted consuming assembler,
   not a caller's old mutually
   matching graph and source.

7. *Distributed use correctness.*
   Intrinsic well-typedness is
   separately checked from
   point-indexed knowledge,
   provenance, authority,
   optional refinements,
   observation/basis and
   correct role-local
   Choreo projections,
   with explicit unknown/
   recovery alternatives.

8. *Production realization and
   authority.* Checked source
   connects to the actual issued
   executor, trusted server
   route, model writer,
   installed source/asset
   and browser plan with
   named qualified premises
   or authentic physical
   correspondence evidence.
   Pre-effect enforcement,
   post-effect detection,
   co-observed records
   and actual causality
   retain different
   claims. Provider
   assumptions remain
   versioned and scoped.

9. *Real HumanHelp Claim pilot.*
   Its root includes public
   production Request,
   RequestAssignment,
   Membership/Organization/
   Location, Claim rule,
   required invariants,
   operation/Choreo,
   helper/authority
   projections, plan,
   assembly, installed
   handler/browser, atomic
   C42 result, selective
   card adoption and
   independent positive
   user outcome.
   Two-helper contention,
   Membership revocation,
   lost response, historical
   replay and one-primary
   safety have qualifying
   positive/negative
   evidence. A toy proof
   fixture cannot pass
   this gate.

10. *Independent product demands.*
    The full HumanHelp
    proving application
    keeps all Part VIII
    user-capability and
    fourteen completion
    gates, including real
    eligible Unclaim,
    Mark-on-the-way,
    Complete, Cancel,
    manager Reassign
    selection, creator-local
    Create, remote advisory,
    one explicit Refresh,
    continuity and the
    separately selected
    response interaction.
    A completed Claim
    proof milestone
    does not silently
    complete this
    independent product
    acceptance program.

11. *Adversarial conformance.*
    The mutation corpus
    has fresh valid baselines,
    isolated source/evidence/
    installation/runtime
    perturbations, predeclared
    expected results,
    independent prohibited-
    artifact/effect oracles,
    actual first boundary,
    stable diagnostics and
    unambiguous incomplete/
    unsupported statuses.
    Reject-all checking,
    infra failures and
    unobserved effects
    cannot be scored
    as success.

12. *Usable developer output.*
    Ordinary source derives
    the checked artifacts
    without proof-assistant
    bookkeeping. Error
    reports are repairable,
    privacy-conscious,
    source-relative and
    correctly distinguish
    malformed construction,
    model counterexample,
    stale dependency,
    unsupported analysis
    and coherent but
    suspicious product
    intent. The generated
    root report exposes
    every relied-on guarantee,
    checking boundary,
    open assumption,
    actual tested/physical
    evidence and incomplete
    independent product gate.

These are intended final-framework
acceptance *obligations*,
not an assertion that
a present Gesso release
already passes them.
Different milestones can
complete at different times;
the report distinguishes
their result classes
and cannot advertise
total completion on
the strength of a
subset or a successful
single browser scenario.

*** Root report, release decision and open results

The root report is a
readable source-derived
inspection of an admitted
construction, not a
caller-writable admission
token. It must let a
reviewer answer:

- What exact application/
  source/claim/profile
  and current generation
  were selected?
- Which original producer
  declarations and
  checked exported semantic
  interfaces justify each
  relied-on guarantee?
- Which mandatory proof/
  source-coverage cases
  passed, failed, remain
  unsupported or were
  not attempted?
- What conditional premises
  were inherited, which
  were genuinely discharged,
  which remain trusted,
  and who owns their
  qualification/expiry?
- Which plans, handlers,
  model writers,
  physical source/assets,
  transaction observations,
  browser effects and
  deployments are actually
  bound or only asserted?
- Which independent positive
  product capabilities,
  races, retries, errors,
  recoveries and remote-
  acquisition rights
  were tested, missing
  or unavailable?
- What first blocked a
  stronger requested claim,
  what dependent artifacts
  were not admitted,
  and what legitimate
  repair/verification
  options remain?

The root does not turn
ordinary checked
schematic rules into
instance-specific
Membership authorization.
It cannot treat HTTP
success, SSE notification,
a pinned domain record
or a current Request card
as a theorem of command
incorporation. Nor may
a successful real
browser acceptance test
forge a missing proof
kernel theorem. Source,
physical and product
evidence are separate
columns of the
same inspectable
construction, not
a single =certified?=
value.

The milestone does
*not* demand a universal
proof of arbitrary
Clojure bodies, XTDB
internals, HTMX,
the JavaScript engine,
the JVM or the
unbounded real network.
For strong claims
that rely on them,
it demands precise
qualified premises,
source-to-physical
relations, checked
or tested scopes
and the appropriate
runtime enforcement.
External formal
metatheorems about
proof rules and
universal refinement
results may strengthen
the root later;
until then the report
cannot invent them.

A release process
checks that every
selected mandatory
gate has its applicable
issued evidence and
that permitted open
premises are honestly
accepted under the
chosen profile.
When a needed
guarantee is missing,
the stronger named
release claim fails
closed. A separately
requested weaker
claim may be usable
without inheriting
the stronger label,
physical rights or
false product
completion.

** Compositional certification invariant

A certified Gesso construction exports *only* the
propositions warranted by the admitted source,
their checked semantic judgments, independently
required obligation/dependency closure, actual
proofs or dedicated checker results, and
explicitly attributed remaining premises. A
raw declaration, normalizing digest, source
filename, copied =valid?= field, test
report, same-shaped Clojure map or
uncorroborated host artifact never
becomes an issued certified
category by resemblance.

The full Clojure host language remains available.
Closed typed semantic fragments have precise
executable meanings; opaque functions enter
through explicit, source- and implementation-
scoped contracts with their assumptions
visible. Policy correctness is not inferred
from a well-typed expression: a coherent
business choice can still be wrong by
product intent. Mechanical invalidity,
counterexample, unsupported checking
and advisory review therefore remain
different conclusions.

Intrinsic typing, source-derived obligation
completeness, guarded transition/induction,
finite-model checking, distributed
knowledge/provenance, valid Choreo
projection, issuer admission,
source-to-implementation/installation
correspondence, runtime actor/transaction
authority, observed browser adoption
and product acceptance are distinct
judgments. They compose through checked,
directional dependency and evidence
interfaces without silently upgrading
one into another or erasing open premises.

Justification dependencies are well
founded; implementation binding,
installation and runtime occurrence
have their own independently
qualified edges. Source changes
invalidate affected dependents
and may require checked compatibility;
implementation or resource changes
can invalidate physical evidence
while leaving an abstract theorem
intact. Cached reports, previous
success, physical stamps and
conveniently similar outputs
cannot establish currentness
or extend a one-use effect right.

The Gesso proof kernel checks only its
admitted derivation language and
named semantic assumptions.
Dedicated checkers establish
only their expressly stated
judgments. Exact finite
checking, conditional
induction, controlled
physical experiments
and runtime effect
enforcement each
retain their actual
subjects and quantifiers.
No complete-looking
submitted DAG can omit
source-required cases;
no successful readback
automatically proves
transaction causality
or universal physical
refinement.

HumanHelp Request Claim is the first
substantial compositional
proving application.
Its typed public model
and assignment semantics
must connect through
Claim operation,
Choreo/projections,
ExecutablePlan,
ApplicationAssembly,
installed route and
asset, guarded model
writer, trustworthy
command-specific
outcome and permitted
browser acquisition
to genuine user-visible
adoption. An upstream
semantic mismatch
prevents stale
dependent construction.
An unverified writer,
unknown command,
stale browser target
or disallowed
assumption cannot
borrow proof
authority from a
neighboring layer.

The independent
HumanHelp product
contract—including
eligible operations,
selective local
Create, advisory
remote updates,
one user-permitted
Refresh, recovery,
continuity and
an explicitly chosen
response interaction—
is not replaced by
the Claim proof
chain. A meaningful
positive program
must remain usable
even as malformed
and unsafe programs
are rejected. The
root report exposes
all admitted claims,
unresolved boundaries
and independent
product evidence
so that developers,
release reviewers
and downstream
checkers can rely
on *exactly* the
guarantees earned
and no others.
* Part X — Formal correspondence and system boundaries
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: part-10-formal-correspondence-and-system-boundaries
:PART_REVISION: 10-20261108
:END:

Part X specifies when an assurance statement about Gesso's admitted
semantics can also be asserted about *the application that actually runs*.
Part IX defines claim categories, checked derivations, issuer-controlled
construction and assumption propagation; this part specifies the additional
semantic-transfer, host, transaction, browser, provider and deployment
relationships that give such claims a physical interpretation. One must
not equate successful model checking, correct assembly, real test execution
and complete production refinement.

Gesso uses ordinary Clojure/ClojureScript construction and implementation,
including opaque full-language functionality. Its supported closed
semantic fragments admit stronger mechanized judgments; opaque
implementations contribute named, scoped conformance premises.
The application and its current trusted models still own business
policy. A generated formal subject may strengthen a source-owned
judgment, but cannot substitute a newly handwritten, more convenient
application for the source or prove the current host installed it.

Single- and multi-node deployments implement the *same* application
semantics, protected operation and participant permissions. Host placement
and routing affect what correspondence, delivery, replay and failover
evidence is necessary, not what a Claim means. The specific distributed
architecture and acceptance cases appear in 10.16–10.19.

This is a timeless finished-system contract rather than a claim about
the implementation at any particular revision. Parts XI–XII own
independent completion and realization ordering. Every assurance
conclusion retains the claim dimensions and evidence classifications
of [[#req-assurance-classification][Part I]], the compositional
issuance boundaries of Part IX and the separate structural, physical
and product categories of [[#req-application-assurance-claims]].

** Semantic ownership and the scope of assurance

*** One application meaning, several checking mechanisms

The source-owned *executable semantic core* specifies those supported
state, operation, proof-relevant value and Choreo transition meanings
that Gesso can inspect. Abstract model subjects, emitted plans,
checked obligations and formal exploration derive from those admitted
definitions under versioned normalization and interpretation contracts.
The model need not use the same representation as a runtime program:
where the representations differ, their *directional correspondence*
is an independent proof/checking or explicitly qualified trust obligation.

An external formal model may be generated from the semantics, or a
separate implementation of the semantics may serve as an independent
cross-check. Neither receives an exemption from that obligation simply
because it bears the original operation name. A more independent
interpretation can detect common bugs, but then must show which exact
source meaning it interprets; reusing implementation logic can help
avoid drift, but creates common-mode risks. A trustworthy argument
cannot be built by freely choosing whichever interpretation passes.

The rejected pattern is:

#+begin_example
handwritten abstract model A -> proof of A
handwritten production machine B -> deployed application
(no checked relation between A and B)
#+end_example

The intended source-derived pattern is:

#+begin_example
original Gesso/application declarations and contracts
                    |
             checked interpretation
                    |
         admitted executable semantics S
           /            |            \
  issued runtime    generated      checked formal
  plans/operations  obligations    subject/proof
           \            |            /
           explicit correspondence and assumptions
                    |
    installed host, actual physical execution, observations
#+end_example

The diagram is a dependency picture, not one proof that every link
is already established. The issuer and trusted assembler reconstruct
the required declarations and proof obligations from the *original*
source. They may not accept an elaborator's conveniently reduced
operation/invariant catalog as a complete application theorem.
Part IX owns those original-source checks; Part VII separately
owns installed application closure and its physical limitations.

| Component | Governing responsibility | Boundary not established merely by invoking it |
|-----------+--------------------------+-----------------------------------------------|
| Source-owned executable semantic core | Defines supported transition and value/operation meanings | Actual server, XTDB or browser execution of those meanings |
| Normalizer and elaborator | Derive typed subjects, obligations, projections, plans and proof candidates from original declarations | Semantic preservation of every transformation or completeness of real deployed writers |
| Dedicated semantic checker | Establishes an expressly stated typing, projection, finite or guarded-transition judgment | Soundness for unrelated judgments or implementation fidelity |
| Small proof kernel | Rechecks admitted derivations from original proposition/subject and retained premises | Independent metatheoretic soundness, opaque business truth or runtime authority |
| External proof/model checker | Establishes the specific formal property under its selected semantics, bounds and logic | Identity/refinement of that formal subject with deployed Clojure/CLJS and providers |
| Trusted application assembler/host | Checks compatible issued products, routes, writers, assets and selected generation | Exhaustive discovery of external bypass writers or a theorem for all physical schedules |
| Runtime authorization and effect boundary | Enforces or authentically observes the particular principal, guard, transaction and browser effect | General theorem from one observed successful invocation |
| Independent conformance harness | Discriminates semantic implementations and exercises identified actual failure seams | Universal proof beyond exercised scope, or current deployment adoption without provenance |

These responsibilities can share implementation modules without
becoming a single evidence class. Running the same evaluator in two
wrappers may establish reproducibility, but does not independently
validate the evaluator. Conversely, a second independent evaluator
may discover a mismatch while proving neither version correct
outside the reference interpretation and tested domain.

A proof that the semantic Claim operation preserves one-primary
RequestAssignment cardinality is conditional on its initial state,
entire source-derived operation catalog, guard/frame interpretation
and other relevant premises. Applying it to HumanHelp additionally
requires correspondence to the *actual* protected public model
operation, its current transaction guard, other writers and
current installed caller. The rule does not become true for real
XTDB merely because the semantic operation was called =Claim=.

*** Proof transfer is a separate, quantified obligation

The claim about a formal subject, a checked derivation and the
claim about a runtime implementation have distinct quantifiers.
For example:

#+begin_example
S: admitted abstract states, events and transition relation
I: a selected implemented machine under a declared environment E
alpha: a checked abstraction of relevant implementation state/events

Abstract safety: every admitted S trace satisfies invariant P.
Realization safety: every relevant I trace allowed by E is
  related through alpha to an admitted S trace, including failure,
  concurrency, rejection and recovery observations.
Physical safety: P transfers to I only where the relation
  and all required implementation/environment premises hold.
#+end_example

This is a schematic proof obligation, not an existing Gesso user
API or a claim that the current physical relation has been proved.
The chosen simulation/refinement direction matters. A single
passing execution, bounded finite exploration, identical source
hashes or matching after-the-fact ledger fields cannot establish
the universal realization condition. Unobservable internal steps,
real operation outcomes, actor and command identities, installation
generation and failure cases need an explicit relation and
applicability envelope. Unknown effects and omitted bypass writers
remain genuine open obligations, not vacuous proof successes.

Progress/liveness requires separate fairness, availability,
retention, scheduling, continued participant and permitted
user-action premises. Proving that a safe terminal state is
reachable does not establish its eventual reachability for
every fair run. Physical safety must not depend on fictional
eventual delivery; a lost response may preserve a committed
transaction while the browser honestly remains unknown.

A checked external theorem can be reused under its exact
semantic assumptions while the compiled artifact, host route,
provider adapter or browser bundle changes. Such reuse does
*not* preserve a previous implementation-correspondence or
runtime-authority judgment. The consumer independently
requalifies each affected physical edge and retains the
same source-derived meaning across single- or multi-host
placements.

*** Evidence belongs to individual claims, not system labels

An assurance claim records at least its proposition and
quantifiers, normalized subject, proof/observation scope,
relevant source and generation identities, inference or
enforcement mechanism, open premises, dependency closure
and applicability conditions. A root report aggregates
heterogeneous claims without assigning one global
=:proved=, =:certified?= or confidence percentage.

The assurance classifications established in Part I remain distinct:

| Evidence class | What it can establish when qualified |
|----------------+--------------------------------------|
| Machine-proved / externally machine-checked | The specific formal conclusion under the formal interpretation, inference rules and assumptions |
| Kernel-checked | Validity of the submitted closed derivation under the stated proposition language and open premise set |
| Exact-finite checked | The stated finite subject and bounds were explored as declared, including non-vacuity and exhaustion information |
| Assembly-verified | The actual checked source/assembly and artifact relation at its named inspection/installation scope |
| Runtime-enforced | A named concrete premise was enforced at the actual trusted boundary for the relevant invocation or resource |
| Trusted | A specified external/opaque implementation or environmental contract is assumed within an explicit qualification envelope |
| Asserted | An application-owned proposition was declared but not established by that declaration |
| Tested | Actual qualified scenarios/observations support the named behavior over their exercised scope |

The words *conditional*, *bounded*, *historical*, *current*,
*installed* and *progress* qualify the proposition or its
applicability; they are not additional evidence mechanisms.
An issued nominal semantic product and a copied report shape
are not independent proof categories. A conditional liveness
theorem remains conditional; a test of a network partition
does not establish eventual fairness in untested schedules.

Each claim must separately expose:

- the source-derived obligation and original semantic subject;
- evidence offered and whether the responsible checker/physical
  gate genuinely accepted it, including independent provenance;
- inherited premises, which remain open, which were discharged
  through an admitted judgment, and which are accepted as trust;
- relevant finite bounds, physical trace/writer coverage and
  model-to-implementation abstraction assumptions;
- unsupported syntax, exhausted budgets, unavailable evidence,
  counterexamples, stale generations and their distinct outcomes;
- the selected profile's *admission decision* and any separate
  release/product completion requirements.

An unsupported proof fragment means the checker has not
established its claim; it does not mean the statement is
false. An actual model counterexample refutes the claimed
property *under the examined model and premises*; it is
not automatically a production XTDB trace. A source-checked
report may be accurate but still not be issuer-controlled
admission, runtime authorization or a durable transferable
certificate. The selected admission policy cannot turn
a failed mandatory proof into a trusted statement without
an explicit permitted change of claim/profile and
reconstruction of the resulting obligations.

A model operation's four outcomes
=:committed=, =:rejected=, =:already-incorporated=
and =:commit-unknown= are not these checking
dispositions. Nor are participant presentation
=:accepted=, =:rejected=, =:unknown= or
Part XI release-gate states interchangeable
with evidence classes.

*** Opaque host code remains useful and visible

Gesso must remain usable with arbitrary Clojure and
ClojureScript. Developers write policies and real model
implementations with normal host-language facilities;
they do not maintain a second handwritten specification
in TLA+, Quint, Recife or Lean. When such implementation
behavior is relevant to an assurance claim but outside
the closed language, it supplies an explicit
*source- and implementation-bound opaque contract*
and any checked or runtime-qualified premises the
selected profile requires.

At an opaque boundary the constructed application
records the declared typed input/output and failures,
effect/authority dependencies, read and write footprints,
required current actor and disclosure context, possible
external/provider interactions, callable/closure and
library/build/configuration applicability, and which
exported claims rely on the contract. Actual effects
and runtime guards are checked at the appropriate
enforcing boundary when the claim requires them;
a structural contract by itself proves neither
the code implements the policy nor that every
relevant branch or writer was discovered.

An independent theorem about pure command-identity
binding need not be discarded when the renderer
contains opaque formatting code unrelated to it.
An opaque Organization-policy predicate, however,
prevents claiming *that predicate's real truth*
from the small rule calculus without a qualified
bridge or visible premise. A raw XTDB writer
outside the admitted operation catalog can
invalidate a whole-domain invariant even if
all declared transitions preserve it. The
source completeness gate and actual writer
coverage are therefore separate evidence
subjects, not two names for one manifest.

An externally checked implementation theorem,
an actual authenticated runtime observation or
a sufficiently qualified provider contract may
justify a *particular* opaque premise at its
exact scope. Substitution/discharge follows
09.11's actual checked entailment and
premise-inheritance rules; a successful test
alone cannot silently become a general proof.
A changed callable, dynamically bound Var,
provider version or resource generation
requires rechecking applicability even if
the abstract interface remains textually
unchanged.

Semantic-policy review is a separate owner:
Gesso checks the rules that the application
declares and detects unaccounted implementation
policy only where inspection can establish it.
HumanHelp decides whether its real Membership,
Organization, Request and RequestAssignment
policy is desirable. The formal checker cannot
invent a missing helper-role business restriction
from a friendly function name. A genuinely
eligible Claim and its adversarial wrong-actor
neighbor are both required positive/negative
controls against a vacuous reject-all policy.

*** Acceptance and counterexample controls at this boundary

The finished framework must discriminate the
following paired cases without changing their
responsible evidence class:

- a source-generated abstract model and
  its corresponding production semantic
  evaluator agree on a discriminating
  operation; a separately handwritten
  model that drops an original Unclaim
  case cannot establish the original
  production claim;
- a genuine checked propositional derivation
  preserves its open premises; a copied
  =:kernel-checked= report, unsupported
  atom truth or circular assumption
  discharge cannot create a theorem;
- a bounded finite invariant check with
  nonempty valid initialization is
  reported under its exact scope;
  truncated exploration, empty/vacuous
  state space or a fabricated proof
  label is not universal assurance;
- a public Request/RequestAssignment
  Claim transition satisfying a
  source-derived one-primary invariant
  is accepted at its abstract scope;
  a hidden alternative writer or
  stale pre-read cannot inherit the
  corresponding physical safety proof;
- a source-issued handler, currently
  installed route and real generated
  browser plan have separately
  qualified correspondence; a
  matching stale source/asset stamp
  does not authenticate their deployment;
- a current authenticated helper
  performs an eligible Claim,
  while a browser-supplied
  helper flag, wrong-Organization
  principal or revoked Membership
  is rejected at the *actual*
  protected model/host boundary;
- a known historical command C42
  is reconciled without new incorporation
  after lost delivery; a present
  Request card alone cannot establish
  that particular past result;
- a permitted creator-local Create and
  one user-granted remote Refresh
  produce scoped physical adoption;
  SSE advisory delivery cannot mint
  another read or a completed DOM effect;
- a correct conditional progress claim
  exposes its fairness/retention/user-action
  premises; a timeout or one positive
  retry is not an unconditional
  liveness theorem;
- a physically safe single-node and
  multi-node execution preserve the
  same operation semantics; a lost
  router/interest registration and
  unqualified replay/gap failover
  cannot be called universally
  safe or convergent by reusing
  a static certificate.

Each oracle names its subject, positive
control, adversarial perturbation,
expected first checking/enforcing
boundary and needed independent
observation before execution. A
source checker cannot claim to
have prevented a physical effect
it cannot observe or gate, and
a physical diagnostic is not
retroactively an abstract proof.

** System-wide assurance targets
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: req-system-assurance-targets
:END:

The system-wide target matrix specifies *what would have to be true* of a
finished Gesso application, not an inventory of guarantees already proved
by any particular implementation. Each family has (1) an exact semantic
property over its admitted source subject, (2) a directional
source-to-runtime realization or trusted enforcement condition,
(3) an evidence method and quantification scope, and (4) at least one
independent positive and adversarial acceptance control. A theorem that
establishes only the first is still useful but must not be promoted
into the second by a common label or shared digest.

Part IX governs source-derived obligation completeness, issued evidence,
checked premise inheritance and application-certificate categories;
10.01 governs ownership and proof transfer. This section states
whole-system proof targets while leaving their detailed theorem
statements to 10.03–10.04, actual transaction/writer refinements to
10.05–10.09, external proof/abstraction boundaries to 10.10–10.12,
trusted host contracts to 10.13–10.15 and multi-node realization to
10.16–10.19. No parallel application-authored formal source is required.

*** System-wide claim/evidence matrix

| Claim family | Source-relative semantic target | Necessary production correspondence or enforcement |
|--------------+---------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------|
| Choreography and projection | Admitted global steps, role projections, permitted local traces and branch discriminators satisfy the stated global-to-local relation | Actually issue, load and run the admitted projected plans; preserve emitted/received payload, cause and identity at real transport boundaries |
| Knowledge, provenance and agreement | Each role knows and may use exactly its justified sources, observations and communicated facts at a given program point | Authenticate source, actor, permitted disclosure, observation scope/frontier and message identity; avoid promoting browser assertions |
| Values, schemas and typed rules | Supported operators, nominal values, optional/nullable states, guard refinements and closed variants follow their declared evaluation and typing semantics | Check actual input codecs and reader footprints; establish portable JVM/CLJS semantics for the selected subset |
| Authoritative operations and invariants | All required initializations and original source operations preserve every claimed invariant under guarded/frame semantics | Install the actual qualified writer; enforce current principal, transaction-local guards, command exclusion, atomic effects and completeness of protected physical writers |
| Progression, observation and consistency | Requirements join without weakening; only sufficient, provenance-correct evidence may discharge a scoped obligation | Qualify the actual authority/XTDB basis and projection coverage, not just a caller's witness or token; bind permitted acquisition to its result |
| Optimism and command outcomes | Provisional state has explicit ownership, command identity, settlement and honest unknown/supersession paths without increasing authority | Correlate real H1/H2 attempts with durable C42 history; protect server authority, final DOM adoption and scoped recovery |
| Browser adapter and effect resources | Portable transition rules preserve execution/resource ownership, stale callback exclusion, retirement and effect-admission invariants | Normalize real HTMX/browser events and recheck a current right *immediately before* managed physical mutation and its completion |
| Portable plans and generated assets | Same supported initial state, plan and admitted events yield equivalent semantic results within the declared language | Verify exact generated/served/loaded bytes, manifest/plan identity, supported codecs, CLJS/JVM boundary and current runtime installation |
| Application closure and capability coverage | Declared affordances have compatible source-to-success/rejection/unknown/recovery paths; independently promised product actions remain required | Ensure currently installed real routes, workers, model callables, emitted assets, response/render paths and dynamic outputs correspond to the admitted assembly |
| Authority and disclosure | Browser-origin proposals never become trusted principals, current role rights, command incorporation or read permissions by assertion | Authenticate protected writes and reads at the actual enforcing entrypoint using authoritative model, tenant and operation context |
| Conditional progress and selective adoption | Named command/observation/advisory/settlement obligations resolve only under specified fairness, availability, retention, quiescence and user-action premises | Supply qualified recovery and notification mechanisms, authorized acquisition and target installation; identify missing premise instead of inventing convergence |

Each source theorem/verification result has its own actor, operation,
state/trace domain, quantifiers, abstraction, open premises and
applicable source generation. Each physical row has a separate
installation, invocation, actual effect and observation scope.
A table entry describing a desired property does *not* discharge
the corresponding physical obligation. Part I's evidence
classification and Part IX's accepted conditionality must remain
attached to the individual proposition when a root report joins rows.

*** Choreography, knowledge and actual role realization

The global language has a closed inspectable transition system and
explicit declared effects. A checked projection preserves the
specified observable global/local trace relation for its supported
constructs, including branch knowledge and permitted hidden local
steps. It must not invent communication, consume a nonexistent
message, omit a necessary discriminator-producing event or allow a
role to act on a protected fact it could not know. Where a global
and local trace relation is many-to-one, the chosen simulation
direction, observation alphabet and acceptable stuttering must
be stated; replaying one convenient schedule cannot prove
all-schedules projection preservation.

A sender may transmit only data justified by its current knowledge
and authority. A receiver learns only the payload and provenance
actually delivered and admitted at its execution point. Local
deterministic computations add only justified results. An
asserted role or copied authoritative-basis stamp cannot
upgrade provenance. Correctness of an abstract communication
step cannot authenticate that actual transport bytes came
from the selected installed projected machine.

Agreement concerns specified facts, scopes and observation
frontiers, not equality of arbitrary timestamps, DOM shapes or
host placement. Two roles may have *different* valid observations
because access and privacy differ. A claim that their authorized
projections agree states which common facts they can legitimately
compare and what compatible authority/basis evidence supports
the comparison. An opaque remote provider or network delivery
assumption stays visible when required.

Representative controls: a helper projection branches after
receiving an admitted public decision, while a projection
branching on an uncommunicated private Organization fact is
rejected. A valid send/delivery witness preserves exact
command/message occurrence, while a copied source ID or
reordered receipt does not satisfy the same schedule.
The strong production claim additionally tests the *real*
emitted and installed plan, not merely an in-memory projection.

*** Types, rule use and portable value semantics

Schema validation, intrinsic typed-rule checking, distributed
use-site knowledge and runtime model-policy truth are different
judgments. A syntactically accepted field is not automatically
present; a present nil is different from absent; a role with
a typed =RequestStatus= value does not necessarily know it
at this program point or have permission to disclose it.
Short-circuit branch refinements and reader footprints
must preserve source evaluation order. A closed variant's
exhaustiveness claim applies only to the actually declared
versioned variant set, not all future or opaque states.

The portable subset explicitly specifies signed integer
precision/range, booleans, strings, nominal enums, absence,
nil, maps/sets/sequences, encoding order where meaningful,
branch exceptions and error classifications. A CLJ
operation returning an exact integer outside JavaScript's
safe numeric range does not become portable by silently
rounding or coercing it. The framework may reject such a
portable plan or use a specifically supported lossless
representation; it must not report JVM correctness
as evidence that compiled CLJS ran it identically.
Arbitrary Clojure model implementation can remain
server-only with typed/opaque boundaries.

Positive controls exercise both present-nil and absent
fields, branch-sensitive rule evaluation and matching
JVM/Node/Chromium results over a discriminating supported
corpus. Negative neighbors reorder a reader across
its guarding predicate, substitute numerical enum
ordering, change an integer at the exact portability
limit or claim agreement after a CLJS path never ran.
A finite differential test is evidence for the sampled
cases; universal portability requires a separately
qualified semantic/correspondence argument.

*** Authoritative incorporation, outcomes and progression

A public model operation owns the business transition.
The source-relative guarded-transition or induction
claim covers its original initial-state condition,
all relevant operations/invariants, simultaneous
writes, frame effects and closure premises. Its
production counterpart requires actual current
guard evaluation and the relevant protected
Request/RequestAssignment/Membership/Organization/
Location facts at the selected atomic XTDB boundary.
A pre-read from an earlier snapshot, a browser-supplied
role or matching transaction-shaped map does not
establish the transaction's internal prestate
or current authorization.

A real successful incorporation must satisfy the
qualified atomicity contract for domain changes,
canonical durable command result and publication
intent where the operation requires them. Actual
command C42 identity remains distinct from physical
attempts H1/H2, transaction receipt, current Request
state, DOM resource, provider basis and application
generation. A failure of H2 after possible H1
incorporation does not show C42 never committed.
Model outcomes =:committed=, =:rejected=,
=:already-incorporated= and =:commit-unknown=
must retain their history and meaning, separately
from presentation =:accepted=, =:rejected=
and =:unknown=. Replay under retention and
current disclosure rules resolves historical
incorporation without silently making a new Claim.

Progression algebra is conservative over genuinely
opaque provider bases. It may merge identical
requirements, retain incomparable ones and discharge
an obligation only with sufficiently scoped,
authority-qualified witness and actual projection
coverage. Arrival order, increasing-looking integer,
SSE notification or client-selected timestamp is
not proof of basis advancement. A read permission,
read execution, query result, DOM install, user
awareness and command-specific settlement are
separate events; no source proof can collapse them.

Positive controls include two real eligible helpers
racing to Claim the same Request with at most one
new active primary assignment, a durable C42
reconciliation after lost delivery, and a read
whose actual provider evidence discharges exactly
the named requirement. Adversaries include
stale Membership, two independent pre-read writes,
a fabricated TransactionKey or basis-advance
witness, and a current card misattributed to
C42 history. Bounded matching ledger/readback
is useful but not sufficient causal proof or
a physical-writer completeness theorem.

*** Optimism, real browser effects and resource ownership

Optimistic state represents a declared local
intent and is never itself authoritative
Request or assignment truth. Each provisional
trajectory has a stable logical command where
appropriate, distinct execution/physical
attempt and resource identity, actual
observation premises where required, and a
typed settlement/recovery policy for commit,
rejection, indeterminacy and newer current
state. A Create intent for an entity not yet
created need not invent a nonexistent entity
basis; its operation may require a distinct
parent/collection observation instead.
Current authoritative supersession does
not retroactively establish whether the
particular command committed.

The browser semantic adapter is the
source of supported transition and
effect admission rules. Each active
asynchronous effect is owned by a
specific execution/resource or a
declared shared owner class. An old
execution cannot act merely because
the same logical target identifier
was reused. Retirement revokes the
effect right before best-effort
transport cancellation or cleanup.
Real abort success is not necessary
for safety if the physical shell
correctly rejects stale callbacks.

The shell normalizes actual events
and must enforce current permission
not only when a callback is received,
but again *at the instant* of
managed DOM, HTMX/OOB, continuity
or transport effect. A response
HTTP 200 or =htmx:afterSwap=
for one target does not certify
completion of a different target,
multi-target batch or interrupted
installation. If an admitted
operation permits a partly applied
physical batch, its explicit repair
contract must preserve safety and
report which parts actually adopted;
one semantic instruction does not
make multiple DOM mutations atomic.

Fragment admission/coordination
requires a declared upper bound
for active and queued *logical*
slots under supported scheduling,
with separately specified handling
for retired physical requests and
metadata retention. A disconnected
transport, deferred callback,
shared fragment notification or
stale continuity owner cannot be
reclassified as current command
execution to evade the bounds.
Incompatible stale plans retire
and recover under the application's
source, acquisition and permission
contract; reconnect never grants
automatic remote board refresh.

Positive controls cover valid
target-specific installation,
late callback rejection after
owner retirement, duplicate
transport resolution, real
partial-OOB failure, and one
authorized user-Refresh
acquisition. Adversaries
reuse a DOM ID under an old
resource instance, defer the
real mutation until after
admission expires, or
silently refresh the remote
board on an SSE advisory.

*** Portable plans, build artifacts and runtime noninterference

A normalized =ExecutablePlan= and its supported
initial state/event stream have a declared
portable semantic interpretation. JVM,
compiled Node/CLJS and Chromium may
require distinct host adapters, but
within the supported subset their
semantic state transitions and
declared outcomes must correspond.
The claim does not require equal
wall-clock ordering, browser layout,
physical network schedules or
provider availability. An executed
Node harness does not substitute
for the real Chromium DOM/HTMX
effect path.

Executable artifact identity is
distinct from compatibility
identity and from proof-sidecar
identity. Build and startup
must relate source-owned
manifest, emitted executable
bootstrap, exact compiled
bytes and installed serving
generation. A deterministic
manifest or matching stamp
does not alone show which
bytes the real browser loaded
or that those bytes implement
the admitted semantics.
Source/build checking, actual
served/loaded artifact
observation and semantic
correspondence retain
different evidence owners.

Proof, diagnostics and external
formal sidecars are
*runtime-nonsemantic*. The
same admitted input, state,
plan and event should not
change its domain or
browser transition because
a proof report was enabled,
absent, cached or stale.
A sidecar can affect whether
a stronger *admission
policy* allows construction
but may not silently
steer an already admitted
machine through a
different semantic path.
Exact sidecar lookup
requires exact artifact
identity; a merely
compatible plan does
not borrow evidence
without its own checked
compatibility rule.

Useful controls compare
admitted execution with
and without optional
diagnostics and verify
no changed transition
outcome; reject a
copied manifest stamp
with mismatched
compiled bytes; verify
a real loaded
browser runtime
matches the current
authorized assembly
and that an old
suspended tab
cannot use a
retired resource.

*** Whole-application closure, capability inventory and authority

The required whole-application
closure joins *real*
rendered affordances,
source operations,
global Choreo,
role projections,
verified trajectories,
portable plans,
emitted/served assets,
transport envelopes,
trusted routes and
server executors,
public model
operations, outcome
mappings, progression,
authorized acquisition
and a renderable
successor for success,
rejection, unknown
and recovery paths.

Static application
preflight rejects an
unknown operation,
missing/incompatible
plan, route or
transport, stale
artifact, wrong
role or capability,
unbound server
operation, absent
model/acquisition
path, incompatible
identity or
undeclared dynamic
recovery. It does
not claim to know
which dynamic
Membership will
exist tomorrow;
instead it
requires the
necessary runtime
guards and typed
failure/recovery
branches under
[[#req-preflight-dynamic-handling-coverage]].
The actual installed
host and generated
physical response
must enforce
the admitted
path; a caller's
successful preflight
map does not attest
which route now runs.

Three checks remain
independent: closure
of *declared*
affordances, an
original application
inventory of
*required* product
capabilities (so
omitted Create/
Unclaim/Reassign
does not pass
vacuously), and
real installed
host/render/asset
adoption. A
raw HTMX control
is legitimate
in its explicitly
ordinary category,
but cannot
impersonate a
protected Choreo
operation or be
silently substituted
for a failed
semantic plan.

The browser may
propose operation,
canonical arguments,
logical command ID,
claimed observation
and correlation
metadata. It does
not provide trusted
authenticated
principal, current
Membership/Organization
rights, actual model
prestate, command
incorporation or
protected read/
subscription
permission. A
source certificate
changes none
of these.
The server
must bind the
real principal,
tenant and
operation at
the actual
trust boundary;
the public model
enforces current
protected policy
and output
disclosure.
Cross-layer
capability or
assertion inflation
must fail before
its privileged
effect.

The HumanHelp
positive acceptance
requires real
eligible Create,
Claim, Unclaim,
Mark on the way,
Complete, Cancel,
manager Reassign,
two-client board
continuity, creator-
local selective
adoption and
user-granted
remote Refresh.
The still-unselected
response-flow
product choice
cannot be filled
in by Gesso's
proof checker.
The independent
Part VIII gates
remain outstanding
until demonstrated,
even if every
declared operation
proof passes.

*** Conditional progress, fairness and multi-node scope

A progress or
convergence claim
states *which*
obligation resolves:
a provisional
command, historical
outcome, queued
advisory, required
read, compatible
basis agreement or
authoritative DOM
installation.
It names
the environment
premises used:
provider reachability,
eventual permitted
read, scheduler/
participant fairness,
required command/
outbox retention,
continued execution,
user action,
sufficient quiescence
and correct
replay/failover
where relevant.

A reachable terminal
state is a possibility,
not eventual
completion under
every fair
execution.
The existence
of a timeout,
Refresh route,
outbox entry or
reconnect
is not a
progress theorem.
Under HumanHelp's
selected explicit-
Refresh policy,
remote creation
or lifecycle changes
are advisory until
the viewer
grants acquisition.
A theorem
conditional on
user action must
not pretend the
viewer is obliged
to act. A
qualified recovery
system may
coalesce or skip
intermediate
advisory events
only when
authoritative
coverage,
acquisition
permission and
adoption contract
justify that
behavior.

One- and
multi-node
deployments
share these
semantic obligations.
Topology adds
physical registration
frontiers, node
health/failover,
durable invalidation
creation and routing,
lost/duplicate
delivery and
gap-recovery
premises. A
completed
single-node
safe Claim
does not prove
every distributed
schedule, and
a dropped advisory
does not
authorize a
background
collection read.
The selected
multi-node
implementation
must preserve
the same
authority and
participant
contract rather
than force
application
authors to
maintain
different
single-/multi-
node semantics.

Safety is not
contingent on
fairness or
eventual delivery:
on loss or
provider
failure,
the operation
remains typed
unknown,
unresolved
or rejected
for an
actually
established
reason. It
cannot invent
command rejection,
provenance,
permission or
whole-board
convergence.

*** Acceptance evidence and root-assurance reporting

A root report
for each family
identifies its
original source,
semantic
subject, named
quantifiers,
actual
checker/proof
mechanism,
finite/test
coverage,
open premises,
qualified
installed
host/provider
scope, source-
to-physical
correspondence,
first enforcing
boundary and
independent
positive/product
oracle. A report
describing a
source theorem
is not an issued
runtime
authorization
receipt.

A completed
assurance target
requires the
stronger
selected profile's
real mandatory
evidence; it
may retain
explicit
premises where
that profile
allows them.
A source proof
