may coexist with
an open
physical
obligation,
a working
runtime guard
may coexist
with an
unproven
kernel
meta-theorem,
and a passing
browser scenario
may coexist
with a missing
product action.
The report
must not reduce
these to a
Boolean
=:certified?=
or convert
timeouts,
unsupported
fragments and
uninspected
writers into
green
verification.

The targeted
evidence includes
static and
semantic-model
checks, independent
kernel/dedicated
checker validation,
exact finite/
formal theorem
artifacts,
source-to-issued
and source-to-
host correspondence,
actual guarded
XTDB and provider
observations,
JVM/Node/Chromium
adversarial
tests, source-
owned build/
runtime
assurance, and
positive HumanHelp
operation/product
acceptance.
Each remains
scoped to
what the
instrument
actually saw.
The detailed
proof/realization
plans appear
in 10.03–10.19,
not in a
second
authored
proof calculus
here.

** Framework theorem contracts

A Gesso theorem family is defined by its original source subject, a closed
executable judgment and interpretation, its domain and quantifiers,
conclusion, dependencies, admissible evidence, and named open premises.
Theorems are not inferred from a source file's name, a checked-looking map,
a compiled artifact, an observed happy path or the existence of a checker.
Part IX owns the canonical source language, proof judgments, issuance,
obligation closure and assumption-substitution rules. This part states
their *theorem targets and production transfer conditions*, not a second
proof calculus that application authors must maintain.

A family may have (1) a syntactic or semantic judgment checked for one
original subject, (2) a theorem about all judgments of that supported
language, (3) a source-relative conditional application invariant, and
(4) a further implementation/physical refinement claim. These conclusions
have different universes. Passing (1) does not prove (2), and (2) and
(3) do not prove (4). An implementation can produce true finite witnesses
without a general metatheorem; conversely, a proved checker metatheorem
does not establish that the deployed route invokes the checked executable.

The finished framework should derive these obligations from ordinary Gesso
model and Choreo construction, discharge only those supported by named
checking mechanisms, and retain every remaining premise in the exact
consumer claim. A partial/unsupported theorem can be useful conditional
evidence, but cannot silently satisfy a stronger selected profile.
Each family has an independent meaningful positive control alongside a
nearby counterexample, including cases that prevent a reject-all
implementation from qualifying.

*** Theorem inventory and the transfer frontier

| Theorem family | Source-level conclusion | Additional production/assurance boundary |
|--------------------------+-------------------------+------------------------------------------|
| Certified composition soundness | Provider guarantee entails precisely the consumer premise substituted at the admitted subject/scope, and remaining premises are inherited | Genuine issuer/checker origin and current implementation/actor applicability |
| Business-rule type and evaluation safety | Supported operations apply only to values admitted by their typed, presence-aware reader contracts and evaluate according to the declared semantics | Correct boundary decoding, real field values, portable runtime interpretation and opaque predicate conformance |
| Rule-use knowledge safety | A role's branch/action uses facts justified at that exact Choreo program point | Authenticated delivered observation, permitted disclosure and actual browser/transport event origin |
| Provenance safety | Source/authority labels cannot be strengthened without an admitted inference or observation | Trusted server/model origin and actual message/read lineage |
| Authority non-escalation | Untrusted browser or projected semantic artifacts cannot derive additional protected privileges | Current principal, tenant, model policy, command and protected read/write enforcement at actual effect boundary |
| Projection preservation | Relevant projected local behaviors satisfy the stated global trace/refinement relation | Issued/loaded plan and actual message, transport, scheduling and physical browser correspondence |
| Executable-plan provenance | Each issued managed plan is derived from a compatible admitted projection under exact source/dependency/version semantics | Built, served and loaded executable bytes and the deployed caller/target binding |
| Stale certificate safety | Incompatible original semantic dependencies cannot justify new certified consumers | Current trusted assembler, deployment generation, callable/asset versions and runtime resource validity |
| Progression preservation | Canonical requirements compose conservatively; only sufficient scoped evidence discharges them | Actual provider basis, authenticated read coverage, permission and correct installation |
| Browser semantic adapter safety | Permitted normalized transitions preserve execution/resource/effect admission and retirement invariants | Current physical effect permission, real HTMX/DOM behavior, deferred mutation and observed completion |

The evidence owner, domain, quantification and independent physical
requirements of a row must not be replaced by its neighbor's successful
report. The corpus in 09.15 and 10.02 supplies paired conformance families;
this section makes the theorem's antecedents, obligations and
nonclaims explicit. The stronger source-to-host refinement records and
physical writer arguments belong to 10.04–10.09.

*** Typed rules, presence, evaluation and atomic propositions

For every admitted *supported* typed rule R and environment E satisfying
R's exact reader and nominal-type contract, evaluation obeys the specified
operator semantics and either returns the declared result type or one
of the explicitly modeled failures. In notation, the target is:

#+begin_example
WellTyped(R, Gamma) and SatisfiesReaders(E, Gamma)
  => Eval(R, E) is a result allowed by the typed rule semantics
#+end_example

This is a family theorem only when quantified over all R and E in the
selected bounded/closed language. Checking a single R,E is an instance
result. Optional absence, present nil, short-circuit reader access,
branch-local refinements, integer/codec restrictions, nominal enums,
and exception/failure behavior are all part of that semantic domain.
An implementation that evaluates a guarded optional read eagerly is
not justified by its final Boolean value agreeing on other inputs.

Rule well-typedness does not establish business-policy truth. An
abstract typed atom may mean an application-owned predicate under an
explicit valuation; the small propositional kernel may reason from that
atom without proving the predicate's actual model implementation.
The *typed-proposition bridge* must separately relate each admitted atom
to the actual typed rule interpretation under the same original source,
binding environment, reader footprint and applicable assumptions.
Finite enumeration establishes agreement on its exact projected domain,
not universally for arbitrary input maps or real server snapshots.

The actual public Request and Membership/Organization models own
Claim eligibility. If a model's policy predicate is opaque Clojure,
its specified contract remains an explicit relevant premise until
qualified by an appropriate implementation theorem or runtime fact.
An application should not rewrite that policy in hand-authored TLA+,
Quint or Recife merely to get a checked result. Source-derived
translation or independent oracle checking must retain the real
public model's semantic subject rather than replace it with a
test-friendly policy.

*** Kernel entailment and proof-checker soundness

For a closed admitted propositional derivation D, named premises Gamma,
and conclusion P, the intended *logical soundness* statement is:

#+begin_example
CheckKernel(D, Gamma, P) = accepted
  => for every valuation v of admitted atoms:
       (v satisfies all premises in Gamma) implies v satisfies P
#+end_example

The statement assumes a versioned interpretation of the connective
language, well-formed source normalization, correctly scoped premise
references, and exact rule meanings. A checker must reject malformed
rule tags, forward references, substituted premises, incorrect
conclusions, incomplete source declarations, unsupported constructs
and circular proof justification before it can issue the relevant
derived category. Open premises remain open; an asserted atom is
not an axiom establishing that atom is true in production.

There are three separate evidence goals:

1. *One derivation:* reconstruct the original-source judgment and
   validate each step and its exact used premises. A truth table
   may independently check the claimed implication for that
   particular finite set of Boolean atoms.
2. *Inference-system soundness:* prove every admitted rule preserves
   semantic entailment, including all supported operands, parameter
   values, substitutions and source/normalization cases. Testing
   a few examples of each rule does not satisfy this quantifier.
3. *Concrete checker correctness:* establish that the actual issued
   checker, parser, normalization and evaluator implement the rule
   semantics the metatheorem concerns. A theorem about mathematical
   inference rules does not by itself prove the Clojure implementation.

No automatic hypothetical-context discharge, arbitrary typed-atom
truth, SMT arithmetic or classical inference may be presumed unless
that operation is in the separately admitted and checked language.
A later proof kernel extension must update its exact theorem and
versioned correspondence; the proof does not silently widen to
all Clojure expressions. Valid checked conditional arguments retain
their original Gamma rather than being converted to unconditional P.

*** Guarded transitions, frames and source-complete induction

For a normalized supported guarded operation T, the relevant theorem
connects an admitted before-state, input and after-state through the
actual typed guard, *simultaneous* assignment expressions and unchanged
unwritten fields (including optional presence). A checked transition
fact therefore has a specified relation, not an arbitrary pair of maps:

#+begin_example
T(s, x, s') :=
  Guard(s, x)
  and for each written field f: s'[f] = RHS_f(s, x)
  and for each unwritten field f: PresenceAndValue(s'[f], s[f])
#+end_example

This relation is defined over the selected source state projection.
It does not represent every XTDB document or every application writer
unless that additional relation and coverage are established.
For a selected invariant I, a full conditional induction target has
both a source-correct base and an operation-complete step argument:

#+begin_example
For every s: Init(s) => I(s)
For every original declared operation op and s,x,s':
    I(s) and T_op(s,x,s') => I(s')
Therefore: all reachable finite abstract states satisfy I,
  under the stated initial-state, catalog and semantic premises
#+end_example

The exact original initialization, operation and invariant inventory
must be independently derived from the source being certified.
A caller-supplied smaller catalog or structurally valid pruned DAG
cannot establish the source's full theorem. Satisfiable initialization,
enabled positive operations and relevant closedness tests are separate
non-vacuity/product obligations: a false Init or reject-all operation
set must not count as a successful HumanHelp application.

The theorem is abstract and conditional. Applying it to real
RequestAssignment one-primary safety additionally requires the
selected actual initial-state boundary, representation of real
Request/assignment status and relationships, transaction-local
current guard and atomic write semantics, coverage of every
relevant physical writer/initializer, preservation of its
unwritten fields, and execution refinement for real rejected,
committed, unknown and recovery outcomes. One captured XTDB
gateway submission or pinned readback can supply bounded
physical evidence while leaving universal causality,
physical writer completeness and backend assumptions open.

A real concurrent two-helper Claim with at most one new primary
is a necessary positive/adversarial physical test. It cannot
be replaced by two sequential model-checking inputs, nor can
one positive experiment prove the all-schedules invariant.

*** Certified composition, premise inheritance and stale dependence

If consumer certificate B uses producer certificate A to justify a
premise Q, sound composition requires a *checked* type/context/scope
substitution showing that A's exported guarantee entails exactly
the Q required at B's subject and observation/actor context.
The resulting conclusion inherits all still-open premises actually
used from A and B. A provider's trusted assumptions may be accepted
by a selected profile but cannot be reclassified as unconditional
guarantees to the consumer.

Proof justification dependencies must be well-founded; runtime
subscription, retry and recovery cycles do not authorize circular
proof references. Original-source-required obligations are separate
from a DAG's ordinary structural validity. Compatibility may allow
an unchanged abstract proposition under a revised interface only
through a directional checked bridge with its own premises and
scope; the new implementation or deployed asset still needs
current correspondence evidence.

Stale certificate safety follows from exact source and required
dependency compatibility, *at the current trusted consumer*.
A matching old certificate and old graph cannot attest current
source. An S18 Request schema may be intrinsically valid while
a Claim rule built against S17 cannot compose. Changed theorem,
checker semantics or obligation inventory invalidates relevant
proof applicability; a changed deployed callable, route, asset
or resource can invalidate physical applicability while leaving
a reusable abstract theorem intact. Mere string names and
hash equality are not either proof or live host authorization.

*** Rule-use knowledge, provenance and protected authority

Knowledge safety states that for every supported projected role,
at each admitted action or branch that uses fact F, the local
state justifies F's value, source, provenance and relevant
observation frontier at that *exact point*, subject to named
disclosure assumptions. A global Choreo rule's intrinsic typing
does not give every local role knowledge of every fact in its
global transition. Required communication, receipt, source
derivation and server authority are separate judgments.

Provenance safety forbids promoting client-supplied role
labels, a copied basis, generic message shape or an asserted
=:authoritative= field into a trusted model fact without an
admitted and actually satisfied inference/enforcement rule.
The receiver's learned knowledge is scoped to what was
sent, received, authenticated and authorized; privacy-aware
agreement does not require disclosing all facts to all
participants.

Protected non-escalation says that a browser-origin
operation proposal, argument, command identifier or
observed revision cannot *by itself* increase the
authenticated principal's capability to claim a Request,
read a protected collection or install authoritative
state. The installed server and public model
must bind actual principal, Request, Membership,
Organization/Location policy and permitted target
at the real trusted enforcement boundary. Even an
admitted abstract authority rule does not grant
a physical permission in the absence of that
enforcement or its qualifying trusted premise.

A pure reusable proof premise is not a linear/one-use
runtime capability. A one-Refresh acquisition grant,
browser execution lease, physical command identity
or active model authorization cannot be cloned
by substituting the same proposition in multiple
proof obligations. The theorem of logical
non-escalation and the actual effect-level
capability check have distinct owners.

*** Projection, lowering and real browser refinement

Global/local Choreo projection states a precise
relation between allowed observable global traces
and admitted role-local traces, with the declared
observation alphabet, causal partial order,
hidden local/environment steps and refinement
direction. For example, a global transition
may correspond to several projected internal
steps; their valid stuttering does not authorize
reordering protected message delivery, inventing
a branch discriminator or omitting an effect
visible to an observer. Both soundness and
completeness of projection are independent
properties when claimed; checking one
realization witness proves neither universally.

Executable-plan provenance then binds each issued
managed plan to the *admitted* projection and
exact semantic sources, lowering version,
declared data/command shape and source-required
dependencies. Semantic compatibility differs
from exact emitted executable-artifact identity.
A proof/diagnostic sidecar cannot steer the
already admitted runtime transitions, and
a valid projected plan need not be physically
loaded in a browser.

Browser refinement connects the portable
semantic adapter's state/event/effect
transition to the *actual* shell, HTMX,
transport, DOM and completion observations.
It must cover stale and duplicate callbacks,
resource-instance retirement, reused DOM
IDs, transport cancellation failure,
deferred physical mutations, partial
OOB installation, failed render and
physical effects occurring after a
callback was admitted. The physical
shell rechecks the current right at
the *effect point*, and may declare
repair for partial batches; it
cannot assume several DOM mutations
are one atomic operation.

A source-level adapter invariant
transfers to real execution only
under the appropriate complete
simulation/refinement relation,
current installed generated bytes
and physical permission/effect
premises. One tested Chromium
scenario is a valuable real
witness, not proof of every
possible browser schedule.

*** Progression preservation, stale observation and conditional progress

The source-level progression algebra
represents opaque authority bases
as obligations, not inherently
ordered timestamps or revisions.
Canonical requirement composition
is conservative: exact equal
bases may coalesce; distinct
incomparable bases remain
required absent trusted
authority-specific progression
evidence. A source-side
=:advances= shape does not
prove that a provider
actually advanced the
basis or that the
returned projection covers
the required scope.

Discharge of observation
requirement R by evidence E
requires checked E
provenance, actual basis,
authorized collection
scope, coverage and
real acquisition/adoption
where the consumer claim
requires them. A recent-
looking SSE advisory,
browser assertion, equal
entity card or faster
transport is not a
sufficient general
witness. Creator-local
Create S and remote
advisory R are
different observations;
one user-initiated
Refresh permits its
selected remote
acquisition only.

Safety is independently
required when progress
premises fail.
A command may be
committed yet its
participant legitimately
remain =:unknown=
after lost delivery.
Liveness/progress
theorems must state
which debt or provisional
state resolves, the
actual fair scheduling,
availability, continued
execution, retention,
authorized acquisition,
quiescence and any
necessary user action.
A trace refinement
allowing unlimited
internal stuttering
does not establish
that anything eventually
finishes. The existence
of a timeout, retry
route or reachable
terminal state is
not a fairness
argument.

The same semantic
safety and conditional
progress contracts
apply to single-
and multi-node
deployment. Router
placement, interest
registration frontier,
outbox durability,
replay/gap recovery,
node failure and
duplicate delivery
introduce additional
*physical*
refinement and
environment
obligations, not
new model authority
or a second
application meaning.

*** Claim-specific theorem report and acceptance controls

A source-relative
root report should
make each theorem
family inspectable:
original subject,
conclusion and
quantifiers, exact
domain/abstract
relation, proof
method and checker
version, source-
derived obligation
ledger, supported
premises, actual
evidence origin,
stale dependencies,
implementation/
physical transfer
assumptions and
independent
positive/product
tests. A report
is not itself
an opaque proof
handle or
authorization
receipt.

At minimum, a
relevant corpus
must distinguish:

- **Typing:** guarded
  optional/present-nil
  evaluation succeeds;
  eager unguarded
  reader, illegal
  enum ordering or
  unsupported integer
  form fails;
- **Kernel:** correct
  derived P from
  Gamma passes;
  forged inference,
  omitted premise,
  wrong source or
  copied =:valid?=
  report fails;
- **Typed atom:** a
  finite typed-domain
  agreement has
  its actual bounds;
  unexamined
  Clojure predicate
  is not declared
  universally true;
- **Induction:** complete
  source catalog
  and nonempty
  initial model
  preserve I;
  pruned Unclaim,
  vacuous Init
  or modified
  frame/guard does
  not certify
  the original
  application;
- **Composition:** a
  valid checked
  conditional guarantee
  substitutes with
  all remaining
  premises; a
  trusted assertion
  or circular
  evidence chain
  cannot discharge
  a theorem;
- **Knowledge:** a helper
  branch on an admitted
  public decision
  passes; an
  undisclosed private
  Organization field
  fails at the
  use site;
- **Authority:** a real
  eligible Claim
  passes current
  model enforcement;
  client role flag
  or a stale
  Membership
  cannot authorize
  a write;
- **Projection:** a valid
  communication
  schedule preserves
  its trace relation;
  a missing
  discriminator,
  reordered delivery
  or fabricated
  sender origin
  fails at the
  correct scoped
  boundary;
- **Plan:** a current
  issued and
  installed plan
  uses exact
  admitted sources;
  a copied
  artifact stamp
  or silently
  downgraded
  ordinary HTMX
  route fails;
- **Browser:** a current
  target owner
  completes a
  justified effect;
  retired callback
  or half-installed
  OOB batch
  cannot mark
  authoritative
  adoption;
- **Progression:** a
  qualified basis
  and permitted
  Refresh discharge
  their exact
  obligations;
  SSE arrival
  does not
  grant a
  whole-board read;
- **History:** committed
  C42 replay is
  reconciled under
  actual retention;
  current Request
  status or H2
  failure does
  not invent
  historical
  rejection;
- **Progress:** a
  specified fair
  recovery path
  may establish
  named
  conditional
  liveness;
  an unqualified
  timeout or
  unrequested
  user action
  cannot.

Each case records
a valid positive
neighbor, an
actual negative
mutation, its
expected first
checking/enforcement
boundary and
independent
evidence of
any claimed
physical effect
before the
case runs.
An incomplete
or unsupported
strong theorem
is not a
proof success;
a correct
negative
source rejection
does not imply
every untested
physical bypass
was prevented.

** Formal proof strategy and production correspondence
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: req-formal-production-correspondence
:END:

Formalization removes a *named* trust gap in the executable Gesso
semantics. The source-owned semantic core, original-source obligation
derivation, small proof kernel, specialized semantic checkers,
generated formal subjects, proof-producing elaboration and external
proof/model checkers participate in one correspondence architecture.
They are not alternative applications, proof certificates for
arbitrary Clojure, or a request that application developers maintain
a second handwritten TLA+, Quint, Recife or Lean system. A successful
formal result applies to installed software only through the separate
relation and premises actually justified at that boundary.

Part IX governs canonical judgments, source-complete derivation,
issuer-controlled admission, dependency evolution and premise
accounting. Sections 10.01–10.03 specify the one-source semantic
ownership and theorem quantifiers. This section defines the
*bidirectional correspondence and evidence-transfer discipline*.
10.05–10.09 own the selected transaction, guard, writer and
HumanHelp-specific realization obligations; they are not
preemptively proved by a formal correspondence report.

*** Source-derived correspondence record and two directions of traceability

For every formal claim whose guarantee is to be transferred,
the original-source authority and trusted consumer derive an
inspectable correspondence record with these distinct components:

1. The original admitted model/rule/operation/Choreo source,
   normalized semantic subject, required original initialization,
   operations and invariants, and exact versioned interpretation.
2. The formal encoding and proof obligation, quantification and
   environment domain, proof or model-check result, checker and
   translator identities, required evidence class and all
   remaining formal premises.
3. The proposed executable realization: issued operation and plan,
   callable/closure, route and model binding, compiled/browser
   artifact, assembly and selected installation generation.
4. An explicit representation/abstraction relation with *direction*,
   event observation alphabet, guards, state frames, permitted
   internal steps, failure and concurrency semantics, and the
   initial-state relation to which it applies.
5. For each transfer premise, its owner, original-source dependency,
   checked derivation, independent physical evidence or allowed
   opaque/trusted qualification, scope, invalidation conditions
   and current consumer policy decision.
6. Source locations, reproducible generation and checking
   instructions, privacy-appropriate counterexample translation,
   unsupported status and the first unestablished enforcing
   boundary.

The record supports **forward semantic derivation**:

#+begin_example
original Gesso/application model and Choreo declarations
                  |
         checked semantic interpretation
                  |
       admitted normalized semantic subject
            /                      \
   generated formal subject       issued operation/plan
            |                      |
    proof/check result        host/asset/model binding
            \                      /
       explicit relation, premises, and evidence
                  |
       qualified production transfer claim
#+end_example

It also supports **reverse traceability**:

#+begin_example
formal obligation, premise, or counterexample
                  |
   exact source/translation/correspondence identity
                  |
   originating model rule, operation, or Choreo step
                  |
   production binding, effect boundary, source location
                  |
   evidence class and still-open implementation obligations
#+end_example

Reverse traceability makes a proof result explainable and a
counterexample repairable. It does *not* prove the converse
inclusion of all abstract traces in real execution, nor
automatically prove that every production execution is
represented by the abstract model. A cached record, matching
digest, correct diagram or copied =:checked= map cannot issue
a certificate, prove an installed route, or authenticate an
XTDB transaction. Required closure is freshly derived from
the trusted *current original source*, not a successful
submitted subset or yesterday's matching graph.

*** Admission soundness, completeness, execution refinement and progress

The theorem claims have different directions and quantifiers.
Let S be the supported formal source semantics, A the actual
admission mechanism, I the installed executable under explicit
environment E, and alpha an abstraction from relevant I
states and observations into S:

#+begin_example
Admission soundness:
  For all supported x, A(current-source, x) = admitted
    => FormalJudgment(S, x, admitted-premises).

Admission completeness (separate, where promised):
  For all supported x satisfying the required judgment and
  independent admission conditions, A can admit x.

Execution safety transfer:
  For every relevant I/E execution starting in the related initial
  state, alpha maps its relevant steps/observations to a valid S
  execution, including the represented failures and concurrency.

Conditional progress transfer:
  Every relevant I/E execution satisfying named fairness, delivery,
  retention, continuing-execution and user-action premises meets
  the selected progress obligation, without forbidden divergence.
#+end_example

These are schematic logical statements, not Gesso API calls.
They leave the actual relation, allowed silent/stuttering
steps, observation projection and premise qualifications
to the admitted source and checker. Agreement over rejected
examples does not establish admission soundness. Refusing
every user operation may avoid some unsafe transitions
but fails required positive capabilities, and is not
admission completeness. Proof of an admitted source
does not mean the installed server invokes that source.

A safety simulation may allow unbounded internal stuttering
while transferring a safety invariant. It cannot thereby
establish liveness; a progress theorem must exclude the
relevant divergent executions under explicitly qualified
fairness and recovery assumptions. Failure of those
assumptions preserves safety and honest unknown outcomes.
Neither a timeout nor a reachable terminal state is an
unconditional eventual-settlement proof.

*** Worked Claim slice: same source, separate formal and physical obligations

The first proof-transfer pilot uses HumanHelp's actual
public production Request, RequestAssignment, Membership,
Organization and Location model interfaces, not a substitute
toy single-map Request with an invented helper field.
The domain owns the authorization and one-primary-assignment
policy. The browser supplies a Request argument, operation
proposal, stable logical command identity and perhaps
untrusted observed basis; the server supplies the
authenticated principal and current authoritative context.

A schematic correspondence *fixture* may have this shape.
Its keys illustrate record semantics rather than prescribing a public
Clojure API; the sample itself is not a checked certificate:

#+begin_src clojure
{:source
 {:operation :request/claim
  :domain-models
  #{:humanhelp/Request :humanhelp/RequestAssignment
    :humanhelp/Membership :humanhelp/Organization
    :humanhelp/Location}
  :semantic-subject :request/claim-O31
  :rules :request/claim-rules-C21}
 :client-proposal
 {:request/id :request-R17
  :command/id :command-C42
  :observed-basis :untrusted-client-observation}
 :trusted-invocation
 {:principal :authenticated-server-principal
  :request :current-authoritative-request
  :membership :current-authoritative-membership
  :organization :current-authoritative-organization
  :location :current-authoritative-location}
 :formal-claim
 {:subject :formal/request-claim-O31
  :proposition :one-active-primary-assignment
  :direction :source-induction-and-execution-refinement}
 :production-obligations
 #{:bind-command-to-principal-operation-and-request
   :check-current-request-and-membership-and-organization
   :enforce-one-primary-assignment-at-atomic-write
   :atomically-record-command-result
   :include-all-relevant-physical-writers
   :bind-issued-executor-to-installed-route}
 :evidence
 {:source-check :required
  :abstract-induction :required
  :installed-model-correspondence :open
  :atomic-tx-implementation :open
  :physical-writer-completeness :open}}
#+end_src

The fixture separates *admission correspondence* (the
particular source-issued Claim plan admitted by production
satisfies the intended checked semantic judgment) from
*execution refinement* (every relevant execution of the
actual installed Claim writer respects the specified
atomic RequestAssignment transition, its command record
and actual failure outcomes). A theorem for the
first does not imply the second. The formal tool
cannot authenticate caller-supplied model Vars, route
IDs, production node or a handwritten
=:installed-model-correspondence :checked= status.

A protected Claim transition may atomically depend on:

#+begin_example
current Request is eligible and still open
current Membership is active for the authenticated actor
Request, Membership, Organization and Location associations
  meet the real public model policy
logical command is bound to operation, Request and principal
one active primary assignment is preserved
domain changes and durable command result share the
  required authoritative transaction/commit contract
#+end_example

The allowed physical mechanism may be an appropriately
guarded XTDB transaction, a qualified conditional write,
or another independently justified atomic implementation.
The theorem needs the *same* relevant atomic boundary,
not identical source syntax. A pair of true pre-reads
followed by unguarded writes fails that obligation.
A command ledger/readback matching the post-state
can corroborate one observed history but does not
alone prove causation, the transaction-internal prestate,
all writer coverage, current actor validity or all
future execution traces. Missing physical evidence
remains an open premise or a failed strong profile;
it is never silently discharged by the abstract proof.

An adversarial implementation may add an unmodeled
priority restriction or take the helper identity from
browser-provided fields while its formal model still
shows the right atomic transition. These are different
correspondence failures: the former can omit concrete
behavior or required positive eligibility, while the
latter violates principal authority. Shared names,
hashes or tests of a happy path repair neither.
A real product acceptance control must demonstrate
the eligible Claim and correctly reject wrong-actor,
revoked-Membership and incompatible-command attempts.

*** Atomic formal actions create specific production obligations

Formal atomicity does not mandate a single thread or
node but does mandate a production correctness boundary
adequate for the claimed property. If a transition
treats current authority checks, domain state changes
and command-result recording as one atomic operation,
the implementation must justify that correspondence
and all external premises used. A process-local
one-shot submission handle alone cannot establish
durable exclusion among independently issued retries
or separately running nodes.

The relevant effect ledger distinguishes:

- source-checked normalization and restricted
  transaction lowering of the declared operation;
- trusted request-local principal/tenant/operation
  and command identity binding, and current relevant
  public model policy;
- the invocation-specific immutable transaction
  submitted by its actual selected gateway/client;
- backend-defined actual receipt, conditional
  commit/conflict and failure/unknown outcomes;
- physical domain and command-result atomicity,
  transaction-local guard and write frame;
- durable historical reconciliation after H1/H2
  response uncertainty, without a second Claim;
- all relevant initializer, job, raw and
  external physical writers that could invalidate
  the protected invariant;
- source-to-deployed route/asset binding and
  browser permission/adoption where claimed.

An API return, a local receipt object, an opaque
TransactionKey, a matching command row and a pinned
readback may be related observations with distinct
evidence origins. A report identifies exactly
which relation is established, and which still
requires the provider's contract or independent
causal proof. If an exception occurs after
submission, the public outcome cannot be
manufactured as =:rejected=. No post hoc
diagnostic check can turn a completed unsafe
write into pre-effect prevention.

The authoritative submission architecture,
guard footprints and physical writer completeness
belong to 10.05–10.09. This section makes their
proof-transfer dependencies unavoidable without
specifying a second competing transaction API.

*** Evidence mechanism, transfer limits and qualified authenticity

| Evidence mechanism | Warranted statement | Additional unproved or qualified boundary |
|--------------------+---------------------+-------------------------------------------|
| External machine-checked theorem | Formal conclusion under exactly the encoded definitions, proof rules and assumptions | Source-to-encoding fidelity and production realization |
| Source-issued checked derivation | Original declared subject satisfies its supported checker judgment and retains open premises | Independent checker metatheory and actual runtime behavior |
| Generated/extracted checker or compiler | Artifact derives from the formal or semantic subject by a selected process | Translation correctness, runtime/ABI/codec semantics, loaded identity |
| Proved representation or simulation | Specified concrete-to-abstract relation holds over its quantified domain | Production object and environment actually in that domain |
| Exhaustive finite comparison | Compared behaviors agree over the enumerated state/input space with recorded coverage | Outside-domain behavior, abstraction validity and real deployment |
| Independent conformance/fault test | Selected actual executions agree with their expected behavior at observed boundaries | All other schedules, writer completeness and eventual liveness |
| Controlled process-local gateway observation | Captured local call inputs/result and related observations at that owned call site | Remote node authenticity, transaction causality, other writers and real served route |
| Inspected deployed host/asset report | Matching source/route/callable/asset facts in the inspected host scope | Which process/bytes users actually reach, dynamic replacement and bypasses |
| Human/code review of handwritten relation | Reviewer judged specified correspondence under recorded assumptions | A machine theorem or authenticated physical occurrence |

A translator can be left inside an explicitly named
trusted computing base or justified by a separately
checked translation/refinement argument. Generated
outputs are *derivatives*, not proof of their own
correctness. An untrusted elaborator may propose
proof terms; a smaller checker must validate the
original-source judgment. Likewise, generated
formal models must not be hand-edited to evade
a counterexample and then presented as still
representing the actual application.

Authenticity is relative to the chosen threat model.
A private JVM registry can establish one
process-local handle origin under a trusted JVM
premise without providing a cryptographic remote
attestation. A controlled captured XTDB client
can justify a local call-site observation without
authenticating a caller-supplied node as production.
A copied report loses process-local identity
warrant unless a supported durable rechecking
or attestation contract restores it. Automatic
signature demands do not replace stating which
boundary is authoritative and who can substitute it.

*** Bind evidence and preserve currentness before substitution

The producer and consumer retain original-source
identity, required obligation coverage, exact
proposition, proof rules/checker profile, used
premises, source dependencies, semantic interface,
selected runtime plan, callable, install/asset
and resource/instance identities as *different*
objects. A certified consumer checks the
current trusted source and relevant
dependency closure before accepting
a producer's purported guarantee.
A successful report or matching old
source plus old graph is not currentness.

An abstract proof and its exact immutable
source closure may be reused without
running its checker on every click if
the actual dependencies and trusted
lifecycle remain valid. Reuse does not
suppress fresh model authorization,
command replay/retention, actor and
tenant context, browser effect ownership
or current installation validity.
A changed opaque callable, regenerated
asset, replaced route, provider or
runtime generation may leave an abstract
theorem intact while invalidating the
stronger source-to-production claim.

When a selected strong profile requires
external checking, timeout, unsupported
syntax, stale subject, failed checker
or missing model correspondence must
yield a typed unestablished/rejected
admission, not a cached green success
or invisible fallback to trusted code.
A subsequent checker outage does not
automatically invalidate a still-valid
independent proof accepted under its
lifecycle, but a refuted required
premise or changed current binding
cannot be hidden behind it.
Weaker conditional use requires an
*explicit separately selected profile*
with its genuine remaining assumptions.

*** Counterexamples return to source rather than creating a second model

For a modeled violation, Gesso retains
correspondence metadata to display the
named invariant, original source/operation,
actor/authority context, smallest useful
trace prefix, failing abstract guard/frame
step, formal translation and abstraction
assumptions, related production binding
and the evidence needed to decide whether
a real implementation shares the defect.
Sensitive Request/actor details are
redacted to the authorized reviewer.

For example, a *candidate defective
semantic model* that checked open
status only at a prior read might allow:

#+begin_example
A observes Request R as open
B observes Request R as open
A incorporates Claim for R
B incorporates a second primary Claim without an intervening release
one-primary-assignment invariant fails in the candidate model
#+end_example

This is a valid abstract counterexample
*only if the formal candidate actually
allows that unguarded commit action*.
It is not a counterexample to a
correctly atomically guarded formal
transition, and it is not proof
that the installed XTDB writer
executed the trace. Conversely,
a correct formal guard can coexist
with an unguarded deployed writer;
that is an open or falsified
*production refinement* obligation,
not an abstract invariant failure.
Model approximation may also
admit a spurious trace; concrete
realizability must be independently
assessed before blaming an actual
producer.

A developer-facing diagnostic
might identify a failing source
guard and a required
=net.humanhelp.site.model.request.core/claim=
implementation check, marking
the actual physical conclusion
=:not-established=. The
illustrative model binding is
not evidence that a particular
runtime route invoked it.
Where a trace does not
uniquely identify the defect,
source-model, translation,
assumption and production
possibilities remain distinct.

The normal repair loop is:

#+begin_example
Clojure/Gesso source and approved model policies
         -> checked semantic construction
         -> generated formal subject
         -> proof/model checking
         -> scoped counterexample or unsupported obligation
         -> interpretation at the original source and physical boundary
         -> human- or assistant-proposed source/translation/binding repair
         -> full regeneration, admission and independent conformance checks
#+end_example

Ordinary application developers
should not need to author or
patch formal-language files.
Framework maintainers may
repair a faulty lowering,
proof checker or external
backend as their own
source changes. Product
policy remains owned by
the application. An
automated assistant may
propose repairs but cannot
silently weaken a named
invariant, mark an opaque
premise discharged, modify
the generated specification
just to pass, or issue
a certificate. Every
approved repair is
re-derived and rechecked
under the appropriate
profile and independent
positive tests.

*** Acceptance criteria for the correspondence strategy

At a minimum the finished
system must demonstrate
paired cases for:

- **One source:** correct
  generated formal Claim
  and issued plan
  correspond to the
  original operation;
  a separate handwritten
  formal F and
  independently executed
  G without a justified
  relation cannot pass.
- **Admission direction:**
  accepted source has
  the required formal
  judgment and checked
  obligation closure;
  an admitted malformed
  rule or pruned original
  catalog violates
  admission soundness.
- **Positive completeness:**
  eligible real Claim and
  required lifecycle
  operations remain
  constructible;
  reject-all construction
  cannot qualify
  even if its abstract
  safety is vacuous.
- **Execution relation:**
  a checked supported
  production trace
  refines the original
  abstract operation;
  copied equal final
  snapshots with
  unmodeled intermediate
  unauthorized effects
  cannot establish
  the same claim.
- **Actor binding:**
  trusted current
  Membership/
  Organization policy
  authorizes an
  eligible Claim;
  browser-supplied
  actor identity
  cannot authorize
  the protected write.
- **Atomicity:** a
  guarded concurrent
  two-helper Claim
  preserves one active
  primary and durable
  command attribution;
  competing stale
  pre-reads and
  unguarded writes
  fail the claimed
  correspondence.
- **Command history:**
  C42 replay after
  lost H1 delivery
  recovers its true
  durable outcome;
  failed H2 or a
  later Request card
  cannot invent
  rejection or a
  second incorporation.
- **Physical evidence:**
  one owned gateway
  call, actual return
  and pinned readback
  support their bounded
  local witness;
  matching records
  are not accepted
  as universally causal
  or as complete
  writer inventory.
- **Provenance:** source,
  deployed operation
  and current plan
  bindings have
  genuine issuer/
  host evidence;
  a raw copied
  proof report,
  node ID or
  stamp cannot
  authenticate them.
- **Currentness:**
  an unaffected pure
  theorem can be
  reused under
  checked source
  compatibility;
  a swapped callable,
  served asset or
  revoked provider
  assumption requires
  renewed corresponding
  physical evidence.
- **Counterexample
  interpretation:**
  the defective
  candidate formal
  action returns
  a specific
  source-relative
  trace;
  the report does
  not automatically
  assert the
  installed writer
  did it.
- **Repair boundary:**
  repairing the
  true source/
  translation and
  rechecking succeeds;
  editing only a
  generated invariant
  cannot change
  production semantics
  or qualify the
  original claim.
- **Liveness:** the
  chosen fair
  recovery/user
  action premises
  justify a specific
  debt resolution;
  a safe stuttering
  trace or timeout
  alone does
  not establish
  eventual completion.
- **Topology:** one-
  and multi-node
  executions use
  the same Claim
  semantics;
  extra routing,
  registration-frontier,
  replay/gap
  and failover
  premises stay
  open until
  qualified.
- **Privacy:** authorized
  reviewers can
  trace a failure
  to its source;
  copyable reports
  cannot leak
  private principals
  or gain
  transaction
  authority.

Each case predeclares
the original source,
positive control,
adversarial perturbation,
expected first
source/checker/physical
boundary, independent
effect observation and
actual open
premises. The
acceptance decision
must be claim-specific,
not one global
=:certified?= flag.
A successful
formal proof,
source checker,
physical test
and product
capability are
different required
pieces of the
strongest
end-to-end
acceptance.

*** The selected transaction realization

The preferred protected-operation realization is a *source- and
invocation-bound transaction gateway*: the trusted application derives
one physical submission from the currently admitted operation,
checks its supported lowering and protected effects, and permits the
selected immutable vector to be submitted through exactly one
invocation-scoped capability. The gateway is a *mechanism* for
establishing specified aspects of source-to-physical correspondence.
Its presence is not proof of current model authority, universal
XTDB transaction semantics, actual command incorporation, complete
writer mediation, or the existence of an installed production route.

The canonical operation remains the public model's guarded transition,
not an independently authored transaction program or a browser
command-shaped map. The framework may issue a constrained gateway
for operations that fit the supported physical subset. Other model
implementations remain legal through explicit opaque contracts and
the selected assurance profile. They do not inherit the constrained
gateway's correctness or physical writer claims without evidence.

*** Transaction authority, issuance and one actual submission

The end-to-end accepted path is a dependency chain, not one
success-shaped status field:

1. *Trusted ingress:* The serving route or explicitly authorized
   worker binds the authenticated principal or service identity,
   tenant, admitted operation, canonical arguments, target and
   stable logical command identity from actual trusted context.
   Browser-supplied role, model prestate, claimed source/basis
   or apparent target is only a proposal and must not
   authenticate those facts.

2. *Source-current assembly:* The selected handler, public
   operation contract, original-source mandatory obligations,
   source-issued executable plan, model policy and target-binding
   interface are compatible at the current trusted consumer.
   A past certificate, copied route report or matching source
   name does not establish the handler actually deployed.

3. *Physical plan admission:* The checked lowering chooses a
   supported bounded operation family and retains exact
   guard and write dependencies, read/absence/uniqueness
   requirements, field presence/frame contract, protected
   document set, expected/current-state provenance,
   durable command-result write and publication intent
   when applicable.

4. *Gateway preparation:* The gateway recomputes or
   independently checks the *entire* canonical immutable
   transaction vector from the admitted source and rejects
   additional, reordered, substituted or unsupported
   physical operations. The caller cannot append raw SQL
   or XTDB operations, substitute a backend client,
   redirect the target, or supply its own submit callback
   inside this claimed constrained path.

5. *One-shot invocation:* The prepared attempt capability
   is issued for a particular physical invocation and
   consumed atomically with respect to local competing users
   before any second submission through that capability.
   The selected gateway owns the actual call of
   =xtdb.api/execute-tx= or an equivalent explicitly
   qualified authoritative backend API; the caller
   does not execute the vector separately.

6. *Outcome and external observation:* The gateway
   records what its own call attempted and returned,
   but hands command settlement to the qualified
   backend/provider and durable command-resolution
   contract. The public response distinguishes known
   rejection, known incorporation, known historical
   incorporation and unknown incorporation. Any
   post-submission diagnostic read is separate
   evidence; it may not manufacture a retry permit,
   commit conclusion, principal authority or
   Live/browser settlement.

This path never turns a process-local issuance handle
into a transferable client credential. Safe persistence
of a proof or source artifact requires its own
admitted rechecking procedure. A controlled test
collector or locally captured transaction receipt
does not authenticate the submitted node, current
HTTP server or deployed public model.

*** Restricted lowering has one documented physical meaning

The supported lowering vocabulary is versioned and closed.
It specifies the exact backend-facing semantics of every
admitted insertion, asserted existence/absence predicate,
conditional update, guarded replacement, allowed delete,
reference/cardinality constraint, typed encoding, null versus
absence and canonical command-result/outbox operation.
Unknown forms reject *before submission* from the constrained
path rather than becoming opaque extra statements appended
after checking.

When an admitted plan contains several physically atomic
operations, the gateway checks the exact ordered or
semantically constrained vector of *all* those operations.
It must say whether order matters, which expected values
came from external reads versus internal transaction
state, how backend conflicts are reported, and how
write/update/delete semantics preserve the abstract frame.
No claim about a complete transaction follows from
matching only one emitted SQL string or only the
nominal Request table.

The guard footprint and write footprint are distinct.
For Claim, current Membership, Request, Organization,
Location and assignment-absence/uniqueness may be
guard dependencies even when only Request and
RequestAssignment, canonical command record and
publication intent are written. A whole-document
replacement can overwrite an unguarded field. A
positive-row CAS does not necessarily protect
a relationship absence predicate. The exact
lost-field, ABA and revision discipline
obligations belong to 10.06; the admitted
gateway must preserve the physical footprint
needed to implement that later proof.

A *same-node pinned pre-read* can help prepare a
conditional transaction, but it is not the
transaction-internal prestate. A backend's
conditional assertions and atomicity/serializability
contract must justify the state on which the
protected transition actually depends. If a
revision is used to exclude ABA, every relevant
writer must participate and wraparound,
delete/recreate and prior-history assumptions
must be specified. An independent physical
writer that evades the revision can invalidate
the guarantee.

*** Logical command identity is not a one-shot attempt capability

A stable logical command such as C42 can have several
physical delivery or submission attempts, H1, H2,
and so on. The one-shot gateway prevents duplicate
submission *through the same invocation capability*.
It does not prevent two separately issued attempt
capabilities from incorporating the same logical
command, nor does it establish that a lost response
means the command was rejected.

The durable authoritative path therefore requires a
command binding containing the permitted operation,
principal, target and canonical arguments; guarded
exclusion or idempotent replay; an atomic relationship
between domain incorporation and its canonical command
result where promised; retention and disclosure rules;
and an explicit compatible-versus-incompatible replay
decision. A retry can receive a fresh attempt
capability *for the same logical command* after
the chosen command-resolution policy allows it.
An incompatible binding must be rejected rather than
relabelled as a valid retry.

The four backend/model outcomes =:committed=,
=:rejected=, =:already-incorporated= and
=:commit-unknown= are distinct from HTTP success,
an XTDB API's returned map, provisional browser
presentation, and a later matching Request card.
A post-submit exception may occur after
incorporation. Unless actual qualified evidence
rules incorporation out, the result is unknown;
a second fresh attempt must respect durable
command exclusion and the possibility that
H1 already committed.

The durable command-result record, domain write
and any required outbox/publication-intent record
need the *specified common authoritative commit
contract*. If outbox intent is committed atomically
while external publication is asynchronous,
the theorem requires durable eventual retry,
gap/replay/duplicate handling under named
liveness premises, not falsely asserting
that SSE notification occurred in the same
database transaction. Duplicated invalidations
are permitted when safe, but cannot create
ungranted collection reads or duplicate
domain incorporation.

*** Request-local parallelism, resource lifetime and retirement

An application is not required to serialize every
logical command through one process-global writer
or a global HTTP request lock. Distinct requests,
tenants and independent commands may execute
concurrently when their real model semantics,
isolation and capacity policies permit it.
Per-attempt one-shot issuance is compatible with
parallel requests; durable conflict protection
for the same Request/command comes from the
qualified model/backend mechanism, not global
thread serialization.

A request-local gateway binding records an
explicit owner, original checked operation,
source/handler generation, authenticated
invocation context, permitted target, bounded
lifetime, and the authoritative submit function.
The binder permits at most the expected
single submission through that capability,
and rejects duplicate or retired use before
submission. After dispatch it retires the
specific capability, even on an exception,
without erasing another request's newly
issued or current writer.

A thread-local binding alone is insufficient for
a callback, deferred task, subscription,
future, async write, response completion or
worker that executes after its original
thread/request scope ends. Such execution
must possess an explicit admissible
context with source identity, actor/service
authority, lifetime and transfer rules, and
must recheck the current state and rights
at the actual effect boundary. A
long-lived authorized job is not a
retained, expired HTTP request capability.

Bounded queues, semaphores and concurrency limits
control operational capacity. They cannot create
authorization, prove atomicity, or change the
logical command state machine. A queue-full
or admission-timeout result is a distinct
operational failure from business rejection,
known transaction nonincorporation, or
post-submit uncertainty. Once a physical
attempt has begun, cleanup or cancellation
cannot retroactively prove it did not
commit.

Where Biff/Ring routes participate, the actual
running server must use the *final* checked
handler rather than an earlier module slot.
Static route-to-writer declarations,
process-local registry observations and
per-request callback issuance are different
checks. Dynamic route parameters, callbacks,
jobs and non-HTTP ingress demand real
source/target/actor binding; an enumerated
static literal route does not prove every
possible request target or future handler.

*** Physical observation and provenance hierarchy

The gateway's strongest report is only as strong
as the trusted physical observation actually
performed. Maintain these categories separately:

| Observation | Warranted scoped fact | What it does not automatically prove |
|-------------+----------------------+--------------------------------------|
| Canonical lowering accepted | Original admitted source/plan has the selected vector and supported protected footprint | The vector was sent to any real backend |
| Issued process-local one-shot consumed | Registered gateway entered one owned submission path | Backend receipt, commit, external uniqueness or principal authorization |
| Captured API call and return | Exact local vector and result/exception observed at that call site | Authenticity of caller-selected node, server adoption or backend semantics |
| Public transaction key/ledger correlation | Identified transaction metadata agrees with a qualified provider view at the inspected basis | Source-specific causality, domain safety, all writers or retry authorization |
| Pinned domain, command and ledger readback | Those observations agree at the named single basis and projection | That this attempt caused the state, or that no other writer intervened |
| Installed route/registered callback observation | The chosen checked local handler path invoked the expected registered writer during one request | Every serving process/route/actor uses it, or no direct XTDB bypass exists |
| Qualified backend transaction proof/contract | A specified atomicity, failure, guard or isolation premise holds for the covered backend version and domain | The actual application supplies correct business guards and complete writer coverage |
| Independently closed physical writer set and current runtime binding | The specified physical writer paths are constrained within the proven host/threat/coverage scope | Unobserved external writers, later replacement or universal host semantics outside that scope |

A physical observation made *after* incorporation may
identify a defect but cannot guarantee prevention.
For a safety claim that requires a pre-effect guard,
the actual enforcing boundary must reject the invalid
request *before* the forbidden write. A copied report,
caller-supplied node or stale process-local handle
cannot stand in for independently collected
physical evidence.

An exact TransactionKey and same-basis readback
may be excellent diagnostic evidence without
showing that the selected attempt caused the
final RequestAssignment state. A transaction
ledger may be corroborative without proving
business guards or command identity.
For full production refinement, the claimed
execution includes actual route adoption,
principal authentication, transaction-local
prestate/frame and write causality, relevant
writer/initializer coverage, command history
and installed/browser observations where
the theorem depends on them.

*** HumanHelp Claim and adversarial production acceptance

A representative protected Claim path binds the
current authenticated helper, Request,
Membership, Organization and Location through
the real public models, uses the admitted
Claim transition and physical RequestAssignment
one-primary constraint, and writes the
canonical command result under its stipulated
atomicity and authority contract.
The browser does not supply the trusted
helper ID or authorize a read merely because
its planned UI was formally admitted.

Acceptance requires a positive eligible Claim
and genuine concurrent two-helper contention,
not only a proof of the abstract transition.
It must also discriminate these nearby cases:

- a source builder changes target or operation
  after independent binding; no one-shot
  execution capability may issue;
- an attacker inserts extra SQL, swaps an XTDB
  node or supplies a different callback;
  the constrained gateway rejects that
  substitution before protected effects;
- a second local caller invokes an already
  consumed one-shot; no second submission
  occurs through that capability;
- a duplicate physical attempt uses a fresh
  one-shot for C42; durable command identity
  and replay policy, not one-shot memory,
  prevent duplicate incorporation;
- H1 commits and its response is lost;
  H2's exception or a subsequent
  Request snapshot does not manufacture
  an original rejection or new Claim;
- a handler is replaced after source checking,
  or another Biff controller/direct XTDB
  writer bypasses the selected registry;
  the unverified scope is reported rather
  than certified as physically complete;
- two unrelated requests use independent
  request-local issuers concurrently;
  a process-global one-shot must not
  become an accidental product limitation;
- a deferred handler continues after
  its request owner has retired;
  it must re-authorize and acquire a
  valid explicit execution context
  rather than borrow stale thread state;
- a valid guarded Claim changes
  RequestAssignment while an
  unrelated writer changes an
  unguarded field; the physical
  frame contract must prevent
  destructive stale replacement;
- the real backend cannot supply an
  authoritative outcome after a
  post-submit failure; the public
  result remains unknown and
  recovery obeys permission,
  command history and retention;
- an outbox invalidation is lost
  or delivered twice across
  nodes; retry/replay preserves
  command safety and keeps
  remote board acquisition
  user-authorized;
- a purportedly complete transaction
  has no genuine command-result
  or protected absence/uniqueness
  guard; its narrow source/host
  check cannot be promoted to
  end-to-end Claim refinement.

Each case names the selected source, route
or worker, current principal/tenant,
logical command, attempt, original and
mutated transaction/handler, expected
first enforcing boundary, and
independently inspected physical
effects. Unsupported forms or unknown
observation scopes fail the claimed
strong admission rather than
disappearing from the report.
The valid Claim and independent
HumanHelp product positives remain
required alongside adversarial rejection.

The restricted gateway is therefore a
*preferred enforceable physical seam* for
supported authoritative operations, not
a theorem that arbitrary host Clojure,
every possible XTDB caller, HTTP routing,
multi-node delivery, or browser effect
has already been certified.
*** Guard dependencies and write footprints are different

A protected operation has at least four related but *non-interchangeable*
footprints:

1. Its *semantic guard dependencies* are every state fact, relationship,
   presence/absence predicate, authority input and observation whose current
   truth or prior history controls whether a transition is permitted.
2. Its *abstract write/frame footprint* identifies the fields or modeled
   entities assigned and those whose presence and value must remain unchanged.
3. Its *physical mutation footprint* identifies the entire persisted
   documents/rows, indexes, command records and other state that the actual
   backend operation can change, including implicit replacement effects.
4. Its *conflict/protection footprint* identifies the physical guards,
   versions, absence/uniqueness constraints and relevant competing writers
   whose behavior must be controlled so the abstract guard and frame
   remain valid at the actual linearization/commit boundary.

These sets can overlap without being equal. A Claim may depend on current
Membership, Organization, Location, Request status, an absent active-primary
RequestAssignment and command identity, yet physically change Request,
RequestAssignment, canonical command outcome and outbox intent. This
does not mean Membership should be rewritten merely because its validity
is a guard. Conversely, a whole-document =:put-docs= can overwrite fields
that do *not* occur in the abstract declared delta. All four footprints
must remain source-derived or explicitly qualified, scoped, and reviewable;
passing an operation-set proof on a smaller abstract projection does not
silently close the physical footprint.

*** Frame preservation concerns presence, not merely named values

For a supported abstract guarded transition, all assigned expressions
use the stated pre-state and input with *simultaneous assignment*,
and the frame preserves all unassigned relevant fields, including
their presence versus absence. A declared optional absent value is
not an existing field containing nil. Physical equality must respect
the admitted encoding and comparison semantics: SQL =NULL=
comparisons, missing fields, nested values, timestamps and
cross-language coercions cannot be treated as Clojure map equality
without a qualified correspondence.

The physical promise depends on the mutation form. An update that
truly changes only the declared fields can have a narrower physical
write footprint than a complete document replacement. A backend
=:put-docs= or equivalent complete replacement modifies the
*entire persisted document*, including possible removal of a
field never named by the source delta. A before/after map of two
business fields does not make it a two-field physical patch.
The protected domain must name the whole document for a whole
replacement, including presence and deletion; claiming to
protect every currently known key is insufficient when
another key could be added.

The following executable Clojure example from the preferred R5
section illustrates the lost-field problem. It models immutable
maps only; it is *not* XTDB code, a transaction-internal
snapshot or a certified operation. A complete-map comparison
includes key presence by Clojure map equality. The real
backend must independently justify an equivalent representation
and comparison policy.

#+begin_src clojure
(def prepared-before
  {:request/status :open
   :request/revision 7
   :request/summary "Original summary"})

(def prepared-after
  (assoc prepared-before
         :request/status :claimed
         :request/revision 8))

;; A writer outside the revision discipline changes an unguarded field.
(def current-before-commit
  (assoc prepared-before :request/summary "Corrected summary"))

(defn checked-field-equal? [expected actual field]
  (and (= (contains? expected field) (contains? actual field))
       (= (get expected field) (get actual field))))

(defn partial-guard? [expected actual]
  (every? #(checked-field-equal? expected actual %)
          [:request/status :request/revision]))

(defn complete-map-guard? [expected actual]
  (= expected actual))

(assert (partial-guard? prepared-before current-before-commit))
(assert (not (complete-map-guard? prepared-before current-before-commit)))
(assert (= "Original summary" (:request/summary prepared-after)))
(assert (not= (:request/summary prepared-after)
              (:request/summary current-before-commit)))
#+end_src

The partial guard accepts the stale prepared replacement, which would
restore =:request/summary= to the original value. The complete-map
guard detects that conflict in this *illustrative map model*.
Neither assertion tests an actual XTDB transaction. A real
guarded physical writer must reject the stale replacement
or avoid losing the concurrent field by another justified
implementation strategy.

*** Qualified mechanisms for guarded replacements

For a whole-document replacement, at least one of the following
must be *actually sufficient under the selected backend and writer
universe*, not merely declared in a source report:

- *Whole relevant pre-state compare:* The backend tests the
  complete covered pre-image—including field presence,
  absence and supported nested representation—at the
  atomic conflict point before replacing the document.
  Comparing previously observed fields alone is insufficient
  if a new key can be inserted. A top-level field-count
  assertion may close that particular insertion gap when
  combined with correct all-field equality, supported
  non-null semantics, stable field-name mapping and a
  qualified atomic =ASSERT=/=PUT= contract. It is
  not automatically a nested-frame, multi-document
  or all-writer theorem.
- *Closed monotonic revision discipline:* Every physical writer
  capable of changing the protected state advances the exact
  same bounded, non-reused revision/epoch and atomic
  comparison checks the predecessor value.
  The claim specifies authorized revision constructor,
  overflow/nonwrapping policy, deletion/recreation
  identity, migrations and operational exceptions.
  A revision increment by *this* command alone
  does not prove the all-writer discipline.
- *Transaction-local derive-and-preserve:* The backend
  computes the replacement from the actual guarded
  current state inside the justified atomic transaction,
  preserving the abstract frame and all required
  failure behavior. An external read followed by
  client-side merge is not transaction-local derivation.
- *Genuinely narrow physical patch:* The backend's
  supported atomic operation modifies exactly
  admitted fields with protected guard and
  absence/uniqueness semantics. A library operation
  called "update" that serializes a full replacement
  is not this strategy.

A mixture of mechanisms may be required for the full
domain. Their exact scope includes all protected
documents and relationships, not just the row with
a Request status field. If the selected lowering
cannot express or independently justify the
necessary guard/frame relation, the constrained
gateway fails its stronger profile *before
submission*. An expressly opaque alternative
retains its own proof/implementation premises
without inheriting a stronger checked-frame label.

The proof is directional. If a physical action
is admitted, then under named backend,
serialization and writer-coverage premises
it must refine the declared abstract transition;
a match between reported field counts does
not entail that every relevant physical state
is covered. The root report states which
fields, documents, mutation forms, conflict
mechanisms, source version, current handler
and backend semantics were actually qualified.

*** External observation, transaction-time guards and actual causality

A pinned external read establishes a particular
observed state at an identified provider basis.
It may supply input to a prepared guarded plan,
or a bounded diagnostic comparing the declared
pre-image with observed data. It does not
establish the transaction-internal prestate
or guarantee no conflicting write occurs
between the read and submission.

A qualified XTDB =ASSERT=/=ASSERT=/=PUT=
implementation can enforce particular
field/count predicates against the state
seen by those assertions at its atomic
execution boundary *if* the reviewed
backend version, operation order,
snapshot/isolation, conflict and failure
semantics support that interpretation.
A checked SQL string, caller-supplied
candidate state or accepted plan shape
does not establish those backend
premises or authenticate the actual
executed transaction vector. A
postsubmission pinned read likewise
does not prove that *this* submitted
operation caused its state: another
writer can intervene or restore
identical bytes.

Separate source/model facts, prepared
lowering, selected actual gateway
submission, transaction receipt,
ledger/domain readback, real backend
atomicity, installed model route,
principal authorization, and full
physical writer coverage. A copied
receipt and a direct XTDB bypass
cannot become an admitted operation
by matching diagnostic identities.
A post hoc frame violation
may be detected and reported;
it cannot retroactively prevent
a forbidden write.

*** Absence, uniqueness and write-skew require predicate protection

Positive comparison of documents that already exist does
not prove *absence* of a matching row or *uniqueness*
of a relationship. The source guard may say there is
no active primary RequestAssignment for R17. Two
different helper transactions can both insert
distinct assignment documents while leaving
every previously read Request field unchanged.
A CAS on the Request status, by itself, protects
the relationship only if the actual model/writer
protocol proves that both inserts must conflict
through that CAS or another shared linearization
mechanism.

A physical absence/uniqueness invariant therefore
requires a qualified atomic predicate check,
exclusive key, constraint, conflict/write
dependency or protocol shown to serialize
all competing relevant writers. The proof
states its target relation and model's
active/terminal semantics, not merely
"no duplicate document ID." Deleting and
recreating assignment records, changing
their active status, switching Organization,
running migrations or bypass writers
must participate in the appropriate
invariant/concurrency argument.
A database's documented unique-index
or isolation behavior is a *specific
qualified backend premise* for a
specific schema and operation order,
not a general Gesso theorem.

For HumanHelp Claim, the source
catalog must include real public
RequestAssignment transitions,
current Request and helper
Membership/Organization/Location
policy and the actual writer
domain. An abstract one-primary
induction theorem remains valid
under its declared operation
catalog even if some real
admin writer bypasses it;
what fails is the stronger
physical-coverage/refinement
claim. This boundary is owned
jointly with 10.07 and
10.08, not erased by
a source proof.

*** ABA, monotonic revisions, identity and history

A complete value compare can admit
an ABA history: a value changes and
later returns to the same value.
This is *not automatically* a
safety failure if the policy
depends only on the actual
current state. A "no intervening
change" theorem, historical
command exclusion, lease
generation or long-lived
observed transition may
instead depend on history,
and therefore needs a
history-sensitive token
or protocol whose scope
actually includes those
changes.

A strictly increasing,
nonwrapping revision
provides a possible
ABA defense only if
the following all hold:

1. The revision has an exact
   total-order representation
   with no narrowing,
   coercion, arithmetic
   overflow or reuse.
2. The original transaction
   requires the expected
   revision and advances it
   in the correct
   atomic write; a
   copied revision or
   arbitrary new value
   is rejected.
3. Every relevant physical
   writer, including jobs,
   migration tools,
   admin operations and
   other nodes, participates
   in the revision discipline.
4. Identity evolution through
   deletion/recreation,
   reset and reinitialization
   cannot resurrect an
   old revision inside
   a logically new
   object instance.
5. The selected database
   actually checks
   the revision predicate
   at the required
   atomic boundary,
   with explicit conflict
   and unknown outcomes.

A source checker may
verify this command's
exact predecessor/successor
arithmetic while leaving
the all-writer/history
premise open. That is
meaningful conditional
evidence, not the
full physical theorem.
A timestamp, increasing
SSE counter, command
ID or XTDB basis
token must not
silently substitute
for the revision
property: each has
different provenance
and ordering rules.
Immutable semantic
identity is a
preservation relation,
not automatically
a monotonic
progression value.

*** Required conformance and independent effect oracles

The checked source,
physical lowering and
real implementation
must be tested with
positive and
adversarial neighbors.
At minimum, the
following controls
are required for
their selected
claim scopes:

- A complete
  document pre-image
  accepts a
  genuinely
  unchanged
  current state;
  an intervening
  summary edit
  must not be
  overwritten
  by a stale PUT.
- The original
  map example's
  partial guard
  accepts the
  conflicting
  summary; the
  full presence-aware
  guard rejects it.
  This is
  *model evidence*,
  not an XTDB
  result.
- A new field
  inserted between
  external read
  and commit
  defeats
  old-field-only
  checks; the
  selected
  whole-document
  protection
  rejects that
  conflict or
  uses a safe
  narrow patch.
- Absent,
  present nil,
  scalar,
  nested and
  deleted values
  are represented
  according to
  supported
  backend codecs;
  unsupported SQL
  equality or
  missing/NULL
  coercion must
  reject or
  remain explicit.
- Two concurrent
  eligible helpers
  can attempt
  Claim while
  preserving
  one active
  primary;
  separate-row
  insertion without
  shared predicate
  conflict
  cannot pass.
- A valid
  revision
  successor and
  current expected
  value may
  admit a
  transaction;
  unchanged
  revision,
  skipped successor,
  wraparound
  and stale
  expected value
  must fail
  the supported
  monotonic
  contract.
- A documented
  ABA restoration
  may satisfy
  a current-only
  predicate;
  it must *not*
  satisfy a
  declared
  no-intervening-
  change
  requirement
  without
  history
  evidence.
- A direct admin
  or external
  writer lacking
  revision discipline
  makes the
  deployment-wide
  monotonic
  guarantee open
  or false;
  one bounded
  writer catalog
  cannot assert
  completeness.
- Actual guarded
  submission,
  backend result
  and readback
  are attributed
  within their
  observed scope;
  matching
