  poststate after
  a separate
  writer is
  not physical
  transaction
  causality.
- Public model
  Claim and
  RequestAssignment
  invariants have
  meaningful
  eligible
  positive paths;
  a gateway
  that rejects
  all physical
  attempts cannot
  pass the
  independent
  product gates.

Each case must
predeclare the
original source
and guarded
policy, tested
backend subset,
positive control,
mutated input
or interleaving,
first expected
enforcing
boundary and
independent
pre-effect or
post-effect
physical observer.
An invalid
attempt rejected
by the source
checker is not
proof that a
distinct external
writer was
prevented.
A timed-out
backend or
incomplete
causal observation
must be reported
as incomplete
or unknown,
not a
checked frame
guarantee.

The goal is
exact protection
of the *actual
claimed state
and history*,
with only those
transactional and
deployment
premises that
have truly
been qualified.
*** Writer coverage reaches beyond HTTP routes

The original operation catalog supplies the *abstract operation set*.
The deployed writer inventory supplies the claimed *physical coverage*.
Those are joined by checked operation identity, relevant guard/frame
footprints and actual effects, not inferred from matching source names.
A source-complete induction proof can be correct for its admitted machine
while a direct XTDB caller invalidates the corresponding physical invariant.
The missing fact is production correspondence or enforcement, not a flaw
that may be fixed by silently deleting the physical writer from the report.

For every protected claim, Gesso must identify the state, collection,
relation, tenant, authority and history it intends to cover and the
potential mutations that can invalidate that property. The inventory
includes ordinary routes, non-HTTP background jobs, imports, service
consumers, scheduled work, administrative and maintenance tools,
migrations, initializers, other processes and external services that can
write through independently held backend credentials. A handler need
not be an HTTP handler and every writer need not have a route. Requiring
a fabricated route for a scheduled operation would confuse placement
with semantic ownership.

A host-supplied enumerator establishes only what that enumerator
actually observed at the named process, registry and generation.
“No inventory available” is *unknown*, never an empty closed
inventory. A source-relative exact operation-ID join is useful but
does not establish that differently named or undiscovered physical
writers are absent, that a callable has its declared behavior, or
that the running service uses the checked registration.

**** A scoped physical writer universe

A strong whole-application claim declares its *protected physical
universe*, including the exact backend/provider and deployment
assumptions, not merely a list of approved Clojure Vars. The record
identifies at least:

- protected domain and property: real Request, RequestAssignment,
  command ledger and any other relevant persisted state, relationship,
  absence/uniqueness predicate, revision/history or effect;
- authority domain: tenant/Organization, allowed principals and service
  identities, current policy, and the intended set of admitted
  operations and explicitly permitted operational transitions;
- effect-capable entrypoint classes: HTTP, worker, scheduler,
  queue consumer, system bootstrap/initializer, migration,
  maintenance CLI, administrator, other service and direct provider
  credential holders;
- actual capability path: credentials, connection pools, clients,
  mutable dependency injection, route and callback/worker bindings,
  executable/handler generations and provider-side grants that permit
  mutation even when no Gesso operation is invoked;
- mutation and conflict footprints: PUT/patch/delete/erase/SQL and
  transaction/vector calls, entire replaced documents, protected
  predicates, expected revision and any domain-specific constraints;
- observation/coverage: the independent inventory source,
  installation scope, last successful reconciliation, open
  unclassified or inaccessible paths, and evidence that the
  enforcing boundary actually covers every relevant mutation;
- lifetime and change control: deployment/credential generation,
  startup and shutdown, dynamic worker creation, route replacement,
  job promotion, provider rotation, external operational access
  and the conditions that invalidate the coverage judgment.

The universe is relative to a stated threat and deployment model.
A capability restriction can exclude a path only when actual backend,
process or credential enforcement prevents that path from writing the
protected domain. A value in a host-declared capability table
=:restriction :host-declared= is not such enforcement. A user
who can import an unrestricted XTDB client, a service retaining
database write credentials, or an operator with direct update access
must be accounted for by real confinement, a separately controlled
exception contract or an explicit still-open premise.

An inventory may be *complete relative to the inspected host
registry* yet incomplete relative to all processes or privileged
writers. These are different claims. The consumer must not infer
universal closed-world coverage by taking the union of several
individually incomplete enumerators. Instead it must justify
the relevant universe and its partition into observed/mediated,
constrained external, and specifically qualified open paths.

**** Three independently established closure judgments

The framework keeps three closure questions distinct.

| Closure subject | What sufficient evidence establishes | Invalid shortcut |
|-----------------+-------------------------------------+------------------|
| Original abstract operation closure | Every original required initializer, operation, invariant and semantic dependency is represented in the checked machine | Accepting the caller's smaller operation list as the source |
| Observed deployed entrypoint and writer correspondence | Each inventoried current host route, worker or other entrypoint is matched to its original operation or explicitly scoped operational writer, callable and declared physical effects | Equating an operation name, stale route table or host-supplied list with exhaustive production discovery |
| Enforced physical writer closure | Every actual mutation capable of invalidating the selected property is mediated by a conforming protected boundary or covered by an independently qualified exception/provider assumption | Assuming “zero unclassified observed writers” means no hidden raw or external XTDB client exists |

An original semantic catalog may be complete while an installed
application has an additional writer. An observed inventory may contain
every registered route while an initializer or service principal writes
directly. A backend-enforced physical closure claim can use a
different implementation from the preferred Gesso gateway, but it
must demonstrate the same protected source-to-effect refinement
at the boundary it actually owns. The strongest claim cannot be
issued by concatenating a source-side proof and a copyable inventory
summary without that missing enforcement argument.

The source-derived catalog should independently account for
operation and initializer obligations; an installed-application
inspection should independently account for route, worker, dynamic
target, server startup and rendered affordance identities.
Source closure and product capability completeness also differ:
an internally closed application missing required HumanHelp
Unclaim or Reassign cannot pass the positive product gate.
A registered job that writes protected state must have its own
corresponding operation/initializer or explicit privileged
maintenance contract; it is not required to masquerade as a route.

**** Mediation, enforcement and operational exceptions

The preferred supported path constrains physical writers through
the admitted source-bound gateway and the qualified backend guards
from 10.05–10.06. A production-wide assurance claim additionally
needs evidence about *access to the backend*:

1. Only specified service principals and operator roles can acquire
   protected mutation authority; grants, network routes and backend
   capabilities are checked at the actual deployment boundary.
2. Normal application ingress paths receive only the appropriate
   source-bound executor/callback or least-privileged backend
   capability. The raw client used by a gateway must not be
   casually exposed through unrelated application closures.
3. A mutation through any class of privileged writer must satisfy
   the matching operation's authenticated authority, transaction-
   internal guard, protected frame, command/result and revision
   discipline, or its explicitly reviewed operational exception.
4. Known bypass-capable credentials or direct clients are either
   technically barred from the covered domain, included under
   an independently enforced and checked contract, or retained
   as open trusted premises that prevent the stronger claim.
5. Current deployed handler/worker/callback and credential
   generation must still match the inspected/issued assembly
   at the time of use. A previously complete startup
   snapshot is not proof of later runtime stability.

An operational exception is not a general “administrator bypass”
with automatically preserved invariants. It names who can invoke
it, its permitted domain and mutation, the required approval and
audit, the protected before/after or migration relation, whether
the invariant is maintained or temporarily suspended, and the
conditions under which stronger dependent certification resumes.
A break-glass write can be necessary, but its presence changes the
scope of any unqualified whole-domain proof.

A release migration can change schemas, rebuild assignments,
reset revisions or create initial records. If those effects are
outside the proved operation catalog, the deployment must either
prove that the migration refines an admitted transition, or
establish a new valid initial state and requalify the affected
invariant and physical realization afterward. Checking that an
abstract invariant held *before* migration does not prove it
holds afterward. A startup initializer has the same
physical responsibility even if it runs only once.

If an external provider enforces a relevant uniqueness,
transaction isolation or credential restriction, the
specific provider version, configuration, scope and failure
semantics enter the claim as checked evidence or a named
external trust premise. Merely using XTDB, Biff, a
container sandbox or a particular route framework
does not automatically provide those guarantees.

**** Dynamic entrypoints, multi-process identity and TOCTOU

Real deployments may change handlers, start workers, restart
nodes, rotate database credentials or replace callbacks while
the application continues serving. Inventory freshness,
currentness and the order of checking/activation matter.
A process-local private registry can strengthen one
in-process caller-origin check without authenticating
the actual serving process, a remote node, the physical
database client or a later deployment generation.

The selected assurance profile must specify how the
actual writer-enforcing boundary remains valid after
startup. A correctly checked route-to-writer table
whose handler is later replaced with a raw XTDB
client no longer establishes current coverage.
A positive request that passed an earlier registry
snapshot does not prove all concurrent or future
requests went through that registered writer.

A robust design may use generation-scoped
capability issuance, immutable checked routing,
runtime enforcement plus ongoing qualified
revalidation, provider-level permission separation,
or another demonstrably sufficient mechanism.
The chosen mechanism must close the relevant
check-to-use gap rather than simply run a
second enumerator after the write.
A post-effect discrepancy is useful
detection, never retroactive prevention.

Multiple nodes do not require a second model of
Claim or a new category of participant authority.
They do require qualification of *all* node,
service, scheduler, administrative and external
writer paths in the protected universe.
A failed host may lose process-local registry
state while its previously submitted transaction
can still incorporate; retry and command history
must remain durable and appropriately scoped.
Router interest propagation, outbox publication
and node-loss replay are different from
database write authority. An invalidation
re-delivered safely may be harmless, but it
cannot create an unmodeled domain write
or a forbidden automatic remote board read.

**** HumanHelp one-primary and command-history coverage

For the real Claim application, enumerate
actual Request and RequestAssignment mutation
entrypoints, plus relevant Membership,
Organization and Location policy dependencies.
An actor can be eligible under the abstract
Claim contract while a raw migration or
manager operation produces a second active
primary outside the constrained model.
The abstract theorem still describes its
declared transitions; the whole-domain
physical theorem does not follow.

A stronger end-to-end Claim invariant requires:
the source-derived original Claim/Unclaim/
Reassign and lifecycle catalog; protected
concurrent assignments including absence
and uniqueness; real public model guards;
all relevant normal and operational writers;
transaction-local current-state/frame
correspondence; durable command identity
and result; and actual installed call sites.
A changed Membership or Organization
may alter authorization before the Claim
commits even if that model is not
written by Claim itself. The physical
guard dependency must therefore be
protected under the qualified isolation
contract, not added spuriously to the
write footprint just to make a catalog
look complete.

A direct maintenance writer might
still be permitted under a
separately approved operation.
It cannot be used to claim
the original all-operations
one-primary theorem without
matching induction/transition
coverage or an explicit
reestablished initial
state. A copyable
=complete?= report
does not grant administrative
authority or turn an unknown
writer universe into
an empty one.

**** Adversarial coverage and honest reporting

Coverage tests require a valid
source/installed operation
and a deliberately selected
negative neighboring writer,
not a reject-all system.
At minimum, demonstrate:

- A registered HTTP Claim
  and separately registered
  authorized scheduled
  operation are both
  accounted for under
  their correct actual
  entrypoint classes;
  the job is not
  assigned a fake route.
- An original source-complete
  operation catalog joined
  with a current route/
  issued-writer table is
  reported as exactly that;
  inserting a raw writer
  the enumerator did not
  report cannot be
  considered disproved.
- A declared table-wide
  =:put-docs= or =:sql-dml=
  capability touching
  the protected domain
  cannot be reduced
  to only the currently
  listed documents.
- A genuine enforced
  read-only role cannot
  mutate the protected
  domain; a host map
  claiming =:read-only=
  while the same
  credential can write
  fails the strong
  closure claim.
- A live admin/migration
  writer that changes
  RequestAssignment
  must carry an
  appropriate source/
  operational transition
  contract; a hidden
  backdoor breaks
  unqualified one-primary
  physical safety.
- A startup initializer
  and later maintenance
  phase satisfy their
  declared initial-state
  and requalification
  obligations; a
  migration that silently
  resets revision/ABA
  history does not.
- A current checked
  Biff handler actually
  invokes its registered
  writer during one
  admitted request;
  source-matched
  registration alone
  cannot certify the
  real deployed
  server or other
  handler generations.
- An async callback
  or worker uses
  explicitly scoped
  service principal
  and execution
  capability; it
  cannot borrow a
  retired request's
  thread-local
  writer lease.
- A privileged
  direct XTDB client
  is excluded by
  real provider/
  capability enforcement
  or retained as
  a named premise;
  a missing enumerator
  entry cannot
  close the universe.
- A new deployment
  generation changes
  an actual handler,
  callable or
  credential; affected
  physical correspondence
  is invalidated,
  while unrelated
  abstract proofs
  can remain valid
  where qualified.
- Two real helpers
  race for a Request
  while another
  permitted writer
  mutates its
  assignment/revision;
  the protected
  one-primary
  invariant remains
  enforced or the
  additional writer
  is shown
  outside the claim.
- A failed transaction
  and dropped/duplicated
  outbox notice preserve
  actual command
  history and permitted
  advisory recovery;
  a router cannot
  turn a notification
  into a new Claim
  or unauthorized
  collection read.

Each test names the original source,
protected domain, capability path,
required source or operational
transition, selected host/credential
generation, first enforcing
boundary and an independent
effect observer appropriate to
its scope. A static mismatch
can reject a claim before
execution; a controlled
post-dispatch observer can
detect a difference *after*
an effect. Neither can
prove that all other physical
writers are absent without
the separate closure mechanism.

Root assurance reports separate
the following conclusions:

| Report result | Meaning |
|---------------+---------|
| =:source-catalog-closed= | Every original required abstract operation/initializer obligation in the inspected source is represented |
| =:registered-paths-classified= | Every writer actually returned by the scoped host enumerator is classified under the inspected generation |
| =:declared-capabilities-covered= | Supplied writer target/mutation declarations correspond to the protected-domain declaration in their stated finite scope |
| =:installed-mediation-observed= | One or more actual selected installed call sites/requests were observed with identified source and writer |
| =:physical-writer-closure-established= | An independently qualified enforcing boundary excludes or constrains *every* relevant writer within a precisely declared deployed universe |
| =:physical-writer-closure-unknown= | The actual universe or its enforcement has not been established; an empty inventory is not sufficient |

The labels above are *normative
report concepts*, not a claim
that today's Gesso exports
these keywords or that a
caller can assert
=:physical-writer-closure-established=
in an untrusted map.
The issuer applies the
selected profile and
the actual supporting
evidence. A checked
source theorem, matched
operation-ID lists
and a convenient
inventory do not
produce the last
result by arithmetic.

The final requirement
is deliberately
strong: every real
effect capable of
invalidating the
claimed invariant
must be included,
restricted, or
explicitly assumed
under a scope
that the claim
truthfully discloses.
*** HumanHelp Claim as a correspondence slice

Claim's public semantic contract, admitted plan, physical transaction, and
participant observation have one connected meaning. The example is the
self-claim case. A separately authorized operation that assigns another helper
must bind and guard that target helper's Membership as well as the actor's
permission; it cannot reuse self-claim assumptions unchanged.

**** Source-owned identities, actor and helper distinction

The *source* of the Claim decision is the current public HumanHelp
production model and the application-selected Claim operation, not a
proof-only Request entity. The correspondence ledger binds the source
generation, actual public model interface versions, normalized Claim
operation, current actor and authority domain, complete original
operation/invariant catalog, role-projected executable plan and
installed executor. Each identity has its own lifecycle: neither
command ID, HTTP attempt, XTDB receipt, model operation ID, browser
resource lease nor proof fingerprint can substitute for another.

The self-Claim principal, helper receiving the assignment and
Request target refer to their own typed identities. They happen to
denote the same person for a genuine self-Claim, but the relation is
proved at the admitted operation, not assumed globally. Manager
Reassign or a separately authorized claim-for-another operation
has a distinct *actor*, *target helper* and existing-primary context.
Its guard includes the actor's authority to select another helper and
the target's independent effective Membership and eligibility.
A source check or UI gesture cannot turn a self-Claim operation
into an authorized manager assignment by swapping a helper argument.

The selected proof projection must name the *representation relation*
from the public Request, RequestAssignment and effective Membership,
Organization and Location records to the abstract model's state and
roles. Derived display labels and cached board cards may stand for
those facts only when the producer, disclosure scope and observation
frontier are known. A single conveniently nullable helper field is
not a second authoritative assignment store; a proof over that
field must account for every primary assignment that contributes
to its meaning. Assertions about actual schema keys must come
from the current public model interfaces, not from illustrative
Clojure data in Part IV.

**** The command envelope and trusted invocation

The browser sends the domain Request identity and stable
=:gesso/command-id= through the admitted command boundary. A transport may add
=:http-request-id= for this delivery. The latter identifies neither the domain
Request nor the command across retries. The server binds the principal from
trusted context and validates the operation, interface, canonical arguments,
and authority-domain binding of the command.

The formal state projection includes the Request and the relationships relevant
to its primary RequestAssignment, Membership, Organization, and durable command
record. Primary ownership is not modeled by inventing a =:request/helper-id=
field. A projection may summarize these relationships, but its representation
relation must explain how the actual records establish that summary.

The simplified candidate in Part IV illustrates a decision over supplied values.
Using a nullable helper field in such a projection does not change HumanHelp's
storage or authority model. Its production correspondence must still account for
the primary assignment and every guarded relationship on which that value rests.

The authority-domain binding must include the Request and selected
Organization/tenant context at the trusted server/model boundary.
An observed basis can justify some *client presentation* obligations
but it does not establish current backend Request status, Membership
or organization policy. The route maps exact typed operation,
canonical arguments, actor and command binding to the selected
public model contract; it does not promote a client-supplied actor,
role, provenance flag, one-Refresh permission or =:authorized?=
field into trusted authority.

The source/installed correspondence must show that this browser
control actually emits the admitted command envelope and that
the deployed Ring/Biff route, authenticated principal, selected
model callable and gateway share the compatible assembly/host
generation. A manually inserted command attribute or synthetic
successful request is permitted as a *route-level fixture*,
but cannot count as an actual browser-originated positive
product witness. A stale served plan or replaced handler
reopens the relevant installed-realization edge even
when the original abstract proof remains valid.

**** Historical command decision precedes new eligibility

The transition distinguishes these branches:

| Branch | Required decision | Authoritative effect |
|--------+-------------------+----------------------|
| Existing compatible command | Validate its full binding and current permission to disclose its recorded result | Return the permitted recorded result without incorporating again |
| Existing incompatible command | Detect disagreement in operation, arguments, principal, or authority binding | Reject incompatible reuse; do not disclose another binding's result |
| New command with satisfied current guard | Enforce the complete current predicate and command exclusion atomically | Incorporate ownership change, command result, and required outbox intent |
| New command with failed guard | Establish the typed nonincorporation outcome under the command-resolution protocol | No successful claim mutation; retain any separately required rejection record |
| Outcome not established for participant | Preserve uncertainty and the command binding | Reconcile; do not invent a second successful incorporation or rejection |

This decision ordering is a *logical semantic requirement*.
The implementation may combine checks in one protected
transaction or route them through a separate authoritative
read, but the observed behavior must be equivalent to
compatible-history reconciliation before treating the
request as a new command. A command key is *not*
a security capability: its result may be disclosed
only under current authorized disclosure policy,
and a mismatched binding must not reveal another
actor's command existence or stored outcome.

An old command can truthfully have incorporated while
current Request state has been changed by a later
Unclaim, Complete or Reassign. Conversely, a current
claimed card does not attribute incorporation to C42.
A not-found command record at one external pinned
basis does not establish permanent nonincorporation
while a prior attempt may still be pending.
Retention expiration and inaccessible history must
preserve an explicit unresolved/unknown branch
unless stronger authoritative evidence establishes
a different outcome.

The existing-command branch is logically prior to applying the new-command
business guard. A successful retry must not fail merely because the first
incorporation made the Request claimed. It still requires compatible binding
and permitted disclosure. A forbidden lookup must not leak whether a protected
command record exists.

For a new self-claim, the commit guard covers at least:

- the Request exists in the permitted authority scope and is currently open;
- the actor is the authenticated helper and has the required active Membership;
- Membership, Request, and the guarded Organization refer to the same
  Organization through the actual association paths;
- the current Organization policy permits this Claim by this principal;
- the primary-assignment conditions and any absence or uniqueness predicates
  required by the public model contract hold;
- the bound command has not already been incorporated incompatibly or won by a
  concurrent delivery;
- any other declared current policy dependencies are guarded as part of the
  same atomic decision.

**** Real guarded transition, physical race and frame

The original-source invariant is stated against the public model's
actual active-primary RequestAssignment definition. A useful
abstract form is that each permitted Request has *at most one*
currently active primary, but the actual source must define active,
historical/terminal, collaborator versus primary, and any
allowed transition of a Request to and from terminal states.
A proof does not establish *exactly one* primary in every
state: an open or unclaimed Request can legitimately have none.
Source-derived induction must include relevant initializers,
Unclaim, lifecycle transitions, manager Reassign and other
assignment writers, not only the Claim step that is easy to prove.

A new self-Claim must check both the public Request lifecycle
and eligibility/relationship guard *at the actual transaction
conflict boundary*. An external source snapshot, card, client
basis or server pre-read may help prepare the attempt, but cannot
authenticate the transaction-internal prestate. Protect
the absence/uniqueness of another active primary even when
competing helpers create *different assignment document IDs*;
comparing only an existing Request status field is sufficient
only if a qualified shared conflict protocol demonstrably
excludes both incorporations.

The abstract frame and physical footprint are separately
specified. A complete-document PUT can overwrite an unrelated
summary; an assignment status or deletion changes primary
cardinality even without a Request row mutation. Document
replacement, field presence/nil, expected revision,
ABA history, command record, durable outbox intent,
and backend guard/commit semantics retain the exact
10.05–10.07 obligations. A controlled two-helper race
must demonstrate the correct positive winner and actual
nonincorporation of the competing *different* command,
without accidentally eliminating unrelated legitimate
concurrent requests.

Request lifecycle change, primary assignment change, durable command result,
and required publication intent share the promised atomic boundary. An abstract
single-record induction example does not establish this multi-record Claim
contract. If the selected physical adapter supports only one-document updates,
Claim's stronger claim remains unavailable until the complete operation has a
qualified realization or an explicitly admitted implementation premise under a
profile that permits it.

The selected atomicity contract also determines how a guard
failure is *known*. A backend conflict or post-submit
exception may not prove which command incorporated,
and request-local transport failure must not be
reported as a public-model business rejection.
A rejection record, if created, has its own typed
authority and historical disclosure requirements.
A gateway's process-local one-shot capability
prevents a second use of that attempt, not two
separate H1/H2 submissions of the same logical C42.
Durable command binding and exclusion remain
independent model/backend facts.

**** Model, participant and observation outcomes

The outcome mapping is explicit:

| Model outcome | Presentation treatment | Evidence retained |
|---------------+------------------------+-------------------|
| =:committed= | =:accepted= for a successful Claim | Command-specific incorporated result and permitted projection |
| =:rejected= | =:rejected= | Typed rejection justified by the public command-resolution contract |
| =:already-incorporated= | Follow the permitted recorded outcome; a recorded successful Claim is accepted | Historical command attribution, with separate current-state provenance |
| =:commit-unknown= | =:unknown= | Original command binding and unresolved outcome obligation |

An =:already-incorporated= result is *historical* attribution
of the original command to its recorded disposition,
not a new successful domain mutation. If the recorded
outcome was a rejection, the permitted replay presents
that rejection rather than treating every compatible
record as successful Claim. An indeterminate attempt
continues to be =:commit-unknown= until a qualified
authority establishes one of the other outcomes.
The browser's =:accepted= is a projection/presentation
status, not an independent XTDB commit certificate.

The real participant trajectory is separately identified:
the originating button/DOM resource, emitted logical
C42, H1/H2 network requests, settled or unknown adapter
state, current owner/target, permitted authoritative
acquisition, actual target-specific HTMX/OOB completion
and rendered card. An HTTP 200, SSE advisory,
optimistic "Claiming…" badge, event handler call,
source-compatible manifest or readback report does
not establish all of those. A completed domain
transaction remains incorporated when rendering
or DOM installation fails; safe recovery cannot
rewrite that historical fact.

A card reacquisition can restore a current authorized presentation. It cannot
by itself prove which command produced that state. Command-result reconciliation
is a separate protected acquisition. Lost disclosure permission or expired
outcome retention may prevent attribution even while a permitted card read can
supersede the old provisional view. The liveness claim must include the needed
retention and disclosure premises.

**** Correspondence edges and independent physical witnesses

The formalization and assurance apparatus produces a *dependency
record*, not a synthetic proof that every stage occurred. Claim
semantics are owned by the public model, transition and Choreo.
Each physical edge uses the actual source of its authority:

- Original source to abstract proof: exact public interfaces,
  admitted source operation, current normalization, original
  operation/initialization and invariant closure, typed
  rule/projection checks, and checked premise inheritance.
- Proof to issued handler: accepted compatible plan, exact
  model callable and source-owned route, current assembly
  artifacts and required trust contracts.
- Handler to real transaction: current authenticated
  principal and permitted operation/tenant, full atomic
  guard, physical assignment and command-result
  footprint, complete relevant writers and the
  qualified backend isolation/failure semantics.
- Transaction to historical outcome: actual canonical
  command binding and stored result under its retention
  and disclosure contract; H1/H2 receipt and later
  poststate observation are distinct evidence.
- Outcome to browser presentation: actual delivered
  response or allowed authoritative reconciliation,
  current execution/target ownership, scoped
  acquisition, physical DOM completion and
  admitted remote advisory/Refresh policy.

For this slice the correspondence ledger must separately show:

| Obligation | Suitable evidence or explicit premise |
|------------+----------------------------------------|
| Abstract Claim preserves the declared invariant | Checked guarded-transition or induction result over the exact projection |
| Physical records represent that projection | Checked representation definition or scoped trusted mapping |
| Current policy dependencies enter one atomic guard | Constrained lowering plus qualified backend guard semantics, or another justified refinement |
| Physical writes implement only the admitted effects | Complete immutable transaction footprint and frame argument |
| Retry cannot incorporate twice | Atomic command exclusion and durable binding/result contract, including retention |
| Actual invocation uses the admitted plan | Installed entrypoint and gateway mediation evidence |
| Commit and outcome are not confused with delivery | Provider outcome qualification and command-resolution enforcement |
| Required remote notice survives the promised failures | Atomic outbox intent plus the selected dispatch/recovery contract |
| Browser effect follows its permitted result | Explicit outcome mapping and final effect/adoption gates |

The ledger's mandatory evidence categories cannot be discharged by
one generic success flag. It should separately expose a checked
abstract-invariant theorem, admitted operation/projection/plan,
conditional model/public-interface mapping, installed route
and loaded asset identity, physical guarded multi-record write,
durable command/outcome and all-writer qualifications, actual
browser installation and independent eligible user/product
acceptance. Unknown/unsupported checks remain open at
their first responsible boundary; missing positive application
capabilities remain product failures even when source checks pass.

An opt-in command-resolution and XTDB readback mechanism may relate a
source-bound plan, process-local return, pinned command record, and
caller-reported outcome within a declared scope. Such physical
*co-observation* does not by itself authenticate an installed production
route, the current principal, the submitted transaction's causal effect,
the full physical writer set, or actual browser command settlement. Its
results never grant permission to retry, acquire a protected collection,
or install a current DOM target.

**** Independent vertical acceptance and failures

The Claim pilot requires a real eligible browser-originated
positive path and discriminating adversarial neighbors:

1. **Eligible self-Claim:** real authenticated Alice sees an
   authorized open Request R17, the issued button generates
   C42 and H1, the trusted server/model accepts and
   atomically incorporates a new active primary, durable
   C42 result and required publication intent, and
   the permitted real card is physically adopted.
2. **Current authority:** after a rendered card but before
   incorporation Alice loses the effective Membership,
   moves outside permitted Organization/Location policy,
   or Request becomes non-open; the actual protected
   write is rejected, not merely the UI disabled.
3. **Two-helper contention:** Alice/C42 and Bob/C43
   have genuinely concurrent protected attempts for
   the same R17; at most one *new* primary is
   incorporated, the loser has a justified typed
   result, and neither leaves a partial assignment.
4. **Historical replay:** C42 incorporates and H1's
   response is lost; a compatible H2 resolves C42
   without a second incorporation or mistakenly
   rejecting it because R17 is now claimed.
5. **Binding/disclosure:** reusing C42 with different
   Request, actor, operation or arguments rejects;
   an unauthorized history query neither reveals
   another principal's outcome nor supplies a retry
   capability.
6. **Distinct actor/target:** a genuine manager-target
   Reassign guards both the manager's and replacement
   helper's effective rights, and does not borrow
   self-Claim assumptions or silently classify
   a takeover as the same operation.
7. **Current state versus history:** an authorized
   later Unclaim/Reassign changes the current
   primary but preserves C42's recorded past;
   current card state cannot stand in for
   historical attribution.
8. **Partial rendering:** domain incorporation
   succeeds but response markup or one OOB
   target fails; presentation stays honestly
   unresolved/partly installed and uses
   appropriate scoped recovery without
   issuing another Claim.
9. **Deferred/stale browser effect:** an old
   execution receives a delayed response
   after the resource/target is replaced;
   physical effect-time rights reject
   its DOM mutation without erasing a
   real committed command.
10. **Remote advisory/Refresh:** Alice's
    creator-local new Request S can
    appear immediately while Bob's
    remote change R is advisory.
    Bob's one user-authorized Refresh
    acquires and adopts only its permitted
    current scope; SSE delivery alone
    cannot force a whole-board read.
11. **Writer bypass:** a raw admin, background,
    migration or other external XTDB path
    capable of creating a second primary
    is constrained, modeled under an
    approved transition, or left as an
    explicit failed/open physical-closure
    premise—not silently omitted.
12. **Evidence provenance:** a bounded pinned
    readback, matching ledger or copied
    proof report is accepted at its actual
    observation scope but cannot assert
    physical causation, universal refinement,
    installed browser identity or product
    completion without the independent
    witnesses those claims require.
13. **Positive product coverage:** legitimate
    Create, Unclaim, Mark-on-the-way,
    Complete, Cancel, manager Reassign,
    board continuity and recovery remain
    independently required; a Claim-only
    proof cannot erase their absence.

Each acceptance case names the original semantic source,
current authority/host generation, selected physical actor,
operation, command, transport attempt, target/asset,
expected first enforcing boundary, positive neighbor,
adversarial mutation and independently observed
domain/history/browser effect. A source-level
rejection does not certify an untested physical
bypass was prevented. A post-effect diagnostic
may identify a violation but cannot retroactively
undo a committed transaction. A timed-out,
uninspectable or privacy-forbidden observation
is incomplete, not a passed physical refinement.

There is no generic call that proves arbitrary Clojure execution refinement
because an implementation Var was named in a map. Each row must identify the
mechanism that actually establishes it, or retain the precise premise. Passing
one Claim scenario is useful integration evidence; it is not a proof of all
concurrent executions.

*** Formal obligations must return to executable production boundaries
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: req-formal-obligations-return-to-production
:END:

A formal statement about Gesso's admitted semantics is useful only when
the corresponding implementation responsibility can be found, qualified
and checked at the boundary that can actually make the statement true
or false. Every correctness-relevant *formal assumption*, operation,
initial condition, resource, message, observation and permitted failure
retains a traceable origin in the original semantic source and a
named production realization obligation. This is *reverse
traceability*, not an assertion of reverse simulation, executable
completeness or proof that every formal trace can occur in XTDB,
a real browser or a deployed multi-node application.

Part IX owns original-source proof obligation completeness, checked
derivations, assumption inheritance and issuer-controlled admission.
Sections 10.01–10.04 distinguish the formal theorem, the checked
source and the concrete-to-abstract execution/refinement relation;
10.05–10.08 spell out the actual gateway, guard/frame,
writer-universe and HumanHelp Claim obligations. This section
connects them without inventing a second proof language or
accepting hand-authored formal machinery as a replacement
for the application. Sections 10.10–10.12 later own external
checker metatheory, finite abstraction and reproducible proof
artifacts.

A formal conclusion with an unestablished physical edge can still be
a genuine abstract theorem. Its *production* consequence is conditional,
unsupported or not admitted under the selected strong profile.
A report that says "source checked" or "formal proof passed"
cannot silently promote that edge to current runtime authority.

**** Production-obligation record and first enforcing boundary

For every transferred claim, the trusted source-derived ledger
records the exact following facts, with no empty slot interpreted
as success:

| Obligation dimension | Required interpretation |
|----------------------+-------------------------|
| Original source | Model public interface, typed rule, operation, Choreo declaration, initializer, invariant or selected product policy that actually owns the meaning |
| Formal subject | Generated normalized transition/proposition, selected abstraction and observation alphabet, quantifiers, checker/backend version and exact source-to-translation dependencies |
| Proposition and conditions | Assumptions and premises used, failure/unknown semantics, source-derived coverage and nonvacuity requirements, required selected profile and proof method |
| Production subject | Actual model callable, installed handler/worker, plan, route, generated/browser artifact, backend client and deployment/resource generation where relevant |
| Concrete representation | State/data and event mapping, actor/tenant/command identity, field presence, association, abstract frame and physical write/guard/predicate footprints |
| Responsible first boundary | Source type/preflight checker, trusted ingress, protected model policy, transactional commit/conflict check, backend outcome, transport/browser effect-time gate or product acceptance |
| Qualifying evidence | Genuine issuer-controlled check or independent physical observation, owner, provenance, freshness and supported backend/installation/threat scope |
| Remaining obligations | Open implementation/provider/opaque assumptions, unsupported checks, incomplete observation and independent positive/product gates |
| Change and privacy | Exact invalidation/requalification rule, safe source span and redacted witness appropriate to the authorized reviewer |

This is normative *record content*, not a prescribed public map API.
Source locations and normalized IDs help developers navigate the
report, but neither a Clojure Var name nor a source fingerprint proves
the installed handler uses the checked operation. A source
transaction target may depend on Request, RequestAssignment,
Membership, Organization, Location and command history; flattening
all those to an unqualified "current state" destroys the information
needed to prove atomicity and policy correspondence.

The boundary's role must be classified accurately. A source/type
checker can reject a malformed operation before issuance; an
authenticated model guard can prevent an unauthorized protected
effect only if it truly executes before the effect; a
transaction ledger/readback can diagnose one completed event,
but cannot retroactively prevent an invalid commit.
A browser effect-time permission check can prevent
a stale DOM mutation but cannot undo an already committed
domain operation. Distinguish *prevention*, *post-effect
detection*, *bounded observed correspondence* and
*unestablished universal assurance*.

**** Formal assumptions create independently checkable production debts

Every modeled capability or favorable environment hypothesis creates a
matching physical obligation. Representative cases include:

| Formal construct or premise | Required implementation/enforcement edge | Insufficient evidence |
|-----------------------------+------------------------------------------+-----------------------|
| Authenticated principal or tenant | Trusted server/session/service identity, current Membership and permitted authority-domain binding at actual protected call | Browser role flag, copied identity, preflight shape |
| Atomic authoritative operation | Real guarded transaction or independently justified atomic implementation, current prestate/predicate, frame and all relevant writers | Correct pre-read, submitted plan name, single success response |
| Absent active primary | Protected RequestAssignment cardinality/absence predicate across competing distinct IDs and status-changing writers | CAS on an unrelated Request field without proved shared exclusion |
| Stable logical command and once-only incorporation | Durable C42 operation/actor/target/arguments binding, atomic command result/exclusion and qualified historical replay under retention | One-shot H1 submission handle or HTTP request ID |
| Trusted authoritative observation | Provider-qualified basis, actual scoped read/projection, appropriate disclosure and adoption; incomparability preserved | SSE notification, numeric-looking version or caller-supplied basis |
| Fresh browser resource and permitted effect | Real resource/owner generation, retirement, effect-time authorization, actual target-specific DOM/HTMX outcome | Reused DOM ID, callback-entry check, HTTP 200 |
| Eventual command/recovery/notice | Qualified retention, delivery/replay/gap repair, scheduler/provider/fairness and necessary user-action premises | Timeout, one successful retry or a reachable terminal state |
| Closed original operation catalog | Independently rederived initializations, all relevant operations/invariants and proof dependencies | Developer-selected smaller formal state machine |
| Closed installed writer set | Qualified provider/credential/host enforcement across routes, workers, migration/admin and external writers | A fresh but incomplete host enumerator |
| Portable semantic execution | Supported JVM/CLJS/codec/plan and loaded artifact relation under its tested or proved scope | Matching source hash or JVM-only execution |

Such edges may be justified by a dedicated checked mechanism,
a verified compilation/refinement theorem, an actual enforcing
boundary, a carefully delimited third-party/backend contract,
or an explicit profile-permitted opaque premise. The evidence
classes and their strength are *claim specific*. An open premise
may remain in a useful conditional theorem; it cannot be marked
discharged by attaching a shape-compatible success report.
A strict profile rejects unavailable mandatory evidence while
an explicitly requested weaker profile may admit a different,
honestly conditional claim. Neither changes original business
policy without source-owner approval.

An atomic formal Claim action in particular creates an
atomic *production* obligation. A sequence of correctly
observed pre-reads followed by an unconditional write
does not satisfy that obligation, because Claim's current
Request status, helper eligibility, relationship guard,
active-primary absence and command exclusion must be
qualified at the actual protected conflict boundary.
The real backend may use a guarded XTDB transaction,
an equivalent conditional mechanism or a separately
proved implementation; identical source syntax is not
required, but the same relevant observable transition
and rejected/unknown outcomes are.

**** Correspondence direction, coverage and non-vacuity

The strong safety-transfer claim is directional: *every relevant
actual admitted production execution* under its stated environment
and initial-state relation must abstract to an allowed semantic
transition or trace. The chosen abstraction identifies which real
states, events, stuttering/internal steps, failed/unknown outcomes,
concurrent writers, side effects and browser observations count.
A successful generated formal trace, matched operation name or
one correct concrete execution is not the required universal
quantification.

A converse inclusion—every formal trace is physically realizable—
is a distinct completeness claim if the selected profile needs it.
A correct source-level counterexample can be physically
unrealizable because of a deliberate abstraction overapproximation,
a stronger deployed guard or excluded environment schedule.
The *formal* safety claim still fails in that selected model,
unless a justified refinement of the model or property removes
the spurious behavior. The production claim cannot be declared
false until the concrete relation and realizability are examined.

A different danger is a model that omits a real operation or
declares Init empty, so its invariant is trivially true.
Source-derived original catalog closure, satisfiable/representative
initial state, real eligible Claim and independent HumanHelp
capability positives prevent such vacuous success from satisfying
the claimed application. A universal proof over a carefully
restricted subset is not a proof that the subset describes
all actual source or physical behavior. A complete submitted
DAG is not necessarily a complete *original-source*
obligation ledger.

Progress transfer has additional fairness, execution-continuation,
retention, availability, delivery, quiescence and authorized
participant-action conditions. A safety simulation that allows
indefinite stuttering need not provide progress. Under
HumanHelp's explicit Refresh policy the browser may legitimately
remain unaware of remote changes until its user grants one
scoped acquisition. Modeling the user as eventually refreshing
without a stated premise changes product semantics and
cannot support an unconditional liveness theorem.

**** Generated formal artifacts derive from source; repair the owner

The preferred generation path is:

#+begin_example
actual Gesso and application semantic declarations
                     |
       trusted original-source normalization/checking
                     |
            admitted semantic subject
               /              \
    checked formal           issued production
    translation              plan/operation
          |                        |
 external formal check        real installed realization
          \                        /
       correspondence + named open premises
                     |
        qualified claim and source-level diagnosis
#+end_example

Do not replace it with:

#+begin_example
handwritten Clojure model  --- manually kept in sync ---
                              separately handwritten formal model
#+end_example

A framework-maintained translation to Recife, Quint/TLA+,
Lean or another supported backend is a derivative of the
admitted semantic source. Backend version, translation
rules, checker inputs, selected bounds/abstractions and
actual generated bytes remain identified and reproducible.
The backend can have its own implementation defects or
soundness premises. A proof about the generated model is
not a proof that the *translator* preserved the original
meaning or that production executed that meaning.

Application developers must not have to author, debug
or hand-synchronize such a second formal specification.
They may inspect or request explanations of emitted formal
code. Maintainers may directly repair the framework's
translation as a source-controlled framework change.
Changing a generated invariant in place so it becomes
weaker and a checker turns green is not an application
repair and cannot establish the previously claimed
property. An intentional weakening of the actual
business invariant is a *visible owner-selected
policy change*, requiring corresponding source,
proof, application and product reacceptance.

**** Counterexamples identify the modeled failure, not an invented physical event

Suppose a *candidate defective* Claim model checks Request
=:open= at an earlier observation and fails to require
that status at its commit action. A formal checker may
produce this bounded trace:

#+begin_example
COUNTEREXAMPLE IN THE FORMAL SUBJECT
Property: Claim requires an eligible, open Request at incorporation.
A observes Request R open.
B observes Request R open.
A incorporates Claim for R.
B incorporates another active primary Claim for R without an intervening release.
Scope: the selected candidate model, initial states and exploration bounds.
Physical XTDB execution of this history: not established.
#+end_example

That is a counterexample to the defective *formal candidate*
if its admitted transitions really allow those incorporates.
It is not a counterexample to a correctly guarded formal Claim
action, nor evidence that the real XTDB model actually performed
both writes. If the generated model purported to include
the current-open guard, inspect source normalization,
translation, property and abstraction before attributing
the counterexample to a production bug.

Conversely, a correct abstract guarded model may pass while
an installed writer uses an outdated Request pre-read and
unconditional PUT. Then the source-level theorem may be
valid while the real refinement obligation is open or
refuted. A matching pinned poststate, command ledger
or local transaction receipt can be bounded diagnostic
evidence without authenticating causation or excluding
other physical writers.

A good counterexample/first-blocker diagnostic retains:

- original named property, its semantic subject and current
  source location; the actual original model and operation
  catalog against which completeness was checked;
- the smallest *reproducible and meaning-preserving* trace
  prefix or typed-rule valuation, including actor/command,
  Request/assignment and observation identities only where
  authorized and genuinely relevant;
- selected formal encoding, checker version, abstraction,
  finite bounds, fair/unfair schedule assumptions,
  source-to-generated relationship and exact failure
  classification (counterexample, unsupported,
  exhausted, vacuous, stale or incomplete);
- the exact failing semantic guard, frame, knowledge or
  premise, if supported by the evidence; otherwise
  the plausible alternative model/translation/physical
  owners still under examination;
- the production callable/route/worker, transaction/
  writer or browser effect and its current generation,
  and the first actual enforcement/observation boundary
  to be checked separately;
- which checked propositions remain valid, which
  specific physical bridge is absent, and whether
  an independent *actual* implementation trace
  concretizes the modeled failure.

This is a data and explanation contract, not permission
to expose raw private Request, Membership, command
record, XTDB query or actor identities in a copyable
report. Diagnostics use stable structured reasons
and authorized redacted source witnesses, with
correlation handles interpreted only at trusted
boundaries. A failing downstream artifact blocked
by one missing root premise is not reported as
a collection of independent semantic bugs.

When reducing a counterexample, an automated shrinker
must retain the discrepancy and the declared source
semantics, not merely find a shorter trace with
a different failure. A minimized finite counterexample
is bounded by the generated/tested language and domains;
it does not become a universal proof or a real
production incident by being reproducible.

**** Source-level and production repair are distinct ownership decisions

The supported correction loop is:

#+begin_example
original Clojure/Gesso source and actual product policy
        -> source-checkable admitted semantics
        -> regenerated formal subject and executable plan
        -> independently classified proof/model-checking result
        -> source-located counterexample or missing obligation
        -> identify semantic, translation, provider, or physical repair owner
        -> owner-approved source/implementation/assumption repair
        -> rerun source, proof, assembler, production and product gates
#+end_example

The possible owners are separate:

| Finding | Correct owner and repair | What cannot count as repair |
|---------+--------------------------+-----------------------------|
| Defective admitted model guard | Application/public model owner corrects the actual rule/transition; rebuild proof and issued plan | Only editing a generated TLA+/Quint/Recife guard |
| Incorrect formal lowering | Framework maintainer fixes translation and rechecks semantic correspondence, checker and emitted artifacts | Weakening the formal property to agree with buggy lowering |
| Abstract overapproximation | Review abstraction and property against original semantics; refine within supported meaning with explicit applicability | Suppressing a real abstract counterexample or declaring it physical by fiat |
| Production lacks qualified atomic guard | Model/host/backend owner repairs the actual guarded write and tests concurrent effects; formal source theorem may remain valid | Adding a true statement to a correspondence report |
| Missing original-source operation or physical writer | Restore source completeness or real writer confinement/qualified exception; recheck dependent theorem | Removing the writer from a host enumerator |
| Current business policy differs from intention | HumanHelp owner explicitly changes and independently accepts model policy and product requirements | Letting a proof tool infer user/product intent from prose |
| Unsupported checker/proof fragment | Add a compatible admitted proof mechanism or retain an allowed precise premise/other claim class | Silent downgraded =:kernel-checked=, timeout-as-success |
| Browser effect occurs after retirement | Repair current owner/effect-time permission and real shell behavior; exercise actual DOM completion | Passing a source-only adapter test while the stale callback still mutates |

An assistant or automated tool can propose and explain
these repairs, but it does not acquire business-policy
authority, trusted source issuance, deployed writer
access or checker acceptance. A proposal is not
a certificate. Repairs must preserve the
same original-source requirement or explicitly
announce a changed policy, applicability or
assumption. Re-run the relevant negative mutation
and a *real eligible positive control*; a repair
that simply rejects all Claim attempts is not
HumanHelp acceptance.

**** Acceptance: both directions of explanation and independent evidence

For each production-transferred formal claim, Gesso
must answer two questions without requiring developers
to manually reconcile two source languages:

1. *Which original semantic object, executable
   production boundary and current host/asset
   generation does this formal subject constrain?*
2. *Which actual evidence discharges each
   correctness-relevant assumption used by the
   formal claim, and which remain open?*

The following positive/adversarial pairs are
required at their applicable scope:

1. **Source origin:** a generated Claim model,
   exact original source and emitted plan share
   checked semantics; a hand-modified formal
   model or stale source-ID pair does not pass.
2. **Original completeness:** all declared
   operations/initializers and invariant
   dependencies appear; a pruned Unclaim
   catalog is rejected as complete proof.
3. **Abstract counterexample:** the defective
   pre-read-only Claim candidate yields a
   scoped source-located trace; a genuinely
   guarded candidate is not falsely blamed.
4. **Correct model/incorrect implementation:**
   formal atomic guard succeeds; an
   unguarded deployed writer fails
   execution/refinement rather than the
   correct abstract theorem.
5. **Trusted actor:** current authenticated
   helper/Organization policy authorizes
   eligible Claim; browser role assertion
   does not discharge actor authority.
6. **Absence and uniqueness:** real concurrent
   different-command Claims preserve one
   active primary; two stale pre-reads
   followed by distinct assignment inserts
   cannot count as guarded incorporation.
7. **C42 historical result:** compatible
   H1/H2 recovery returns the qualified
   recorded result; a current Request
   card or missing row at one basis
   cannot invent historical rejection.
8. **Physical witness scope:** one selected
   actual gateway call and pinned readback
   support their reported local facts;
   copied receipt, wrong node or third-party
   intervening writer cannot gain
   universal causal authority.
9. **Stale resource:** current browser owner
   adopts only permitted target content;
   retired callback cannot mutate a
   reused DOM ID even if HTTP 200 arrived.
10. **Notification and permission:** a durable
    advisory with qualified eventual
    delivery/replay may support the named
    progress claim; SSE arrival alone
    cannot grant remote Refresh.
11. **Tool failure:** a finished supported
    proof check can be distinguished from
    timeout, unsupported translation,
    empty finite Init or lost external
    checker; none is success by default.
12. **Counterexample provenance:** a finite
    model trace maps back to exact source
    and explicit open physical question;
    source-located report does not
    invent an actual XTDB incident.
13. **Correct source repair:** changed
    original guard or verified translator
    regenerates all dependencies and
    passes relevant checks; editing only
    the emitted model is insufficient.
14. **Physical repair:** an actually
    guarded deployed writer prevents
    the competing invalid effect;
    a post hoc ledger discrepancy
    cannot be called pre-effect
    prevention.
15. **Product non-vacuity:** an eligible
    self-Claim and required
    Unclaim/Reassign/other Part VIII
    capabilities remain exercised;
    reject-all is not completeness.
16. **Topology:** single-/multi-node
    deployments preserve the same
    abstract Claim meaning, with
    separate routing, credential,
    writer and failure premises;
    node loss is not an
    authority grant or
    unconditional convergence.

Each case states the original source,
profile, positive control, adversarial
mutation, formal abstraction and bound,
first checker/physical enforcing boundary,
and independent relevant observation.
The report distinguishes prevention,
scoped diagnostic detection, proof
counterexample and unobserved uncertainty.
An uninspected route or external
database writer remains open, not
conveniently absent.

The final invariant is that formal
assurance *constrains the implementation
Gesso actually installs and operates*.
It cannot become an independent story
that is true only of generated models,
nor can a real passing test fabricate
a theorem that has not been checked.
*** External formalization has a concrete first target

The first external theorem target is the *closed propositional proof
kernel* and its acceptance relation, because its language and trusted
judgments are small enough to specify independently of arbitrary
Clojure, XTDB transactions, the browser and the full Choreo machine.
The purpose is to remove a specific trust assumption from Part IX's
proof issuer, *not* to assert that having a proof assistant has already
proved the framework or every application using it.

Ordinary application authors define rules, model operations and
Choreo constructions in Gesso's admitted Clojure/data interfaces.
The framework derives the formal subjects and proof obligations.
They do not maintain a second handwritten HumanHelp specification
or write Lean tactics, Quint, TLA+ or Recife models to use an
ordinary admitted operation. Framework maintainers may choose a
proof assistant such as Lean, another proof-producing checker or
a mechanized semantics with a suitably small trusted checker.
The architectural requirement is the theorem and evidence-import
contract, not a permanent commitment to one tool vendor or syntax.

Part IX supplies the original subject, typed proposition source,
small proof rules, source-derived dependency closure, premise
inheritance, checker admission and explicit open assumptions.
Sections 10.01–10.04 specify formal/theorem versus runtime
correspondence; 10.09 names the independent production discharge
obligations. External formalization must preserve these boundaries
rather than add an unrelated parallel assurance scheme.
10.11 owns exact-finite exploration/abstraction and 10.12 owns
the broader reproducible evidence package.

**** Specify the closed inference system before proving it

The initial formal calculus covers the same *seven* inference rules
as the admitted Gesso propositional kernel, with their exact
well-formedness, arity, ordering, reference and conclusion
restrictions:

| Admitted rule | Semantic consequence and required shape |
|---------------+----------------------------------------|
| =:premise= | A declared named premise P remains open and entails P |
| =:truth-introduction= | Truth is derivable without taking an unrecorded atom as true |
| =:implication-reflexivity= | For the same well-formed P, P implies P |
| =:conjunction-introduction= | From admitted P1 ... Pn, n at least two, derive the matching conjunction in the selected source order |
| =:conjunction-elimination= | From a checked conjunction derive exactly its selected indexed conjunct |
| =:implication-elimination= | From P implies Q and P, in the required reference order, derive Q |
| =:disjunction-introduction= | From P derive a disjunction containing exactly that P at the declared supported position |

A calculus statement quantifies over well-formed finite formula trees,
finite derivation sequences, all valid rule parameter values and
all Boolean valuations of the distinct admitted *opaque atoms*.
The atom declarations are inert for this propositional theorem:
the theorem does *not* decide whether an embedded age,
Membership or Request policy predicate is true of real
application state. Formula syntax admits its defined truth
connectives; the seven *inference rules* do not thereby acquire
additional proof operations. Neither the presence of
=:not= or =:false= in a proposition nor a valid semantic
tautology licenses an unimplemented classical proof rule,
arithmetic solver, arbitrary rewriting, atomic-truth axiom
or hypothetical-context discharge.

Let =Gamma= be the named open source premises, =D= a
well-formed source derivation, =P= its exact goal and =v=
a total Boolean valuation of the opaque atoms in the
admitted formulas. The initial external soundness target is:

#+begin_example
For every supported original source Gamma, D, P:
  If the defined small-kernel derivation relation accepts D
  from Gamma with conclusion P, then
  for every Boolean valuation v:
    (every premise in Gamma that D actually depends on
     is true under v) implies P is true under v.
#+end_example

The antecedent must use the *defined inference rules*, not an
opaque call to Gesso's own implementation checker—otherwise the
proof could accidentally assume precisely the correctness it is
meant to establish. The formal theorem states how used premises
are computed by rule references and what happens to declarations
not used by a particular step. The source admission path may
additionally require all declared premises/steps to participate;
that stricter input discipline must not be confused with a
logical rule that discharges unused assumptions. A finite
closed derivation with =Gamma= empty is unconditional
*only for the admitted opaque-Boolean interpretation*.

Proofs may be vacuous under inconsistent premises; a valid
logical entailment does not prove that the application can
ever reach a state satisfying those premises. Nonempty
initial state, reachable eligible operations, authenticated
actor context and real product capability have different
independent obligations. A theorem proving
=Gamma |= P= cannot silently produce =P= unless
=Gamma= is actually discharged or separately justified.

**** Five distinct theorem and implementation claims

The formalization has at least five separately reported
objectives. A later result may depend on earlier ones, but
a single passing artifact does not collapse them.

1. *S0 — Inference-rule soundness.* Every admitted rule
   schema preserves Boolean entailment for all legal
   formulas, arities, indices and reference patterns.
   Formalize the rules independently and prove their
   preservation lemmas, including the premise rule's
   open-assumption effect.

2. *S1 — Derivation-system soundness.* Induct on the
   finite ordered derivation. Each source step inherits
   exactly the used named open premises of its valid
   predecessor steps, and the final step entails the
   declared goal. Forward references, cycles,
   wrong-conclusion substitution, undeclared premise
   use and unsupported rules are outside the admitted
   derivation relation rather than trusted exceptions.
   A mathematical induction proof is not evidence
   that a particular Clojure parser enforces it.

3. *S2 — Actual Clojure checker correspondence.*
   For all supported concrete inputs accepted by
   the *production* parser, normalizer, proof checker
   and current admission path, establish a semantics-
   preserving relation to the formal derivation
   relation of S1. Include original-source normalization,
   nominal variable/subject identity, premise and step
   references, source rejection, malformed encodings,
   resource limits and implementation/version binding.
   This can be a proven implementation/refinement,
   verified extraction, an independently checked
   translation or a separately qualified trust
   premise. Simply invoking the production checker
   from the formal model is not independence.

4. *S3 — Typed atomic-proposition correspondence.*
   Relate opaque Boolean atom valuations to the
   actual supported typed-rule evaluator under its
   original source, reader footprint, presence/nil
   semantics, runtime variable bindings and
   evaluation/error contract. The conditional
   propositional theorem cannot establish any
   arbitrary Clojure implementation predicate,
   model eligibility or current server input.
   A bounded typed-atom oracle establishes only
   its enumerated original bindings unless an
   additional abstraction/correspondence theorem
   justifies wider scope.

5. *S4 — Issuer/composition and source-to-production
   transfer.* Bind the exact source derivation and
   checked theorem to the trusted current source,
   original-source-required obligation ledger,
   certificate issuer, selected admission profile,
   premise inheritance, compatible consuming
   operation and installed execution boundaries.
   The actual server model guard, XTDB write,
   loaded browser asset or protected read needs
   its own qualification under 10.04–10.09.
   A correct calculus theorem does not mint
   runtime authorization or a durable
   transferable certificate.

A final application claim must state exactly which S0–S4
edges were established and which remain conditional,
tested, source-checked or unknown. It is legitimate
to prove S0–S1 before S2–S4. That yields a useful
formal result but *not* an externally proven Clojure
checker, sound whole-application composition or
formally verified HumanHelp deployment.

**** Checker semantics, resource bounds and fail-closed admission

The actual acceptance relation includes more than
the names of seven inference rules. It must define
which original source forms are admissible: metadata-
free/plain structures where required, qualified IDs,
exact keys, typed nominal contexts, formula
depth/arity, atom encoding, duplicate or unused
steps, strictly prior references, all required
dependency/assumption bindings and the exact goal.

A bounded production checker can soundly reject
inputs because of a configured depth, formula-node,
proof-step, premise, atom or computation budget.
Such conservative rejection does not refute
*soundness* of what it does admit.
Completeness—for example, admission of all
otherwise valid derivations in the advertised
supported/bounded domain—is a separate
usability/property target. The strong
product acceptance must not be satisfied by a
checker or constructed application that
rejects every legitimate Claim.

A successful proof result, a genuine semantic
counterexample, a malformed-source rejection,
an unsupported rule/judgment, exhausted
resource budget, external tool failure and
unavailable checker are distinct dispositions.
If a selected profile requires S2 or another
external theorem at construction, an unavailable,
timed-out or mismatched check fails that
*new* admission. The framework may continue
serving a previously admitted still-current
assembly under its actual lifetime contract;
it cannot silently downgrade the profile,
invent a checked theorem or grant
an unauthorized protected operation.

Preprocessing and normalization belong inside
the correspondence boundary. An independently
sound rule calculus cannot compensate for a
normalizer that drops a premise, changes the
formula tree, coalesces distinct typed atoms
incorrectly or maps source proposition A
to theorem subject B. Revalidating just
the resulting normalized formula is not
necessarily validation of the *original*
source claim. A checked trusted source-to-
normal-form semantics relation is needed.

**** External backend and theorem evidence import

The external backend must produce evidence whose
meaning is independent of source-level report
labels. The evidence package identifies at least:

- the immutable formal theorem statement, explicitly
  admitted axioms or trusted primitives, proposition
  and proof-rule definitions, theorem/checker version,
  backend/toolchain configuration and claim category;
- the canonical original-source semantic subject,
  normalized representation, dependency/obligation
  closure, source-to-formal encoding and all versions
  required to interpret them;
- a proof term or independently checkable result
  where the backend supports one, together with the
  exact trusted checker/admission mechanism;
- finite-domain or generated conformance coverage,
  resource/execution budgets and any unsupported
  language features when these are supplementary
  *tests*, not the external universal theorem;
- current exact issuer/consumer binding, selected
  semantic source, required open/used premises,
  installed asset/plan identity if the claim
  transfers to production, and all unresolved
  S2–S4 implementation/environment obligations;
- a reproducible invocation and observed disposition
  with privacy-appropriate diagnostics, source
  correspondence and invalidation/rechecking triggers.

A Lean proof might be one implementation of the S0–S1
evidence. A separate kernel/checker or supported
proof-producing tactic may be used, but the trusted
assumption set must state the actual proof-checking
kernel and any imported axioms. A successful CLI
exit code, copyable EDN report or saved
"proved" label is not itself trusted proof origin.
A checker-based import should recheck the actual
proof/evidence at the selected current consumer,
or rely on a properly qualified persistent
attestation/lifecycle contract rather than
raw purported hashes.

The external checker does not need physical
XTDB/network/Chromium access to prove S0.
That is precisely why the abstract theorem and
its independently qualified runtime transfer
are separate. Proof/diagnostic sidecars must
not change an already admitted runtime
state transition or become a principal,
one-Refresh grant, command retry authorization
or browser effect lease.

The tool-independent exchange need not be a
single universal serialization format, but
every backend must preserve the exact canonical
judgment and evidence class. A backend may
reject unsupported constructs honestly;
it cannot silently translate them to
axioms, omit difficult cases or assert
all application obligations discharged.

**** Independent oracles, mutations and common-mode bugs

Gesso's own independent rule-interpretation
and finite audits are valuable *falsifiers*
of claimed correspondence. They can expose
a changed inference index, missing premise,
malformed step, normalized atom mismatch
or deliberate invalid rule. Running the
same Clojure normalizer in two wrappers
does not independently validate the
normalizer; an independently written
reference can discover more bugs but
requires its own domain/soundness
qualifications.

An exhaustive truth table over one
finite set of opaque atoms proves
only the particular local entailment
within that declared domain. Checking
one representative for each of the
seven rule tags does not quantify
over every formula tree, premise
combination, conjunction arity,
conjunct index, depth or
malformed source form.
A compositional source-level
induction over a finite derivation
is stronger for *that derivation*
than checking only its final
Boolean valuation sample, but
its local rule and interpreter
premises must remain explicit.
Neither result automatically
establishes the universal
mathematical metatheorem or
production Clojure implementation.

A required acceptance corpus includes paired
positive/adversarial controls:

1. A valid derivation of a source premise is
   accepted *with that premise open*; the
   same source with the premise omitted
   must not yield an unconditional theorem.
2. Premise-free truth introduction and
   implication reflexivity are checked
   for arbitrary supported well-formed
   formulas; an invented arbitrary
   typed-atom truth axiom is rejected.
3. Correct two-or-more conjunction
   introduction and indexed elimination
   preserve their source order; reversed
   premise order, invalid arity or
   out-of-range index is rejected.
4. Implication elimination requires its
   exact implication and antecedent;
   swapped references or changed
   consequent fails the rule.
5. Disjunction introduction requires
   the indexed embedded source
   conjunct; a different injected
   atom or unsupported position
   cannot be inferred.
6. Valid references use previously
