its *named acknowledged boundary*; no
unnecessary per-recipient permanent success
ledger is imposed when duplicate authorized
advisories and bounded replay/recovery
suffice. That choice does not license
unbounded duplicate amplification, false
completion acknowledgments or lost required
notification semantics.

The release evidence separately records
authoritative commit, retained outbox
intent, dispatcher claim, broker/router
acceptance, selected interested host,
SSE frame attempt, client receipt,
authorized acquisition and physical
DOM adoption. Neither a broker acknowledgment
nor an SSE write demonstrates that every
subscriber received or adopted the change.
A duplicate invalidation may ask a
permitted client to recheck current state;
it never creates a second Claim or grants
permission to adopt a remote board.

*** Close interest-registration and router-failover gaps

An initial subscription races with
authoritative changes. A committed change
may precede an interest being effectively
known to the router; a host-local filter
may have learned a client the replacement
router has not yet learned. The selected
protocol must establish a registration
fence, replay/gap record, qualified
comparison frontier or conservative
authorized re-acquisition sufficient
for the claimed subscription semantics.
The system cannot infer currentness from
silence on a stream.

Effective interest, retained publication
interval and covered authoritative basis
must be related by an independently
qualified coordinate or checked bridge
when they use different token schemes.
A token echoed from the request, a
router-local "seen" bit, or a healthy
backup process is not evidence that an
interested recipient's interval was
covered. Loss, reordered registration,
expired replay cursor, changed filter
or routing cutover must either preserve
the intended coverage or expose an
unresolved gap that blocks the stronger
currentness/delivery claim.

A distributed interest filter is an
optimization over an authorized
notification candidate set. A
partitioned or hierarchical filter
cannot exclude a recipient solely
because its local view is incomplete.
Replica/filter completeness,
version exchange, stale-router fencing,
fall-back fanout and bounded
conservative redelivery are eligible
mechanisms when their own capacity,
leakage, deduplication and coverage
premises are met. A failed router
may be recovered by re-sending more
notices than necessary; correctness
does not require remembering every
earlier successful destination if
that larger delivery is safe and
its work bound is justified.

Overdelivery may still leak tenant
membership, Request existence,
participant activity or routing
metadata. Current authorization
at dispatch, subscription and
protected read remains obligatory;
"conservative" does not mean
broadcasting protected data to all.
A receiver cannot claim delivery
of a required invalidation that
never reached it merely because
another router had a compatible
Bloom/vacuum filter or a host
reported itself healthy.

After an observed gap, the system
may refuse to claim current
coverage and retain advisory or
recovery debt until a current
permitted read at sufficient
provider basis discharges the
specified scope. It cannot turn
an unobserved missing event into
a fictitious positive stream
receipt or silently clear debt.

*** Preserve source progression, authorization and selective adoption

A replacement host reads under a
qualified provider, transaction
basis and query scope; the
frontier must be a real observed
provider fact and sufficient for
the required original semantic
progression. Transaction time,
valid time, domain revision,
command causality, stream cursor,
interest-frontier and browser
knowledge are not exchangeable
scalars. A lagging read or
unsupported provider option
returns a typed insufficient/
unavailable state rather than
reporting that the requested
basis was attained.

Each host and router reestablishes
current authenticated principal,
Organization Membership,
operation eligibility, protected
subscription, result disclosure
and query coverage at their
actual trusted boundaries.
An old connection, host ID,
serialized certificate, source
digest or stale permission
snapshot cannot authorize a
new effect after revocation.
A replacement process may
retain valid command evidence
while properly denying an
ineligible principal the
result.

For HumanHelp, Alice's own
qualified committed Claim can
settle her scoped pending
action. Bob's remote Request
lifecycle change remains
*advisory* until his
explicit user-authorized
Refresh, subject only to
the separately declared
own-command and affected-card
repair exceptions. A new
router, host, websocket/SSE
reconnect, asset reload or
backfilled invalidation never
manufactures a Refresh grant.
The permitted read must
cover the required cohort
and progression; an old
callback cannot install into
a new DOM resource or erase
incomparable newer advisory
debt. Withheld authorization
requires nondisclosure,
not fabricated convergence.

Direct participant-message
features may have independently
specified ephemeral or
durable delivery semantics.
A best-effort typing
message is not a recoverable
domain-state invalidation.
No universal global actor
directory, durable suspended
choreography engine or
router language is necessary
for ordinary Request
interactions; if a selected
direct-message feature
promises stronger receipt
or persistence, its own
protocol and tests remain
mandatory.

*** Establish real mixed-release, resource and fault evidence

The release profile fixes the
actually reachable A/A,
A/B, B/A and B/B client/server
directions from 11.08,
complete source-derived
continuation contracts and
retained assets from 11.09,
and semantic retirement/
command recovery from 11.10.
A safe per-host activation
does not prove an
all-host atomic cutover.
Host replacement and
failover must exercise
compatible request and
browser asset paths,
pending work ownership,
old/new schema reader
and writer safety,
stale client/stream
retirement and current
credential/authorization
conditions.

The physical acceptance suite
uses independently isolated
application processes and
the actual selected XTDB,
transaction adapter,
router/broker boundary,
installed Ring/Biff handlers,
real browser/transport assets
and representative authenticated
users. Test setups which
share in-JVM process state
where independence is claimed,
intercept only a test wrapper
or label two local maps
as two hosts cannot establish
this milestone. A negative
case is credited only when
the intended *real*
enforcing boundary rejects
the invalid action, and
a related eligible positive
case succeeds through
that same gateway.

A production performance and
failure envelope identifies
host/router/dispatcher count,
process and queue limits,
interest/filter cardinality,
outstanding outbox/debt,
event rates, retention,
replay pressure, failover
latency, load-balancing
strategy, target/browser
population, backend
consistency/availability,
network partitions and
supported recovery duration.
It measures capacity,
isolation, overload,
queue backpressure,
misrouting and leak-free
retirement under those
specific conditions rather
than quoting only peak
successful request rate.
Unbounded memory, queued
callbacks, publication debt
or retained assets do not
become acceptable because
a short throughput test
passed.

Recovery/progress evidence
names when backend and
network service return,
router/filter knowledge
converges, durable records
remain available, current
authorization permits
disclosure, and a participant
actually performs any
required Refresh.
Without those premises,
safety and honest blocked/
unknown status remain the
required result; unconditional
eventual browser convergence
is not promised. Revoked
Membership may make correct
outcome nondisclosure rather
than success. The selected
release's stricter progress
claims need appropriate
fairness and anti-divergence
evidence, not just successful
finite examples.

*** Multi-node positive and adversarial production histories

| Required qualifying history | Nearby invalid result or claim |
|-----------------------------+--------------------------------|
| Independent A and C processes exercise one original production Claim meaning | Two process labels share one process-local registry while claiming host independence |
| Real XTDB model guards permit one of two competing helpers to become primary | Cross-host stale reads permit two active primary assignments |
| C receives C42 original binding and authorized replay or historical result | C creates fresh command C43 merely because A's response was lost |
| C preserves truthful =:commit-unknown= until sufficient command evidence exists | Current Request state or missing record is falsely attributed to C42/rejection |
| Committed Request, command result and required publication intent survive A loss | A dies after commit and sole in-memory callback loses notification debt |
| Surviving dispatcher safely repeats an unacknowledged advisory | Failed acknowledgment doubles the authoritative Claim |
| Broker/router acknowledgment is labeled only for its real boundary | SSE send or broker success is claimed as every browser's receipt |
| Subscription registration is fenced with read/replay coverage | Commit between initial read and effective interest is silently missed |
| Replaced router covers stale or unknown interest via checked recovery | Healthy backup with stale filter silently drops required notice |
| Conservative authorized redelivery repairs uncertain routes under resource bounds | Replayed event exposes other Organization's protected Request metadata |
| Expired replay cursor produces typed gap and permitted re-acquisition | Stream silence or echoed cursor is reported as current authorized observation |
| C performs sufficient provider-basis read or reports insufficiency | Lagging snapshot is installed as satisfying a newer progression frontier |
| C authenticates current principal before protected command/result read | Old A session or source digest reauthorizes revoked Membership |
| Bob gets remote advisory, then explicitly refreshes authorized covered board | Cross-host notice or reconnect automatically adopts new remote rows |
| New owned browser resource installs current result under justified basis | Retired A callback overwrites B's DOM or clears newer debt |
| Genuine compatible mixed A/B client-server routes remain enforced | Sticky routing test misses failover to unsupported old writer/decoder |
| Supported rollback respects actual schema, pending durable work and assets | Prior passing binary is activated against incompatible migrated state |
| True router or host loss is injected and independently observed | Crash simulation does not terminate claimed process or real link |
| Real positive protected Claim succeeds beside adversarial rejection | Reject-all handler passes negative-only tests |
| Bounded queued/debt/filter work recovers after declared overload | Unbounded memory/worker leak hidden by short throughput sample |
| Unauthorized ephemeral typing is discarded under current recipient rights | Best-effort message is treated as durable Request incorporation |
| Root ledger records open physical writer/host premises and exact topology | Local report, copied status or two-host demo is called universal deployment proof |
| Required liveness progresses once declared fairness/availability/user-action conditions hold | Offline Bob with no Refresh is said to have adopted every update |
| After principal revocation, safe nondisclosure is observed | Repair/replay leaks protected historical command result to old session |

These are *prospective* physical,
source-semantic and deployment
tests, not observations that
an implementation presently
satisfies this milestone.
A successful two-host pilot
may satisfy selected bounded
cases while failing the
required production load,
failure or route/interest
envelope. The complete
claim retains the original
selected requirements and
every missing mandatory
case; it cannot shrink
the denominator to
successful observed paths.

*** Milestone decision and remaining scope

The multi-node production
milestone is admitted only
for its exact specified
topology, authoritative
backend/adapter, installed
source and artifact
generations, selected
fault and resource
envelope, exposed routing
directions, current
security assumptions and
authentic observed tests.
It verifies that the same
Gesso/HumanHelp operation
semantics survive the
claimed host movements,
publication and interest
gaps, command uncertainty,
authorized acquisition
and release overlap, with
all required external
premises transparently
qualified.

The root result identifies
original-source required
coverage, actual installed
host/writer/dispatcher and
router evidence, selected
provider qualification,
positive and negative
fault oracles, load and
retention bounds, completed
gates, still-open
assumptions and any
unsupported profile
requirements. Source
theorems, formal proof
issuance and current
runtime/operation authority
retain their own named
claims: neither production
resilience nor successful
fault injection proves
general semantic
soundness or independent
kernel meta-soundness.

A safer, narrower deployment
may be separately admitted
where its independently
selected profile and
actually enforced routing/
recovery restrictions
permit it. A failing
strict multi-node claim
cannot silently be reported
as complete under a
different profile. The
same semantic machine
remains the target of
one-node and many-node
implementations; later
routers, brokers, Rust
optimizations or new host
layouts are physical
replacements requiring
their own appropriate
correspondence and failure
qualification, not a
second application policy.

*** The four scopes do not collapse into one status

Completion is a set of *four separately justified milestone judgments*,
not one status called "Gesso complete" or an ordering constraint on
project implementation. The subjects are:

| Milestone | What its complete result actually establishes | Other conclusions that do not follow |
|-----------+----------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------|
| Operational application | All independently required HumanHelp product capabilities work through qualified installed model, host and browser paths within the selected operational profile | Independent kernel soundness, unbounded formal proof or production multi-node resilience |
| Compositional certification | The named source-complete, non-vacuous typed/checker/issuance chain and genuine multi-record Claim pilot meet their selected profile | Every HumanHelp interaction works, the checker is independently proved sound or the real physical backend is universally refined |
| External formal verification | The exact accepted independent formal theorem and qualified S0–S4 correspondence frontier of the selected external profile are established with their premises | Current Request authorization, complete product behavior or arbitrary installed XTDB/browser correctness |
| Multi-node production | The original single-machine semantics survive the selected actual independent-host, router, recovery, compatibility, security and load/fault envelope | An unbounded theorem, all possible topologies or independent proof-kernel soundness |

These milestones have independent *requirement denominators* derived
from Parts VIII–X and 11.13–11.16. Their work can overlap, and
one can be complete before another. They are not aliases for
development stage numbers, a cumulative project percentage,
or automatic implications in either direction. A successful
Claim proof pilot can coexist with missing Response interaction;
a usable operational application can coexist with an unproved
external checker; a physically resilient two-host application
can still have an unestablished semantic theorem.

They are also distinct from the *four release decisions*
of 11.02: candidate admission, installation eligibility,
activation eligibility and completion. A candidate can be
correctly admitted but never installed, installed but not
activated, or active under an allowed smaller release intent
without meeting a separately requested stronger completion
milestone. An abstract completion theorem does not authorize
installation or a live command. A permitted operational
release does not become a failed release merely because
an unselected formal milestone remains unfinished;
conversely, it cannot satisfy an originally requested
strict formal or multi-node release profile by silently
renaming the requested claim.

*** Completion records bind original requirements and actual evidence

A completion record is a *checked result for one named
release intent, milestone, subject and environment*,
derived from a source-complete requirement ledger and
qualified evidence. It is not an independently authored
status word. The root human-readable and machine-readable
views use the same validated underlying records; neither
can issue a certificate, invoke a protected operation or
change a source requirement by editing an explanation.

The record identifies all applicable coordinates:

- *Original subject:* canonical source and independently required
  product/model obligations, their owner, version and complete
  denominator, including separately unresolved product choices.
- *Selected claim:* one milestone or an explicitly requested
  collection of milestones, selected assurance profile,
  required positive/negative histories and predeclared
  release intent before checks execute.
- *Semantic candidate:* source-bound normalized rule/operation,
  Choreo, projected/executable and application-assembly identities;
  admitted artifacts, exact browser manifest and compiler/receipt
  relations, with their relevant generation/versions.
- *Installed realization:* actual selected Biff/Ring handler,
  guarded writers, providers, backend, workers, host/router
  and serving/loaded asset bindings; site, topology, configuration
  and evaluation window to which physical evidence applies.
- *Four release decisions:* separately current candidate,
  installation, activation and completion subjects, evidence
  and applicability. A stale host or newly revoked backend
  premise must not inherit an older activation result.
- *Each required gate:* original obligation ID, exact intended
  proposition or effect, issuer/observer and evidence class,
  original source, environment, physical/semantic boundary,
  checked result, qualified premises, dependencies and
  reproducible or authorized evidence reference.
- *Eight gate-result classifications:* =:passed=, =:failed=,
  =:incomplete=, =:unavailable=, =:unsupported=,
  =:skipped=, =:stale= or =:missing=, used only after
  the corresponding source and evidence record is
  genuinely checked. A different report vocabulary
  may summarize milestones without changing gate truth.
- *Current limitations:* mandatory unmet obligations, genuine
  accepted trusted premises, unselected product decisions,
  unavailable jobs, exclusions, finite proof bounds,
  tested physical fault/scale conditions, unresolved
  command/Live/recovery horizons and explicit liveness premises.
- *Change lineage:* previous claim/evidence subjects, exact
  source and implementation differences, dependency
  invalidation, reused still-applicable evidence and
  separately required requalification.
- *Outcome:* each milestone's computed complete, partial,
  blocked or otherwise accurately limited disposition,
  the first responsible failure boundaries and the
  stronger claims not established.

An explanatory record can display =:partial=,
=:prototype= or =:not-complete=, but those labels
do not replace the eight gate results and are
not proof issuer handles. A complete disposition
requires every *mandatory original gate* in
the selected profile to have genuine applicable
success or a specifically allowed conditional
qualified premise under the predeclared policy.
Mandatory unproved obligations cannot be
reclassified as voluntary assumptions because
their checker failed.

The initial denominator is not whatever a
generated catalog happens to expose. A missing
HumanHelp Response route, an undiscovered
external writer, a proof family omitted by
an elaborator or an unavailable physical test
is still counted when independently required.
The record can separately report closure of
the currently exposed assembly and coverage
of all original required product capabilities;
it may not combine their percentages or
replace the latter with the former. An
approved real change of product scope
creates a new identifiable requirement
subject and retains the old comparison
and authorization for that change.

*** Applicability is current and claim-specific

A historical completed result states what
was established *then*, about the exact
release, source, assumptions and environment
it actually checked. It is not a permanent
property of a repository, branch, application
name, model key, deployment label, digest
or browser cache. An independently proved
theorem can remain mathematically sound
after a runtime configuration change
while its claimed application to the
newly installed runtime becomes stale.

A change-impact computation follows the
dependencies of the exact affected claims.
A change in a source rule, original requirement,
normalization, proof checker, issuer, trusted
premise, production writer, backend incarnation,
provider, Biff handler, emitted browser artifact,
installed router or release compatibility
may invalidate different portions of the
evidence graph. The affected result is
marked stale, incomplete or blocked as
appropriate until independent requalification.
A genuine unaffected theorem, source
relation or valid physical observation
may be reused with its original subject
and current applicability established.
"No need to rerun everything" is allowed;
"keep every green line after a dependency
change" is not.

Known revocation of an accepted principal,
Organization Membership, credential,
model policy or backend safety premise
fences the dependent protected runtime
effect or disclosure at the actual trusted
boundary. A report's historical success
cannot preserve execution permission.
Likewise, an invalid previous assembly
is not safe fallback merely because
a newer installation failed; 11.07
governs current rollback, recovery
and restricted service.

Change status also preserves *what kind
of evidence survived*. A valid abstract
invariant may persist while the
source-to-physical writer coverage is
stale; a complete bounded model check
does not become an unbounded theorem;
a sound external kernel theorem does
not requalify a changed production
parser; an application preflight report
does not prove the running listener
uses the admitted handler; and a
historical successful client does not
authenticate the bytes loaded by a
later sleeping browser.

A change to documentation can alter
the *requirements* and thus the
claimed target, with the usual
requirement-version and denominator
reassessment. Editing documentation
cannot itself establish that code
has passed a newly described test.
The editorial acceptance of a
normative Part is not any of the
four implementation milestone
completion judgments.

*** Worked record: useful progress with four different answers

Consider a **hypothetical** HumanHelp
candidate with some genuinely checked
Create, Claim, board option and
explicit Refresh paths, but without
an independently selected and
accepted Response interaction
contract. It also has useful
conditional proof and two-host
experiments. The correct report
does not flatten these facts
into a single green project result:

| Completion subject | Hypothetical established evidence | Unmet original requirement and permitted conclusion |
|--------------------+-----------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------|
| Operational application | Some actual original production-model and browser capabilities plus installed assembly paths are qualified | Response contract and user scenario remain missing; report a partial operational slice, not the full milestone |
| Compositional certification | Typed Claim/guard, source-bound conditional checks and part of the issued proof chain are qualified | Required broader judgment or source-to-issued-plan obligations remain open; report only the exact checked pilot |
| External formal verification | A bounded derivation or finite exploration has actually been checked | Universal S0/S1 kernel metatheorems and selected S2–S4 production transfer remain open; do not report full external verification |
| Multi-node production | Two genuinely independent processes can access current shared model state and selected limited advisory behavior works | Host-loss, publication/interest gaps, compatible mixed generations and production load envelope remain missing; report a prototype or bounded observation |

The following is *schematic explanatory
data*, not a concrete Gesso API, a
runnable acceptance fixture, an
issued certificate or an executed
test result. All identifiers are
illustrative rather than references
to real checked evidence.

#+begin_src clojure
{:record/kind :illustrative/completion-explanation
 :release/intent :illustrative/humanhelp-operational-intent
 :requirements/original :illustrative/part-viii-required-set
 :candidate
 {:source :illustrative/original-source
  :semantic-assembly :illustrative/assembly-A
  :assembly-generation :illustrative/generation-G
  :browser-artifact :illustrative/exact-bundle-G}
 :installation
 {:host :illustrative/host-H
  :handler :illustrative/guarded-handler-H
  :backend :illustrative/selected-backend}
 :required-product
 {:selected-policy :remote-lifecycle/explicit-refresh
  :open-decisions #{:humanhelp/response-flow}
  :verified-scope #{:request/create :request/claim
                    :board/options :board/explicit-refresh}
  :missing-scope #{:request/respond}}
 :examples-of-gate-results
 {:operation/claim {:status :passed
                    :evidence :illustrative/claim-observation}
  :operation/response {:status :missing
                       :evidence nil}
  :physical/host-loss {:status :missing
                       :evidence nil}}
 :completion-explanation
 {:operational-application :partial
  :compositional-certification :partial
  :external-formal-verification :not-complete
  :multi-node-production :prototype}
 :warning :not-admitted-evidence}
#+end_src

Even in this illustrative record, a
=:passed= label has **no evidentiary
force** without independent issued or
observed matching evidence. The
=examples-of-gate-results= are not
the required complete gate inventory;
the missing entries cannot be
treated as inapplicable. A real root
record must resolve every mandatory
gate and its subject, admitted
issuer/observer, original source,
environment, premises and actual
receipt. The =:illustrative/=
identifiers authenticate nothing.
One actual original-source
Response contract cannot be
replaced by a placeholder button
or a copied result map.

The remote lifecycle policy in the
example is an *already selected*
explicit Refresh rule, not another
unresolved product decision.
Remote advisories cannot be
silently adopted because a new
runtime was installed, and a
recovered own-command outcome
does not confer unrelated board
acquisition authority. If the
Response choice is later actually
selected and all required
operational gates are exercised
and qualified, the same product
may attain operational completion
while the formal and multi-node
milestones remain independently
partial. A release permitted
by its actual operational profile
need not await an unselected
stronger milestone. A release
that originally requested a
strict external proof cannot
obtain permission by changing
the displayed claim label
after the proof failed.

*** Acceptance controls for completion records and applicability

| Required valid result | Nearby false claim to reject or contain |
|-----------------------+------------------------------------------|
| Four milestones retain independent original requirement sets | One green "Gesso complete" status erases missing formal or product obligations |
| Four release decisions name candidate, installed host, activation and completion separately | Valid candidate assembly map becomes proof of actual traffic activation |
| Every mandatory gate has checked evidence or explicit blocking disposition | Missing physical observation disappears because only generated passing rows are counted |
| Accepted conditional proof retains named actual trusted premises | A presumed XTDB/issuer premise is reported as an independently proved theorem |
| Real HumanHelp Response decision is selected and positively exercised before full operational claim | Claim demo or placeholder Response button satisfies full product denominator |
| Selected remote lifecycle explicit Refresh remains current and its grant scoped | An unrequested remote reread is treated as adopted after host replacement |
| Valid old semantic theorem is reused when only physical adapter changes | Reused theorem is presented as new installed handler qualification |
| Changed original rule or required proof checker invalidates dependent evidence | Old certificate handle, report hash or copied status stays green by default |
| New browser bytes or serving host requires its relevant physical checks | An old emitted-asset receipt certifies unrelated currently loaded browser code |
| Known revoked Membership fences protected actions regardless of release badge | Historical completion continues granting old actor new rights |
| Full requested strict release fails when its mandatory stronger milestone is open | A failing proof is reclassified as an optional smaller release with the same claim ID |
| Separately approved narrower preview retains original missing scope | Smaller exposed UI operation inventory becomes full product completion |
| An operational release remains eligible when unselected external work is partial | All four milestones are incorrectly imposed as mandatory for every deployment |
| Real two-host observation is credited only to its bounded topology and test | Shared XTDB and two process names become universal multi-node completion |
| Finite formal result retains its bounds and independent source | One model run or fabricated external report counts as proof-kernel metatheorem |
| Missing command result remains unknown under current disclosure and retention | Cached historical report or Request state is treated as command attribution |
| Valid release change marks only genuinely dependent claims stale | Every edit discards unrelated sound theorem, or no physical recheck is performed |
| Primary gate failure survives cleanup-report processing | A secondary report failure masks the reason the release was blocked |
| Root machine-readable and human summaries derive from the same checked ledger | Human text or serialized EDN status becomes an alternative issuer |
| Prior completed release remains historical with exact environment/provenance | An earlier green completion label is treated as permanent correctness |
| Conditional liveness requires actual availability and user-action premises | Offline user who never Refreshes is counted as converged |
| Genuine positive supported candidate works under the same gate rejecting invalid candidate | Reject-all release mechanism passes only negative controls |

These are prospective first-boundary
and positive/adversarial checks, not
executed acceptance observations.
The record may explain partial
progress while every still-required
gate remains visible. Its value is
that a downstream consumer can
identify *which source proposition
has been checked, for which actual
subject, by whom, under which
premises, through what enforcing
boundary, and what changed since*.
The completed record never becomes
an independent source of business
rules or a command/DOM authority.

** Acceptance for changes to the release mechanism

The release and certification mechanisms are themselves *part of the
system being qualified*. An application can have correct rules and
still be deployed incorrectly because an obligation was not
discovered, a stale certificate was trusted, a source-equivalent
adapter change escaped physical requalification, or a tested
handler was never installed. This section defines change-driven
and adversarial acceptance of the *actual release path*.
Parts I–X own the underlying semantic, proof and physical
contracts; 11.01–11.17 own candidate admission, evidence,
activation, compatibility and completion scopes. This section
checks their composition without creating another business
policy, issuer or arbitrary host-language proof mechanism.

A release-system test must have an independently fixed
original requirement, a declared eligible positive,
a controlled invalid or interrupted alternative, the
specific expected first rejecting boundary, an observable
result/absence-of-effect oracle, and an attributable
implementation/environment subject. A passing report
produced by the mechanism under test is not an independent
oracle that the mechanism was invoked or correctly enforced.

*** Challenge dependency invalidation and trustworthy evidence reuse

A correct change-impact decision follows the actual
meaning and implementation dependencies of each claim.
Semantic identity, normalized source, proof and checker
rules, premise qualification, concrete callable/provider,
exact emitted bytes, installed host/route and client
continuation are distinct coordinates. A change can
invalidate one layer without changing another. Both
unsafe reuse *and unnecessary global invalidation*
are rejected when the selected reuse contract promises
incrementality.

| Controlled change | Required re-evaluation | Independently positive counterbalance |
|-------------------+------------------------+---------------------------------------|
| Change Claim eligibility or a rule's presence/refinement meaning | Rebuild the changed original-source semantic/operation/plan dependency cone and recheck its required proof and interface claims | Unrelated unchanged search rule/theorem remains reusable under verified dependencies |
| Change an opaque implementation, XTDB adapter, model writer or physical provider while retaining semantic operation identity | Requalify the affected implementation and actual authoritative transition/writer correspondence; keep a sound abstract theorem only in its original scope | Legitimate current Claim still passes through the qualified changed writer |
| Change normalizer, proof rule, checker, proof importer or issuer version | Recheck the dependent inference and certificate-applicability subjects under current admission rules | A valid unchanged supported derivation can be re-admitted and still use its justified premise set |
| Corrupt, forge, truncate or replay a cached package or passing report | Safe decode and genuine checker/issuer re-admission reject or independently reconstruct from original source | Unchanged genuine immutable issued evidence can still be reused under its specified currentness contract |
| Change compiler, manifest, browser bytes, decoder, handler, deployed route or serving provider | Requalify the exact affected build, installation, transfer, load and protected runtime boundaries | Supported old/new clients use only the direction and assets their release actually admits |
| Change principal, Membership, credential, provider-incarnation or backend safety premise | Fence affected new protected effects/disclosures and requalify the actual current premise | Other authorized and otherwise unaffected requests continue within their admissible scope |
| Add, remove or fail to discover an original product capability, non-HTTP writer, proof branch or external obligation | Recheck independent requirement and source completeness; block unchanged full claim where an obligation is missing | A separately approved narrower preview is accurately labeled without pretending to complete the original claim |
| Reorder physical startup, activate concurrently, replace a host or fail after partial initialization | Qualify the actual installation, effect fence, coherent activation and cleanup/rollback applicability | Still-qualified previous work continues and valid new activation succeeds under its actual policy |

The release ledger records the changed proposition and
every dependency reconsidered, which evidence was
validly retained, which physical claim became stale,
and why unrelated evidence remained applicable.
A green cached summary cannot issue or preserve
a certificate by itself; an abstract theorem that
remains valid does not authenticate a newly deployed
adapter, selected handler or browser bytes. Required
checks that cannot execute stay explicitly nonpassing,
not implicitly accepted because recomputation is costly.

*** Test the exact decisions and mandatory gate vocabulary

The selected release intent and original independent
capability/proof denominator are fixed *before*
candidate gate evaluation. Construction then derives
its closed required ledger from actual source and
selected deployment scope, including branches,
writers, protected reads, browser paths and
required positive user capabilities. A generated
partial catalog, missing UI control, unreachable
test, absent proof producer or disabled policy
cannot shrink the unchanged intended subject.

Every mandatory gate retains the closed result
classification =:passed=, =:failed=,
=:incomplete=, =:unavailable=, =:unsupported=,
=:skipped=, =:stale= or =:missing=. A malformed
result is an error, not a ninth success value.
The actual checker/observer and applicable evidence
must justify a =:passed= disposition; a copyable
status row or unobserved test completion cannot.
Failing, unexecuted or expired required gates block
the exact requested decision. A valid trusted
premise can remain *conditional* if the selected
profile permits it; it is not independently proved,
and a mandatory failed theorem cannot be moved
into a premise list without changing the claim.

The four release decisions are challenged separately:
candidate admission; actual installation; traffic
activation under coherent overlap and safe existing
work; and named milestone completion. A candidate
may be correct without being installed, a genuine
installed guarded Biff handler may not be selected
by a running listener, and a locally activated host
does not establish global mixed-node compatibility.
The four independently scoped completion milestones
of 11.13–11.16 are likewise not aliases for the
four release decisions or a single green bit.

Test the required *positive* candidates under the
same actual gates as invalid ones. A release
mechanism that rejects all candidates, disables
every protected button, fails all external
proof checks or never emits an executable
artifact cannot claim success because its
negative safety controls are all green.
A legitimate supported conditional proof must
retain precisely its permissible premises,
while a release that originally requests
a stricter proven result must refuse any
post-failure silent downgrade to a narrower
assurance profile.

*** Observe activation, rollback and physical failure windows

The qualifying observation ladder reaches the
selected physical boundaries: original semantic
checker; genuine proof issuer/re-admission;
generated application assembly; actual Ring/Biff
handler and protected non-HTTP writers; emitted,
served and loaded browser artifact; chosen backend
transaction; subscription/router transport;
and independently authorized browser acquisition
and DOM installation. Each observation is credited
only at its real boundary. A test-only wrapper,
invented receipt or observed HTTP 200 cannot
authenticate a different production gateway
or prove business command incorporation.

For each possible failure schedule identify
the earliest *actual* protected effect,
the candidate/host/asset generation and
applicable current authority, the fault
injected, the intended rejecting/fencing
boundary, any effect already committed,
and the permitted final user-facing status.
An invalid attempt should fail before the
forbidden physical effect where the
enforcement contract requires it.
Detection after an irreversible commit
may be diagnostically useful but cannot
be counted as prevention of that effect.

Concurrent installation and activation
must not expose a half-published mix
of routes, executors, guards, providers
or browser assets. A stale candidate
cannot silently overwrite a newer
active generation. Partial initializer
failure accounts for acquired sockets,
workers and publications even if
there is no returned resource map;
cleanup failures retain the primary
gate error and independently fence
unadmitted effects. Fallback to a
previous candidate is allowed only
while its *current* backend, security
and release premises remain valid.
Rollback is new checked activation
against actual migrated state and
retained work, not reversal of
committed domain history.

A response timeout or host restart
after possible authoritative submission
does not imply that the command was
rejected. The original logical
command binding and identity survive
release retirement, compatible
reconciliation and any admitted retry.
A current Request read does not
attribute a prior C42. Durable
publication, SSE delivery, current
authorized acquisition and visible
browser adoption have independently
named status and recovery obligations.
Retiring old execution removes
obsolete effect and DOM rights
without erasing truthful historical
command evidence.

*** Require real browser, distributed and product oracles

For every profile that claims real
user or installed-system behavior,
exercise the actual rendered
user control and issued plan,
selected protected backend/handler,
source-owned outcome, loaded
browser/HTMX/SSE runtime and
qualified physical read/DOM result.
A manually synthesized internal
command bypassing the rendered
affordance has narrower coverage.
A successful optimistic effect,
transport event or stream frame
is not an independently observed
authoritative transaction or
remote user's adoption.

HumanHelp retains its independent
product capability denominator,
public model authority, six
lifecycle mutations and still-open
Response product choice. The
remote lifecycle adoption policy
is already selected as advisory
until explicit authorized Refresh,
subject to its narrow own-command
and affected-card recovery.
Neither release restart nor
router reconnect creates a
one-use Refresh grant or
clears incomparable newer
advisory debt. An outdated
browser resource cannot
overwrite newer authorized
state. A full HumanHelp
operational claim must show
real eligible success for the
required user capabilities,
not only rejections or Claim.

A multi-node claim requires
independently running processes,
shared authoritative semantics
under actual selected XTDB
premises, protected command
result and outbox failure
windows, subscription
registration fences, stale
router/filter failover,
authorized replay or
qualified re-acquisition,
and actual A/A, A/B, B/A,
B/B directions. A healthy
backup router with an
incomplete interest filter
is not proof that a required
notification was delivered.
Conservative redelivery
remains eligible when its
authorization, resource
and recovery constraints
are demonstrated. No
universal participant
fabric or one particular
router implementation
is demanded.

Conditional liveness
retains its backend
availability, fairness,
history retention,
network, reconnect and
explicit user-action
premises. An offline
recipient who has not
Refreshed is not
reported as having
adopted all updates.
An unavailable or
timed-out physical
observer cannot issue
a positive result merely
because it did not
observe a counterexample.

*** Acceptance matrix: eligible release versus nearby defect

| Positive required behavior | Invalid nearby result or mechanism to reject |
|----------------------------+----------------------------------------------|
| Changed Claim rule invalidates complete semantic cone; unrelated search proof remains reusable | Unrelated proof always rebuilt or changed rule keeps stale proof |
| Current abstract theorem reused with changed physical adapter separately qualified | Old adapter's successful XTDB test silently applies to changed writer |
| Genuine proof source/issuer re-admits only supported derivation | Corrupt cached success or copied report becomes proof capability |
| Exact mandatory operation and product denominator stays fixed | Missing Response or writer disappears from generated inventory |
| Correct strict profile blocks when required theorem is unavailable | Mandatory proof is called optional or trusted after failure |
| Explicit allowed assumption stays conditional with dependent claims | Accepted premise is labeled proved or missing obligation invented to block valid narrower claim |
| Each required missing, stale, skipped, incomplete, unsupported, failed or unavailable check blocks | A missing shard, status string, timeout or unsupported backend is counted as pass |
| Legitimate eligible Claim works through actual selected enforcement gate | Reject-all route or test-only guard passes negative-only suite |
| Genuine checked Biff handler is selected by the live listener | Correct unused handler map is mistaken for installed server adoption |
| Current exact compiled JS is served and loaded with applicable receipt | Stale JS, reused filename or forged artifact hash is called current |
| Concurrent B activation preserves coherent binding and predecessor condition | Late C, built against A, silently overwrites active B |
| Failed partial setup retains primary error, owned cleanup and still-valid A | B cleanup stops A shared resource or accidentally exposes B worker |
| Invalid old credential/backend premise fences A even if B installation fails | Previously green A is kept accepting unsafe writes as fallback |
| Real rollback qualifies old code against current migration and pending work | Historic passing binary is restarted with incompatible old writer |
| C42 may commit, response is lost, and current authorized resolver preserves uncertainty | Timeout becomes rejection, or retry allocates new command C43 |
| Current protected lookup observes genuine historical command record | Current Request state or user-supplied command ID is treated as proof of past effect |
| Committed effect and required outbox intent survive dispatcher/host loss | Sole in-memory SSE callback disappears and report declares delivery complete |
| Duplicate delivery asks authorized receiver to recheck state, without repeated Claim | Duplicate invalidation repeats authoritative mutation or leaks tenant metadata |
| Subscription read/registration and router failover preserve scope and coverage | Healthy router with stale filter silently misses interest interval |
| Permitted A/B and B/A directions have qualified routes, decoders and assets | Happy-path sticky session hides invalid failover to old server |
| Current principal and browser target rights are checked after release change | Old assembly proof freezes Membership or late callback installs into retired DOM |
| Bob's remote board remains advisory until one eligible Refresh | Host restart or SSE message automatically adopts unrelated remote row |
| Independently required real HumanHelp features have positive browser controls | Disabled Reassign/Response is counted as working because Claim passes |
| S0/S1 formal subject and S2–S4 conditional transfer remain distinct | Finite fixture or report claims universal kernel/physical proof |
| Actual two-host fault and bounded load cases have attributable observations | Simulated two-host labels or fast one-worker run certified as production |
| Required job inventory and test receipt provenance are verified | Unexecuted worker, flaky failure or caller-authored success row is hidden |
| Legitimate narrower preview has separate original claim identity and excluded obligations | Failed strict release keeps same ID after shrinking its scope |
| Named conditional-liveness premises are met before progress is claimed | Dead network or missing user Refresh is described as convergence |

These are future positive/adversarial conformance
requirements. Their existence in a document,
test name or coverage table does not establish
that they were executed. Positive behavior
must use the same real admission/enforcement
path whose invalid neighbor is challenged.
The acceptance report names original required
subjects, actual evidence issuers or observers,
selected hardware/software/environment,
reproducible fault schedule, verified
non-effects, unresolved premises and the
first actual enforcing boundary for each
relevant case. Production and formal claims
are not interchangeable merely because
both report success.

** Working rule for every semantic or release change

For every framework or application change
participating in the compositional chain,
ask *what exact proposition this layer
establishes, for what original subject,
under which premises, through what
genuinely checked or observed evidence,
and which next layer is entitled to
consume it*. If that question cannot
be answered at the required interface,
the corresponding edge remains an
explicit allowed premise or an
unsatisfied obligation for the
selected claim. It is not silently
inferred from matching names,
successful status maps or a
running server.

*** Keep a typed handoff at each layer

The ordinary change and release
workflow accounts for:

| Handoff | Required question before the next claim |
|---------+-----------------------------------------|
| Business rule and model to admitted operation | Are the independently selected product meaning, source owner, types, guards, readers, effects, frame conditions, and writer dependencies complete? |
| Operation to global Choreo and role-local projection | Are placement, knowledge/provenance, authority, progression, outcomes and terminal/recovery paths preserved by the checked source-relative relation? |
| Projection to browser/server executable construction | Are plans, canonical routes, transport envelopes, effects and resource/acquisition ownership matched to the original admitted semantics? |
| Typed artifact to derivation and proof checker | Does genuine accepted proof or dedicated checking discharge the exact proposition, with all relevant hypotheses and checker versions retained? |
| Proof/checker result to issuer and application assembly | Are the exact source, dependencies, required obligations, original denominator and current proof premises validated before any admitted certificate/assembly product is issued? |
| Assembly to installed handler, backend and browser | Does the *actual* listener, protected writer, selected XTDB/provider, built/served/loaded browser and runtime shell implement the checked subject within the named premises? |
| Current execution to participant observation/adoption | Do authoritative result, command incorporation, source/progression, user authorization, Live notification, acquisition and present DOM resource ownership justify this effect? |
| Installed realization to activation and release | Are current candidate, installation, traffic/overlap, rollback, resource lifetime and four milestone scopes individually justified by applicable evidence? |
| Prior release to changed release | Which semantic, issuer, trust, physical, product and environment dependencies changed, what evidence remains reusable, and what must be rechecked? |

A direct physical shortcut may
be a valid independently
admitted implementation,
but it must satisfy its
own actual semantics and
release profile. Application
authors should declare
business rules and Gesso
construction, not maintain
parallel proof-assistant
policies or manually
manufacture a certification
record. The executable
semantic core remains the
operational source;
a proof kernel checks
derivations, dedicated
checkers establish their
named judgments, and
production guards enforce
current runtime rights.

*** Track the exact evidence class and residual frontier

The framework reports which
claims are *proved under
a named formal system*,
*checked by a genuine
source-relative proof
issuer*, *exact-finite
checked within an explicit
domain*, *assembly-verified*,
*physically qualified*,
*runtime-enforced*,
*tested through observed
paths*, *asserted only*,
or *trusted under visible
premises*. These are
qualifications of specific
propositions, not
substitutable values on
a single ascending ladder.
A real installed browser
test cannot issue an
unbounded mathematical
theorem, while a formally
proved inference rule
does not show that the
running server actually
uses the corresponding
guard.

Evidence propagation
retains every undischarged
premise along the actually
used justification. A
trusted backend atomicity
assumption must be
qualified at its named
backend and scope; a
proof subject cannot
replace a verified actor
or current Membership;
a report cannot act as
an authorization token.
An unavailable required
checker is blocking under
the originally selected
profile. A permitted
conditional smaller claim
must keep its distinct
identity and all its
declared accepted
assumptions.

When a layer changes,
the owning application
or framework constructor
reconsiders only genuinely
dependent claims, while
still validating source
completeness and current
applicability. The
generation and host
binding of the old
completed record remain
historical. A stale
physical receipt does
not become fresh through
a semantic digest,
and sound unaffected
theorems need not be
reproved solely because
a different file changed.

*** Final rule: admit only the actual compositional subject

A candidate is admitted
because the original
requirements, selected
proof and operational
obligations, current
issuer and dependency
checks actually justify
that candidate. An
installation is eligible
because the *real*
selected host, protected
writers, browser assets
and external premises
satisfy their physical
qualification. Activation
is eligible only under
current coherent
traffic/continuation,
resource and rollback
conditions. A milestone
is complete only for
its exact required
capabilities and evidence
scope.

These decisions are
not reversible historical
decorations: their
dependent runtime rights
can cease when a current
principal, backend or
release premise becomes
false. The release
mechanism must fail
closed at the first
actual enforcing
boundary, preserve
truthful committed and
unknown command state
through its own failures,
and support permitted
positive user operations.
No automatic rollback
of authoritative domain
facts, universal
distributed liveness,
or proof of arbitrary
Clojure/browser/XTDB
execution is invented.

The intended system
therefore does *not*
claim "everything is
formally verified."
It can identify which
source-owned guarantees
are proved, checked,
conditionally justified,
physically qualified,
runtime-enforced,
observed or still
open; which current
realizations they
concern; and exactly
when an implementation,
premise, application
or deployment change
requires re-admission.
If a required handoff
cannot demonstrate
its semantic or
physical relationship,
the requested stronger
construction, release
or completion claim
stops there rather
than allowing
incompatible premises
to drift into an
application that
merely appears to work.

* Part XII — Implementation order and final invariants
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: part-12-implementation-order-and-final-invariants
:PART_REVISION: 12-20261108
:END:

This part defines a construction order for the system specified in Parts I–XI.
It starts from the required semantics and observable application behavior, then
connects their implementation, checking, qualification, and release evidence.
It is a design from zero, not a report of completed work or a migration checklist
for a particular repository snapshot.

Eighteen stages organize the work. Their numbers are navigation and a useful
reading order, not a requirement to finish every lower-numbered stage before
beginning a higher-numbered one. The dependency table identifies the branches.
The four completion scopes remain those of Part XI; a stage number is not a
milestone badge and a sophisticated proof fixture is not a usable application.

Stage order is a *contract dependency and delivery priority*, not a serial
project-management lock. Distinguish a semantic prerequisite, a normally earlier
implementation task, exploratory feedback that may be obtained sooner, optional
early hardening, and a completion dependency for a named claim. Later work may
expose a missing earlier contract; repair that contract at its actual owner and
reconsider only the dependent evidence. A prototype can inform the design
without borrowing the acceptance status of a completed stage.

** Delivery discipline

*** Construct one useful path and strengthen the same objects

The first integrated path is a real HumanHelp Claim using public production
models, the canonical application construction, the generated browser plan,
the actual trusted invocation and transaction boundary, and an admitted visible
result or recovery path. Build only the supported breadth needed for that path
before generalizing, while keeping its missing obligations explicit.

The path must include RequestAssignment ownership, current policy dependencies,
command identity and replay, and unknown-outcome recovery from the beginning.
A single-document demonstration can qualify a narrower mechanism. It cannot be
renamed as the completed Claim path while those relationships are absent.

The integrated witness must include an eligible actor authorized by the current
trusted model, an actual Request and RequestAssignment with the guarded
one-primary relationship, a stable logical command, the installed route and
trusted writer that submit the actual effect, and a scoped authoritative
observation for the outcome or its unresolved recovery. A declared operation,
a generated route, a browser fixture, an optimistic card, and a committed
Request are not interchangeable evidence that this complete path worked.
Where real backend or application behavior has not yet been observed, the
record names the still-open physical or product claim.

Pair that eligible success with nearby failures: a competing Claim, an expired
Membership, a missing or incompatible effect capability, a request that may
have committed before its response was lost, and a callback from an obsolete
browser execution. Reject each defect at its first legitimately informed
boundary, or retain uncertainty and the explicit recovery obligation when
the boundary cannot decide. A later visible card alone cannot reconstruct
which earlier logical command incorporated.

The Claim path is the first integration slice, not the whole HumanHelp product.
The independent capability inventory in Part VIII remains fixed while the rest
of the application is constructed. Removing a difficult operation from the
exposed registry cannot make its requirement disappear. A still-unselected
HumanHelp Response interaction likewise remains an explicit product-owned
requirement, not a plausible behavior inferred from the working Claim slice.
The selected remote-board policy remains advisory until an authorized
scope-limited, one-use Refresh or an explicitly narrower local exception;
Live delivery and automatic DOM swap do not silently grant adoption.

The ordinary construction must remain useful for arbitrary Clojure and
ClojureScript behind explicit contracts. Closed proof languages establish
supported properties; opaque implementations retain named premises and their
runtime enforcement. There is no second unmanaged application architecture for
code that the prover cannot analyze. A supported opaque Clojure function may
carry named, checked-at-use runtime obligations; its opacity must not be
treated as an implicit proof, automatic exclusion from the source inventory,
or permission to bypass the application's admitted execution path.

*** Establish the real serving boundary before calling a slice runnable

A declared first path requires a compatible, actually installed host substrate.
The selected supported Biff lifecycle and FX contracts, the application
assembly, its stable startup/preflight gate, and the effective Ring/HTMX routes
must be qualified for the path actually served. In particular, a listener must
not expose a supposedly admitted operation before the required preflight and
startup checks have passed. Startup failure fences newly acquired resources
rather than leaving an unchecked handler serving.

This does not demand the final universal closure checker or all later formal
theorems before any useful application work begins. It demands a genuine
enforcing seam for the selected scope and an honest account of what it does
not yet inspect. A green assembly map, successful compilation, manually
invoked handler, or test fixture does not by itself show that the deployed
listener, active writer, loaded browser asset, and Biff execution flow are
the ones whose contracts were checked.

The exact supported Biff and backend profiles are selected and qualified as
implementation subjects; they are not extra business-rule owners. Changes to
an FX invocation contract, initializer, protected writer, browser bundle,
served route or provider configuration trigger reconsideration at the
affected physical boundary even if the abstract rule is unchanged.

*** Start cross-cutting obligations at their first boundary

The following work accompanies construction throughout the roadmap:

| Concern | Begins when | Required discipline |
|---------+-------------+---------------------|
| Source ownership and identities | The first semantic object is declared | Derived objects retain their actual source and interpretation dependencies |
| Obligation and premise accounting | A claim is made | Preserve the original obligation and distinguish checked evidence from accepted premises |
| Positive and negative tests | A boundary can admit or reject | Exercise a useful valid case and the relevant defect at the intended boundary |
| Physical correspondence | A semantic action first reaches an effect provider | Bind the issued plan, actual invocation, physical operation, and observation origin |
| Diagnostics | A checker or runtime boundary can fail | Identify the failed obligation, scope, source, and repair owner |
| Artifact and release integrity | A candidate is built or served | Verify the actual plan, manifest, bytes, installed bindings, and selected profile |
| Resource and recovery limits | Work can wait, retry, queue, or outlive its owner | Bound retained work and preserve unresolved obligations honestly |
| Backend qualification | A claim uses provider semantics | Name the exact assumption and applicable adapter/version/configuration envelope |
| Original capability inventory | A product or application scope is chosen | Preserve independently required actions and the full denominator even when assembly discovers fewer routes or features |
| Actor, disclosure, and current authority | A request can observe or change protected facts | Bind the authenticated principal, model-owned guards, scope and actual trusted read/write boundary; never derive them from browser metadata |
| Actual application admission | The first handler, worker, or browser artifact is installed | Check the real covered path and retain the uninspected or bypassing effect inventory as an explicit obligation |
| Publication and command continuity | A commit, notification, retry, or host loss is possible | Separate durable incorporation, notice intent, transport, authorized resolution, and participant knowledge; state the selected recovery premises |
| Selective presentation adoption | A remote update can reach a client | Distinguish advisory interest, authorized acquisition, one-use user Refresh, physical adoption, and outstanding visibility debt |

Later stages expand these mechanisms. Their existence does not permit earlier
work to ship with placeholder checks, silent fallbacks, or unclassified proof
claims. Static preflight checks the declared handling paths for dynamic failures;
it does not predict that the network, Membership, or database will remain valid.
A dynamic permission change must still be enforced by the authoritative
operation or qualified read at the time of use. A failed after-commit
notification must not retroactively turn a committed transaction into
rejection; the selected publication profile must either retain its durable
intent or name the weaker recovery and availability assumptions.

For example, Alice's eligible Claim may incorporate at the trusted transaction
boundary while the HTTP result disappears. Her original command remains
unresolved to the client until qualified command-specific evidence permits
settlement; an arbitrary retry under a new command identity would be a new
intent. Bob's Live notification is merely an advisory about a remote change,
not automatic authority to replace his adopted board. These obligations
begin at the first Claim and first subscription, not at a later roadmap
stage devoted to recovery or multi-node deployment.

*** A stage result is a scoped evidence record

A stage record names its supported subset, source and artifact identities,
original obligations, selected profile, accepted premises, actual enforcing
boundaries, acceptance results, and unresolved requirements. It distinguishes
implemented machinery, exercised behavior, and a completed claimed scope.

A supplied map or a successful-looking report is not an admitted artifact. A
checker-issued local object is not durable authority. A test observation is not
an unbounded theorem. The evidence classes in Part I and result statuses in Part
XI apply without reinterpretation.

The record separates the original required capability set from the supported
subset, the chosen conditional or stricter profile from unmet mandatory gates,
and source-derived evidence from actual installed enforcement. It names
successful eligible witnesses as well as adversarial exclusions. A partial
stage can be useful and truthfully complete for a deliberately narrower
claim, but it does not make a missing product action, unknown physical writer,
unresolved premise, or unexecuted test disappear from the stronger requested
claim. Four Part XI release decisions and four independent completion
milestones remain different result subjects.

The next useful task is the earliest unmet obligation on the selected delivery
path whose prerequisites are available. A physical failure is repaired at the
owning boundary, then dependent evidence is reconsidered. Adding another report
layer without closing a required boundary is not progress toward that path.
Early exploration of a future proof, different provider, or multi-node router
is appropriate when it exposes a real missing contract. It must feed that
finding back to the original semantic or physical owner, not produce a
second architecture whose success is then counted as the missing original
application guarantee.

** Construction stages

*** Stage 1 -- Semantic ownership, identities, and claim contracts

Establish the vocabulary and construction interfaces shared by runtime code,
checkers, application assembly, and evidence reporting. This is the foundation
of the permanent executable semantic core, not a promise that all physical
behavior has already been formalized.

The source-owned semantic subject includes the actual actor, target, relationship,
operation and policy dependencies, not just a friendly function name. A real
HumanHelp Claim refers to public Request and RequestAssignment meaning, the
current principal and Membership/Organization relation, one-primary
responsibility, protected observation and atomic effect. Choreo describes
coordination and knowledge; views select affordances; checkers assess named
judgments. None of those consumers may create a second, subtly different
Claim rule or infer current model authority from its metadata.

Stage 1's semantic-first position does not waive the earlier R4 physical
substrate obligation. The actual Biff lifecycle/preflight, model FX
invocation, trusted writer and installed host path must be established at
the first *claimed runnable* scope, as stated in the delivery discipline;
their complete coverage is elaborated in the later host and operation
stages. The permanent executable semantic core is neither the small proof
kernel nor an invented second runtime for unsupported Clojure code.

Deliver:

- single ownership of domain rules, public operations, choreography, projection,
  runtime transitions, and application declarations;
- distinct semantic-subject, implementation, artifact, assembly-generation,
  command, execution, transport, authority, and resource-instance identities;
- versioned claim and judgment records with subject, proposition, scope,
  assumptions, required dependencies, and evidence mechanism;
- an immutable original obligation ledger with separately derived dispositions;
- contracts for opaque host-language functions and their proof-relevant input,
  output, authority, state footprint, effects, and failure behavior;
- the independent product-capability inventory and semantic-policy audit shape;
- stable structured diagnostics and a minimal source-derived inspection surface.
- an explicit source-to-consumer mapping for business rule, nominal value,
  reader/relationship, actor authority, guarded effect and observation-basis
  dependencies, including which are checked, opaque, asserted or still unknown;
- a source-independent product requirement inventory whose denominator cannot
  shrink to currently declared operations or currently generated routes;
- the distinction between semantic subject, source syntax, normalized
  interpretation, checker result, issuer handle, physical implementation,
  generated asset, deployed host and current execution authority.

The independent HumanHelp requirements retain Create, Claim, Unclaim,
other lifecycle operations, real Reassign, and the still-unselected
product-owned Response interaction. A proof of one Claim conjunct or a
closed but reduced application registry may satisfy a narrower named
profile; it may not be reported as the complete product or as coverage
of obligations never discovered by the generator.

Acceptance requires that same-shaped objects from different subjects cannot be
silently substituted, a premise remains attached to its dependent claim, and a
missing product capability remains visible even when the smaller declared graph
is internally closed. An unknown inventory is not an empty complete inventory.

Canonical interfaces must be small enough to compose, but must include every
meaning-changing dependency used by the consumer. A declaration's name or source
location is provenance, not a proof of its semantics or implementation.

For instance, a structurally well-formed description or digest can identify
a semantic *interface* without proving its meaning, its source-to-implementation
correspondence or a safe effect at the trusted physical boundary. A copied
certificate-shaped map, a same-shaped Request from another Organization,
an old issuer status and an unbound client actor label must fail to
substitute for a qualified current subject and evidence. The original
source and its true dependency footprint determine required checking;
a missing inventory is *unknown*, never an empty complete set.

A correctness-relevant policy may also be well typed and nevertheless be
the *wrong intended policy*. The public model's auditable semantic surface
retains explanation, intended actor/target binding and independent product
approval. Human or heuristic review may detect an error and propose repair,
but cannot manufacture a proof or authority. Ordinary Clojure and
ClojureScript functions remain available: unsupported or hidden reads,
effects, time dependence, partiality and provider behavior become named
opaque obligations or independently enforced exclusions, not silently
omitted duties.

*** Stage 2 -- Typed semantic rules and executable judgments

Implement the closed rule language and the versioned judgment contracts of
[[#req-certified-rule-language]] and Part IX. The rule interpreter and checker
operate on the same admitted meaning used by operations and their proofs.

Stage 2 makes four claims distinct: closed *syntax* with an exact reader
footprint, intrinsic *typing* under named reader types, *evaluation* over
one admitted immutable binding, and *use-site admissibility* with justified
knowledge and current authority. Passing one does not discharge the next.
The baseline certifiable expression language consists of bounded literals,
declared reads and presence tests, strict Boolean negation, ordered
short-circuit conjunction/disjunction/implication, typed equality and
ordering, and finite-set membership. Its exact arities, input decoding,
failure behavior and resource limits are part of the versioned meaning.
It does not include arbitrary function calls or EDN reader evaluation.

The full R4 target still includes typed relationship and field access,
nominal variant discrimination, exhaustive closed match/case,
deterministic derivations and independently specified extension
primitives. These are explicit future extensions with their own syntax,
type, evaluation, source mapping, effect and proof/premise contracts;
they are not secretly certified by the small baseline grammar.
Supported application Clojure may be elaborated to the closed term under
a checked source-translation contract, or represented by a named
opaque dependency. Merely copying an equivalent-looking term is not
evidence that it realizes the original public rule.

Deliver:

- closed AST forms, exact reader footprints, operator arity, and semantic types;
- the supported scalar, nominal-enum, optional, and nullable value contracts;
- strict Boolean interpretation and left-to-right short-circuit semantics;
- presence and null refinements scoped to the paths and subjects that justify them;
- conservative normalization that preserves evaluation and access order;
- explicit value codecs and target-runtime limits for portable evaluation;
- typed interfaces for opaque policy or relational extensions, with unproved
  properties retained as premises;
- executable typing, evaluation, and rule-use judgment definitions with source
  diagnostics and stable interpretation versions.
- exact separation of absent, present nil, present false and present zero:
  presence and non-nil are different justified refinements;
- reader/type identity bound to the source, observation subject and
  evaluation path, with incoming-path joins retaining only shared facts;
- source-to-AST elaboration and conservative interpretation-preserving
  normalization, with no silent short-circuit reordering or omitted
  source-meaning dependencies;
- distinct interpretation and proof obligations for JVM/CLJS numerical,
  codec, overflow, range and external-reader behavior, where selected.

For example, the following rule about one supplied optional, nullable
integer binding requires each guard to dominate its dependent read:

#+begin_src clojure
{:readers #{:case/score}
 :expression
 [:and
  [:present [:read :case/score]]
  [:not= [:read :case/score] [:literal nil]]
  [:>= [:read :case/score] [:literal 10]]]}

{:case/score {:type :integer :optional? true :nullable? true}}
#+end_src

This is illustrative rule and reader-type data, not a complete policy,
a production read or a certificate. Moving the final comparison before
the presence/non-nil guards is a type error, not ordinary predicate
false. Replacing a conjunction with a disjunction may express a *different*
well-typed business policy. The interpreter, type checker and any future
proof/translation must agree on the actual left-to-right evaluation paths.

Acceptance pairs well-typed successful evaluation with wrong-type, missing-reader,
absent/null, invalid enum, unsupported-operator, and malformed-shape cases.
A coherent but product-wrong policy remains representable. Typing does not prove
its truth, and evaluation to true does not establish current server authorization.

A rule that is intrinsically valid can still be unusable at a choreography point
because the role lacks its inputs, provenance, refinement, or authority. Stage 7
composes those distributed judgments; Stage 2 does not invent them from schema
acceptance. Arbitrary host functions remain available through their contracts.

Acceptance also distinguishes positive eligibility from reject-everything
success: valid typed expressions must evaluate over supported nonvacuous
bindings while wrong enum, absent/nil, undeclared read, unsupported
operator, malformed AST, overflow/codec mismatch and unsafe
refinement-order cases receive exact diagnostics. A timeout, resource
limit or unsupported construct is neither a Boolean false nor a
successful theorem. A rule may be typed but violate the product's
independently selected policy; a true evaluated rule may rely on
stale, fake or unauthorized bindings. These are separate failures.

Normalization may disregard specified irrelevant map/set ordering or
equivalent mathematical integer notation, but must preserve nominal
domains, reader IDs, optionality, nullability, operator and operand
order, failures, interpretation versions and binding identity.
A stable abstract rule fingerprint after a provider or installed-browser
change cannot reuse stale physical enforcement evidence. The eventual
proof kernel, source-elaboration checker, authority gate and physical
correspondence tests retain independent responsibilities and premises.

*** Stage 3 -- Small proof kernel and guarded proof mechanisms

Build a small, inspectable *proof-checking* foundation alongside the
permanent executable semantic core. These are different components:
the semantic core supplies runtime transition meaning; a propositional
kernel checks derivations of its own closed logic; dedicated transition,
initial-state and induction checkers establish their specified conditional
judgments. Proof-producing elaboration proposes derivations but cannot
create an inference rule or issue authority by calling a trusted-looking
function. The proof stage is a prerequisite for claims that need its
judgments, not a universal requirement that every useful application
operation await independent mathematical formalization.

*** Close the initial propositional checking boundary

Use the original, versioned proposition source with an exact subject,
nominal variable environment, declared premises, step graph and final
goal. The initial calculus has only seven inference-rule families:

- premise use;
- truth introduction;
- implication reflexivity;
- conjunction introduction;
- conjunction elimination;
- implication elimination;
- disjunction introduction.

The checker independently parses and typechecks every source proposition,
validates rule-specific arities and exact conclusions, and requires each
referenced step to precede its use. A derivation claiming a stronger goal,
using the wrong subject/nominal atom, inventing a step, hiding a required
premise or relying on an unsupported rule fails. Every required original
obligation remains visible independently of the supplied derivation.
The supported source format may additionally require every declared
premise/step to be used; that completeness discipline does not itself
prove that an original application rule or physical writer was inventoried.
