There is no initial axiom asserting an arbitrary atomic predicate,
unrestricted excluded middle, arithmetic/SMT solving, hypothetical premise
discharge, arbitrary host Clojure evaluation or transactional authority.
A conditional derivation establishes a conclusion *assuming* its admitted
source premises; it does not establish that those premises hold in the
current Request, browser, database, or installed application. A checked
derivation and its report are not a signed authorization or issuer handle.

*** Derive guarded consequences without enlarging the logical kernel

Represent a selected typed guarded transition with pre-state and input,
current guards, simultaneous post-state assignments and an explicit frame
for untouched fields, including presence as well as value where relevant.
A dedicated proof mechanism may derive exactly supported guard,
assignment, frame, conjunction and equality-substitution consequences.
It checks original transition source and matching-relation assumptions.
It cannot generalize a one-document assignment to a multi-record
RequestAssignment invariant, silently infer hidden external writes, or
turn a postcondition into evidence that a particular XTDB effect ran.

For conditional induction, freeze one *original-source* operation catalog,
its initial condition and every required invariant. Each invariant needs
a justified initial condition and preservation argument for *every*
declared operation; a missing operation, malformed guard, changed frame,
omitted invariant, unsupported consequence or falsely discharged premise
keeps the stronger judgment open. Every claimed operation and initializer
also faces independent source/physical completeness challenges. A finite
set of tested initial constructors establishes coverage only of its
declared finite catalog, not that every physical initializer satisfies
the initial predicate. The selected model must retain eligible initial
states and meaningful enabled positive operations, rather than pass an
unreachable or reject-everything machine.

Do not confuse an induction obligation with an issued universal proof.
Successful checker-local reasoning may remain conditional on original-source
coverage, initial-state existence, operation-catalog completeness, abstract
transition semantics, checker soundness and source-to-installed-effect
correspondence. Scoped checking of the complete declared set does not
establish the completeness of all potentially bypassing physical writers.

*** Keep proof, issuance and formal transfer independently accountable

Elaboration and search can construct candidate proofs or finite witnesses,
but must submit their *source* to the relevant independent checker.
Malformed derivations, stale subjects, step/reference mistakes,
unsupported substitutions, skipped branches, result-map forgery and a
mutant elaborator must not obtain a stronger accepted claim. Exhaustion,
incompleteness, a timeout and an unproved premise are not success
statuses. Nearby eligible positive derivations and useful transitions
must still pass; a mechanism that rejects everything cannot earn
completion for a functional Claim path.

Certificate admission separately binds the checked source, dependency
closure, original obligation denominator, issuer scope, validity
conditions and unclosed assumptions. A copyable report, old certificate
description or fabricated fingerprint cannot mint a current capability.
Logical facts in a derivation may be reused under logical inference
rules; one-use physical effect rights and resource ownership are not
duplicated merely by duplicating a proposition.

Independent mathematical soundness of the kernel, the production checker
acceptance implication, typed-atom semantics and actual physical
application correspondence remain distinct later formal and release
claims. In particular, a sound theorem about a seven-rule abstract
calculus does not by itself prove the concrete JVM checker, issuer,
Biff/XTDB writer, generated browser plan or deployment. Keep every
unproved bridge as a named obligation and never promote finite model
checks, successful unit tests or source inspection into such a theorem.

Acceptance of this stage is the precise scoped checking of positive
and adverse *source-bound* proofs, guarded consequences and induction
candidates with their remaining premises honestly recorded. Complete
cross-namespace certification, independently established kernel
soundness and production effect qualification remain separate milestones.

*** Stage 4 -- Qualified host, lifecycle, and invocation context

Select and qualify the *actual* Biff, Ring/Aleph, runtime, XTDB,
compiler and browser/HTMX versions and interfaces used by the
application. “Final Biff 2” is not an API, compatibility contract or
reason to wait for an unspecified release. A selected host profile
names concrete dependency identity and configuration, effective
request/FX value flow, lifecycle semantics, handler adoption,
backend behavior and the implementation assumptions on which a
claim depends. These are implementation subjects, not new owners of
domain rules.

*** Install the real application boundary before exposing traffic

Deliver:

- explicit current invocation input and prior-output value flow for
  generated and handwritten Biff/Graph/FX construction; no accidental
  assumption that previous output is implicitly merged into context;
- stable native module identities, declared resource/dependency owners,
  correct phase ordering, acquisition, initialization, start and cleanup;
- private candidate construction, required preflight/assembly checks,
  current handler installation and a qualified admission boundary before
  the selected application behavior is externally reachable;
- an exact relation between the checked candidate, concrete module,
  installed Ring handler, server's actual adopted handler, active routes
  and served/loaded browser artifacts, with unqualified bypasses reported;
- actual protected principal, model, request and transaction context
  assembled at the trusted boundary, not supplied by client metadata;
- independent concurrent request scopes and explicit supported transfer
  of a qualified context to deferred responses, streams, workers and
  subscriptions, with generation/owner-bound retirement;
- selected backend/HTMX/compiler qualification, real valid/invalid
  conformance tests, and honest residual assumptions for other host paths.

A host may have multiple physical lifecycle phases. In a selected Biff
integration where all module initializers run *before* the ordered
start phase, putting preflight first in start order does not prevent an
earlier initializer from opening a socket, publishing a worker or
performing a protected write. Every such initializer must be separately
classified, safely private/fenced, or admitted before its relevant
effect. The final guarded application must not be exposed through an
unchecked listener under startup failure, missing provider or later
handler replacement. Safe resource cleanup follows revocation of
active effect rights; failed or partial cleanup does not restore them.

*** Preserve concurrency, asynchronous ownership and real observability

Application admission and a physically installed handler do not
automatically qualify every dynamic render, alternative Ring response,
migration, external writer, worker or browser entrypoint. An HTML
serialization gate covers the canonical responses actually sent
through it; a pre-serialized or substituted handler remains an open
bypass unless independently instrumented or excluded by a real
enforcing boundary. The actual server must be shown to use the
guarded handler and asset set before physical correspondence is
credited; a staging report or matching handler key is not such proof.

Each request, command, execution, stream, delayed callback and browser
resource has its own relevant scope and retirement rules. A single
process-wide, one-use writer lease, thread-local dynamic binding or
global request context is not a sufficient model for concurrent
requests and retained asynchronous effects. A context transferred
to a worker needs a declared owner, authority basis, permitted effects,
lifetime, cancellation and post-retirement behavior. Current protected
reads and writes still require trusted checks at their use points;
a formerly admitted request context is not everlasting Membership.

Acceptance challenges startup from a genuine valid candidate as well
as missing/misordered modules, an initializer effect before start,
host handler substitution, failed preflight after resource acquisition,
duplicate module identity, concurrent request cross-talk, stale
deferred writes, unsupported context transfer, and asset/route mismatch.
The check observes the first real physical effect/serving boundary,
not only a helper report claiming the boundary would have blocked it.
Eligible normal requests and authorized deferred completions must still
work under the selected profile, with observed cleanup and bounded
resource behavior.

This stage supplies scoped lifecycle, invocation and enforcement
interfaces. It does not assert Stage 10's complete whole-application
closure, Stage 11's production release admission, or independent
formal/physical correspondence. A health or private probe may use a
separately declared and actually enforced narrower scope; it cannot
quietly expose ordinary unchecked application routes.
*** Stage 5 -- Public authoritative operations and command resolution

Construct public model operations with explicit preparation, guarded incorporation,
and after-commit work. Choreography and views consume their public contracts
rather than private model internals. HumanHelp's public Request, Membership,
Organization, and RequestAssignment contracts own the relevant business truth;
application assembly and the executor cannot define a second Claim policy.

The *source-owned transition* is the original subject. For Claim it includes
authenticated actor/target binding, current helper Membership and protected
Organization association, eligible Request lifecycle, absence or uniqueness of
the primary RequestAssignment, every guarded write and its frame, and the
disclosure contract for the returned or later recovered result. A server
pre-read may prepare a proposal, but is not itself a current commit-time
authorization or a certificate that the write protected all dependencies.

*** Bind one logical command without confusing it with an attempt

The public operation is declared before any particular command exists. A
logical command receives its identity and immutable binding before the
first possible transmission; a request, retry, execution, host, transaction,
transport attempt and browser resource each have other identities. The
trusted ingress must establish the authenticated principal, selected
operation and target, canonical argument semantics and allowed authority
scope. A client-supplied command ID is a correlation value, never proof
of permission, incorporation, current Membership or result disclosure.

The complete binding is retained with the command's authorized historical
disposition. A compatible retry or resolution consults that history *before*
testing new-incorporation business guards: a successfully incorporated Claim
can legitimately leave its Request no longer open. It must be possible
to report that original success without executing Claim again or falsely
rejecting the historical command. Reusing the same ID for changed arguments,
principal, operation or scope is a typed incompatibility, not a new intent.

A newly incorporable command must atomically protect its current business
conditions, complete multi-record effects and required durable command
outcome. Where the selected reliability profile requires durable notice
intent, its record belongs in the same suitable atomic authoritative
boundary; asynchronous SSE publication is a subsequent delivery step.
Separate after-commit attempts must not make an already incorporated
domain transition appear rejected. A command record is not a permission
to disclose private history to an unauthorized resolver.

Deliver:

- typed inputs, current authority requirements, guarded dependencies, write and
  frame contracts, result/disclosure contracts, and durable-work obligations;
- stable =:gesso/command-id= binding before first possible send, covering operation,
  interface, canonical arguments, principal, and authority scope;
- compatible existing-command lookup before applying a new-command business guard;
- atomic command exclusion, authoritative mutation, result recording, and required
  publication intent;
- model outcomes =:committed=, =:rejected=, =:already-incorporated=, and
  =:commit-unknown=, with explicit presentation mappings;
- protected command reconciliation, retry, retention, and expiry behavior;
- public composition of cross-model constraints without pretending that separate
  transactions form one atomic operation;
- a source-complete ledger of permission, relationship, existence, uniqueness,
  guarded change, command-result, disclosure and publication requirements,
  including independently required actions not yet implemented;
- explicit separation of attempt-local transport outcomes, authoritative
  command incorporation/exclusion, historical recovery, and actor-visible
  presentation or Live advisory progression;
- canonical outcomes with qualified origin and scope, preserving unknown
  incorporation after a possible send rather than inferring failure from
  connection loss, read timeout, absent command record or abort of one attempt;
- the independent server read and authorization required to disclose a retained
  command result, including retained history, expiry and compatible old-client
  recovery under a changed host generation.

A command is not safely retryable merely because a new physical attempt is
possible. Retained identical command binding and appropriate authoritative
resolve-or-incorporate exclusion are needed to prevent duplicate effects;
on indeterminate evidence the contract must say who retries, rereads,
reconciles or waits, and under which availability and retention premises.
A failed individual attempt does not exclude a concurrent other attempt.
Nor does current Request/assignment state by itself attribute success
to one particular earlier command.

*** Admit the complete source effect, not a convenient document fragment

Claim's domain mutation, primary RequestAssignment creation or reassignment,
canonical command-result creation and required publication intent are one
declared authoritative effect where that strong profile is selected.
A sequence of individually successful writes is not equivalent to an atomic
multi-record transition. Other source-owned operations, including Unclaim,
Reassign and terminal transitions, need their own eligible and adversarial
execution paths; a successful Claim neither implies their correctness nor
shrinks the independent HumanHelp capability denominator.

Outcomes =:committed=, =:rejected=, =:already-incorporated= and
=:commit-unknown= remain model/command-level claims with qualified evidence.
The browser's provisional/accepted/rejected/unknown presentation does not
constitute a database transaction result. A known committed outcome may
still have undelivered Live advice or an unadopted remote presentation;
a successful SSE send does not grant remote collection Refresh. A
postcommit publication failure never retrospectively invalidates the
authoritative result. Preflight may reject structurally unsupported
operation/effect shapes early, while changing current domain predicates
must be rechecked at their trusted incorporation boundary.

Acceptance pairs a genuine successful Claim with typed guard rejection,
compatible historical replay, incompatible command reuse, changed Membership
or association, simultaneous competing Claim, stale server pre-read, lost
response after possible submission, and recovered command truth after a
later lifecycle mutation. It also challenges a forged principal, missing
RequestAssignment write, omitted command record or outbox requirement,
unknown outcome incorrectly marked rejected, and a retry under a new
identity. The first boundary with sufficient legitimate evidence must
reject or retain the exact uncertainty; no reject-everything candidate can
count as a completed usable operation.

The Claim scope guards Request state, helper Membership, Organization policy,
association and primary-assignment conditions together with its writes. A
pre-read or a self-asserted eligible flag cannot establish those current facts
at incorporation. Replaying C42 after an Unclaim or other later event requires
authorized *command-specific* historical evidence, not merely a currently
claimed Request. Stage 6 separately qualifies the actual backend, guard
semantics, transaction-internal prestate and all physical writing paths.

*** Stage 6 -- Physical transaction mediation and provider qualification

Bind the authoritative plan to the actual physical submission boundary.
The supported implementation may use a narrow mechanically checked lowering
or an explicit opaque adapter whose remaining assumptions cannot disappear.
For a selected strong claim, the admitted source, complete guarded plan,
lowered immutable transaction vector, issued executor, exact one-shot physical
submission, authenticated authority context and observation provenance must
refer to the *same* execution subject. The selected provider/backend profile,
transaction options, encoding and trusted host route are distinct identities.

*** Protect prestate, write footprint and the exact frame

The canonical abstract transition evaluates its guards against a declared
pre-write state and applies its supported assignments atomically. A concrete
XTDB implementation must show that its ASSERT predicates and transaction
operations faithfully implement that transition under the selected API
semantics. For a supported ASSERT-before-write lowering, checking ordering
and transaction-vector shape is a useful prerequisite, not proof that the
provider's *transaction-internal* prestate equals a separately pinned
external read. A snapshot token, ledger row, transaction key or later matching
card cannot authenticate an unseen internal guard evaluation.

Guard and write footprints are different. A guard may depend on Request
status, helper Membership, Organization policy, a relationship's absence or
uniqueness, and command history while the admitted writes touch a different
set of documents. An opaque predicate or external writer can invalidate
the proof unless the selected mechanism establishes its coverage or retains
a named premise. Every mutation, effective transaction option, hook, and
update/replace semantics must be accounted for.

Whole-document replacement can erase a concurrently added field even
when all previously visible values compare equal. A sound frame contract
must protect **presence and value**, including newly introduced and
deleted fields, using an admitted complete field-count/footprint guard,
monotonic history-sensitive revision, suitable partial update operation
or other independently qualified mechanism. Full-value comparison alone
does not eliminate ABA (A→B→A); if forbidden intervening history matters,
the chosen identity/revision/transaction-history discipline must actually
exclude it, including bypassing writers.

Absence, uniqueness, cardinality and one-primary RequestAssignment are
predicate/relationship obligations, not merely a cached false value.
Their physical realization must survive two concurrent attempts and every
admitted writer. No pre-read test or synthetic concurrency schedule is
a substitute for a real protected physical contention case.

Deliver:

- immutable admitted plans and complete physical transaction derivation/checking;
- one submission owner that cannot accept appended raw writes or a substituted
  backend client/callback through its normal interface;
- guard footprints separate from write footprints, including absent/unique
  relationship predicates and all effective transaction options or hooks;
- frame preservation for whole-document replacement, with complete comparison,
  a justified revision discipline, or a qualified alternative update mechanism;
- local attempt and provider-return observation correlated to the issued invocation;
- provider-qualified outcome, read-basis, progression, and atomicity interpretation;
- a real writer inventory and mediation contract covering routes, jobs, imports,
  maintenance, migrations, and external write credentials where the claim requires it;
- explicit backend-assumption qualification and invalidation from Part X;
- one source-to-physical and target-bound submission relation: the caller
  cannot append raw SQL, alter the protected table/target, change transaction
  options or swap the backend callback after the admitted plan is issued;
- transaction-internal prestate and actual guard/action correspondence, or a
  precise conditional premise and reproducible real-provider tests where
  the provider exposes no independently authenticated internal witness;
- complete protected physical frame and presence/write-footprint evidence,
  including caller-supplied actual values, absent relationships, monotonic
  revision policies and history-sensitive conflict assumptions;
- independently qualified process/request/execution/host context, preserving
  parallelism while limiting individual submit capabilities to the intended
  one-shot attempt and retiring stale physical effects;
- separate submitted-operation provenance, provider return, ledger/commit
  status, authoritative command record, read basis, scoped progression,
  actual actor readback and browser adoption, without treating agreement
  between two observations as causal proof;
- independent source/assembly and host-observed writer inventories plus
  mediation or explicitly admitted external writer assumptions for
  migrations, background tasks, maintenance clients, extra processes
  and directly credentialed XTDB connections.

*** Challenge real submission, concurrent writers and evidence limits

Acceptance uses actual backend concurrency and failure windows. It requires
at least one eligible physical success and controlled negatives for stale
Request status, revoked/changed Membership, changed association, competing
primary insertion, duplicate command, additional field erasure, ABA,
loss of command record, unauthorized writer, provider exception after
possible submission, insufficient read progression, and changed adapter
or configuration. The actual transaction's lowered operations and protected
targets must agree with the original plan. Supported values distinguish
absence, null, false, collections, and physical encodings under selected
runtime codecs.

Physical evidence has several independently limited layers. A plan-shaped
checker result proves construction of a *form*, not that it ran. A
process-local one-shot callback or captured return proves only its
correspondingly scoped observation; it is not a cryptographic, durable
command record. A pinned poststate and ledger observation may be
consistent with the returned key without proving which physical writer
caused the observed domain state. A genuinely authenticated protected
physical writer, complete internal-guard coverage and actual submission
can establish stronger bounded claims; a universal refinement theorem
still requires the stated semantics, source completeness and
independent proof/correspondence premises.

The selected strong application profile must survey *all relevant writers*
rather than only HTTP routes or Gesso-issued operations. Independent
host/process/credential coverage is needed before treating a source
registry as a physically closed world. Where the environment cannot
enumerate or constrain an external writer, the stronger no-bypass
claim remains unestablished even when the registered local callbacks
all agree. Deployment changes invalidate the appropriate old physical
evidence while possibly preserving an unrelated sound abstract theorem.

A pinned external pre-read is not a transaction-internal state witness; later
matching post-state is not proof of causality; local return observation is not
a universal refinement theorem. Complete field comparison without history
does not exclude ABA. The required external behavior, physical prestate
relationship, and closed-writer premise remain named and testable.

The stage reports exactly which physical forms, provider versions, writer
paths and authority scopes are supported. One-document coverage cannot
satisfy HumanHelp's multi-record Claim contract. A host-supplied writer
enumerator cannot prove that undisclosed direct XTDB writers are impossible,
and a registered one-shot callback need not be the one a deployed route uses.
The release and cross-layer checker may claim only the smaller supported
subject until actual installed submission, open writer effects,
unknown-command recovery, retained publication and protected readback
are covered by qualified evidence and nonvacuous testing.

*** Stage 7 -- Portable choreography, distributed admissibility, and projection

Construct one source-owned global choreography and its derived role-local
machines around the public operations, typed semantic values and authoritative
observation contracts established earlier. The permanent executable semantic
core defines global behavior and its distributed observation alphabet;
verification decides a selected set of well-formedness, value availability,
role knowledge and admissibility obligations; projection emits one canonical
role-local =ExecutablePlan=. These are distinguishable judgments, not three
independently authored copies of the application.

*** Establish one meaning across roles and knowledge sources

Deliver:

- distinct role, principal, actor, host, authority, execution and operation
  identities, including which identity binds a trusted server-side operation;
- a small typed global operation vocabulary, with local action, authoritative
  invocation, branch, participant communication, environment await and terminal
  result distinguished by their actual observable meanings;
- source-owned public operation inputs, required capabilities, closed outputs,
  failure and recovery results, and no browser-provided authorization premise;
- declared messages with required, optional and correlation fields, exact schema
  and default-closed semantics; open transport extras do not acquire semantic
  knowledge or bypass disclosure rules;
- role-local knowledge/provenance from entry input, declared communication,
  qualified authoritative invocation or observation, deterministic derivation,
  and explicitly identified asserted premises, never from a globally convenient
  value store or a matching property name;
- source, actor, program point, observation basis and progression-sensitive
  refinements, with required facts available on every relevant incoming path;
- behavior-sensitive branch discrimination, including who can distinguish
  continuations through an admitted value, message or authority observation;
- communication/authoritative causal barriers, terminal ownership, waiting,
  interruption, and declared recovery or durable handoff where later action
  depends on an effect or participant;
- checked global-to-local projection, canonical plan and compilation identity,
  portable schema/value codec and separately qualified JVM/Node/Chromium
  interpretation for the supported language;
- distinct structural verification, projection preservation, runtime trace,
  physical transport and authorization evidence classes.

A semantic global value may exist without a particular role knowing it.
Receiving a closed message can justify declared payload knowledge, but does
not authenticate a server, refresh Membership, grant a principal's role or
establish a newer authoritative basis. A participant send is not a receive;
a browser local =:await= is not participant communication; a reread of
authority is not a newly committed domain mutation. Source and compiler IDs
may be erased from an executable plan only when the checker/sidecar retains
the exact source-to-plan relation; a proof-shaped sidecar cannot change
runtime behavior or become an authority token.

*** Admit behavior-sensitive branches and genuine causal progress

A branch at one role may be private only if other roles' projected behavior
does not depend on which branch was taken until they can distinguish it.
Identical message keywords or overlapping receive shapes are not sufficient
evidence that two continuations are equivalent. The verifier and projection
must reject when an undistinguished foreign branch changes a receiver's
required action, payload meaning, destination, protected effect or terminal
obligation. Closed alternatives need justified disjointness, not a
first-matching-case convention. A purported optional value is not definitely
known on a path where it was never provided.

An authoritative operation is a global causal event even when some other
role has no direct local action at that state. Its projected successors
may not execute dependent work before the admitted causal communication,
observation or alternative predecessor has occurred. A sender's local
completion or a browser role reaching =:return= does not prove a required
receiver acted or that the entire global choreography terminated.
When the contract requires durable waiting, retry, timeout, participant
acknowledgment or a future execution, its owner and actual recovery path
must be specified. A later execution cannot inherit another retired
browser execution's private resource rights or unresolved command outcome
without an independent admission and qualified transfer.

Acceptance pairs a useful global Claim/authoritative result and justified
recipient continuation with: private branch leakage, overlapping receive
contracts, sender-unknown payload fields, missing declared FX inputs,
premature authoritative-success effects, a forged authority assertion,
an optional reader used as definite, confused participant/await events,
and a disconnected recovery branch. Fail known contradictions at the
earliest verifier, projection, assembly or guarded use point; maintain
a named conditional premise for genuinely external facts.

For the same admitted source, initial semantic state and normalized event
sequence, portable machines must produce the declared equivalent semantic
observations under the selected bounded interpretation and representations.
That requirement does not assert identical network schedules, fair delivery,
transport authenticity or an unbounded proof of implementation refinement.
Stage 13 and later formal work can strengthen proof of projection and
cross-layer correspondence without introducing a parallel production
runtime. A useful positive role-local trace and actual issued plan must
remain independently exercisable; a reject-everything compiler cannot
satisfy application delivery.

*** Stage 8 -- Browser semantics and physical effect enforcement

Realize the selected =ExecutablePlan= through a portable pure browser
transition function and a narrow explicitly owned physical shell:

#+begin_src text
AdapterState x NormalizedEvent -> AdapterState x AbstractEffects
#+end_src

The adapter owns semantic execution, normalized-event admission,
target/fragment/resource generations, desired abstract effects,
provisional/authoritative progression and retirement. The shell owns
DOM objects, timers, transport handles, HTMX observations, continuity
snapshots and other physical resources, returning exact completion and
failure events. Neither layer may silently substitute an independently
handwritten business workflow for the admitted plan. An untrusted browser
must never execute the server-authoritative operation merely because
the same operation name appears in its projection.

*** Bind events and effects to current resource rights

Deliver:

- distinct logical command, execution, transport attempt, effect instance,
  resource instance, target incarnation and application-generation identity;
- owner-relative event admission for both execution-private effects and shared
  fragment/subscription events, including their exact issued-work identity,
  currentness, payload schema, legal state and provenance class;
- retirement that revokes effect rights before fallible physical cleanup,
  without erasing separately retained command recovery or current shared
  resource ownership;
- permission revalidation at the *last protected physical mutation*, not
  just at an earlier event or scheduling point; delayed, reentrant and
  secondary effects must obey the same selected scope;
- guarded HTMX request, swap, OOB-target, install and settle boundaries using
  the actual documented lifecycle of the selected HTMX version, rather than
  invented generic hooks or a pre-swap report treated as completion;
- logical single-flight and coalesced queued refresh requirements with
  independent boundedness for metadata, pending callbacks, browser requests,
  retained snapshots, subscriptions and failed physical cleanup;
- typed provisional state, known rejection, historical incorporation, unknown
  outcome, supersession, optimistic rollback and canonical installation,
  with no silent elevation from provisional intent to model authority;
- explicit actual authoritative presence/absence, exact scope/basis progression,
  partial-installation repair, installed coverage and undisclosed/cannot-read
  obligations; response receipt is not participant adoption;
- continuity as compatible local UI presentation (search, sorting, selection,
  scroll, focus), never as current model truth or a retained write permission;
- stale plan/generation compatibility, source-bound asset and route identities,
  safe retire-or-reconstruct decisions and explicit recovery ownership.

An event arriving early, twice or after retirement may be consumed only under
its registered source, generation, current resource owner and legal progression
rule. A callback's earlier accepted Boolean is not a future physical permit.
A resource reincarnated under the same DOM ID is not the same resource. An
abort can fail after physical work, so cleanup failure cannot restore an
obsolete permission. Logical slot bounds do not imply bounded physical
XHRs, orphaned timers or resource metadata; those require independent
limits and honest reclamation or failure assumptions.

*** Keep physical installation and semantic adoption distinct

The active HTMX/Ring integration must distinguish request admission,
transport receipt, response parsing, before-swap decision, OOB secondary
swaps, actual installed DOM, post-swap settlement and authoritative
acquisition/adoption. A successful HTTP status, newer-looking token,
permitted swap, or completed root replacement does not prove every
required target was installed or that the result covers the authorized
query/progression scope. Record the actual effect completion and
correspondence before discharging its installation obligation. A
failed partial swap keeps the uncovered debt, repairs or retires the
affected resource, and does not expose enabled controls for an
unverified inconsistent result.

Live invalidation is an advisory about a possibly relevant change, not
an authoritative result and not a user grant. Under HumanHelp's selected
remote policy, Bob's other-user Create or lifecycle change may mark
the board stale or display an advisory, but does not automatically
replace his adopted collection. A *separately authorized*, scoped,
one-logical-read explicit Refresh can acquire a qualified result;
physical installation and its coverage must then complete before
the covered debt is discharged. Failed or partial OOB completion
does not mint an additional Refresh or erase an unresolved one.
Creator-local adoption and narrowly correlated command recovery
are separately selected exceptions, not blanket remote adoption.
Reconnect, lost notice, changed browser generation and a rising
progression token cannot independently grant acquisition or DOM
replacement. An authorized manual acquisition path must still
be available when a notice never arrived or an interest was learned
after its publication.

A Create projection does not need a fictitious prior entity
observation when the entity did not exist. Its provisional intent is
bound to an eligible operation and whatever enclosing facts are
actually known. Conversely, a newer Request read may justify
current presentation repair without proving the historical C42
command outcome. Retiring the optimistic execution or losing
its DOM does not erase its independently owned pending resolver,
permission checks, retention horizon or authorized recovery path.

*** Challenge the actual browser and trusted shell

Acceptance uses both portable event-order exploration and independent
real Chromium/HTMX tests of the generated physical plan and effect
handlers. Required positive histories include a usable Claim,
authorized canonical settlement, controlled local continuity,
genuine creator-local Create, a delayed but permitted callback,
and one explicitly granted remote Refresh that installs its
declared scope exactly once. Pair them with stale and duplicate
callbacks, recycled resource IDs, failed abort, partial OOB install,
a continuation across incompatible assets, a later stale rollback,
lost command response, unauthorized automatic remote read, missing
required target, incomparable authoritative basis and resource
leak under continued retries.

The physical tests must exercise the actual served artifact,
lifecycle hooks, DOM mutations, errors and deferred effects at their
first enforcing boundaries. A model-only event name, injected
trusted-looking settlement, skipped console failure, or a test
harness that asserts only final text cannot prove real HTMX
integration, browser refinement or current user authorization.
Controlled expected failures must not hide unrelated page,
request, console or application exceptions. Source-to-physical
admission and all relevant writer/read disclosure boundaries
retain their own evidence and assumptions.

Stage 8 thus establishes an explicit owned browser realization,
not a universal liveness theorem or proof that every current
HTMX version and browser schedule behaves alike. Its completion
still depends on source/plan correspondence, qualified physical
effect shells, actual installation evidence and nonvacuous product
acceptance. Choreo proof, browser status, delivery success and
model truth remain separate claims.
*** Stage 9 -- Live publication, observation coverage, and selective adoption

Close the authoritative commit → required publication intent → dispatch →
subscriber awareness → authorized acquisition → actual browser adoption path
without confusing any two of those events. Gesso Live transports advisory
invalidation and opaque progression requirements; it does not carry a
second copy of domain truth, grant a protected read, or install browser
content by publishing a notice. The selected authoritative provider owns
the meaning of consistency, basis comparison and read coverage, rather
than a universal integer revision or arrival-time ordering.

*** Derive publication obligations from authoritative source

The public model operation owns which committed changes require notice,
the affected domain scopes, permitted recipient disclosure, necessary
progression and the durability/recovery profile. Expansion rules may
derive invalidation scopes from the original change but cannot invent
new authoritative basis evidence or infer recipients' complete interests
from a local ephemeral cache.

Where the chosen profile promises publication across writer crash or host
replacement, incorporate *durable publication intent* together with the
guarded domain effect and command record under a suitable common atomic
boundary. Dispatch, retry, duplicate suppression, retention, dequeue,
acknowledgment and delivery ownership are later responsibilities with
explicit failure windows. An outbox record establishes that a notice
was owed, not that every client received it or that a protected
projection may now be revealed. A publisher failure after known commit
must never be reported as a rejected domain operation; residual notice
work remains owned. If a weaker profile is selected, state which crash,
retention, availability or user-recovery guarantees are *not* claimed.

Deliver:

- a source-derived change/invalidation/interest/fragment relation,
  independently qualified for its exact assembly and publication profile;
- an atomic durable intent and qualified dispatcher when required,
  with exact owner, handoff, retry, idempotency, expiration, failure and
  recipient/disclosure scopes rather than an implicit best-effort callback;
- per-authority opaque progression, with orderless composition of distinct
  requirements unless a trusted provider supplies explicit entailment
  or comparison evidence;
- explicit separation of advisory frontier, authorized acquisition
  requirements, actually covered read, physically adopted result,
  current source knowledge and still-outstanding obligation debt;
- initial fragment acquisition or a justified existing observation,
  with a usable protected read route even when no advisory arrives;
- registration/subscription fencing, replay or qualified gap detection,
  and reconnect/failover ownership for interests learned after an
  invalidation or transferred between hosts and routers;
- admissible authorization and scope binding for advisory payload,
  follow-up acquisition and negative/exclusion observations, including
  the cases in which an entity is undisclosed rather than absent;
- per-fragment logical single-flight, debt coalescing, retry/backpressure,
  bounded metadata and separately bounded physical resource remnants,
  with explicit retention and availability assumptions;
- a convergence or honestly weaker eventual-user-recovery contract
  that does not depend on receiving every transient notice or
  inventing provider progression from a successful HTTP response.

*** Establish the initial-interest and lost-notice recovery seam

A durable outbox by itself cannot close a missed-subscription gap.
At initial registration, a subscriber can discover its interest only
*after* an invalidation was computed or dispatched; a replacement
router can also lack the departed router's interest. The first
useful managed projection therefore needs an admitted observation
and a registration/acquisition fence, qualified replay, or a
documented gap/reacquisition protocol under the source authority.
Do not interpret silence from a router as authoritative freshness.
A subscription token, published cursor or membership in a coarse
routing filter is not automatically equivalent to a complete
provider read basis or physical board adoption.

A claimed strong multi-host path must make durable notice recovery,
interest registration, failover, redelivery and recipient knowledge
separate obligations. Idempotent invalidations may be redelivered
conservatively; their duplication cannot mint a second business
command, alter current authorization or consume a fresh user grant.
No particular broker, hierarchical router topology, Rust process,
global durable actor or fixed consumer graph is mandatory in the
timeless specification. The chosen topology must establish its own
coverage, takeover, ordering/gap and liveness premises. A single-node
profile obeys the same semantic contract with fewer physical owners.

An authoritative absence is a *positive qualified negative fact*:
it binds the permitted principal, query, entity/membership scope,
source basis, negative/disclosure semantics and physically adopted
coverage. An absent DOM node, local filter, failed request, undisclosed
entity, no matching interest or unfulfilled subscription does not
establish domain absence.

*** Acquire only with an authorized scope and selected product permission

An advisory requirement may make an existing board stale, but it
cannot authorize a subsequent database read or replace the DOM.
Acquisition checks current trusted principal, source/query scope,
permitted provider progression, current fragment/target owner and
the *separately selected grant policy*. A qualified observation
discharges only those requirements for which the provider proves
coverage, scope, temporal compatibility and physical installation.
An incomparable or insufficient basis remains outstanding; a
successful HTTP 200 or echo of a requested token is not that proof.
Newer observations may cover earlier advisory debt without
assuming all opaque tokens are linearly ordered.

For HumanHelp's selected ordinary remote Create and lifecycle
policy, the incoming notice remains *advisory only*. Bob's
one-use explicit Refresh grant authorizes exactly its selected
logical board acquisition under the currently admitted applied
query and disclosure context. A new notice arriving during that
cycle may be covered by its already qualified result if the
provider establishes entailment; otherwise its debt survives.
It never silently issues a successor acquisition, even if the
first physical HTMX attempt completes or fails. A new grant
requires the selected new user action or separately declared
authorized recovery policy. Creator-local acceptance, a
narrowly correlated own-command reread and trusted revocation
are different scopes, not general permission to auto-adopt
remote content. Local filters and visible cohort membership
do not become server read authority.

Acceptance must witness an eligible first acquisition, durable
commit-to-advisory path, authorized one-use Refresh and actual
scope-complete DOM installation alongside: crash after commit
before dispatch, duplicated/reordered notice, early registration
race, stale backup filter, failed router, dropped notice with no
recorded debt, insufficient or incomparable basis, omitted card,
partial OOB installation, authorization change, reconnect and
concurrent new notice during Refresh. The recorded result
distinguishes incorporated state, owed notice, attempted delivery,
recipient interest, permission to read, complete observation
and adopted presentation. If availability or fairness is not
established, safety may remain valid while convergence remains
explicitly conditional.

*** Stage 10 -- Whole-application construction and actual installed closure

The ordinary managed application is built from *one source-owned
construction*, not independently hand-maintained route, model,
browser, proof, recovery and diagnostic registries that merely
use compatible names. The product's independently chosen required
capabilities and current public policy are the denominator for
closure. A closed discovered graph can be a useful narrower
application but cannot define away a required HumanHelp operation,
Response-flow decision, protected writer, publication obligation
or uninspected correctness-relevant predicate.

*** Establish source, assembly, and physical-implementation joins

Deliver:

- the typed application graph linking original policy/rule subjects,
  public model operations, Choreo, role-local plan, generated artifact,
  route, transport, trusted handler, execution capabilities,
  transaction/command outcome, notice, fragment and acquisition;
- independently required product-capability and protected-effect
  inventories, cross-checked against the source-derived admitted
  operation catalog rather than reduced to what the generator found;
- source-derived requirements and selected evidence mechanisms,
  distinguishing proven, runtime-enforced, assembly-verified,
  conditional, trusted/opaque, unsupported, inconclusive,
  contradicted and uninspected claims at their exact scopes;
- closed required/supplied capability and FX invocation contracts,
  route method/path identity, collisions with anonymous HTMX,
  actual provider bindings, model/operation source versions and
  declared recovery paths for every required dynamic outcome;
- canonical browser manifest, checked build/compile provenance,
  exact artifact bytes, immutable publication set and serving/
  loaded-asset correspondence under generation/release identity;
- actual Biff/Ring lifecycle dependencies, before-exposure
  preflight, qualified installed handler/executor binding,
  protected writer/read capabilities and independently examined
  alternative route, worker, migration and backend paths;
- real dynamic rendered Hiccup/HTML/HTMX affordance checks at the
  earliest supported pre-serialization boundary, including
  deferred responses and any selected supported streaming scopes;
- one read-only, source-derived policy/operation/authorization/
  disclosure/lifecycle/dependency/assurance audit with
  exact completeness and opaque-premise annotations;
- stable typed errors, first knowable failure owner, incompatible
  versus missing resource distinctions, and nonexecuting repair
  guidance tied back to the same original source.

*** Fail at the earliest legitimate boundary, not at a convenient report

Static checks reject a known missing operation/view/route/plan/artifact/
model edge, unsupported effect/required recovery contract, inconsistent
command binding, ambiguous route or absent provider before installing
the affected managed behavior. Dynamic conditions need a *declared,
structurally admissible* continuation with a real owner, required
knowledge, permitted effects, trigger and terminal/uncertain outcome.
Preflight does not assert that Membership, XTDB, network, permissions
or clocks will remain valid. The trusted invocation/transaction
boundary rechecks facts whose truth becomes knowable only there.

A real rendered response is checked before the supported HTML
serialization step; that boundary does not automatically inspect
arbitrary pre-serialized Ring HTML or a later substituted handler.
The actual Biff module initialization/start order and the server's
adoption of `:biff.ring/handler` (or explicitly selected equivalent)
must be qualified independently. One inspected application map,
green assembly result or forged preflight report is not evidence
that the deployed listener served the checked handler, accepted
the issued executor, bound its protected writer or delivered the
recorded asset bytes. Under a strong production claim, an
uncalled optional checker or an unenumerated physical writer
is an open obligation that prevents stronger admission.

A rendering or transport failure *after* a qualified committed
Claim does not undo that commit. It may block browser installation,
leave unknown attribution at the client or create publication debt,
each with its own recovery owner. When canonical rendering fails
before response delivery, the supported fail-closed output gate
must not release an unchecked affordance. Concurrent startup,
reload, deferred output and version change preserve their
actual generation and resource lifetimes; stale artifacts and
obsolete handlers cannot borrow the successor's admission.

*** Audit policy honestly, including opaque or unexamined code

The semantic audit is a projection of the original admitted
semantic and assembly objects, not a second authority or a
complete interpretation of arbitrary Clojure source. Each
correctness-relevant predicate affecting authorization,
eligibility, disclosure, lifecycle, ownership, command
acceptance or transition either has an admitted source-owned
contract, a derived proof/inspection relation, or an
explicitly open opaque implementation premise. The checker
must report what it actually inspected and which other
callbacks, handlers, writers and external services remain
outside the scope. Zero escapes found in an incomplete scan
does not mean zero escapes in the application.

Independent source-policy adequacy is separate from formal
internal consistency. A perfectly checked but product-wrong
policy cannot earn full product completion. Missing or
unselected HumanHelp Response, Reassign or other required
lifecycle functionality remains visible even if every
discovered operation passes preflight. Genuine positive
Claim, Create, lifecycle, search/Refresh and browser
scenarios must remain possible under the specified profile;
a reject-everything application is not complete.

Acceptance tests the source-to-physical installed path with
a real eligible operation, then controlled removal or
substitution of every named important edge: missing
view/plan/route/provider, unbound clock/principal,
unrealizable dynamic recovery, stale build, wrong
browser target, anonymous HTMX route collision,
replaced Biff handler, pre-serialized response bypass,
direct XTDB writer, incorrect CSS/JS publication
generation, bogus audit claim and unsupported
opaque policy predicate. Errors occur at the first
boundary able to know the defect and otherwise retain
a typed *open* limitation. Independent observation of
actual serving, current authority and protected writes
is needed before declaring production-path enforcement.
Ordinary genuinely non-Choreo HTMX remains legal
under its own explicit contract and may not inherit
the managed application's stronger claims.

The later release, product and compositional-certification
milestones still require their own independent evidence.
Stage 10 establishes the source-owned application
construction, exact scope and admissible installed
enforcement boundaries; it does not establish all
possible arbitrary Clojure behavior, universal backend
semantics, full HumanHelp acceptance or actual proof
soundness merely by assembling a graph.
*** Stage 11 -- Release integrity, reuse, and bounded compatibility

Implement the four subject-specific release decisions of
[[#req-release-evidence]] and the directional compatibility
contracts of [[#req-bounded-release-compatibility]] for the
application's independently chosen intent and assurance profile.
Admission, installation, activation and completion have different
subjects and required observations; they are not four states of
one trusted Boolean or four independent completion milestones.
This stage integrates obligations already active at the first
managed deployment; delaying Stage 11 work does not permit
the first installed application to expose unchecked handlers,
stale browser assets or unauthorized protected effects.

*** Bind the original release intent before generating results

The original application, product and deployment requirement
denominators, selected evidence policy, source/operation versions,
target hosts, protected writer universe and requested milestone
are fixed before the associated checks run. A generator must not
derive the complete requirement set exclusively from the
operations, gates or tests that happen to succeed. A mandatory
unselected product decision, unsupported physical writer or
unexamined Clojure policy stays an explicit blocker or conditional
premise for the *relevant* strong claim; it cannot disappear into
a smaller closed report. A deliberately narrower operational
release remains legitimate when its stated profile permits it.
Its status must not impersonate a stronger requested profile.

Deliver:

- an immutable candidate identity binding original source, public
  rules, required capability inventory, exact operation/plan
  and route graph, artifact/manifest/issuer inputs, source
  dependencies, evidence policy and selected environment;
- four separately admitted and reported judgments: candidate
  construction/admission, actual host installation, current
  activation/exposure and named completion milestone;
- exact gate coverage and closed result dispositions, distinguishing
  proven or checked, passed runtime/physical test, conditional,
  trusted premise, unsupported, missing, inconclusive, failed,
  inapplicable and excluded *according to the selected Part XI
  contract*, without laundering a premise through an aggregate
  green status;
- dependency-cone invalidation and selective reuse of unaffected
  abstract theorems, while separately requalifying changed
  adapters, issuer dependencies, installed handlers, providers,
  direct writers, browser assets and current authorization;
- robust cache deserialization, original-source rechecking and
  fresh issuance wherever an in-process proof handle or
  qualification cannot safely be transferred as raw bytes;
- actual generated/staged/served and client-loaded artifact
  correspondence, including expected bootstrap, codec,
  transport, role and executable-plan identities;
- coherent compare-and-activate, bounded old/new overlap,
  failure fencing, writer/reader capability withdrawal,
  private installation cleanup and host-level observation
  of the serving generation;
- source-derived continuation and retirement contracts for
  old clients, requests, streams, deferred effects, workers,
  migrations, persistent data and surviving command-recovery
  ownership, with explicit compatibility and retention limits.

*** Check directional overlap, not adjacent version labels

Four release coordinates must not be misrepresented as four
version identities: source-derived semantic identity, installed
physical realization and client artifact/continuation identity
are three separately qualified subjects; the *fourth
coordinate is a directional compatibility relation* for an
origin, target, operation and actual overlap condition.
A/A, A/B, B/A and B/B are checked when reachable in the
selected routing and deployment topology. Equality of
labels, route names, nearby Git revisions or plan digests
neither proves cross-direction compatibility nor establishes
current read/write permission. One old browser may reach
a new server while a new browser reaches an old server,
and their decoders, payloads and state transitions may
differ.

Before a protected read, authoritative command or DOM
installation, the active gateway verifies the applicable
origin/target relation and current principal/scope/
resource rights. Missing or unsupported compatibility
must refuse the effect or use an independently admitted,
non-mutating recovery path; it cannot silently downgrade
to an anonymous HTMX route, ignore changed command fields,
replace another client's adopted board or run an obsolete
unsafe writer. Retain only the old assets, decoders, command
records and other resources needed within their declared
horizons; retention is not indefinite authorization.

A pending old command C42 may have incorporated before
the old execution retired and its response was lost.
The target release may supply a new *authorized historical
resolver* for the same immutable command ID and binding
without admitting the retired mutation implementation,
reconstructing the old browser execution, or assuming
current Request state attributes C42. If retention,
authorization or evidence is insufficient, preserve
unknown status and the selected recovery or explicit
terminal-exclusion policy. Current-state acquisition,
command-specific settlement and browser continuity have
different owners.

*** Activate one safe generation and retain honest failure debt

Installation validates the exact private host resources,
Biff/Ring handlers, trusted writers, provider configurations,
worker processes and asset-serving paths. Activation then
checks the current predecessor and exposed traffic before
permitting the successor to serve. A failed candidate
cannot borrow an old green report or leave new privileged
callbacks alive by relying on best-effort cleanup; revoke
their active rights before retiring physical resources.
A predecessor may remain active only while its own
physical, semantic and security premises still hold.
Reactivation or rollback is a *new checked transition*:
neither a code rollback nor a browser swap reverses
a durable Request/assignment/command history.

A selected production run must test useful valid admissions,
installations, activations and unchanged-evidence reuse,
not only mutant rejection. Adverse cases include omitted
mandatory gate, forged report/issuer, stale cache, changed
source/premise, suppressed check, changed XTDB adapter,
wrong served or loaded JS, post-check handler substitution,
concurrent activation, stale external writer, unsupported
A-to-B/B-to-A continuation, partial cleanup and C42 lost
response across retirement. The earliest enforcing
boundary rejects, retains conditionality or preserves
a recoverable unknown; pass-by-skipping is never success.

An accepted operational release does not automatically
prove compositional certification, independent external
formal soundness or multi-node production. Those four
completion milestones and their separate evidence subjects
remain as defined in Part XI, not as a linear sequence
of required construction stages.

*** Stage 12 -- Complete HumanHelp proving application

Complete the *independently selected* Part VIII product
capability set through the real production public model,
admitted Gesso application, actual installed Biff/XTDB/
HTMX/CLJS paths and observable browser behavior.
The early Claim vertical slice is a useful architecture
test; it is not a replacement for Create, all other
lifecycle operations, selected Response interaction,
search/details/continuity, recovery and multi-user
adoption. Product acceptance is not a consequence of a
structurally closed generated registry. HumanHelp must
remain a proving *application*, not a special case baked
into the framework's generic runtime or proof kernel.

*** Preserve the original product denominator and authority

The protected model and its public core APIs own
Request, RequestAssignment, Organization, Membership,
User and Location semantics. Actual sign-in produces
separate authenticated principals and current read/
write/disclosure scopes; a browser session label or
helper name cannot confer those permissions. Each
eligible operation must cross a real rendered control,
bound command, trusted server operation, multi-record
guarded effect where needed, authoritative result and
physical browser adoption/settlement path. One-primary
assignment, current helper eligibility and
Organization policy apply at incorporation.

The six independently required lifecycle capabilities
are *Claim, Unclaim, Mark on the way, Complete, Cancel
and Reassign*. Reassign is not ordinary self-Claim:
an authorized manager must choose an actual distinct
eligible target helper, and the guarded transaction
must preserve primary-assignment history and current
authority. Create, authentication, Refresh, search/
options, details/continuity, response handling and
fault recovery have their own positive product gates.
Conditional ineligibility is legitimate, but a
permanently disabled control or unimplemented handler
cannot satisfy a required reachable positive case.

The Response interaction remains an independently
owned, *unselected* HumanHelp product contract at
[[#decision-humanhelp-response-flow]]. The framework
must not invent a default Response workflow just to
turn a progress report green. A selected design will
specify its actor, lifecycle relation, command/response
semantics, rendering, disclosure, completion and
positive/adverse tests. Until that choice is made
and qualified, the full operational HumanHelp
completion claim stays open, even if an independent
narrow Claim assurance pilot succeeds.

*** Use the adopted board cohort and selected user policy

Creator-local Create success may show the creator's
new authorized Request promptly under the declared
scoped exception, even when it falls outside the
currently applied board filter; its membership and
projection effect must be explicitly defined rather
than changing a global query invisibly. The same
exception does not grant acquisition of unrelated
remote content or erase pending advisory debt.

For any other actor's remote Create *or lifecycle
change*, including changes to an already-visible
Request, the ordinary selected HumanHelp policy
remains *advisory until explicit Refresh*. The
advisory may expose only the permitted pending
indicator/status, not protected changed Request
contents or automatic collection membership. A
user-created grant permits one scoped board
acquisition under the current principal, Location/
Organization and applied-query context. Its
authorized observation must establish the covered
cohort, relevant progression and physically complete
adoption before discharging debt. A new notice during
Refresh may be covered by that same justified result,
but cannot create an ungranted successor request.
User-selected reauthorization, rejected/unknown
own-command affected-card recovery and trusted loss
of disclosure rights are distinct explicitly scoped
paths. Reconnect, plan change, delivery success or
server push alone does not grant remote adoption.

Search, ordering and presentation options operate on
the *already adopted, currently permitted cohort*.
They may support newest/oldest, mine-first,
unclaimed-first and terminal visibility without
a covert read of newer remote membership. Disclosed
title/details/location and permitted search labels
form the search surface; undisclosed personal data
cannot become a side-channel through search matching.
The JVM/CLJS normalization, option semantics and
current viewer projection must be compatible under
their declared profiles. A locally filtered or hidden
row is not an authoritative absence.

Details, active selection, focus, editing drafts and
scroll continuity are compatible browser-local state,
not durable domain facts or a license to restore
obsolete provisional DOM. A stale Claim control can
remain visible under remote-advisory policy, but a
click must still face current Request and Membership
guards; the resulting rejected or uncertain command
has an honest affected-card recovery path without
automatically importing unrelated collection rows.

*** Prove full product behavior at actual enforcing boundaries

Each of the **fourteen independent Part VIII completion
gates** must have its own original requirement,
meaningful eligible positive, applicable rejection/
concurrency/fault cases, actual observed result
and declared source, build, host, backend, browser,
actor/scope and evidence provenance. They cover
production model authority, one admitted application
source, installed host/writers, actual client assets,
real Claim, all six lifecycle actions, rich-board
behavior, multi-client selective adoption, explicit
Refresh, fault/recovery, real runtime enforcement,
semantic/assurance evidence, physical substrate
qualification and independent real-browser acceptance.
A green browser fixture, passed model check or
deployed handler by itself cannot substitute for
another gate.

Acceptance uses actual Chromium/Playwright sessions
and rendered controls, not invented transport fields
injected by a test; real current production models
and backend truth, not parallel sample rules;
persisted readback after reload, not only optimistic
DOM; multiple genuinely distinct users and
current Organization/Membership policy; and
deterministic contention/failure fixtures with
precisely attributed outcomes. Negative tests
must fail for the intended reason and unexpected
console/page/request errors must still fail the
test. An HTTP 200, disabled button, uninstalled
browser artifact, fabricated stored state or
unimplemented Response cannot count as an
eligible successful product capability.

Deliberate adverse scenarios include competing
Claim and Reassign, revoked Membership between
read and commit, lost C42 result then later
lifecycle change, malformed route/manifest,
Create during another client's pending remote
debt, one-use Refresh with a later advisory,
lost SSE/registration fence, incompatible
old assets, OOB partial installation, unknown
outcome, failed continuity, changed reader
permission and unauthorized disclosure.
A dropped advisory must have an independently
permitted current-state acquisition path:
reconnect alone is neither the only trigger
nor a user grant. The result distinguishes
actual domain truth, authorized observation,
installed presentation and unresolved command
attribution.

The genuine product can finish its operational
milestone while independently stronger
compositional, external-formal or multi-node
milestones remain open if they were not
required by its selected release intent.
Conversely, no degree of formal Claim analysis
can declare the unfinished product complete.
Completion requires all original Part VIII
requirements actually discharged, with
remaining conditional or unqualified physical
claims reported exactly and never hidden by
a narrower generated inventory.
*** Stage 13 -- Source-derived certification and the real Claim pilot

Compose the admitted public model semantics, typed rules, guarded operations,
global Choreo, role projections, executable plans and whole-application
construction into the *source-derived* proof and evidence architecture of
Part IX. The checked hierarchy is an interface and dependency relation,
not a demand that every namespace implement a nominal certificate class
or that a printable graph, source digest or successful test report become
a certificate. Its reference subject is the actual original application
source and selected claim, not the conveniently checkable subset the
proof generator happened to construct.

*** Compose declared guarantees through an independently required closure

The original source and requested assurance profile determine the
required guarantees, source/semantic interpretations, declared operation
and invariant catalog, dependencies, current issuer qualifications and
independently required product capabilities. For each supported
schema/domain/relationship/rule/operation/Choreo/projection/plan/application
interface, record the exact exported proposition and subject, premises
*used* to justify it, versioned interpretation, producer and consumer,
source dependency, and any implementation/physical reliance.

Deliver:

- original-source acquisition and a coherent immutable construction
  generation, with source, normalized semantic, issued implementation,
  generated artifact, installed host and live resource identities kept
  separate under checked compatibility when they change;
- generated required-obligation and dependency manifests, independently
  checked against original declarations and selected profile rather
  than accepted merely because a caller-provided DAG is acyclic;
- a small proof kernel for its exact inference rules and separate
  guarded-transition, finite-checking and conditional-induction
  mechanisms for their *different* propositions, with proof-producing
  elaboration always submitting candidate work to the appropriate
  independent checker;
- precise typed substitution across exported guarantee interfaces,
  retaining subject, nominal types, actor/Request scope, observation
  basis, assumption origin and checked semantic equivalence or
  direction-sensitive compatibility;
- claim-specific used-premise propagation and genuine discharge by
  independently checked evidence of the *same* proposition in a
  compatible source, temporal, authority and implementation context;
- closed source-relative proof and dependency admission, in-process
  checked issuance where supported, exact current consumer rechecks,
  and safe inert durable packages which undergo new trusted
  validation/issuance on import;
- controlled reuse of still-valid abstract results with invalidation
  of every dependent semantic/implementation/physical obligation
  affected by changed source, provider, callback, writer, host or
  artifact, without requiring unrelated proofs to be discarded;
- a readable source-derived root proof/assurance ledger distinguishing
  checked facts, conditional theorems, admitted premises, separately
  observed behavior, physical installed qualifications, missing,
  unsupported and inconclusive required checks;
- source-complete positive and adversarial admission oracles, and
  three separately reported results for the actual HumanHelp Claim
  pilot defined at [[#req-humanhelp-certification-pilot]].

The source-derived *proof* graph and independently verified
*required* dependency manifest must agree; their equality cannot
be established by letting the prover write both inputs.
A missing Unclaim, Reassign or guarded writer invalidates a
whole-catalog Claim invariant argument even if a smaller graph
is internally closed. Such a smaller abstract proof remains
honest only when its *reduced subject* is named and the
stronger original application claim is left open.

*** Propagate conditional evidence without laundering assumptions

A derivation of proposition P conditional on Q may be accepted
as a conditional result with exactly the premises used for P.
An assertion with the same name as Q, another actor's verified
Membership, a previous read basis, a copied =:passed= report
or a structurally valid certificate does not discharge Q.
Discharge requires a checked matching proposition with
compatible source/subject, authority, temporal, model and
provider scope; its own premises remain transitive obligations.
Circular proofs, mismatched versions and unestablished current
runtime facts do not become unconditional results by
composing two green-looking nodes.

For conditional induction, the original catalog specifies
a shared initial condition, all required invariants and
every admitted operation. Each invariant has an initial
case and a preservation obligation under the *combined*
invariant hypothesis for every relevant operation. Coverage
of actual initializers, external writers, real cross-model
interference, physical transaction semantics and independent
checker soundness is a further claim or named premise.
A vacuous initial condition, disabled Claim or reject-all
catalog may pass a narrow mathematical implication while
failing a demanded *usable nonvacuous* application proof.
A finite model check may close its exact finite state
space without proving an unbounded Clojure/XTDB program.

A source-qualified certificate or issued callable is
not an installed executable, signed portable permission,
issuer-independent theorem, transaction authorization or
real-browser result. A durable package is untrusted data
until admitted under its current source/profile and
issuer context. The proof/evidence sidecar remains
runtime-nonsemantic. A failed optional post-write
observer must not retroactively reject a potentially
committed command; a selected mandatory gate must
prevent the prohibited effect at the real first enforcing
boundary.

*** Certify the actual HumanHelp Claim subject in three dimensions

The pilot uses production public =User=, =Membership=,
=Organization=, =Location=, =Request= and
=RequestAssignment= semantics *where they actually matter*.
It does not invent a =:request/helper-id= field, collapse
assignment history into a scalar status, manufacture a
Claim-only model or write duplicate proof-specific business
rules. At most one active primary assignment, current
actor/Organization eligibility, changed request status,
command binding and historical result, source-owned
publication intent, supported transaction frame and
physical writer coverage are distinct obligations.
The invariant/catalog checks include Reassign,
Unclaim and all other operations that can affect
the protected aggregate, or retain exact gaps.

The independently evaluated pilot outcomes are:

1. *Semantic checking:* the original public model,
   rule/operation/Choreo/projection/plan contracts and
   selected source-complete abstract proof judgments
   are accepted with their exact premises and limits.
2. *Production binding:* the issued operation, actual
   installed Ring/Biff route, protected XTDB effect,
   authoritative command outcome, build/served/loaded
   browser artifact, current principal and qualified
   scope correspond to that source under independently
   recorded physical or open-premise evidence.
3. *Real product behavior:* a genuinely enabled
   browser Claim control sends the bound command,
   the real current multi-record model authoritatively
   incorporates or rejects it, and the permitted
   client settles/adopts from qualified evidence,
   surviving reload and paired concurrency/recovery
   scenarios within the selected environment.

A typed scalar Request update cannot substitute for
the assignment/relationship/actor proof. A complete
abstract Claim theorem cannot attest a deployed
Biff writer, and a valid Chromium UI test cannot
attest that the checker is sound. C42's compatible
historical replay may succeed when a new Claim guard
would fail after the Request became claimed; a
later Reassign/current card does not prove C42's
incorporation. A server response or provisional
DOM badge alone satisfies none of the stronger
physical/accounting claims.

The independent HumanHelp product inventory of
Part VIII still requires all six lifecycle
operations, actual manager-target Reassign,
Create, scoped creator visibility, selected
Response interaction, adopted-cohort controls,
remote advisory/one-use Refresh and fourteen
independent real product gates. A completed
narrow Claim assurance pilot does not remove a
missing product capability; an unfinished Response
choice stays owned by the product and blocks its
affected full operational completion claim.

Acceptance rejects omitted source dependencies,
missing operation cases, an invalid premise
substitution, forged issued handle, stale cached
proof, changed abstract or physical interface,
replaced executor, unsupported provider,
unqualified external writer or substituted
browser asset even if a root report still says
successful. It also requires a real eligible
Claim and appropriate legal variants to pass.
A green report based on no enabled commands
cannot satisfy this pilot.

*** Stage 14 -- Systematic mutation and generic boundary coverage

Turn the paired eligible/adverse cases already
required at each semantic, application and
physical boundary into a reproducible,
independently observable mutation corpus under
[[#req-certification-mutation-corpus]].
The intent is to show *where* a forbidden source
or effect is refused, with what specific
disposition, and whether the relevant
physical effect was prevented, rather than
merely obtaining a high mutant-kill percentage.
The corpus does not create a second policy
database or prove correctness of arbitrary
Clojure code by passing a fixed suite.

*** Make each mutant an exact predeclared claim

Before running a mutant, record its original
valid baseline, profile, subject, source and
generation, changed assumption or declaration,
injection point, expected first legitimately
enforcing boundary, exact result/error class,
effect or admitted artifact that must not
occur, observation mechanism, and an
independent valid positive control.

The injection point distinguishes:

- original unadmitted model/rule/operation
  source or proof-elaborator candidate;
- checked-dependency or imported package
  input, including a coherent-but-stale
  source and semantically changed interface;
- application declaration, route, plan,
  protocol and rendered-affordance source;
- exact generated/served artifact,
  installed handler, writer, browser effect
  or resource-generation boundary;
- external fault window, concurrent
  transaction, transport drop, provider
  version, router interest gap, expired
  principal or postcommit delivery failure.

A case rejected at a certificate checksum
boundary does not establish that an
unreached model authorization or XTDB
atomicity boundary was tested. Likewise,
a source/type failure should not be
reported as a browser robustness success.
The verdict is tied to the **actual first
responsible boundary** and the independently
observed prohibited effect, not a generic
downstream =:missing-plan= cascade or the
