mutant's own claimed =:effect-observed?= flag.

*** Cover the language, joins and physical fault cuts

Include at least these independently scoped
families, extending them as new supported
features acquire checking rules:

- schema/nominal type, enum, variant,
  optionality and absence-versus-nil;
- rule arity, reader declaration,
  short-circuit path refinement,
  unsupported primitive and evaluation
  or representation mismatch;
- public model authorization, business
  guard, relationship cardinality,
  RequestAssignment uniqueness and
  protected disclosure;
- Choreo role-local knowledge,
  provenance, branch discrimination,
  communication causality and
  unpermitted authority assumption;
- global-to-local projection, plan
  compilation, nonsemantic sidecars,
  browser event currentness and
  shared-resource ownership;
- original-source obligation catalog,
  initial-case existence, invariant
  preservation and missing operation
  or required product capability;
- proof-elaboration/derivation error,
  wrong subject, copied certificate,
  reused hash, forged issuer, stale
  dependency and false assumption
  discharge;
- operation/FX input, command binding,
  compatible replay, unknown outcome,
  transaction guard/frame/presence,
  ABA, competing writer and backend
  transaction-internal prestate;
- source-to-executor, admitted route,
  browser asset and actual Biff host/
  physical writer correspondence;
- Live outbox/notice, late interest,
  subscription replay, authorized
  one-use Refresh, real HTMX swap/OOB
  completion, stale/suspended browser
  and delayed physical effects;
- policy completeness and opaque
  source escapes, missing recovery,
  skipped mandatory release gate,
  directional rolling compatibility
  and failed-resource retirement.

Use generated one-step mutations where
their exact semantic effect is well
defined, and hand-authored adversarial
history for concurrent Claim/Reassign,
lost C42 response, a successful commit
with failed publication, changed
Membership, partial OOB installation,
stale writer and lost router registration.
Mutation generation may use source
annotations but must not independently
rewrite the business-rule semantics or
select the expected oracle after seeing
the result.

*** Distinguish correct rejection, intended acceptance and incomplete evidence

The runner preserves at least five
meaningfully different outcomes:

- *Prevented correctly:* the required
  boundary refused the mutant before
  the forbidden construction, write,
  disclosure, browser adoption or
  deployment, and an independent
  qualified observation found no
  prohibited effect within its
  actual scope/window.
- *Accepted by design:* a semantically
  well-formed intentional product-policy
  variation was admitted under the
  selected rules; it must not be
  counted as a missed invalid
  mutation merely because it changed
  previous behavior.
- *Conditionally admitted:* the exact
  selected profile permits specific
  open premises; those remain
  attached to the result and are not
  counted as independently proved.
- *Detected too late or incorrectly:*
  a forbidden physical effect occurred
  before diagnosis, the wrong
  boundary/reason failed, or an
  unrelated exception replaced the
  expected controlled error. This
  fails a prevention claim.
- *Unsupported or incomplete:* the
  required checker lacks support,
  the test did not run or finish,
  resource exhaustion occurred,
  or instrumentation cannot decide
  whether the effect happened.
  It cannot silently raise the
  supported-rejection success rate.

An explicitly expected =:unsupported=
disposition can validate that an
unsupported input is *refused* by its
actual supported gate; it does not
demonstrate correctness of an
unimplemented inference or become a
passed proof obligation. Counterexample
reports, timeouts, missing events,
model-only simulations and absence
of log lines are not independent proof
that a physical mutation was prevented.
An optional post-effect observer may
accurately detect harm, but it cannot
be credited as a before-effect guard.

Keep per-category counts for all required
rule families, originally required
operation/outcome/branch cases,
mutants planned and exercised,
valid and accepted variants,
rejected/conditionally admitted,
unsupported, inconclusive and
physical boundary observations.
A visited state does not establish
that each predicate branch,
reader-path, backend writer or
browser interruption was exercised.
Positive success remains independently
required for each applicable gate;
a fail-everything checker cannot earn
completion by rejecting every mutant.

*** Demonstrate framework-generic reuse, not new special-case products

Small non-HumanHelp example domains
challenge accidental framework
coupling: an approval flow tests
policy change and disclosure; a
reservation or checkout-like
operation tests competing command
identity and unknown incorporation;
an ephemeral presence/typing receipt
tests bounded admitted communication
without pretending a durable
Request-like business fact exists.
These are *contract-driven tests*
through the same Gesso semantics,
not three new production apps,
a mandatory new pub/sub transport
or a replacement architecture.

Actual browser cases use the
selected real HTMX lifecycle and
qualified emitted JavaScript;
backend cases use the actual
supported XTDB/FX submission;
concurrent cases preserve distinct
request/command/execution scopes.
A fault injection must fail for
its predeclared reason without
suppressing unrelated console,
page, request or server failures.
The test's own instrumentation,
eligible control and independent
physical oracle have separate
identity and trust assumptions.

Stage 14's operational mutation
checks start as soon as the first
relevant boundary exists. Later
proof-specific campaigns can
expand this corpus independently.
Full external soundness checking
is not a prerequisite to ordinary
application use, and passing
mutation coverage does not
discharge source completeness,
unbounded formal correctness
or physical correspondence.
*** Stage 15 -- Explainability, counterexamples, and source-level repair

Complete the read-only source-relative explanation contract established
from Stage 1 onward. The explanation is *derived from* the admitted
public semantic subjects, operation and policy inventory, dependency
and obligation ledger, checker judgments, installed-realization
evidence and actually recorded observations. It is not a second
maintained business-rule registry, proof issuer, alternative policy
interpreter or execution gate. The intended reader may be a developer,
auditor, application owner or advisory assistant; none acquires
authority merely by reading or editing the explanation.

*** Explain the first knowable failure and its actual claim

Deliver:

- a compact inspection view of the original model-owned operations,
  actor/target authorization, guarded lifecycle, relationship and
  disclosure policy, role-local knowledge, Choreo branches, protected
  effects, generated plans, routes, artifacts, Live/acquisition debt
  and independently required product capabilities;
- stable operation and source-span references, dependency paths,
  exact claimed proposition and subject, selected assurance profile,
  mandatory judgment, checker/interpretation version, needed
  versus supplied facts and accepted/open premises;
- a primary first *legitimately informed* blocker, with later
  unconstructed dependent objects classified as consequences,
  not competing root causes; independent defects may also be shown
  with their own distinct sources;
- precise categories for syntax or type error, absent/null
  refinement, unavailable knowledge/provenance, current
  authorization/resource loss, proof/derivation error,
  missing required source coverage, stale dependency, actual
  counterexample, unsupported judgment, incomplete checking,
  profile-premise exclusion and advisory business-intent finding;
- evidence origin and disposition: locally checker-verified,
  conditional, exact-finite, source-only, trusted/opaque, caller-
  reported, actually observed physical, unsupported, failed,
  inconclusive or not inspected, without compressing overlapping
  categories into a fictitious percentage of universal correctness;
- the exact *uninspected* Clojure/host predicate and external
  writer domains relevant to a claimed policy, even when the
  checked subset reports zero detected escapes;
- source-linked and privacy-appropriate diagnostic outputs
  that do not disclose another user's protected Request,
  Membership, principal or confidential rule inputs;
- an explicit repair owner and minimal affected dependency
  cone, including changes to source rule, Choreo/knowledge,
  model/FX, provider/handler binding, browser installation,
  physical writer or genuinely approved product requirement.

A valid but product-wrong rule cannot be labeled a mechanical
type error merely because an assistant suspects a missing
Membership guard. Conversely, an observed policy escape in
actual host code cannot be counted as mechanically checked by
placing its name into an audit. An unknown uninspected source
area is *unknown*, not proof that no correctness-relevant
branch, bypassing writer or extra authority condition exists.
The original product capability denominator and current
release gate remain independent of the explanatory inventory.

*** Attribute abstract counterexamples without inventing production events

A model-checker trace must identify the generated formal/model
subject, original semantic source and admitted representation,
selected state/input/operation schedule, exact violated
property, abstraction and finite bounds, checker result and
open environmental assumptions. Reverse links map each
formal transition or assumption to the corresponding source
rule/operation and required *production* enforcement or
correspondence claim. An abstract counterexample falsifies
the claimed property of its declared abstract subject and
premises, not necessarily the running Clojure/XTDB/browser
implementation. A production incident needs its own
authenticated observation and source-to-physical link;
neither a simulated trace nor a copied test-report map
can provide that observation.

The explanation declares whether its trace came from an
illustrative fixture, a genuine generated model backend,
a bounded independent finite oracle, a concrete physical
fault exercise or a separately qualified transfer theorem.
Stage 15 may use a representative fixture to verify the
diagnostic format before Stage 17 has a generated external
backend. A release profile that *claims generated-backend
counterexample translation* must actually execute that
generated path and preserve the witness/derivation
provenance. Do not silently present a fixture as a
Recife, Quint, TLA+ or proof-assistant run.

For example, a conditional Claim model may permit two
active primary RequestAssignments because the original
declared abstract operation catalog omits a relevant
Reassign or repair transition. Explain the exact
original requirement, omitted source edge and checker
assumptions first. Separately ask whether the actual
backend writer inventory is complete, the selected
XTDB transaction guards protect the relationship,
and the installed browser ever observed the state.
A successful abstract correction does not, without
those further checks, prove that a physical race is
prevented.

*** Repair only at the owning source and recheck what changed

Mechanically invalid source may receive a well-scoped
candidate repair; a stale dependency needs source/consumer
reconstruction; a missing external witness needs the
proper test, checker, physical observation or an explicitly
permitted open premise. If an invariant is weakened,
a rule is changed, or a premise is added, that is a
*different claim*, not an invisible repair that preserves
the old proof or product approval. A suggested alternative
in an explicit closed enum may be useful only when it
preserves the actually selected semantic requirement.
Where several valid business policies exist, the product
owner chooses; a diagnostic does not invent a uniquely
correct answer.

Ordinary Clojure remains the authoring surface. A confirmed
new requirement enters its actual public model or declared
operation/invariant/contract through the appropriate
application authority. Gesso then regenerates the semantic
source, dependent formal model, checked proofs, plans,
served assets and affected realization checks according
to their dependency cone. Editing generated TLA+, Quint,
Recife, cached proof objects, emitted JavaScript or
explanatory report content alone is not a repair of
the admitted source or installed application.

Human/LLM review is optional and *advisory only*: it
may flag asymmetry, surprising positive behavior,
missing role/disclosure restrictions or conflicting
product rationale, but cannot issue certificates,
change admissible operations, discharge premises,
relax current authorization or silently modify
a client/server effect. The visible explanation
must remain read-only and redacted at the same
principal/scope boundary as the underlying
protected facts.

Acceptance pairs understandable source-local diagnoses
with ordinary valid source, actual independent
counterexample fixtures and corresponding source
repair/recheck. Challenge a wrong-but-well-typed
policy, misleading secondary error, copied checker
report, source-stale trace, finite/external mismatch,
claimed production incident with no physical witness,
missing opaque-source inspection, unauthorized
diagnostic disclosure and an assistant-produced
unapproved policy change. A generated-backend
claim has the extra positive obligation to exhibit
an actual generated trace and reverse source link.

*** Stage 16 -- Independent formal soundness of the stable kernel

Establish the concrete external soundness target of
[[#req-formal-production-correspondence]] for the closed
seven-rule propositional derivation system. The
independently formalized syntax, inference semantics
and acceptance relation are small enough to isolate
a meaningful proof from arbitrary Clojure, Biff,
XTDB and browser behavior. Their truth is not
supplied by reusing the same Clojure implementation
as both specification and checker. This stage
shrinks a *specified* trusted assumption rather
than declaring the entire Gesso framework proved.

*** Prove the exact initial calculus with open premises

The initial seven inference families remain:

- named premise use with its precise *open*
  source assumption and proposition;
- truth introduction;
- implication reflexivity;
- conjunction introduction, with its supported
  minimum arity and exact source operand order;
- indexed conjunction elimination;
- implication elimination with the admitted
  implication/antecedent reference pattern;
- indexed disjunction introduction.

Formalize finite proposition trees, inert declared
opaque Boolean atoms, nominal subject/context,
well-formed premises, ordered derivation steps,
reference/currentness restrictions and the final
goal. State the satisfaction and entailment
relation over *all* supported Boolean atom
valuations. If Gamma entails P is proved,
Gamma still names the accepted premises; a
premise assumption is not an unconditional
atomic truth axiom. The calculus does not
gain arbitrary embedded Clojure evaluation,
unbounded arithmetic, SMT reasoning,
hypothetical-context discharge, classical
excluded middle or new inference rules
because the formula language contains an
operator with a similar name.

For the selected mathematical rule system,
each admitted inference step must preserve
entailment. Derivation soundness then
follows by induction over any finite
accepted derivation, not from testing
one representative of each rule tag.
Explicitly quantify over permitted
formula shapes, conjunction arities,
reference orders, indexes, source premises
and all Boolean valuations. An independent
proof must state any axioms, trusted
checker/kernel, definition versions and
semantic interpretation assumed.

*** Preserve five separate conclusions and their trust gaps

The external program reports at least
five distinguished objectives:

1. *S0 — Inference-rule soundness:* the
   seven formal rules preserve the defined
   Boolean entailment under their exact
   arity/premise/typing restrictions.
2. *S1 — Derivation-system soundness:* any
   admitted finite proof term derives
   its goal from exactly the legally used
   source premises by a valid ordered
   derivation under the formal acceptance
   relation.
3. *S2 — Actual Clojure checker
   correspondence:* the real source
   parser, validator, normalizer, checker
   and certificate admission accept
   only concrete inputs that correspond
   to S1 under a qualified versioned
   decoding/source-to-formal relation.
4. *S3 — Typed atomic-proposition
   correspondence:* the selected source
   typed-rule evaluations, reader
   footprint, absent/nil/false behavior,
   immutable bindings and failures
   genuinely realize the opaque Boolean
   atoms in the formal system in their
   declared scope.
5. *S4 — Issuer/composition and
   source-to-production transfer:* the
   original application rule and
   obligation ledger, trusted issuer,
   dependencies, admitted operation and
   current installed Clojure/XTDB/HTMX
   execution bear the required checked
   relationships, retaining any
   physical writer, current authority
   and environmental premises.

S0 and S1 may be independently established
before S2–S4. That is a valuable real
theorem but not a theorem that the
production Clojure checker is sound,
that an arbitrary Membership predicate
is true, that the issuer is safe against
hostile JVM code, or that the installed
HumanHelp Claim is correct. A finite
truth table over the actual bounded
set of atoms is separate exact-finite
evidence; it cannot prove the unbounded
all-derivations result or transfer
opaque typed atoms/physical effects.
No single =:proved= field collapses
the five objectives.

*** Bind the theorem to an actually checkable artifact

The proof evidence includes its exact
theorem statement, canonical source
and formal encodings, admitted axioms
or trusted primitives, versioned syntax/
rules/semantics, model and proof-tool
versions, checked proof object or
equivalent reproducible derivation,
actual verification disposition,
resources/bounds, and all open
applicability conditions. Raw
tool exit status, an EDN report,
a digest or a claimed theorem
name without checked content cannot
issue independent proof authority.

A sound checker is not necessarily
complete for all valid derivations
under finite production resource
limits. Its advertised supported
domain, plain-data/metadata and
type decoding, formula depth,
step/premise count, atom encoding,
conclusion identity, normalization
and failure behavior must be
specified and challenged. A
conservative resource-limit rejection
may preserve safety but cannot
be counted as proof of the
rejected statement or as a
successful eligible product case.

An actual proof-assistant/kernel
result, an incomplete proof,
counterexample to an admitted
lemma, unsupported syntax,
tool interruption, timeout and
malformed imported proof are
different evidence outcomes.
If a strict selected profile
requires a currently available
S2/issuer-qualified theorem,
a missing or invalid result
blocks *new* affected admission
without downgrading its profile.
It does not retroactively
change a committed command's
history; a still-current
previously admitted deployment
may continue only within its
own qualification/lifetime.

Independent adversarial checks
include omitted premise, false
truth axiom, changed nominal
atom, reversed implication
references, invalid index,
conjunction arity, cycle,
transformed normalization,
tampered formal artifact,
changed axiom, unsupported
tool result and false S2
checker correspondence. Pair
each with valid proof derivations
and an admitted usable
application operation. The
prohibition is at the actual
mathematical/issuer boundary,
not a copied report's status.

*** Grow formal assurance along real transfer edges

After the small theorem, add
typed-rule and absent/nil
interpretation, guarded atomic
transitions and frames,
conditional induction/source
catalog coverage, role-local
knowledge/projection, partial
progression and browser/XTDB
refinement only through named
formal subjects and independently
qualified transfer premises.
Correctness of S0/S1 does
not automatically establish
soundness of these additional
logics, the runtime framework,
arbitrary host Clojure, real
provider serialization or
all multi-node schedules.

Application developers
continue declaring business
rules, model operations and
Choreo in supported Clojure
interfaces; Gesso owns
generation and checking of
formal representations.
Lean, another proof assistant,
Recife, Quint or TLA+ may
serve a precisely chosen
checking/exploration role;
no one tool and no handwritten
parallel HumanHelp formal
specification is made mandatory.

Operational release,
real-browser product testing
and authoritative transaction
safety remain active while
these theorems are developed.
Completion of Stage 16 is
a specifically evidenced
external soundness result for
its admitted formal subject,
not a blanket “framework
formally verified” status.
*** Stage 17 -- Formal-to-production transfer and release-bound evidence

Connect independently checked formal and source-derived results to the *actual*
production checker, issuer and execution subjects that consume them. The
correspondence direction, observation alphabet, source representation,
selected environment, complete original obligation inventory, remaining
trust and invalidation triggers must be stated for each claim. A genuine
abstract theorem is still valuable when a physical bridge is open; its
production applicability then remains conditional or unestablished rather
than being silently promoted by a successful test or report label.

*** State the direction of each transferred guarantee

The source-owned model, executable Gesso semantics, generated formal
subject, production checker, admitted operation, protected writer and
installed browser are related through explicit *distinct* judgments:

- *Admission soundness:* every admitted concrete source/checker result
  in the claimed supported domain denotes a valid formal judgment
  under the specified translation, decoding, versioned semantics and
  premises. This is a direction from actual accepted inputs to the
  formal relation, not the assertion that all formal judgments are
  implementable or accepted.
- *Admission completeness/usability:* legitimate source cases in the
  separately advertised supported domain have the intended admissible
  path. A conservative checker may preserve soundness while refusing
  valid constructions; that cannot satisfy positive application gates.
- *Execution safety refinement:* every relevant physical execution
  or observed protected effect, under an explicit initial-state and
  step/observation relation and environmental premises, is represented
  by an allowed abstract behavior, possibly with justified stuttering.
  Proving a formal step is allowed is not proof the XTDB/host step
  implements that atomic step.
- *Progress and liveness transfer:* only under explicitly selected
  scheduling, fairness, continuing authority, user action, delivery,
  retention and resource assumptions. Safety simulation alone
  cannot establish convergence, execution completion or message
  receipt.
- *Reverse traceability:* every relevant original formal assumption,
  atomicity claim, source operation, knowledge requirement, provider
  read and environmental premise points to the exact corresponding
  production enforcement/observation duty. This direction of
  explanation is *not* automatically a reverse simulation theorem.

These relations bind the same original source, subject, actor, authority,
version, reader/guard footprint, operation catalog, initial state,
current proof scope and selected physical environment. Distinct
source-derived semantic identity, implementation identity, physical
installation and live execution generations are not interchangeable
because a digest, route label or proposition spelling matches.

*** Carry every formal assumption back to its enforcing boundary

For each transferred proof or model result, derive an exact production
obligation ledger: theorem, formal syntax and axioms, original model
rule/operation/invariant, abstraction map, concrete entry path, guarded
reads/writes, full frame and relationship footprint, decoder/normalizer,
issued executor, authenticated principal and actual installed handler,
provider/transaction contract, browser/Live interpretation and applicable
environmental assumption. Mark each edge as proven, source-checked,
physically observed within a bounded scope, independently qualified
trusted, open, contradicted, unsupported or incomplete as appropriate.
One opened edge does not become discharged merely because its
dependent high-level abstract theorem remains valid.

The first S0/S1 seven-rule formal result does not itself prove S2
actual Clojure checker correspondence, S3 typed-atom/reader meaning,
or S4 issuer and source-to-production transfer. The production
normalizer's acceptance of a changed atom or omitted premise is
a concrete S2 failure even if the abstract rule calculus is sound.
A finite generated-model example or independently implemented
bounded oracle can falsify a claim; it is not a quantified implementation
refinement theorem without a justified abstraction/coverage relation.

A formal atomic Claim must correspond to a selected physically
atomic guarded multi-document Request/RequestAssignment transition,
including current Membership and Organization conditions,
one-primary/cardinality, all relevant writer paths, presence/frame,
historical command result and required publication intent. A
pre-transaction external read does not attest the transaction-internal
prestate, a returned XTDB transaction key does not identify every
internal guard input, and matching readback cannot alone establish
which writer caused the state. If the selected backend cannot
independently expose such a witness, preserve the precise trusted
serialization/refinement premise and test that selected backend and
allowed physical forms rather than claim all XTDB has been proved.

Every original application initializer, bypassing writer, external
provider, direct database client, asynchronous host path, loaded
browser artifact and resource-generation change that matters
to the proof remains an independent coverage or physical
assumption. The original source's operation/invariant and product
denominators are independent of a generated checked subgraph.
A profile demanding proved transfer cannot relabel an opaque
assumption, absent physical observation or unexecuted test
as an admissible theorem. A narrower explicitly selected
conditional operational profile may remain legitimate.

*** Qualify generated evidence, source repair and release use

Generate formal artifacts, checked plans, proof/evidence packages
and explanatory sidecars deterministically from the admitted
original semantics and selected toolchain/versions. The issuer
rechecks the actual current source, complete obligations,
theorem/axiom/derivation evidence and allowed premises; cached
proof-shaped maps and external tool exit codes do not grant
permission by themselves. A changed checker, translator,
provider, route, writer, served JavaScript or installed
generation invalidates the affected *applicability* evidence
without necessarily disproving an unchanged abstract theorem.
Rebuild the smallest sound dependency cone while preserving
mandatory checks and actual physical requalification.

A formal counterexample with an actual generated-backend claim
must come from that generated backend and retain its model,
trace, assumption, abstraction and source-reference provenance.
A fixture or synthetic schedule is useful only under its
accurately declared evidence class. Editing generated TLA+,
Quint, Recife, proof data or code-emission output to avoid
a counterexample cannot repair the original source; an
authorized model/operation/requirement change and its
dependent rechecks are required.

Acceptance pairs eligible current checker admission, a real
permitted authoritative Claim and a correctly bound
physical/browser result with stale theorem, changed
source/normalizer/issuer, forged proof report, omitted
obligation, invalid abstraction, uncovered physical
writer, swapped asset, unsupported transaction guard
and an unavailable mandatory external checker. The
first *actually enforcing* boundary must prevent
the disallowed effect; an after-effect diagnostic
does not establish prevention. Finite conformance
vectors, a successful test suite and source inspection
are separate scoped evidence and cannot replace a
required universal S2/S4 transfer theorem.

Stage 17 strengthens the release machinery already
required by Stages 4, 6, 8, 10 and 11. It does not
introduce source freshness, installed handler safety,
real-browser tests or actual protected authorization
for the first time. Ordinary useful applications may
be accepted under their explicitly narrower profiles
while unproved stronger formal scope remains open.

*** Stage 18 -- Qualified multi-node realization

Realize the *same admitted Gesso semantic machine*
across actual independently failing application
processes, shared authoritative storage, physical
router/dispatcher instances, browsers and compatible
release generations. Single-node and multi-node differ
in *placement and environmental correspondence*,
not in the public model's Claim authority, logical
command identity, Choreo meaning, provisional
browser status, opaque provider progression or
HumanHelp selective adoption policy. The baseline
and separate production milestone are defined by
[[#req-multi-node-realization]] and
[[#milestone-multi-node-production]].

*** Separate actor, command, host and authority identities

An authenticated principal, model actor, Choreo
participant, browser execution, server process,
interest router, database authority, HTTP attempt,
logical command, physical submission and
resource owner are different identities. Moving
a request from host A to C does not transfer
authorization to C as a business rule or mint
a new command. Each new trusted read/write
revalidates the selected principal and
scope at its current boundary; client and
router assertions do not supply Membership.

One logical Claim C42 can be attempted on A,
lose the response after possible submission,
and be resolved or retried through C under
the *same immutable* original command binding
and current authorized disclosure. A process-
local success/abort report at A is not
distributed command history; C must consult
qualified retained authoritative command
records or preserve unknown. A later Request
state and matching card may show current
model truth but cannot attribute C42's
incorporation. A retry under C43 is a new
intent, not historical resolution.

Deliver at least two genuinely independent
application processes under a declared
topology, actual load balancing, controlled
host replacement, a selected qualified shared
authoritative backend, protected writer
and reader coverage, current session routing,
browser assets and directional old/new
protocol compatibility. A two-process
prototype with a shared DB can test meaningful
failure schedules before all other milestones
are complete, but is not thereby a
full production distributed release.

*** Make publication durable without assuming delivery

For a selected strong durability profile,
derive notice intent from source-owned
committed changes and incorporate that
intent, canonical command result and
guarded domain effect in one suitable
authoritative atomic boundary. Production
publication must not depend on the write
host's transient memory or on a complete
snapshot of every browser's current
interest; a missing interest at write time
must not erase required change/recovery
information.

A dispatcher claims durable work through
a declared concurrency/lease/fencing or
equivalent ownership discipline, publishes
with bounded retry/backpressure and records
only acknowledgments whose meaning and
failure boundary have been selected.
A successful broker acceptance, router
forward, connection write and final
browser receipt/adoption are distinct
facts. No per-recipient successful-send
ledger is required merely because notices
can duplicate: the selected scheme may
redeliver a conservative superset after
probable router failure if it preserves
recipient disclosure, idempotency,
bounded-resource and recovery premises.
A guessed failure window alone is not
a durability or eventual-delivery proof.

Publishers may crash between commit and
dispatch, after dispatch before accounting,
and during router handoff. Duplicate
invalidations must never incorporate
duplicate domain operations or silently
consume a fresh one-use user Refresh.
Sender completeness, routing filters,
late registration, received progress,
protected acquisition and actual DOM
adoption each have separate proofs,
observations or declared conditional
gaps. Publication after commit may
create outstanding work or advisories,
but cannot retroactively reject the
already incorporated domain transaction.

*** Fence registration, route interested scopes and recover gaps

A distributed router cannot infer that its
interest graph is complete merely because
its own local process knows no subscriber.
A partitioned coarse/fine interest filter,
replicated filter table or hierarchical
routing graph may be used, but the actual
topology must establish where interests
are stored, propagated and fenced,
which router can lose information,
and how replacement/partial propagation
recovers missed changes. A successor
router with a stale filter must not
silently certify that no subscriber
cares about a notice.

An initial authenticated, scoped
authoritative observation and
interest registration require an
appropriate qualified fence, replay,
gap-detection/reacquisition relation
or an explicitly weaker user-recovery
guarantee. The design must cover
the interval when an invalidation
occurs before a web node learns or
shares its new interest. An outbox
alone does not solve that gap:
persistence of a change is not proof
of the receiver's eventual interest
or ability to reconstruct its
advisory requirement. A lost notice,
router crash or failover must not
make the next authorized acquisition
path depend on receipt of that very
notice.

Safe duplicate forwarding may be
an intentional optimization. Its
semantics are advisory only,
subject to current recipient scope,
authorization/disclosure, honest
provider progression and declared
work/memory/connection bounds.
Neither a coarse “maybe interested”
match nor the highest numeric
token authorizes private detail
or grants an automatic board read.

*** Preserve selective acquisition and convergence across hosts

For HumanHelp, remote Create and
remote lifecycle changes remain
advisory to Bob on any host.
A permitted one-use explicit Refresh
authorizes one scoped board acquisition;
a second notice during the cycle
cannot create another user grant.
A qualified newer result may cover
earlier debt when the trusted
provider proves its exact scope
and progression. An incomparable
basis, missing Request, partial
OOB installation or failed
disclosure check retains its
corresponding debt or blocks
adoption. Authorized initial
acquisition and an explicit
Refresh path remain usable
when a notice was never received.

Creator-local and narrowly scoped
own-command settlement/recovery
are separately admitted exceptions,
not automatic remote board updates.
A later node cannot use a
background SSE delivery to grant
browser adoption, force
independent user action, disclose
currently revoked Membership
or resurrect an old execution's
one-shot writer/DOM capability.

The strong convergence property
must quantify the relevant
current authorized scope, retained
records, registration/replay,
provider progression, actual
read availability, continued
principal rights, fair scheduling,
bounded recovery resources and
*user action when the product
deliberately requires it*.
If Bob never chooses Refresh,
the selected policy cannot
promise automatic visible
convergence. It can promise
bounded advisory or independently
available authorized acquisition
under its actual stated
environmental premises.

*** Test physical faults, realistic workloads and honest proof scope

The production milestone requires
a measured fault envelope and
actual multi-process, multi-client,
authoritative-backend, browser
and resource observations:

- host A dies before submission,
  after possible C42 commit and
  before HTTP result; C attempts
  exact authorized resolution;
- commit and outbox succeed,
  publisher dies before notice,
  then replacement dispatcher
  drains/replays under the
  selected acknowledgment model;
- notice forwards twice or to a
  stale coarse filter; the
  recipient neither leaks
  protected data nor duplicates
  a user grant or command;
- B registers interest between
  source change and router
  propagation; fence/replay/gap
  recovery prevents silent
  false freshness;
- two routers fail or transfer
  ownership with incomplete
  interest knowledge, while
  eligible independent
  acquisition still works;
- Bob reconnects through C
  with appropriate principal
  binding, old/new client
  protocol and non-adoption
  until his permitted Refresh;
- provider basis comparison
  fails or is incomparable;
  the system retains unresolved
  debt, never invents order;
- Membership is revoked
  during fault recovery;
  protected reads/old command
  results remain gated by
  current disclosure rights;
- delayed and duplicated
  physical effects from an
  obsolete node/client fail
  at their actual fencing
  and resource-owner boundary;
- unrelated routers, ordinary
  traffic, long-lived SSE
  subscriptions and repeated
  failures stay within the
  selected memory, queue,
  connection, replay and
  latency envelope.

Non-HumanHelp examples should
use the same distributed
semantics, not a new service-
specific invalidation engine.
A Clojure implementation
first and a later Rust
router are permissible
engineering choices, not
two frameworks or a
different semantic contract.
Direct participant messaging,
durable suspended
workflows and a universal
distributed fabric remain
separate optional
capabilities, not
prerequisites for ordinary
authoritative rendezvous.

Real fault tests and finite
model exploration can expose
bad schedules and provide
bounded production evidence;
a universal distributed
safety/refinement or liveness
theorem needs its own formal
subject and justified
environmental transfer.
Multi-node production
completion is distinct
from operational
HumanHelp, compositional
certification and external
kernel verification.
The accepted release must
state exactly which
processes, clients,
routers, backend,
assets, workloads and
failure windows were
physically qualified,
which premises remain
open, and where the
stronger requested
completion is not met.
** Dependency structure and delivery checkpoints

The eighteen stages provide *contract navigation and normal delivery priority*,
not a strict serial project plan, implementation-progress percentage or evidence
that every earlier stage has passed all of its strongest exit gates. One admitted
application can be built and evaluated in an explicit supported scope while
larger proof, product or multi-node work proceeds separately. Every result must
retain the original subject, the selected claim, actual positive behavior,
missing mandatory duties and exact evidentiary strength. Part XI independently
owns release and completion decisions; this section only maps their inputs.

*** Classify dependency edges before using the stage table

The roadmap distinguishes five different relationships:

- *Semantic prerequisite:* a consumer cannot legitimately interpret or use a
  subject without the earlier exact semantic contract and required facts.
- *Implementation priority:* completing this construction first usually
  reduces rework, although independent exploration may begin sooner.
- *Exploratory feedback:* bounded prototype or finite/model/browser test
  may reveal a missing source contract; its result does not gain the stronger
  qualification of a finished downstream system.
- *Optional early hardening:* cheap identity, proof, instrumentation, mutation,
  lifecycle or release safety mechanisms may close an immediate real defect.
  Their early presence does not certify all later stage responsibilities.
- *Completion dependency:* the requested *named* milestone/release profile
  cannot pass until every independently required gate has actual applicable
  evidence or an explicitly allowed and declared premise.

A dependency in a checker source, proof DAG, generated route registry or
document stage list is not automatically evidence that the *original*
required capability, writer, initializer, policy predicate or physical path
inventory is complete. Independently establish the relevant denominator
before declaring source-closed coverage. The checked subset and complete
requested application/product must remain distinguishable.

The delivery priority is: establish original public semantics, typed rules
and actual Biff/XTDB host; make one real, permitted Claim work through
admitted operation, Choreo, browser, guarded transaction and scoped
recovery; close the same application's source/physical path; expand the
real HumanHelp product and generic adverse coverage; compose proof
claims and independent mathematical obligations; then qualify
production-formal transfer and actual multi-host fault envelope.
A small external proof, two-host experiment, or source-derived
diagnostic can start as soon as its real prerequisites exist.
No advanced proof fixture repairs a missing enabled browser Claim
or bypassed writer, and no working Claim excuses an unproved
mandatory source/correspondence obligation.

*** Principal contract graph for the eighteen stages

The table names the *minimum construction contract normally consumed*,
not full completion of every predecessor. “Selected slice” means the
specific admitted source/implementation profile named in the claim.
The full original milestone still needs all applicable stronger gates.

| Stage | Principal contract inputs | Scope of this edge |
|-------+---------------------------+--------------------|
| 1 | Original public model and independent requirement owner | Define source semantics, stable subjects, policy/actor identities and obligation inventory; do not self-approve adequacy |
| 2 | 1 | Closed/versioned rule judgments and explicit opaque Clojure assumptions; intrinsic typing is not authority |
| 3 | 1, selected 2 | Propositional and guarded/induction proof mechanisms only for requested claims; external soundness and physical realization are separate |
| 4 | 1 and selected host/provider interfaces | Actual Biff/FX/XTDB and browser invocation/lifecycle semantics; first runnable scope already needs its physical safety seam |
| 5 | 1, relevant 2, 4 | Source-owned operation/command and current trusted guarded effect contract; later actual writer qualification is not inferred |
| 6 | 4, 5 | Exact supported transaction/writer/reader realization and its assumptions; full external-writer closure may remain open |
| 7 | 1, relevant 2, 5 | Global Choreo, role-local knowledge, justified projection and canonical plan; no replicated domain-policy owner |
| 8 | 4, 7 | Pure adapter and qualified physical browser effects/HTMX; last-effect permission and retirement apply from first use |
| 9 | 5, 6 for publication; 8 additionally for browser acquisition/adoption | Durable notice, opaque progression, interest/replay, permission and installation each have distinct evidence |
| 10 | Selected 4–9 plus original 1 and applicable 2–3 | One admitted, actually installed application scope with source, route, asset, handler and effect coverage; strict proof only when requested |
| 11 | Selected 10 and exact release/profile/host intent | Four current release decisions and directional compatibility; its safety seams begin earlier than this integration stage |
| 12 | Selected 5–11 and independent Part VIII product inventory | Real HumanHelp all-required-capability and fourteen-gate completion, including separate Response choice |
| 13 | 1–3, 5, 7 and selected 6, 8–10 as Claim realization requires | Actual source-complete compositional Claim pilot: abstract checking, production binding and real-browser acceptance remain separate |
| 14 | Each boundary under test; 3 and 13 for proof-specific cases | Mutations start early with positive control, first enforcing gate and independently observed forbidden effects |
| 15 | 1, 2 and actual currently available boundary evidence | Source-local first-blocker and policy review begin early; generated formal counterexample claims need actual backend provenance |
| 16 | Stable 3 calculus and 2 where typed-atom transfer is claimed | Independent S0/S1 theorem may precede S2–S4 production/issuer transfer; exact scope and axioms required |
| 17 | Relevant 3, 6, 10–11, 13 and 16 under selected formal profile | Distinguish checker admission, source/physical safety simulation, liveness and reverse production obligations |
| 18 | Selected real 4–11 semantics, host/authority and recovery profile | Exploratory multi-host path may precede 12–17 completion; production needs independent Part XI topology/fault gates |

This graph is not a demand to implement every capability of Stage 9 before
*publishing a first durable notice*, or every feature of Stage 8 before
*exploring multi-node command failover*. The publication half consumes
authoritative operation/transaction contracts; physical browser
adoption adds browser rights, user grant and actual installation.
Similarly a conditional seven-rule kernel theorem need not await
production HumanHelp Response, while S4 transfer to its installed
writer cannot be claimed without corresponding physical coverage.

A runnable Claim slice consumes the actual trusted route/FX and
protected transaction path before its first observed user-facing
effect, even if Stage 10's *general* closure and Stage 11's *complete*
release management are unfinished. An early narrow staging instance
needs its own valid installation and enforced safety scope; a
green in-process assembly is never evidence the tested/production
listener used the checked handler. The same distinction applies
to the actual emitted/served/loaded browser artifact, not just
a correctly shaped manifest or generated file name.

*** Avoid apparent construction and evidence cycles

The selected source, checked subject, physical plan, actually
installed executor and observed command are different objects.
Their relationships can be built in increments without allowing
a later report to retroactively manufacture an earlier right:

- A *startup* preflight seam exists before broad whole-app closure;
  its first served profile rejects the known missing inputs and
  unsafe early initializer/handler effects. Full source/writer/
  alternative-route coverage is a separately checked later claim.
- A *source-derived* operation and provisional browser plan may
  exist before all formal proofs; first actual user acceptance still
  requires current model authority, correct physical effects,
  honest error/unknown handling and independent positive evidence.
- An *initial* Live read and registration mechanism precedes
  mature durable routing. Multi-node late-interest fencing,
  publication replay and user-authorized acquisition may be
  explored early, but a prototype cannot claim full availability
  or remote automatic adoption from an advisory.
- A *first* diagnostic/finite counterexample can be checked
  before generated external-formal semantics; an illustrative
  fixture cannot be relabeled an executed generated-backend
  counterexample or a theorem about production.
- Source-proof/issuer admission and physically installed
  realization are linked by selected correspondence relations,
  not by matching digests. An incomplete actual writer inventory
  is an open premise even when the submitted proof DAG is closed.

When downstream exploration exposes a missing rule, actor distinction,
guard/frame, source obligation, dynamic recovery branch, interest
fence or incompatibility, repair the *original owning contract*.
Rebuild only the actually affected semantic, proof, plan, handler,
browser, routing and installation evidence dependency cone;
do not copy new policy into a separate prover, router or browser
machine to evade the source. A genuine unmodified abstract theorem
may be reused while its previous physical applicability becomes stale.

*** Useful integrated checkpoints and honest positive witnesses

A checkpoint names the *first independently useful integrated result*,
its allowed evidence and its still-open stronger obligations. It is
neither a schedule promise nor a permanent success status.

| Checkpoint | Required useful result and first admissible positive | What remains separate or cannot substitute |
|------------+-----------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------|
| Public semantic operation | Real model-owned Claim with actor, Request/RequestAssignment, current guard/effect/command and original capability ledger | No claim that a typed map or one-document example committed an atomic multi-record effect |
| Physically guarded command | Eligible Claim incorporates through selected actual XTDB writer, with competing/unauthorized negative and C42-specific historical unknown/replay | Pinned external read, local receipt or later matching card is not a universal transaction-internal-prestate/causality theorem |
| Actual browser Claim slice | Installed emitted artifact presents enabled control, reaches trusted Biff route, settles/recovers permitted result and survives reload | A browser fixture, HTTP 200 or optimistic card is not persisted authority; Claim is not the complete product |
| Live selected acquisition | Initial authorized board can be acquired; advisory and explicit one-use Refresh are separately exercised with actual scope/installation coverage | Lost notice, late interest, incomplete OOB, remote auto-adoption or missing router gaps remain tracked |
| Closed installed application profile | Original selected source/capability edges, preflight, handler, route, asset, effect and required recovery are qualified for the *actual served* scope | Cannot infer all source policies, external writers or a larger requested product denominator from green assembly |
| Real HumanHelp product | All Part VIII independent capabilities and fourteen positive/adverse product gates, including six lifecycle actions, real Reassign and selected Response | Claim-only pilot, disabled button, synthetic session or general formal theorem cannot replace user acceptance |
| Compositional Claim certificate | Same original model/relationship/operation/Choreo/plan and real pilot bound by accepted source/issuer obligations with exact assumptions | A copyable report, closed caller DAG or narrowed operation catalog cannot assert full source or physical closure |
| Independent kernel theorem | Actual checked S0/S1 theorem for the stable selected calculus with reproducible proof, premises and axioms | Finite truth table, CLI return, S2 production checker and S3/S4 typed/physical correspondence are different subjects |
| Qualified formal transfer | Selected S2–S4 obligations and concrete-to-abstract execution relation are proved or accurately qualified as the named profile demands | Admission theorem alone cannot establish XTDB atomicity, browser execution or unconditional progress |
| Production multi-node | Actual independently failing hosts, original command/history and durable notice recovery, fence/replay, protocol overlap and measured fault/load envelope | Two host labels, shared database alone, guaranteed receipt of every SSE event or user-independent visible convergence |

Each checkpoint has paired eligible/adversarial tests at its *first
legitimately enforcing* boundary. A defect prevented only after an
unauthorized write or browser disclosure cannot count as
before-effect prevention. A reject-everything implementation
does not earn credit for its negative results without a usable
valid operation. A resource, backend or test that has not been
physically exercised remains an explicit limitation, not a
counterfactual pass.

A complete real Claim path includes compatible replay and
=:commit-unknown= after possible transmission, changed current
Membership, genuine competing assignment, and ordinary creator-
local/remote-board distinctions. A new browser execution,
reconnect or host switch does not authorize the old one-shot
effect or erase command-specific resolution. Strong physical
readback, proof, browser installation and model authority
each report their own observations and assumptions.

*** Completion mapping and honest progress reporting

Part XI owns the original *four independent completion milestones*,
their subject-specific qualification and the *four release
decisions* (candidate, installation, activation, completion).
The release decisions do not themselves determine which
milestone has been achieved; stage labels do not establish
either result. The following is a dependency map, not a
second completion policy or an ordered percentage scale.

| Independent milestone | Evidence path required for its chosen profile | Non-substitutable gap |
|-----------------------+-----------------------------------------------+-----------------------|
| [[#milestone-operational-application][Operational application]] | Real installed 1, 2, selected 4–12, plus applicable adverse/runtime evidence from 14–15 and all independent Part VIII gates | Missing Response, real Reassign, protected writer, installed browser, explicit Refresh or eligible user positive |
| [[#milestone-compositional-certification][Compositional certification]] | Selected 1–3 and 13 with original source/operation/invariant coverage, genuine Claim path, current issuer and applicable 14–15 checks | Closed reduced proof DAG, copied certificate, toy Request/assignment or unqualified installed bridge |
| [[#milestone-external-formal-verification][External formal verification]] | 16–17 for *the requested S0–S4 frontier*, actual theorem/tool identity, conditional premises and corresponding source/production use | Finite samples, formal theorem for disconnected model or a claimed S4 without physical transfer |
| [[#milestone-multi-node-production][Production multi-node]] | 18 plus selected 4–11 authority/release and actual topology, failure, recovery, workload, security and browser evidence | Two successful node requests, non-replayable lost advisory, unqualified interest filters or unconditional liveness |

Do not infer that the *operational* milestone has to wait for
every S0–S4 theorem or the final multi-node topology, or that a
small real two-host fault experiment can be counted as the
*production multi-node* milestone. A release explicitly requesting
those stronger claims must meet its independently predeclared
requirements. A claim-specific conditional proof may be genuinely
valuable without satisfying an independent product-completeness
milestone.

For every progress measure, freeze the original required numerator/
denominator subjects *before* checking the currently exposed
application. Report eligible product capabilities, source/assembly
closure, semantic judgments, physical installed-path enforcement,
formal transfer, mutation first-gate quality, fault recovery,
asset/host compatibility and executed tests as distinct dimensions.
Distinguish =:passed=, =:failed=, =:incomplete=, =:unavailable=,
=:unsupported=, =:skipped=, =:stale= and =:missing= at the actual
Part XI gate boundary. Do not infer that uninspected == empty or
that unavailable == inapplicable. A stricter requested profile
may not be silently replaced after a failing check by a new
smaller one.

A checkpoint report binds its source, selected claim, known
environment, admitted model/plan, actual installed host/writer,
served browser artifact, issued/observed evidence and remaining
premises. An original product owner can approve a *new*
requirement subject, with old and new counts preserved; a
generated registry cannot lower the old denominator itself.
A previously valid abstract theorem can survive an unrelated
CSS change while the deployed asset/generation still needs
independent physical compatibility checking. Conversely, a
changed protected writer can invalidate physical applicability
without retroactively disproving the unchanged theorem.

The next useful work item is the missing *highest-consequence
currently required boundary* for the chosen claim, not
automatically the next stage number or the easiest proof/report
to generate. Exploratory discoveries may increase the list
of named open work without reversing genuine completed
applicable evidence. Progress remains net improvement
against the stable obligations, not a forecast based on
revisions, tests or checked-file counts.
** Worked Claim path: one meaning through the stages

Follow *one* HumanHelp Claim source through construction, actual execution,
recovery and increasingly strong evidence. This is an acceptance contract and
illustrative failure history, not a collection of eighteen differently
implemented Claim applications and not an invented Gesso API. R4's sketches
of calls named =admit=, =issue=, =prepare= or =check= were conceptual
checking boundaries, not guarantees that those exact callable functions
exist. The description here names the source, proposition, authority and
physical observation that each real supported implementation must establish.

Assume an authenticated, currently eligible helper *Alice* claims an
existing open Request R from its permitted Organization. The original
authoritative model owns Request, Membership, Organization and the separate
RequestAssignment relationship. The active primary assignment is **not**
a persisted =:request/helper-id= invented for a convenient demonstration.
*Bob* is another authenticated user with a separately authorized board
and the selected remote-advisory-only presentation policy. Alice's
Claim intent is logical command *C42*; it may have multiple actual HTTP/
server/transaction attempts. Its operation, request target, arguments and
original principal binding must remain immutable and compatible through
recovery. The names are narrative identifiers, not prescribed string,
UUID or keyword encodings.

*** One original operation, several identities and evidence subjects

The static public Claim declaration records the original subject,
canonical arguments, business policy/guards, expected input readers,
protected relationships, guarded effects, results, permitted disclosure
and recovery. It has **no particular actor, command ID, execution ID,
transport attempt, source read basis or browser resource** yet.
Its generated Choreo and view attach an affordance to this same model
operation without becoming a second implementation of Claim.

The following coordinates remain distinct throughout the trace:

| Coordinate | What it identifies | What it cannot grant or prove |
|------------+--------------------+------------------------------|
| Public =:request/claim= operation and model source | Original business transition, authoritatively owned policy and versioned dependencies | Alice's current Membership or one transaction's outcome |
| Request R and RequestAssignment aggregate | Target and protected one-primary/relationship history | That C42 was incorporated merely because R is now claimed |
| Authenticated Alice and target Organization | Actual trusted principal/relationship for one permissible disclosure or effect | Eternal authority after session, Membership or Organization changes |
| Logical C42 and canonical binding | Exactly one intended model command across compatible attempts | Authentication, commit, result disclosure or safe new submission by name alone |
| HTTP request/transport attempt and host A or C | A particular delivery, connection or serving process | Identity of C42, all other attempt results or domain truth |
| Execution and one-shot physical submission | One admitted attempt, actual plan, provider and bounded effect permission | Universal transaction-internal prestate or durable command history from a local receipt |
| Browser plan, target/resource instance and effect generation | Exact installed and currently permitted local behavior | A new command, server authorization or right to mutate a recycled DOM target |
| Assembly, browser artifact and release generation | Checked source-to-plan/route/build/host interpretation | Actual listener adoption, loaded bytes or old/new compatibility without physical qualification |
| Provider basis/qualified read and original command record | Scoped authoritative observation or C42-specific historical evidence, respectively | An orderable integer frontier or equality of current card and old command outcome |
| Proof, issuer, test and physical observation identities | Evidence of exactly their checked propositions and environments | An arbitrary stronger theorem, deployment credential or product completion |

The browser may transmit C42, a route target and protocol data;
an actor label, client-provided basis, certificate-shaped map or
displayed Claim button is never trusted identity or authority.
Trusted server admission reconstructs the authenticated principal,
the selected original operation, canonical target, clock, required
current model/Graph inputs, permitted disclosure, execution context
and applicable handler/provider profile. Structural admission
still cannot promise that Alice's Membership or R's open status
will remain true at actual incorporation.

*** Stage-by-stage construction remains one trace

The table names the minimum meaningful *same-source*
construction/evidence join. Later stages strengthen the
scope instead of reimplementing the business transition.

| Stage | Same Claim subject and added work | Exact boundary or open premise |
|-------+-----------------------------------+--------------------------------|
| 1 — semantic ownership | Original HumanHelp Request/RequestAssignment model, Alice/R/Organization policy and independently required product duties | Public model owns semantics; original source adequacy and physical realization remain separate |
| 2 — typed rules | Source-derived supported guard/read/nominal/absence interpretation and explicitly opaque Clojure policy dependencies | Correct typing is not current actor authorization; unknown/unsupported expressions are not true |
| 3 — small proof mechanisms | Original Claim abstract guarded transition, initial/invariant obligations and eligible proof candidate | Seven-rule or induction checking is conditional on exact catalog, premises and checker soundness |
| 4 — qualified host | Actual selected Biff/Ring/FX/XTDB invocation, lifecycle, clock/principal and trusted effect context | Startup order, real installed handler, protected writers and unsafe early initializer effects require qualification |
| 5 — authoritative operation | Static Claim, immutable C42 binding, resolve-before-new-incorporation and current business guard/effect specification | Server pre-read does not prove transaction-current Membership, cardinality or old command history |
| 6 — physical mediation | Complete guarded multi-record transaction, command-result and selected durable notice intent through actual writer | Internal prestate, presence/frame, uniqueness, ABA, real contention and all relevant writer paths remain physical duties |
| 7 — global Choreo | Alice/authority roles, required knowledge, authoritative action, causal result/recovery, projected role-local plans | Browser does not know global truth or gain server authority from a role label |
| 8 — browser realization | Pure adapter, generated plan, exact target/effect rights, real HTMX/DOM install and optional optimism | Provisional display, HTTP 200 and before-swap are not authoritative adoption or physical completion |
| 9 — Live/adoption | Source-derived change/debt, selected durable dispatch, qualified read basis and explicit user-granted remote acquisition | Advisory delivery and router interest are neither protected read permission nor Bob's board adoption |
| 10 — application closure | Original source-to-operation/plan/route/model/handler/asset/acquisition graph and first physical preflight | Green assembly is not actual deployment or an independent full product/writer inventory |
| 11 — release | Candidate, installation, activation, compatibility and evidence/currentness of the exact served generation | Old asset, old report or A-to-B compatibility does not automatically cover B-to-A or current effects |
| 12 — HumanHelp product | Actual enabled Claim, all other lifecycle operations, rich board, Response selection, selective Refresh and product gates | A successful Claim slice is not full HumanHelp completion |
| 13 — compositional pilot | Source-complete Claim obligations and three separate semantic, installed and real-browser conclusions | Reduced operation/proof DAG, copied certificate or real card cannot establish omitted obligations |
| 14 — mutation | Positive Claim plus competing, revoked, lost-response, stale-writer, stale-browser and false-evidence mutations | Defect must be refused at first qualified enforcing boundary before forbidden effect, with independent observation |
| 15 — explanation | Source-relative first blocker, open physical premise and actual/illustrative counterexample provenance | An explanation or advisory product-intent suggestion is neither proof issuance nor a policy edit |
| 16 — independent kernel | Formal S0/S1 seven-rule soundness under named axioms, proof tool and assumptions | Does not establish actual JVM checker S2 or typed original model atoms S3 |
| 17 — formal transfer | S2/S3 and S4 issuance/source-to-physical links, concrete-to-abstract execution refinement when selected | A theorem, finite model and matching physical-looking readback are not interchangeable |
| 18 — multi-node | Same C42 and model truth across A/C hosts, retained outbox, interest fencing/failover and Bob's selected one-use Refresh | A host replacement, duplicate advisory or new current card is not command attribution, publication receipt or automatic adoption |

The operation is not “proved” just because a stage's table row
exists. Each strengthening is attributable to an actually executed
checker, approved source, issued handle, qualified external assumption,
installed physical boundary or observed result. Claim completion and
the independently required Part VIII capabilities have different
denominators. In particular, real manager Reassign can later affect
the same aggregate and must appear in a claimed full invariant
operation catalog even if this specific trace follows Alice's self-Claim.
The independently selected Response interaction at
[[#decision-humanhelp-response-flow]] remains an open product
requirement until the owning application makes and qualifies it.

*** Trusted incorporation: one command, complete guards and writes

A genuinely eligible positive path needs a rendered and enabled Claim
control bound to the admitted semantic operation and installed plan;
the generated browser sends C42 to the actual effective route.
The serving handler qualifies its original model/FX inputs and
authenticated Alice, binds R's target independently of client
role claims and checks a compatible historical command record
*before* treating C42 as a new incorporation attempt.

For a genuinely new C42, the actual atomic guard protects R's
open/eligible status, current Alice Membership/Organization
association, absence or permitted history/cardinality of active
primary RequestAssignment, the correct immutable command
binding/exclusion, and all relevant source-owned policy reads.
A selected strong profile atomically applies the real Request
lifecycle mutation, creates or updates the appropriate **separate**
assignment/history, retains the C42 canonical result and records
required durable publication intent in the same suitable
authoritative boundary. Optional after-commit dispatch is a
separate effect and cannot turn an incorporated Claim into
a rejected command.

The selected XTDB transaction must actually implement the full
guard/effect/frame, including presence and previously unseen
fields, uniqueness, revision or history-sensitive ABA exclusions
when required, and other relevant writers. The actual statement
or immutable lowered transaction, exact provider, authentic
submission and qualified transaction-internal prestate relation
are different pieces of evidence. An external pre-read, a
syntactically valid ASSERT/PUT, a process-local one-shot return
or a matching later Request card does not independently prove
all four. If a required physical witness or all-writer
enforcement is unavailable, record the precise open provider
premise or fail a profile that mandates proof.

A successful incorporation must support an eligible positive
physical readback after appropriate provider progression.
A competing valid helper's attempt, revoked Membership,
association change, same-ID incompatible binding, missing
primary guard, duplicate assignment or stale snapshot must
receive its intended typed rejection/unknown outcome; a
runner that only proves such mutants fail while no real
Claim works has not demonstrated the operation.

*** Failure schedule C42: authoritative truth and actor knowledge diverge

Assume the selected strong profile has an atomic domain/command/
outbox record and the requisite shared authority. The following
is a *prospective controlled execution schedule*, not a report
that the current HumanHelp app or multi-host runtime has run it.

| Step | Physical or user event | Established fact and outstanding obligation |
|------+------------------------+---------------------------------------------|
| 0 | Alice has the permitted R affordance and creates C42 before its first possible send | Original logical intent/binding exists; no commit or enduring actor privilege follows |
| 1 | Host A admits an attempt; C42's new-command guarded transaction actually incorporates | Actual authority now holds the protected result under backend qualification; command/outbox persistence is in the selected atomic profile |
| 2 | A's response is lost after possible physical submission | Alice's client may be =:commit-unknown=, regardless of the already committed backend fact |
| 3 | A dies before dispatching the durable notice and her old browser plan/resource retires | C42 and publication debt survive independently; obsolete effect/DOM rights do not |
| 4 | Host C receives a permitted recovery/resolution for *the same bound C42* | Current authenticated disclosure and canonical historical record determine =:already-incorporated= or permitted result; never a second Claim |
| 5 | Replacement dispatcher claims/retries original notice intent; a router redelivers an advisory | Duplicate Live signals are idempotent and do not duplicate domain writes or user grants |
| 6 | Bob's router learns or restores his scoped interest; he may receive the advisory late, twice, or not at all | A fence, replay, gap/reacquisition or named weaker contract owns lost-interest recovery; notice is not an authoritative board read |
| 7 | Bob is shown an allowed pending indicator and explicitly selects Refresh | One scoped acquisition grant exists under Bob's currently permitted principal and applied board query |
| 8 | An authorized provider read returns a qualified basis/coverage result and the actual browser finishes all required HTMX/OOB installation | Only this actually covered and installed authorized cohort can discharge applicable debt; insufficient/incomparable progression or missing target remains open |
| 9 | A subsequent Reassign/Unclaim occurs or Bob's Membership/visibility changes | Current card/permissions may change, but neither proves nor retroactively cancels C42's original historical incorporation |

At step 4, **successful compatible historical replay is not new
incorporation**. A new Claim guard may now reject because R is
already claimed; the resolver must first check the retained exact
binding and independently authorize disclosure of the old result.
If C42's record is absent, unreadable, expired, not yet visible
at a qualified basis or outside current disclosure, a new current
card cannot manufacture attribution; the status remains unknown
until appropriately established or excluded by the selected
protocol. An attempt on A failing or aborting does not prove
a concurrent attempt on C never incorporated. A different C43
is a different intended command, not a safe replay of C42.

At steps 5–8, Live invalidation is *advisory* for Bob, including
remote lifecycle changes to already-visible cards. An eligible
manual Refresh must remain possible even when the advisory is
lost entirely. The current user grant covers one logical
acquisition, not one new acquisition for each arriving notice
or one per network retry. Provider scope/basis and actual
physical OOB/DOM completion establish which debt it covered.
A newer-looking token or HTTP 200 does not create provider
entailment; an advisory arriving mid-Refresh cannot silently
mint a successor read. Creator-local Create and narrowed
own-command recovery are separately declared exceptions,
not automatic Bob-board replacement.

*** Alternate schedules expose the necessary distinctions

A complete acceptance corpus also includes these nearby cases:

- **No incorporation:** Alice's Membership is revoked, R is
  no longer eligible or another primary Claim wins *at the
  actual guarded transaction*. The corresponding new command
  rejects with the typed actual reason; a rejected fresh
  command is not an inferred outcome for earlier unknown C42.
- **Potential incorporation without available history:** an
  HTTP timeout or host crash leaves command record access
  unavailable. Preserve =:commit-unknown= or the precisely
  permitted unresolved result; do not treat “no record
  seen” as exclusion without a qualified fence.
- **Same command, multiple attempts:** attempt A1 aborts
  under contention while A2 incorporates C42; the
  command outcome is not the Boolean result of A1.
  Incompatible actor, arguments, operation or scope
  reuse under C42 is rejected rather than replayed.
- **Bad browser continuation:** a delayed callback from
  Alice's retired target or an old release tries to
  write a new DOM incarnation; last-effect ownership
  prevents it even if an earlier scheduling check passed.
- **Publication/interest gap:** commit persists, dispatcher
  fails, backup router carries an incomplete coarse filter,
  or Bob registers interest after notice generation.
  The admitted recovery path must not certify false
  freshness from silence, nor disclose protected
  details to a merely *possibly* interested recipient.
- **Proof and installation substitutions:** a conditional
  abstract Claim theorem is supplied with an omitted
  Reassign operation; a checked artifact receipt is
  offered for bytes another host served; or a valid
  local wrapper is bypassed by deployed routing.
  Each requires source/inventory or actual physical
  rejection before claiming full certification.

The test oracle records its *original requirement*, injected
change, eligible positive, first legitimate rejection point,
actual observed forbidden physical effects and applicable
limitations. Seeing a failure afterward or reading a
copied report is not the same as prevention or independent
physical conformance.

*** Certification uses the *same* source, not a proof-only Claim

The source-owned Claim policy, original complete relevant
operation and invariant catalog, supported closed typed rules,
guarded relation, Choreo, projected plan and application
assembly are the source subjects of Part IX's
[[#req-humanhelp-certification-pilot]]. The proof checker
and dependency issuer establish only their own propositions
and exact open premises; source dependency completeness
cannot be inferred from an applicant-provided DAG.
The original model still owns opaque Organization policy
and real multi-record RequestAssignment meaning.

The pilot keeps **three distinct outcomes**:

1. Semantic source checking and conditional abstract proof:
   verified derivations/finite assertions over the selected
   original operation catalog, with correct nonvacuous
   initial/Claim examples, declared premises and bounds.
2. Production binding: current issued operation and
   active trusted Biff/Ring route, guarded XTDB writer,
   authenticated principal, command result, selected
   outbox/Live and built/served/loaded browser artifact
   match the admitted source under appropriate independently
   checked or explicitly still-open physical correspondence.
3. Real product behavior: an actual enabled Claim in
   supported Chromium/HTMX, authenticated Request and
   Membership, guarded persistence, reload, permitted
   settlement and controlled failure/recovery occur
   through the real production-backed model/installed UI.

A small propositional kernel proof may establish S0/S1
over its seven inference rules; it neither establishes S2
actual Clojure checker correspondence, S3 typed policy
atom interpretation, nor S4 source-to-installed physical
transfer. Formal admission soundness and concrete
execution safety simulation are separate propositions.
A changed provider, verifier, compiler, asset or host can
invalidate physical *applicability* while leaving an
unmodified abstract theorem sound. An early finite
example, a successful model-only fixture or a browser
test by itself never closes the missing intermediate edge.

Evidence labels must identify original source, current
subject, checker and actual proof/run status, issuer,
premises, provider/host/asset qualification, observation
window and selected release profile. A copyable
certificate-shaped map, named theorem, fingerprint
or locally matching readback cannot be substituted
for an independently checked issuer or physical fact.
The four release decisions and separate operational,
compositional, external-formal and multi-node *completion*
milestones retain their Part XI definitions; a narrow
Claim proof pilot cannot silently finish the independent
HumanHelp product inventory.

*** Source changes preserve the claim and invalidate its dependents

A legitimate change in HumanHelp's Claim eligibility or
Organization policy is made through its original public
model/requirement owner. The dependent rule, operation,
Choreo knowledge/projection, plan, application closure,
relevant proof and issuance, currently served browser
bytes, runtime guard and selected real-user/fault
evidence must be rechecked when their semantics or
qualified implementation dependencies change.
Unrelated Search evidence and an unaffected abstract
theorem may be reused only after checking their
actual dependency/interpretation scopes.

A new XTDB adapter, added direct writer, Biff handler,
host version, browser build or router topology need not
change the original mathematical Claim meaning, but
does require the relevant physical/writer/asset/fault
requalification. A copied old receipt or cached result
cannot mint a new current release admission. The
corrective action belongs at the first owning source
