or physical boundary, not by teaching the browser,
router or proof generator a second Claim policy.

Across all eighteen stages this is **one continually
strengthened Claim**: the model supplies truth and
policy; Choreo supplies justified interaction and
role knowledge; the browser owns only provisional
and adopted presentation; the physical writer owns
authoritative incorporation; command history owns
C42-specific attribution; Live owns advisory
publication/recovery; checkers own their exact
abstract propositions; release admission owns
current installed applicability. Every stronger
claim needs evidence at its own actual boundary,
and every missing original HumanHelp capability
remains visible outside the successful Claim slice.

** Cross-stage acceptance invariants

Gates A–H apply from the *first boundary at which their subjects are
constructed, interpreted, installed or used*. They are not a final
ceremonial release checklist, nor a fresh, competing policy layer.
The owning Parts and original source define their full semantics.
Each gate names: the original admitted operation or requirement,
the boundary that can first know/enforce it, the permitted positive
behavior, an independently falsifying neighbor, the actual checker
or physical observation, and any residual premise. Completing
a generated graph does not prove that its original obligation
denominator, deployed writer or independent product inventory
was complete.

Gates A–H therefore connect the permanent executable semantic
core to its selected implementation, runtime and evidence
boundaries. Gates I–P additionally govern admission by
representation, product completeness, outcome knowledge,
adoption rights, proof/evidence scope, source audit, formal
transfer and human intent review; the two groups must be
jointly satisfied for a release profile that requires them.

*** Gate A -- No silent semantic downgrade

A public semantic operation retains its original model-owned
command, required inputs, role/authority, typed results, recovery
and effect contract through view construction, Choreo projection,
generated plan, route, browser event and trusted invocation.
A missing or incompatible binding is rejected at the first
knowable boundary or the affordance is explicitly unavailable.
It may not become an unmarked ordinary HTTP/HTMX request,
anonymous route, browser-only imitation or direct backend
mutation simply because the managed metadata is absent.

The source-derived application and generated artifact must
distinguish deliberately ordinary, separately declared HTMX
from a semantic operation whose managed origin was stripped.
A valid ordinary form remains permitted under its own
narrower guarantee, but cannot claim a managed operation's
assurance or authorization. An explicitly unavailable
managed affordance may be structurally sound while still
failing an independent positive product gate requiring
an actual usable Claim/Reassign action.

*Positive/adverse oracle:* a genuine enabled authorized
Claim reaches the matching trusted route and model;
removing its =:choreo/op= or plan/route binding does
not preserve a working anonymous Claim. Check the
actual generated/rendered surface and installed route,
not only a local "unavailable" report.

*** Gate B -- One connected semantic subject

Runtime, tests, source proof/finite-check subjects,
global Choreo, role-local projection, executable plans,
issuer results, generated assets and their actual
installed consumers derive from *one original admitted
semantic meaning*, or have a specifically checked,
direction-sensitive representation/refinement relation.
The subject need not have identical data layouts in
every representation. It must not change business
guards, scope, actors, command identity or allowed
outcomes without preserving a justified relation.

The permanent executable semantic core is not
replaced by a proof kernel or one-off test reference
machine. A seven-rule propositional checker, guarded
transition checker, independent formal backend,
browser adapter and physical XTDB writer own
different propositions. Nonsemantic sidecars
may explain their source correspondence but
must not change runtime execution or issue
permission. A valid abstract Claim theorem
is useful under its premises without
proving that the deployed handler performs
the same guarded transaction.

*Positive/adverse oracle:* original
Request/RequestAssignment Claim with current
Membership runs through the supported plan;
a proof-only model using invented
=:request/helper-id= or omitting Reassign
is refused as a full-subject correspondence
even if its reduced model checks internally.

*** Gate C -- Source ownership stays single

Public model/core interfaces own Request,
RequestAssignment, Membership, Organization
and other domain business semantics. Choreo
owns participant interaction and justified
knowledge; application construction
joins the public semantics to actual plans,
routes, effects and protected acquisition.
Proof obligations, operation summaries,
policy audit, code generation, diagnostics
and tests derive from the *same* original
declarations rather than maintaining
plausibly synchronized business copies.
The browser and router are not alternative
owners of Claim or remote read permission.

Ordinary application Clojure may express
genuinely complex domain policies. Where
a correctness-relevant host function
cannot be checked in the supported closed
rule language, its original owner supplies
the typed/effect/dependency contract,
selected trusted boundary and an honestly
open conformance premise. An empty
source-audit catalog, a smaller proof DAG
or an opaque implementation body cannot
be relabeled complete mechanical
inspection. HumanHelp-specific rules
may occur in the HumanHelp product model,
not be hard-coded into generic Gesso.

*Positive/adverse oracle:* a changed
Organization Claim policy changes its
source-owned affected judgments and
dependent execution/assurance; a
hand-maintained "helper eligible"
predicate in the browser/prover/router
that disagrees with the model is rejected
or recorded as a source-conformance gap,
not accepted because both names match.

*** Gate D -- Authority remains at the trusted boundary

A browser-supplied role, principal,
request/tenant identifier, plan, certificate,
basis, correlation ID, DOM field or
=already-authorized= flag grants *no*
protected authority. Trusted ingress
binds the authenticated actor and exact
operation/target; a real authoritative
model/read boundary checks current
Organization/Membership, scope,
disclosure and operation policy at its
applicable use. Each protected write
must guard changing conditions at
incorporation, and each protected read,
subscription or historical command
resolution must independently establish
current permitted disclosure.

A source-checked proof is not a runtime
authorization token. A legal HTML
affordance is not protection against
a manually constructed hostile request.
An old accepted membership observation
does not continue authorizing operations
after a relevant revocation. An opaque
provider progression witness may
justify the *scope of an observation*
when its authority was independently
qualified, but cannot manufacture
the actor's right to perform a read
or adopt a remote collection.

*Positive/adverse oracle:* authenticated
eligible Alice Claims R using the
current trusted model; a forged
client helper role or revoked
Membership fails at the protected
model/transaction boundary even
when the previously served UI
still displays Claim. Test
the direct hostile route, not
only the disappearing button.

*** Gate E -- Exact artifact and implementation binding

Where a release or proof claim depends
on exact correspondence, preserve the
subject and immutable interpretation
through source, issued plan/callable,
generated manifest, emitted bytes,
served bytes, actual client-loaded
bootstrap, selected handler, live
provider and installed generation.
A matching title, timestamp, route
name, local receipt, copied hash or
source similarity is not an
authenticated production observation.

A build receipt may bind the approved
manifest to locally emitted JavaScript
bytes; it does not prove a server
served those bytes, a browser loaded
them, or a later substituted Biff
handler used the source-checked route.
Actual installation/activation and
user-facing entrypoint evidence
remain separate. Exact byte identity
and checked semantic compatibility
are different relations; A-to-B
old/new compatibility does not
imply B-to-A. Changed implementation
invalidates affected physical
applicability without necessarily
invalidating an unaffected
mathematical theorem.

*Positive/adverse oracle:* a
qualified browser build loads its
actual current plan and the
server invokes the matching
checked handler; a stale CDN
asset, forged manifest, post-
preflight Ring replacement or
changed XTDB adapter cannot
reuse a green candidate report.

*** Gate F -- Dynamic premises remain dynamic

Static preflight rejects *structurally
known* missing, incompatible or
unsupported realization and requires
the actual declared handling/recovery
path for a relevant dynamic outcome,
as owned by
[[#req-preflight-dynamic-handling-coverage]].
It cannot guarantee future
Membership, Request state, network
delivery, scheduler fairness,
transaction prestate, principal
revocation or resource lifetime.
Declared handling means a real
source-derived continuation with
owner, trigger, required knowledge,
permitted effects and terminal or
explicitly unresolved outcome;
a boolean =:recovery-exists?=
or copied success report is not
structural coverage.

The trusted invocation, guarded
incorporation, live acquisition,
browser last-effect mutation
and historical command resolver
enforce actual current facts at
their respective boundaries.
An aborted HTTP attempt after
possible C42 submission does not
prove C42 rejected; missing
history or unknown outcome must
retain its uncertainty. A
lost Live advisory must not
make manual authorized
acquisition impossible; an
advisory alone grants no
automatic user Refresh.
Safety can hold when optional
liveness/fairness assumptions
do not.

*Positive/adverse oracle:* current
eligible Claim and its admitted
unknown-result resolution work;
a fake recovery branch hides
missing issuer/read authority,
or preflight claims that
the future provider succeeds.
Reject the missing structural
contract early; after an
actual possible submission,
retain precisely scoped
=:commit-unknown= rather than
invented rejection.

*** Gate G -- Real physical integration remains required

Portable semantic/projection checks,
finite exploration, source inspection
and proof checking cannot by themselves
establish actual Ring/Biff handler
adoption, XTDB guarded transaction,
transaction-internal prestate,
complete physical writers, current
principal, real Chromium/HTMX
request/swap/OOB installation or
cross-host fault recovery. A
release or completion claim
records exactly which *physical*
subjects, versions, sessions,
entrypoints, bytes, witnesses
and fault windows were exercised,
with untested or trusted premises
retained.

A required check that is failed,
skipped, missing, stale,
unavailable, unsupported or
incomplete does not pass.
A successful *negative* test
must reach the intended real
enforcing boundary and
independently observe that the
forbidden write/disclosure/DOM
mutation did not occur within
the stated observation scope.
A different earlier exception
or a post-write diagnostic
cannot count as prevention.
Every applicable negative
has a nonvacuous eligible
positive through the
same installed path. If
the requested assurance
requires an independent
external proof rather than
bounded test evidence,
a physical test cannot
substitute for that proof.

*Positive/adverse oracle:* real
authenticated Claim succeeds,
survives reload and is
visible through a permitted
installed browser; competing
physical Claim, missing FX
clock, stale served artifact
and actual OOB partial swap
have distinct appropriately
typed results. A successful
mocked model-only browser
fixture cannot certify the
installed production path.

*** Gate H -- Reject contradictions when they become knowable

A contradiction is refused at
the *first boundary with
sufficient information and
legitimate authority* to
recognize and enforce it.
A malformed typed operation,
unrealizable Choreo knowledge,
missing route/FX capability,
incompatible plan/asset or
required recovery contract
should fail construction or
pre-installation checks,
before the associated
managed effect is exposed.
A malformed rendered
Hiccup/HTMX affordance
fails at the supported
real pre-serialization
boundary; an invalid
invocation fails at
trusted ingress; a stale
or unauthorized guarded
transaction fails before
incorporation; an expired
browser callback fails
before its physical DOM
mutation.

A static checker must not
pretend to know future
permissions, race outcome,
physical network state or
target incarnation. Nor
may a late diagnostic
describe itself as
preventing an already
incorporated command or
previously disclosed
response. A failure
after an authoritative
commit may block HTML
installation, create
publication/recovery debt
or leave client knowledge
unknown, but cannot
retroactively turn the
committed model
transition into rejected
truth. The observed first
blocker must not be a
cascading =:missing-plan=
error when the original
cause was an earlier
invalid rule or lost
permission.

*Positive/adverse oracle:* one
genuine valid Claim reaches
the appropriate physical
model/DOM boundaries;
missing =:biff.fx/now=
is detected before the
required invocation can
issue a protected effect,
revoked Membership is
rejected at current
incorporation, an invalid
render blocks actual
response delivery, and
a retired callback is
stopped at its last
mutating effect.
If the discovered bug is
only detectable after an
effect, report late
detection and surviving
uncertainty rather than
a false prevention claim.

The gates apply to every
supported entrypoint and
effect path within the
selected guarantee. A
narrow declared legacy
HTMX path may remain
valid, but cannot inherit
stronger managed proof,
installation, policy or
runtime claims without
the corresponding checks.
Their report preserves
which original source,
installed generation,
profile, eligible
positive, adverse case,
actual observer and
open obligations justify
each successful gate.
*** Gate I -- Representation does not confer admission

A represented value is not an admitted semantic subject or privileged
capability merely because it has the expected tag, nominal identifier, map
keys, opaque-looking bytes, source digest, certificate-shaped fields or
serialized form. Every elevation of status belongs to the responsible
*actual* boundary: original-source type/semantic checking, trusted
model/principal acquisition, canonical command-history admission,
issuer-controlled proof checking, current resource/effect admission or
qualified physical persistence and installation.

Distinguish at least the following from each other:

- original model rule or operation declaration, checked semantic term,
  generated plan and actually issued executable callback;
- proof candidate/report, source-rechecked in-process proof handle,
  independent checked theorem artifact and transferred production proof;
- browser claim/role/correlation token, currently authenticated actor
  and authoritatively verified permission to invoke or disclose;
- command ID and canonical immutable binding, physical attempt,
  retained original-command result and current authorized resolution;
- proposed basis/progression witness, trusted provider-qualified
  observation and authorized physically adopted fragment;
- local function/plan object, installed host binding and actual
  protected backend or DOM effect.

A versioned decoder may reject malformed input without thereby proving
that all well-shaped data is trusted. A JVM-local checked handle
prevents ordinary copy-and-paste substitution inside its admitted
scope; it is not a hostile-JVM sandbox, transferable capability,
signature or runtime authorization. Importing a durable report or
proof package requires fresh checked source/issuer and applicable
premise admission; one printable field cannot confer a stronger
evidence class. An adversary supplying their own compatible-looking
graph does not establish the required original-source dependency
closure of the intended application.

*Positive/adverse oracle:* an actually issued Claim executor and a
current original-source proof handle are accepted for the exact
supported subjects; a copied EDN certificate/report, forged role,
replayed stale resource generation, mismatched C42 binding or
browser-supplied provider witness cannot cross the corresponding
trusted admission boundary. The eligible positive must remain
usable after rejecting its counterfeit.

*** Gate J -- Capability completeness is independent of closure

The required product and original assurance inventories are
*independent inputs*, not whatever the implementation currently
registers, compiles, projects, tests or proves. A closed Choreo
graph, source-derived report, finite operation catalog or
internally consistent proof DAG can certify its explicitly
smaller declared subject without satisfying the original
stronger application or HumanHelp completion claim.
The generator may not define its own denominator by
discarding difficult capabilities, positive cases,
external writers, invariants or dynamic recovery paths.

For HumanHelp, the independent positive product set
includes Create; Claim, Unclaim, Mark on the way,
Complete, Cancel and manager-target Reassign;
search/order/options/details/continuity on the
authorized adopted cohort; current authentication/
Membership/Organization policy; multi-client
advisory-only remote lifecycle; one-use explicit
Refresh; eligible unknown-command recovery; and
the separately selected Response interaction.
The fourteen independent Part VIII gates also
include real production-model authority,
installed Biff/XTDB/HTMX paths, physical
assets, true browser acceptance and failures.
The Response decision remains product-owned
and *unselected* until its authorized
requirements are chosen and implemented.
A placeholder, deliberately disabled control
or missing registry entry does not count
as a completed positive.

A genuinely narrower selected Claim pilot,
external S0/S1 theorem or bounded prototype
may pass its *named* partial profile; it
must not relabel that profile as complete
HumanHelp, all-writer closure, external
formal transfer or multi-node production.
The original requested release profile
and requirements are fixed before
evaluation. An unsupported or missing
mandatory gate cannot be silently
made inapplicable after it fails.

*Positive/adverse oracle:* all required
original product actions have genuine
eligible paths and their separate negative
cases before a full operational claim
passes; removing Reassign from the
exposed registry and the checker
catalog, or omitting Response and
its positive oracle, does not make
the full requirement set smaller.
A legitimate partial Claim release
must be reported as partial rather
than refused as if no useful
scoped work were possible.

*** Gate K -- Incorporation, delivery, and knowledge stay distinct

The authoritative database's actual
incorporation, a command's durable
historical attribution, an HTTP attempt's
delivery/return, a subscriber's advisory
knowledge, the user's permitted
authoritative read and the browser's
adopted presentation are separate
facts and evidence subjects. A
connection timeout, abort, host loss,
retired execution or absent immediate
response does *not* prove a possibly
submitted command was rejected.
A known committed operation stays
committed after postcommit render,
publication or transport failure.

One logical command C42 retains
its immutable principal/operation/
target/arguments binding across
compatible retries and multiple
physical attempts. The trusted
resolver checks its exact retained
historical result and *current*
permission to disclose that result
before using a fresh operation's
eligibility conditions. A Claim may
be historically incorporated even
when Request R is no longer open
for new Claim. Reusing C42 for
different actors/arguments is a
typed incompatibility; creating
C43 is a different intent, not
automatic safe replay of C42.
Failure of A1 does not exclude
incorporation by concurrent A2.

An authorized read of current R can
repair a stale optimistic card
without proving which previous
logical command produced that state.
A missing, unreadable, expired
or insufficiently progressed
command-result record must not
be replaced by a guess from the
card, request status, basis token
or a timeout. The selected
resolve/retry/fence protocol
preserves =:commit-unknown=
until valid command-specific
evidence establishes a compatible
original outcome or its qualified
exclusion. A local result receipt
cannot authenticate all other hosts'
physical attempts.

*Positive/adverse oracle:* a real
C42 Claim incorporates, loses its
HTTP response and later permits
historical =:already-incorporated=
resolution under current disclosure,
without a duplicate primary
RequestAssignment. A newer
post-Reassign card or A1 abort
does not falsely prove that
C42 succeeded or failed.
A fresh eligible command still
has a valid permitted success.

*** Gate L -- Recovery preserves scope and adoption permission

An advisory is a scoped statement
that a relevant authoritative
observation may need refreshing;
it is not an authority token,
permission to issue a protected
read, permission to replace a
collection or guarantee of
physical installation. Source,
principal, Organization/Location,
actual applied query, fragment,
target/resource owner, provider
basis and required coverage
remain bound through retry,
reconnect, failover and release
retirement. Unrelated changes
and unresolved obligations must
not disappear because one newer
or locally successful result
was installed.

Under the selected HumanHelp remote policy, Bob's other-user Create and
lifecycle changes, including changes to cards he already sees, remain
advisory until he explicitly grants a scoped one-use Refresh. Its default
grant permits **one logical authorized acquisition with one physical read
budget and no automatic successor**. A separate selected recovery policy
may authorize a bounded retry under its actual remaining physical budget,
or a new explicit user Refresh/Retry may issue a new grant; an SSE notice,
failed attempt, queued intent or reconnect cannot authorize another
physical read by itself.

A new notice during the granted acquisition may be covered by the
already authorized observation only when the trusted provider establishes
its progression, scope and coverage and the browser finishes every
required actual HTMX/OOB installation. An insufficient or incomparable
basis, missing target or partial swap retains the uncovered debt; it
cannot create a successor grant or silently widen the original query.

A permitted manual Refresh
and initial acquisition remain
available even when no notice
arrived or no interest was
registered in time. A
subscription reconnect,
routing filter hit, local
Create exception, unrelated
own-command settlement or
new plan generation cannot
implicitly grant Bob remote
collection adoption.
Creator-local accepted
Create and a narrowly
correlated authorized
own-command reread are
separate selected scopes.
Revocation blocks future
protected disclosures and
effects at the current
boundary; already disclosed
offline data cannot be
retroactively erased.

An authoritative absence
requires a qualified *negative*
observation under the correct
query, principal, disclosure
and basis, not simply an
absent DOM node, local filter
or failed network request.

*Positive/adverse oracle:* Bob
can choose one authorized Refresh
without a preceding SSE event,
and the complete installed
result discharges only covered
debt. An O2 advisory arriving
during A1 cannot issue an
ungranted A2; a lost notice,
unmatched OOB target or
recycled DOM resource cannot
authorize remote content or
declare false freshness.

*** Gate M -- Evidence retains its scope through composition

Each assurance conclusion keeps
its original proposition, normalized
semantic subject, actor/operation/
state scope, premises used,
evidence and checker class,
quantification domain, relevant
version/implementation/host
generation and actual observation
window. Source completeness is
checked against the *independently
required* original obligation
manifest, not inferred from the
elaborator's candidate graph.
Copied identity fields, a
replayed successful report or
matching source hash do not
establish that the current
issuer, installed host, physical
writer or browser was admitted.

Maintain distinct strength for:
a propositional derivation,
guarded abstract transition,
conditional induction,
exact finite exhaustion within
its declared state/input domain,
bounded test, externally checked
theorem, source/assembly
preflight, scoped actual
physical observation and
implementation refinement.
A genuine S0/S1 soundness
theorem need not be dismissed
because S2 production checker,
S3 typed atoms or S4
issuer-to-physical transfer
are open; it equally may
not impersonate those
missing claims. Tests that
exercise one physical
schedule do not prove
unbounded scheduling,
transaction-internal
prestate or all-writer
closure. A proven abstract
theorem may survive an
unrelated source change
while old installed
physical evidence becomes
stale.

The four Part XI release
decisions—candidate,
installation, activation,
completion—keep separate
subjects. The four
independent operational,
compositional, external
formal and multi-node
milestones keep separate
denominators. The selected
profile's required results
are recorded using the
complete declared gate
vocabulary: passed, failed,
incomplete, unavailable,
unsupported, skipped,
stale and missing. A
reported =:passed= without
authenticity/applicability
checking is still not
accepted evidence.

*Positive/adverse oracle:* a
qualified unchanged abstract
Claim theorem is reused under
an actual valid dependency
relation, while the changed
XTDB adapter and emitted
browser asset receive new
physical checks. A copied
certificate map, finite
truth-table result,
unexecuted browser test,
narrow proof graph or
receipt from an older host
cannot make a stronger
current release green.

*** Gate N -- Policy visibility has an honest inspection boundary

Correctness-relevant application
semantics are inspectable as
original source-owned public
rules, operations, identities,
actor/relationship/disclosure
constraints, guarded effects,
recovery, lifecycle invariants,
required capability inventory,
dependency graph and explicitly
named opaque or external
conformance premises. The
audit and explanatory report
are *read-only derived views*
of the same construction
and supplied evidence, not
a second business policy
registry, separate runtime
interpreter or new admission
issuer. Real domain
complexity is not a defect;
no arbitrary ratio of
policy lines to total
implementation is an
acceptance criterion.

Inspection states precisely
which Clojure rule bodies,
callbacks, model predicates,
FX, writer paths,
administrative operations,
startup/replacement handlers
and protected acquisition
points were actually
examined. A condition
influencing authorization,
eligibility, disclosure,
command acceptance,
relationship uniqueness
or observable lifecycle
cannot appear mechanically
verified merely because
some other part of the
application graph is
closed. Where Gesso cannot
inspect the relevant host
code, require an original
source-owned typed/effect/
dependency contract and a
named implementation-
conformance premise, or
refuse a stronger selected
profile that requires
its discharge.

A known opaque branch
must be visible at the
first boundary capable
of identifying its influence;
unexamined code is
reported as not inspected,
not as absence of policy.
The original operation
inventory and physical
writer universe remain
independent: no list
of observed Gesso
executors proves that
outside XTDB clients
cannot mutate the same
business state.
A privacy-scoped view
never discloses protected
actor or organization
facts to a reader
unauthorized to see them.

*Positive/adverse oracle:* a
real public model-owned
Membership guard is
listed with its source,
dependencies and qualified
coverage; an arbitrary
Clojure callback with
uninspected extra
authorization is not
reported as fully proved
because the semantic-audit
operation list is empty
or contains no detected
escapes. A valid
complex domain policy
must remain expressible
with honest assumptions.

*** Gate O -- Formal assumptions create production obligations

A formal proof is about its
precise source-derived subject,
definitions, axioms and
premises. Every correctness-
relevant assumption needed
to apply its result creates
an *owned production obligation*,
not merely a diagnostic note.
For a model that treats
Claim as an atomic guarded
action, the selected real
Request/RequestAssignment
writer must implement the
same protected transition
or the correspondence
must retain a named,
unproved physical premise.
Passing model exploration
does not establish that
arbitrary Clojure or XTDB
executes the checked
transition.

The transfer ledger binds
the exact original
initializer/invariants
and complete operation
catalog, declared actor
and current Membership/
Organization policy,
read/guard footprint,
relationship absence or
one-primary cardinality,
multi-document write
footprint and protected
frame (including new
field presence), command
binding/retained outcome,
publication intent,
provider consistency/
progression, model-to-
concrete state relation,
installed handler/executor,
and every relevant
physical writer.
A pinned external read
is not a transaction-
internal prestate witness;
an ASSERT-before-PUT
shape, local submission
receipt, ledger key or
matching later card is
not independently a
universal backend
refinement theorem.
Full-value endpoint
comparison does not
exclude ABA without
a history-sensitive
mechanism when required.

If the formal subject
assumes authentic
communication, fair
delivery, resource
currentness, authorized
observation or eventual
browser convergence,
the actual selected
transport, router,
read permission,
HTMX effect and
user-action policy
carry separate physical/
environmental duties.
HumanHelp's advisory
remote policy cannot
prove unconditional
automatic visible
convergence when Bob
does not grant Refresh.

*Positive/adverse oracle:* a
qualifying actual guarded
multi-record Claim and
relevant external writer
inventory support the
stated concrete-to-
abstract safety relation;
concurrent duplicate
primary assignment,
unprotected newly added
field, missing trusted
Membership, incorrect
XTDB prestate claim or
lost router interest
leaves the exact
assumption open or
fails its requested
physical admission.
An unaffected abstract
theorem remains a valid
theorem under its
original premises,
not proof of the
broken production step.

*** Gate P -- Intent review and repair preserve the evidence boundary

Human, model-assisted or
LLM-assisted intent
review may identify an
internally well-typed
policy as surprising,
asymmetric, under-
constrained, inequitable,
incomplete or inconsistent
with independently
stated product needs.
Such a finding is
*advisory*. It cannot
be promoted into a
proof result, new
runtime authorization,
automatic source
mutation, denied
valid program,
discharged formal
premise or modified
release gate solely
because a reviewer
expressed confidence.

Only the legitimate
product/policy owner
may decide whether a
new requirement changes
business intent. A
confirmed decision
becomes an original
public model rule,
declared invariant,
operation/authorization/
disclosure contract or
explicit requirement.
Gesso then checks
the supported meaning
and regenerates
affected Choreo,
proof obligations,
application plans,
build assets and
current physical
qualification. A
changed assumption,
weakened invariant
or removed capability
is a *new claim* whose
original/revised
denominators and
evidence stay
distinguishable.
A generator or
review report cannot
edit the required
product inventory
until it appears
complete.

A mechanistically invalid
rule, unavailable
knowledge, missing
dynamic recovery, or
unsafe deployed effect
belongs to its first
appropriate typed
semantic, preflight,
trusted model,
issuer or physical
owner. An unprovable
opaque Clojure policy
remains a declared
premise or unsupported
assurance request
until independently
qualified, rather
than silently being
rewritten into a
convenient rule that
can be proved.
Ordinary Clojure
remains the developer
authoring surface;
Gesso owns generation
of formal models,
not a requirement
that HumanHelp
developers handwrite
a second TLA+/Quint/
Recife business model.

*Positive/adverse oracle:* a
product owner approves
a revised current
Membership requirement
at the original model
source, and the affected
proof/plan/physical
evidence is rechecked
without discarding
unaffected sound
results. A reviewer
who merely dislikes a
valid policy cannot
modify it through a
diagnostic report,
weaken the invariant
in generated formal
code, alter a green
status or conceal
the unselected
Response decision.

Together Gates A–P
remain *independently
scoped recurring
checks*, not one
undifferentiated
completion badge.
They reject an
invalid candidate
at its first real
owner, preserve
valid usable
positives and
leave genuinely
unknown, conditional,
uninspected and
unsupported duties
visible. A final
accepted release
must meet its
original selected
profile without
changing its
requirements after
seeing failures.
** Worked stopped candidate: a green-looking release is not admission

This is a *controlled acceptance counterexample* spanning all Gates A–P.
It shows why passing local semantic checks, building JavaScript, and
observing several browser successes cannot make a defective candidate
an admitted production release. The candidate is schematic and
deliberately inconsistent. It is not executable Gesso API, a real
HumanHelp defect report, or evidence that the corresponding checks
have run. The literal names below identify narrative subjects,
not supported constructor functions or wire encodings.

Assume the original approved release intent requests a real
HumanHelp operational application, source-derived compositional
Claim assurance, and a selected external-formal/checker
correspondence profile. The required gates and product capabilities
are fixed *before* candidate generation. Some deliberately
narrower release could be independently requested, but this
candidate cannot change the original intent when its stronger
requirements fail.

The candidate reports success for an abstract Claim derivation,
a compiled browser bundle, an earlier Chromium journey and a
source-derived application graph. Those observations can all
be true within their own scopes while the current candidate
remains inadmissible.

*** The illustrative candidate and its conflicting subjects

The following is *illustrative EDN data only*, not a Gesso
constructor, accepted schema, current API or test result:

#+begin_src clojure

  :bytes-observed :previous-build}

The `:response` entry means only that the *independent*
product requirement is still owed. Its precise Response
interaction semantics remain a HumanHelp product decision
at [[#decision-humanhelp-response-flow]]; this example
does not select a workflow. The synthetic provider list
is likewise an example of required/supplied mismatch,
not a complete real Biff FX contract.

The operation's actual RequestAssignment history,
current Membership, original command record,
transaction write footprint, installation/activation
identity, subscription registration, and trusted
progression are intentionally missing from this
green-looking report. Their absence is *not* proof
that they were safely implemented elsewhere.

*** Classify each defect at its earliest legitimate owner

Do not feed the entire broken candidate to one late
release check and treat the first random exception as
coverage of every gate. Record individual mutations
of a previously eligible baseline, the expected
first enforcing boundary, the required result and
the independently observed absence of forbidden
effects. A defect rejected during source assembly
prevents later candidate installation; a separate
controlled eligible instance is needed to challenge
a runtime-only or physical fault.

| Defect or false inference | First capable owner | Gates | Expected result / protected effect |
|---------------------------+--------------------+-------+------------------------------------|
| Missing trusted clock causes silent ordinary HTMX fallback | Source-derived required FX/route and actual trusted invocation | A, F, H | Reject managed assembly/invocation; no unguarded Claim |
| P23 browser manifest or old bytes offered for P24 | Current compiler/build/assembly, then actual serving/loaded-asset check | B, E, M | Reject incompatible artifact; no stale plan effect |
| Browser-supplied principal, helper role or basis accepted as authority | Trusted ingress, current protected read and model incorporation | D, I | Refuse forged authority before write/disclosure |
| Independent model or proof uses scalar =:request/helper-id= | Original model/operation and source-checked proof subject | B, C, M | Reject full Claim correspondence; real RequestAssignment retained |
| New Organization/Claim policy paired with old certificate | Original source, dependency issuer and selected evidence admission | B, E, M | Stale proof applicability, not a copied pass |
| Proof DAG omits Reassign, initializer or original invariant operation | Independently required source/operation/invariant inventory | B, J, M | Reject full catalog proof; smaller conditional result stays scoped |
| Response and manager-target Reassign omitted from exposed actions | Independent Part VIII product requirement admission | J, P | Full product completion remains missing, not silently excluded |
| Model-owned Claim eligibility duplicated or changed in browser/router | Public model source and source-to-plan/policy correspondence | B, C, N | Reject disagreement or expose opaque implementation premise |
| Uninspected Clojure predicate or raw XTDB writer called proved absent | Source-audit and independent physical writer scope | C, N, O | Mark uninspected/open; no false complete certification |
| Old Membership pre-read substituted for current commit authorization | Trusted guarded transaction and selected provider consistency | D, F, O | Deny invalid incorporation; pre-read is not guard witness |
| Submitted XTDB effect appends an unaccounted write | Physical statement/gateway and relevant all-writer footprint | G, M, O | No strong execution-refinement admission |
| Replacement document erases newly added field or permits duplicate primary | Transaction guard/frame/cardinality and all relevant writers | D, G, O | Prevent forbidden transition or report physical premise unproved |
| Same C42 rejected by new open-Request guard despite stored success | Trusted original-command binding/history resolver | K, F | Resolve compatible historical result before new incorporation |
| A1 abort/HTTP timeout/current claimed card used to infer C42 result | Authoritative command history and qualified disclosure | I, K | Retain =:commit-unknown= unless C42-specific evidence arrives |
| Dispatcher dies after commit, notification debt erased | Original atomic publication-intent and selected dispatcher recovery | F, K, O | Domain commit stays committed; owed notice survives under strong profile |
| Late subscriber or failed backup router silently reports freshness | Registration fence, replay, gap recovery and authorized acquisition | L, O | No false freshness or inaccessible authorized manual Refresh |
| SSE/reconnect changes Bob's board without a user Refresh | Scoped read/adoption policy and last physical browser effect | D, L | No unauthorized remote acquisition or DOM adoption |
| O2 notice creates ungranted A2 while A1 is pending | One-logical-read grant, qualified progression and installed coverage | L, K | Preserve new debt; no unsolicited successor read |
| Partial OOB install or retired callback declared settled | Real HTMX completion and target/effect generation | G, L, H | Keep installation debt; prohibit obsolete DOM mutation |
| Preflight predicts future network or recovery flag has no real branch | Original dynamic outcome/recovery structure | F, H | Reject missing coverage before exposing effect; don't predict availability |
| Checked local Ring wrapper but production listener uses old handler | Actual Biff host installation and current activation | E, G, H | No installed/activated production claim for substitute handler |
| External theorem covers different checker or copied proof map | Independent formal import and production S2–S4 relation | I, M, O | Keep abstract proof scoped; fail requested transfer |
| Skipped required test or prior Chromium fixture credited as current | Named release gate/evidence issuer and actual browser installation | G, M | =:skipped=, =:stale= or =:missing= rather than passed |
| Human/LLM flags an odd but valid business rule | Product intent owner, not mechanical proof checker | C, P | Advisory only; no unauthorized policy rewrite or false proof failure |

The defect matrix is a *falsification plan*, not
a claim that one running candidate visits all
these boundaries. Every chosen mutant starts
with its corresponding real eligible baseline,
then changes one owned condition while holding
other known prerequisites fixed enough to reach
the declared check. If an earlier unrelated
contradiction masks it, the test is inconclusive
for that target boundary rather than a
successful kill. A post-effect observer can
diagnose harm but cannot prove prevention.

A physical check reports the *actual* submitted
transaction, executed handler or browser
effect and its independent observation window.
Silence in logs, absence of a rendered card,
an EDN =:passed= status, expected test-runner
exception or a disconnected fixture does
not independently demonstrate that a
forbidden write or disclosure never happened.

*** Stop the candidate without changing model truth

The above release intent has *four distinct
decisions* under Part XI:

| Decision subject | This defective candidate's disposition | What it must not imply |
|------------------+----------------------------------------+------------------------|
| Candidate construction/admission | Block the selected strong request on known incompatible artifact, missing FX/recovery, original capability and proof coverage | A generated green subgraph cannot redefine the requirements |
| Host installation | No permission to present this candidate as a valid installed generation; a separately admitted repaired candidate needs actual handler/writer/assets observed | A local system map is not an installed listener |
| Activation/public exposure | No permission for this candidate to take over traffic or continue incompatible old callbacks | Earlier deployment or old theorem is not successor permission |
| Requested completion | Operational HumanHelp, compositional Claim and selected external formal qualifications remain independently unestablished | Failing one profile does not retroactively invalidate any genuine narrower theorem or committed domain history |

The full original requirements cannot be silently
relabeled =:inapplicable= after a blocker. For a
mandatory result, distinguish Part XI's
=:failed=, =:incomplete=, =:unavailable=,
=:unsupported=, =:skipped=, =:stale= and
=:missing= instead of replacing all with
one =:false=. A genuinely =:passed= local
gate still retains its precise subject
and applicability; it does not make
the combined strong release eligible.

A candidate whose static assembly is known
invalid is stopped before newly exposing its
managed effects. That does *not* assert that
every possible dynamic race was exercised.
If an earlier separately admitted generation
already incorporated C42 before a later
response, render, notice or host failure,
the authoritative commit is *not rolled back*,
and C42's client outcome remains uncertain
until valid command-specific evidence
establishes it. Retire this candidate's
unissued or obsolete effects and keep
separately owned command/disclosure,
publication, and recovery obligations
according to their true histories.

An old generation may remain active only
while its own qualified policy, writer,
principal and release assumptions still
hold. Changing the planned artifact does
not resurrect a stale browser callback;
rollback of code does not undo a durable
RequestAssignment or authorize replaying
an unknown command as a new C43.

*** Reconstruct at the original owner, not by editing success flags

The repaired candidate is a *new qualified
construction*, not the old candidate with
renamed file digests or hand-edited
`:passed=` fields. Re-establish the
following owned sequence; independently
satisfy its original selected profile
rather than allowing the release report
to choose a smaller denominator.

1. **Source and requirements.** Reacquire
   current public HumanHelp model and
   original product decisions, including
   RequestAssignment, Membership,
   Organization, actual Reassign target
   selection, all six lifecycle actions,
   Create, search/options, scoped
   Refresh, pending Response decision,

   and protected writer obligations.
   Select the Response contract through
   the product owner before claiming
   full operational completion.
2. **Construction and type/Choreo
   admission.** Regenerate the supported
   typed rules, source-owned operations,
   global/local Choreo, executable plans,
   route/FX requirements and real declared
   recovery branches. Reject new
   contradictions *before* installation;
   do not invent a browser-specific
   Claim policy or silent legacy route.
3. **Trusted providers and backend.**
   Bind actual clock, actor, Request,
   Membership, Organization and selected
   protected models to the real serving
   handler. Establish current principal,
   immutable logical command binding,
   transaction guard/frame/cardinality,
   exact submitted writer and required
   durable command/publication storage.
   The physical provider's internal
   prestate and all-writer coverage
   require their actual qualified
   evidence or disclosed premise.
4. **Browser and publication.**
   Rebuild from the current semantic
   manifest; check emitted/staged bytes,
   actually served/loaded bootstrap,
   current Biff handler, real HTMX
   request/swap/OOB completion and
   resource permissions. Preserve
   Bob's remote advisory-only policy,
   one-use scoped Refresh, independent
   manual acquisition if no notice
   arrived and honest uncovered debt.
5. **Proof and release evidence.**
   Regenerate original-source obligation
   closure and certificate candidates;
   recheck issued handles, used premises,
   changed implementation dependencies,
   mandatory external checker S0–S4

   Claim proof is useful but not

6. **Reevaluation.** Re-run each applicable
   independent positive and targeted
   negative test at its legitimate

The sequence above describes
*dependencies and evidence subjects*,
not functions named =prepare!=,
=compose-application!=, =admit-generation!=
or =release/admit!=. R4 used

implementations may combine
phases while retaining the
separate subject and
check/observation obligations.

*** Demonstrate nonvacuous recovery and bounded claims

A fixed source is not enough:

** Final unified invariants

The unified design is one coherent account of what an application *means*,
which participants may learn and do, how authoritative facts change, which
physical effects implement that meaning, and exactly what the available
evidence establishes. Its purpose is not to replace ordinary Clojure web
development with a proof-only application language. It makes the supported,
correctness-relevant web domain narrower and more explicit than arbitrary
computation, so construction, source-derived checking and real enforcement can
work together without giving either a fictional authority.

These are the closing invariants of Parts I–XII, not a second model language,
an additional runtime policy registry, or new completion criteria. Each
applies only to its admitted subject and selected assurance/release profile; a
stronger conclusion requires the independently named supporting source,
theorem, observation and physical correspondence. The final sixteen Gates A–P
and four independent Part XI completion milestones retain their existing
owners and cannot be replaced by this summary.

*** Application meaning and executable construction

A Gesso application has *one original public semantic construction*. Models
own business policy, actor/relationship eligibility, disclosure, authoritative
state and permitted effects. Choreo describes typed interactions and the
knowledge participants must possess; its global machine admits no operation
whose projected local participant cannot justify its relevant inputs, causal
order or branch choice. Projection constructs local machines from that same
meaning. Views attach those operations to actual affordances and presentation;
application construction joins models, plans, routes, effects, transports,
browser artifacts, acquisition and corresponding checking into one
source-derived object, not independently hand-maintained copies.

Knowledge is not the same thing as data existing somewhere in a globally
described application. A participant knows only what its declared local input,
valid communication, authorized observation, deterministic derivation or
explicitly admitted trusted assertion establishes. Communication is one way to
produce knowledge, not the definition of distributed knowledge. Role,
participant, principal, resource, transport attempt and server host have
distinct identities; none may be inferred or authorized from another merely by
giving them matching names.

The portable **executable semantic core** is the permanent source of the
supported machine behavior. It is not identical to the small propositional
**proof kernel**: the former runs defined Gesso semantics, while the latter
checks specific derivations under an explicit logic. Finite checking, theorem
elaboration, independent proof assistants, generated model checking and test
instrumentation have distinct jobs; they neither replace the executable core
nor become new owners of HumanHelp's business rules. A pure browser transition
boundary and the relevant Clojure/JVM implementation can be compared only
through declared semantics and qualified correspondence, not through parallel
human-written versions of the same policy.

Ordinary Clojure remains the application author's medium, including complex
domain behavior and existing supported libraries. Gesso generates accepted
internal rules, obligations, plans and formal representations where its
precise language permits; authors need not maintain handwritten parallel TLA+,
Quint, Recife or proof-assistant specifications of their app. Host-language
policies outside the closed checked language require honest public typed,
effect, dependency and authority contracts with explicit opaque or trusted
implementation-conformance premises. Neither an unknown Clojure predicate nor
an unsupported program is made verified by calling it a rule. The checked
subset must not define away independently required application operations.

The source semantic owner remains single when the original business policy
changes: change the model/requirement and regenerate the affected Choreo,
projections, proof subjects, application closure, artifacts and actual
installation qualifications. A browser, router, auditor, report or formal
generator may not silently repair itself by inventing a second policy owner.
Source-derived audit and readable first-blocker diagnosis are projections of
that same original source, with their actual inspection coverage and
unexamined code made explicit.

*** Authority, commands, and observations

The browser is adversarial relative to authoritative model truth. It cannot
grant server rights by posting a principal, role, tenant, Request identifier,
capability-shaped map, proof report, claimed basis, plan label, provenance or
saved client state. Trusted server boundaries authenticate the principal,
select the admitted operation/target and reauthorize *current* read,
subscription, command-result disclosure and mutation. A presented affordance,
nominal value or checked theorem does not substitute for the guarded
authoritative action.

The authoritative transition enforces the current original model policy and
all required source-owned writes in its declared atomic frame. For HumanHelp
Claim that includes the actual Request, independent RequestAssignment
one-primary relationship, current Membership/Organization eligibility, command
history and any selected durable publication intent. A stale external read,
typed transaction plan, locally accepted write receipt, matching later card or
checked ASSERT/PUT syntax does not independently attest transaction-internal
prestate, all relevant writers, preserved unrelated fields, ABA history or
physically committed outcome. The selected backend's exact enforcement and any
open provider premises remain visible. XTDB may be deliberately chosen as the
implementation substrate when it simplifies real correctness; semantic
concepts should not be confused with incidental XTDB representation or
burdened by speculative portability requirements.

A static operation, one logical command, a particular attempt, physical
submission, transport request, browser execution and later observation are
*not* interchangeable identities. A command preserves its immutable original
binding across admitted retries. Incorporation, durable historical
attribution, transaction/provider result, HTTP delivery, participant
knowledge, current state and physically adopted presentation remain distinct.
A lost response after possible submission leaves a genuine unknown until
qualified command-specific evidence establishes the original result or valid
exclusion. A later Request state cannot establish that C42 incorporated, even
when it looks compatible; another attempt's abort does not exclude a
concurrent incorporation. Historical compatible replay may be permitted even
after a new-command Claim guard becomes false, but current result disclosure
remains authorized independently.

An authoritative read identifies its principal, scope, original
query/relationship meaning, projection, trusted provider position and
coverage. An authoritative *absence* is a qualified negative observation under
the appropriate disclosure semantics, not a missing DOM row, local filter,
silent subscriber or failed network request. Domain revision, transaction
basis, valid time, provider progression, observation, command, request,
resource instance and assembly generation remain separate coordinates. Generic
Live cannot invent total ordering from opaque basis strings, timestamps,
invalidation arrival or source names. Only the chosen trusted authority can
establish the progression and coverage relation needed by a read or
command-resolution claim.

*** Presentation, resources, and recovery

Optimism is typed, nonauthoritative, provisional knowledge of one command or
user intent under its admitted source and available basis. It may display
expected consequences but cannot claim incorporation, authorize new actions or
suppress unknown command outcomes. A creator's Create intent does not require
a fictional earlier observation of an entity that does not yet exist.
Provisional settlement, rejection, unknown status, supersession and postcommit
UI failure have different meanings and recovery owners.

The browser realizes its local machine through a small portable pure
state/event-to-abstract-effect transition boundary and a deliberately narrow
host-effect shell. HTMX retains the ordinary request/response, out-of-band
target, swap, settlement and lifecycle work it already owns. Gesso gates or
observes the documented boundaries needed for semantic safety; a bespoke HTMX
extension or replacement client network stack is not an architectural
prerequisite. Gesso-owned timers, DOM effects, deferred callbacks, continuity,
optimistic presentation and related browser resource effects have explicit
ownership and observable completion.

Semantic retirement revokes the relevant execution/ resource owner's effect
rights *before* best-effort physical cleanup. Shared resources independently
owned by other live executions retain their own legitimate rights. A callback,
HTTP response or timer must recheck its actual current effect/ target
ownership at the last physical mutation, not only when scheduled. A reused
logical DOM ID, failed abort, replaced plan or newer browser generation cannot
resurrect retired rights. Installation is recorded after the selected actual
physical effect completes, not merely on HTTP 200, response parsing or an
intended swap. Selection, scroll, focus, compatible drafts and details
continuity preserve local presentation only; they do not freeze model truth or
grant obsolete continuation authority.

Gesso Live transports scope-bound **advisory** information that relevant
authority may have changed. It is not a second database, automatic read
permission, authentic command result, subscription receipt or DOM
installation. A selected durable profile records the required original
publication intent in a suitable authoritative commit boundary and separately
owns dispatch, retry, deduplication and failure accounting. Neither an outbox
nor a locally complete router filter proves that a late subscriber cannot miss
an invalidation. Initial observation, registration fencing, qualified
replay/gap detection, failover and independently permitted reacquisition have
explicit owners and reliability premises. Duplicated advisory redelivery is
safe under its actual disclosure, resource and idempotency contract; it never
duplicates business incorporation.

Acquisition and *visible adoption* require their own current authorization,
source/query scope, trusted observation coverage, selected user grant when
applicable, and actual completed browser installation. For HumanHelp, remote
Create and remote lifecycle changes, including changes to already- visible
cards, remain advisory until Bob explicitly grants one scoped logical Refresh
under the selected ordinary policy. A notice, reconnect, router failover or
later advisory arriving during that cycle cannot mint an unrequested successor
read. A provider- qualified already covered newer observation may discharge
the corresponding debt; incomparable basis, incomplete OOB install or
uncovered query retains it. Creator- local accepted Create and narrowly
correlated authorized own-command recovery are separately declared exceptions,
not general remote auto-adoption.

Lost command outcome, lost notice, expired authority, invalidated browser
resources, provider failure and changed release need separately owned
recovery. Convergence and liveness are conditional on the named fairness,
retention, availability, scope, authenticated user action and environmental
premises. In particular a policy requiring Bob to press Refresh cannot promise
automatic visible convergence if he never does so.

*** Evidence, release, and topology

Every accepted conclusion keeps its exact source, proposition, scope, original
required obligation inventory, selected profile, premise set, checker or test
mechanism, observation/evidence provenance, interpretation version and actual
implementation and installation applicability. Original product/
operation/invariant requirements are independent of the currently discovered
proof, route, browser or writer graph. A closed smaller graph proves or checks
only its named smaller subject. A generator cannot silently remove Reassign,
Response, another relevant writer, a required dynamic recovery or a positive
operation and thereby complete the requested larger claim.

Mechanically derived proof status is reserved for what an accepted formal
semantics and actually checked derivation establish under named assumptions.
Conditional induction, finite state exhaustion, production test,
original-source type/preflight, physical writer observation, independent
mathematical theorem and formal-to-production refinement are distinct evidence
classes. Exact finite checking establishes its finite bounded subject;
unbounded transfer requires sound abstraction or another qualified theorem.
Tests remain essential for trusted host interfaces, libraries, actual
Chromium/HTMX, Biff/XTDB, deployment, security, faults and scale; they are not
a synonym for proof. Likewise a certificate-shaped map, hash, copyable report
or tool exit code is not proof issuance, runtime authorization or an installed
execution capability.

The closed seven-rule kernel's possible external theorem has explicit S0
rule-level soundness and S1 derivation- system soundness subjects. S2 actual
Clojure checker correspondence, S3 typed source-atom interpretation and S4
issuer/application to physical transfer are separately qualified. A sound
abstract theorem can remain true when a backend, handler, artifact or external
writer changes; its *physical applicability* must then be requalified. A
source- derived proof hierarchy cannot invent its own complete application
catalog or authenticate untested physical observations.

A released application is not defined by one green map. The original selected
requirements and permitted evidence mechanisms precede evaluation; the
candidate, actual installed host, current activation and named completion
claim require four subject- specific decisions. Application safety is enforced
from the first served managed effect, not postponed until full formal or
distributed qualification. Directional old/new client/server compatibility,
retired effect rights, real served/loaded artifact identities, protected
writers, command history, source generation and failure recovery are
independently checked where relevant. Rollback of code neither reverses a
durable transaction nor erases a pending historical command.

Operational HumanHelp completion, compositional certification, external formal
verification and production multi-node realization are four distinct milestone
claims with their own original requirements and evidence. The full HumanHelp
product includes six lifecycle actions, Create, manager-target Reassign,
current model authorization, rich adopted- board behavior, selected Response
interaction, explicit Refresh and fourteen independent positive/adverse
acceptance gates. A narrow Claim proof does not complete the product; an
operational application need not claim all external metatheory, and a two-
host prototype does not qualify every production topology. A reject-
everything candidate or a never- executed mandatory test cannot satisfy a
usable completion gate.

Multiple physical hosts realize the same logical authority, command, Choreo
and browser contract. They do not make a new business semantics. Durable model
facts remain the ordinary cross-host rendezvous; selected authoritative
command history, publication recovery, subscriber interest, authenticated
acquisition, router failover and browser adoption carry their real failure
windows. A node's interchangeability does not prove exactly- once effects,
complete interest knowledge, all-message receipt or participant liveness. A
Clojure router and a later Rust optimization may implement the same semantic
contract; neither a particular router topology nor universal durable
participant messaging is mandatory for ordinary single-node Gesso.

*** Source-owned audit, intent, and repair

An application's correctness-relevant policy is visible as named original
rules, operation inputs and effects, authority and disclosure, lifecycle
transitions, dependencies, admitted assumptions and required capabilities. The
audit identifies the code and physical paths it actually inspected, and which
Clojure predicates, callbacks, FX, external services and writers remain opaque
or uninspected. “No detected escape in the inspected subset” does not mean
“all source policy was inspected.” The report is a read-only explanation under
the same disclosure policy, not a second source of authority or an issuer.

A diagnostic finds the earliest legitimately knowable blocker and retains the
dependent failures as consequences. A model counterexample refers to its
actual formal subject, trace, abstraction, bounds and premises; a fixture
cannot be passed off as a generated external checker run or a real XTDB
incident. Mutants need a predeclared first enforcing gate, a usable valid
positive, and independent observation of the prohibited effect within the
actual scope. A late detection is not before-effect prevention, and no
accepted status may be manufactured by silently relaxing the selected profile.

Human or AI-assisted review may identify surprising intent, missing business
restrictions or reasonable alternative policies. It does not prove a
well-typed policy wrong, issue admission, grant new rights or change source.
Only the authorized product owner can select a new business requirement and
promote it into the original public model/semantic contract. Repair then
regenerates and rechecks only the affected source, proof, plan, adapter, host,
asset and physical evidence cone. Weakening an invariant, adding an axiom or
removing a required feature is a new claim, not an invisible way to make the
old claim pass.

*** Final design principle

#+begin_quote
A Gesso choreography is a typed, source-owned description of how participants
acting for principals interact with evolving authoritative facts, communicate
justified knowledge, and execute permitted local behavior.

One executable semantic machine joins public model truth, global and local
Choreo, declarative HTMX-facing views, typed provisional browser behavior,
trustworthy guarded transactions and scoped advisory recovery. The framework
generates the proof and assembly machinery around that meaning rather than
asking application authors to write separate business rules for every runtime
or theorem prover.

The same design is valid on one node or across multiple hosts. Its logical
meaning is stable while physical registration, publication, command history,
installation and recovery carry explicit real-world premises.

Gesso may prove the supported claims it has actually checked, and may accept
explicitly qualified trusted assumptions, but it may not transform a typed
label, finite test, diagnostic, report, compilation, browser success or
source-consistent graph into a stronger certificate or production fact without
the corresponding evidence and actual enforcing boundary.

Success is usable, authorized product behavior with its true source, physical
effects, proof scope and remaining obligations visible. No apparently green
subset, missing required capability, unchecked writer, silent downgrade,
fabricated command outcome, unauthorized adoption or unexamined assumption can
stand in for that result.
#+end_quote
